title: 3 Body Problem Books
description:
Dive into the boundless cosmos of Cixin Liu's acclaimed 3 Body Problem series, now available at Books2Door. With its compelling narrative, visionary storytelling, and profound exploration of the human condition, this series is a must-read for any science fiction fan. 

Whether you're a seasoned enthusiast or new to the genre, these books offer a captivating glimpse into the infinite possibilities of the universe. They invite readers to ponder the mysteries that lie beyond the stars. Explore the collection today and prepare to be spellbound by the wonders that await within its pages.

Overview of the 3 Body Problem Series
Embark on a riveting adventure spanning three novels: The Three-Body Problem, The Dark Forest, and Death's End. Set against the backdrop of a turbulent universe, each instalment seamlessly weaves together elements of hard science fiction, philosophy, and history to create a truly immersive reading experience.

In The Three-Body Problem, readers are introduced to a world on the brink of chaos as humanity grapples with the impending threat of an alien invasion. Through the eyes of protagonist Ye Wenjie and a cast of intriguing characters, Liu explores themes of resilience, morality, and the consequences of scientific discovery.

Continuing the saga in The Dark Forest, Liu delves deeper into the complexities of interstellar diplomacy and the existential challenges posed by extraterrestrial civilisations. With its intricate plot twists and philosophical musings, this instalment offers a compelling examination of the human condition in the face of existential threats.

The epic conclusion unfolds in Death's End, where the universe's fate hangs in the balance as humanity confronts the ultimate showdown with its alien adversaries. As the boundaries between reality and fiction blur, Liu delivers a breathtaking finale that will leave readers pondering the nature of existence long after the final page is turned.

Meet Cixin Liu: 
Born in 1963 in Yangquan, China, Cixin Liu is a visionary author whose works have captivated readers around the globe. With a background in engineering, Liu brings a unique perspective to his storytelling, blending scientific accuracy with imaginative speculation to create worlds that are as awe-inspiring as they are thought-provoking.

Liu's fascination with the cosmos and its mysteries is evident in his writing. He seamlessly integrates cutting-edge scientific concepts with richly developed characters and intricate plots. His ability to envision grandiose scenarios while grounding them in scientific reality has earned him critical acclaim and a devoted following among fans of the genre.

Over the years, Liu's contributions to the science fiction genre have been recognised with numerous awards, including the prestigious Hugo Award for Best Novel, making him the first Asian author to receive this honour. His work inspires readers and fellow writers alike, cementing his legacy as one of the foremost voices in contemporary science fiction.

title: A Series of Unfortunate Events Books
description:
A Series of Unfortunate Events: The Delightfully Dreadful Collection by Lemony Snicket

If you are looking for a story with a happy ending, you have come to the wrong place. The A Series of Unfortunate Events collection is a masterclass in gothic children's fiction, chronicling the turbulent lives of the Baudelaire orphans. Violet, Klaus, and Sunny are charming, intelligent, and resourceful, but they are also exceptionally unlucky. From the moment they lose their parents in a mysterious fire, they are pursued by the nefarious Count Olaf, a villainous master of disguise who will stop at nothing to steal their family fortune.

Whether you're a long-time fan of the Lemony Snicket books or a newcomer drawn in by the hit Netflix adaptation, this series remains a permanent fixture in the "unputdownable" canon of middle-grade literature.

1. The Baudelaire Journey: From Bad to Worse

This 13-book saga is renowned for its unique narrative voice, dark humour, and educational "word of the day" asides. It’s the perfect series for readers aged 9-12 who appreciate a story that respects their intelligence and isn't afraid to explore the more "miserable" side of life.

  • The Complete Series of Unfortunate Events Set: Why experience only one tragedy when you can have all thirteen? Our complete box sets are the most cost-effective way to follow the Baudelaires from The Bad Beginning to the aptly titled The End.

  • Standout Chapters in Misery: Our collection includes individual titles for those looking to replace a worn-out copy of classics like The Hostile Hospital or The Penultimate Peril.

2. Why Readers Obsess Over Lemony Snicket

Lemony Snicket (the elusive pen name of Daniel Handler) created a world that feels both timeless and strangely modern. The series has stood the test of time because it balances high-stakes peril with a profound sense of justice—or lack thereof.

  • The Villain We Love to Hate: Count Olaf’s increasingly ridiculous disguises and terrible acting provide a comedic counterpoint to the genuine danger the children face.

  • The Power of Resourcefulness: Each orphan has a specific skill—Violet’s inventing, Klaus’s research, and Sunny’s... unique biting abilities. These books empower young readers by showing that even in the face of adult incompetence, children can be the smartest people in the room.

3. Build Your Own Library: Bulk Lots & Joblots

For schools, libraries, or the most dedicated collectors, we occasionally offer massive bulk collections and joblots. These are perfect for shared reading groups or ensuring every classroom has a copy of this essential series.

title: A. A. Milne Books
description:
A.A. Milne, an Iconic British Author 

Alan Alexander Milne was born in London in 1882 and for many years was a playwright before the emergence of the nation's much-loved bear. After serving in both World Wars, Milne lived in East Sussex with his wife and son, Christopher Robin. Much to Milne’s annoyance, Winnie the Pooh became a phenomenon and a household name, earning Milne fame across the globe for creating the nation's favourite bear. 

Winnie the Pooh and Friends 

The Winnie the Pooh stories and characters we love today were inspired by Milne’s son and his teddies. Christopher Robin Milne and the fun he would have with his toys is what sparked the imagination of his father. You can still visit Christopher Robin’s original toys which are housed in The New York Public Library. 

Much of A. A. Milne and his real-life adventures with his son are featured within the Winnie the Pooh stories. Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore, Kanga, Roo and Tigger are based on his read soft toys and the Hundred Acre Woods is based on Ashdown Forest which was outside their farmhouse in Sussex. E. H. Shepard, the illustrator that brought the stories to life, even drew on the landscapes of Ashdown Forest as inspiration for many of the illustrations he provided for the Pooh books. 

Milne’s classic children's stories have been adapted on screen many times, so far there are a total of thirteen movies based on his characters. The Most recent is the 2018 adaptation called Christopher Robin starring Ewan McGregor as an older Christopher Robin revisiting his childhood.

Books by A.A. Milne have also been a popular choice as gifts for children, making these a beautiful addition to their reading library. We have a beautiful Winnie the Pooh Complete Collection 30 Books Box Set which features thirty stories broken up into small books. Reading these short stories out loud with children is a lovely way to bond and encourage their development in reading or listening skills. This boxset will look perfect on any bookshelf, whether they are a gift for a baby shower, a birthday present for a little one or for pure nostalgia purposes, this beautifully decorated box is the perfect addition to anyone's literary collection. 

We also have a collection aimed at babies and toddlers, Disney Baby Winnie the Pooh My First Library 12 Board Books. These books include simplified stories and everyday learning stories for you and your child to read along with. For example, this collection includes Count with Pooh, A Bath with Tigger and Hundred Acre Walk to name a few. Alternatively, we have Winnie-The-Pooh The Complete Collection 6 Books Set, which is aimed at older readers. Whether it is the first time your child is reading it or if it is a story they are familiar with, this book collection is a great introduction to longer texts and reading more independently. Each book contains beautiful illustrations and comes in a charming slipcase to keep them all together. 


For other classic children’s novels, be sure to check out our World of Peter Rabbit Complete Collection or our Paddington Bear Classic Collection as well as our full range of classic children's books.

title: Accessible Books - SEN, Disability, Struggling Readers
description:
Welcome to our accessible books collection! It includes a range of books that could be suitable for SEN readers, those with disabilities, struggling readers, dyslexia, or any other circumstance that makes traditional books unsuitable.

To support readers who face challenges with traditional formats, we’ve carefully curated this collection of accessible books, perfect for those who need additional support or for anyone looking to share these stories with loved ones who do.

At Books2Door, we believe literature should be for everyone - its magic deserves to reach every corner of the world. We recognise that not all readers experience books in the same way, and we are committed to ensuring that stories remain open to all.

We know that accessibility is an ongoing journey, and there is no one definiton of an SEND book. While our collection isn’t yet perfect, we’re working hard to make it as inclusive as possible. In the meantime, we invite you to explore what we offer- let’s find the perfect book for you together!

Dyslexia Friendly Books

Our collection of dyslexia friendly books is designed to make reading more comfortable and enjoyable for those with dyslexia. These books feature:

  • Special Fonts: Printed with dyslexia-friendly fonts that help prevent letters from appearing jumbled.
  • Tinted Paper: Cream or yellow paper to reduce glare and visual stress.
  • Engaging Content: Written by award-winning authors, these books maintain high-quality storytelling.
  • Illustrations: Accompanied by illustrations that aid comprehension and keep readers engaged.

Be on the lookout for titles like Of Mice and Men and The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie by Barrington Stoke, which are known for their tailored features for dyslexic readers.

Kids Audiobooks

For children who prefer listening to stories or have difficulties reading text, our kids' audiobooks offer an excellent alternative; after all, adults love audiobooks now in this fast-paced world. Audiobooks can help develop listening skills, comprehension, and a love for storytelling. We provide a wide range of audiobooks, from popular series and standalone titles, that captivate young minds and make reading accessible to everyone.

Every Cherry Publishing

Every Cherry Publishing is dedicated to creating inclusive and accessible content for young readers. Their books often feature diverse characters and stories that resonate with children from all backgrounds. With an emphasis on representation and accessibility, Every Cherry Publishing offers books that come with symbolised adaptations and illustrated and accessible editions of the world's greatest classics. These editions now feature symbols alongside the text to support reading, allowing everyone to enjoy these world-renowned titles.

Barrington Stoke Books

Barrington Stoke is a renowned publisher that specialises in dyslexia-friendly books. Their titles are designed with the following features to support readers with dyslexia:

  • Custom Font and Layout: Uses a unique dyslexia-friendly font and spacious layout to make reading easier.
  • High-Quality Paper: Cream-coloured, heavy paper reduces glare and prevents text from showing through.
  • Accessible Content: These books are expertly edited to ensure clarity without patronising the reader. They are both engaging and challenging.

Books such as Animal Farm by George Orwell and Lark by Anthony McGowan are part of our Barrington Stoke collection, offering high-quality, accessible literature for young readers.

We hope this collection ensures that readers of all abilities can enjoy the joy of reading with content tailored to support their needs.

title: Adam Kay Books
description:
Adam Kay is a British author, comedian, former doctor and screenwriter who shot to fame for his bestselling book This Is Going To Hurt.

Adam went to Dulwich College before studying medicine at Imperial College, London. This was where he first began performing as a comedian whilst he was still studying medicine and formed a musical comedy group called Amateur Transplants. Following this he worked as a gynaecologist and obstetrician before he finally decided to retire as a doctor and write his debut novel. 

Drawing from his experience as a NHS doctor, Kay wrote This Is Going To Hurt as a hilarious take on the plight of NHS doctors. As a doctor himself; Kay gives the readers a detailed insight into his experience with the NHS. This makes for some exceptional and entertaining reading material. 

The book is written in an accessible, episodic, and engaging way to give a real picture of what some doctors go through in their profession. The book is narrated through diary entries of Adam Kay’s experience as he ascends from a junior doctor to being a consultant. He specialises in gynaecology and has both funny and sad stories to tell. Kay shares how he decided to quit the job as a doctor because of an incident that changed his life. He reveals how he has discovered that those in the profession want to come out because of how they are treated. Kay reveals how the doctors are expected to work extra hours without any compensation for the extra work. Which in turn impacts their mental health and lives. As Kay shares the plight of NHS doctors with his readers; in doing so he makes the world empathise with his fellow doctors.

Even though the book focuses on British health systems, some of their flaws cut across many medical systems in many countries. The author uses humour when detailing the nuances of working in healthcare. Which makes the heart-wrenching realities of these stories bearable, even engaging to the reader.

Kay's second book, Twas the Night Shift before Christmas, also went on to become the number one Sunday Times bestseller, selling millions of copies. In this classic, Adam Kay delves back into his diaries for a hilarious, horrifying and sometimes heartbreaking peek behind the blue curtain at Christmas time. This is a love letter to all those who spend their festive season on the front line, removing babies and baubles from the various places they get stuck, at the most wonderful time of the year. 

Yet another bestseller; Adam Kay’s new book about the NHS; Undoctored is also a major success. It is a hilarious, heartbreaking and humbling account of a doctor’s experience. Undoctored is about what happens when a doctor hangs up his scrubs, but medicine refuses to let go of him. Yet again, the book is a heartbreaking story told in a humorous fashion.

Undoctored is about an extraordinary medical school education but it is also about opening old wounds and examining the present-day scars, about hospital admissions and personal ones. Adam Kay's Undoctored is a rollercoaster of drastic feelings—there are bits that will have you in tears and there are parts that will have you in splits. An astonishing portrait of a life in and out of medicine, from one of Britain's finest storytellers. 

These three of Adam Kay’s books may be centred around the hospital and doctor’s experiences but they make great reading material for everyone. Anyone that has ever been to a hospital or been sick and everyone that works within the NHS; will find Adam Kay’s accounts touching. Whilst Kay’s ability to narrate real experiences and stories using humour makes his books engrossing reads for readers across ages.

That said, Adam Kay’s children’s books—Kay’s Anatomy and Kay’s Marvellous Medicine are both in a league of their own.

Kay's Marvellous Medicine for children aged 9+  is a fun, absurd and wild exploration of Ancient Egypt. The book answers questions like why Ancient Egyptians thought the brain was just a useless load of old stuffing that might as well be chucked in the bin, why teachers forced their pupils to smoke cigarettes, why hairdressers would cut off their customers' legs, and why people used to get paid for farting. A gross, gruesome but highly entertaining look at the human body and its functions; this book is guaranteed to inspire the next generation of medics.

Kay’s Anatomy for the same age group of children is also a discovery of all the weird and wonderful things that go on inside our body. The book covers key stage 2 / 3 human biology syllabus in a slightly repulsive, hilarious but fascinating way. Funny and informative; this is another Adam Kay book that every aspiring little doctor must read.

United by their shared fate, they embark on an unforgettable journey that explores the fragility of life, the power of human connection, and the urgency to truly live when faced with imminent death. With eloquence and sensitivity, Silvera crafts a narrative that examines themes of love, friendship, and the value of every precious moment we have.

What If It's Us is Co-authored by Becky Albertalli, this enchanting collaboration introduces us to Arthur and Ben, two boys whose paths cross one summer day in the bustling streets of New York City. As the universe conspires to bring them together, they embark on a whirlwind of missed connections, serendipitous encounters, and heartwarming possibilities. With endearing characters and a narrative brimming with humour and heart, Silvera and Albertalli explore the exhilarating and unpredictable nature of love. Through the ups and downs of their relationship, Arthur and Ben navigate the complexities of their own identities, learn the importance of honesty and vulnerability, and discover that sometimes, the universe has its own plans for us.

Prepare to be moved by this emotionally charged novel that delves deep into grief, loss, and the complexities of moving on. History Is All You Left Me introduces us to Griffin, our protagonist, who is shattered by the sudden death of his ex-boyfriend and first love, Theo. Battling his own inner demons, Griffin embarks on a journey of healing, filled with memories, secrets, and the hope of finding closure. Silvera skillfully weaves together past and present, as Griffin navigates the blurred lines between love and friendship, truth and perception. Through his exploration of grief, Silvera reminds us of the power of forgiveness, the strength of human resilience, and the enduring bonds that connect us to those we have lost.

As you peruse our carefully curated collection, you'll discover the immense power of Silvera's writing, which captures the rawness of human emotions and the intricate tapestry of relationships. Each book explores profound themes such as identity, self-discovery, love, and the eternal quest for belonging. Silvera's prose is as evocative as it is relatable, transporting readers into the hearts and minds of his characters with vivid authenticity.

Whether you seek a heart-wrenching tale that will leave you breathless or a heartwarming love story that will uplift your spirits, Adam Silvera's books are sure to captivate your imagination. With his unique storytelling style and his ability to create complex and relatable characters, Silvera has earned a devoted following and critical acclaim.

Indulge yourself in the unforgettable narratives of They Both Die at the End, What If It's Us, and History Is All You Left Me. Each book offers a thought-provoking and emotional journey that will stay with you long after you turn the final page. We invite you to immerse yourself in this collection, lose yourself in Silvera's extraordinary worlds, and experience the transformative power of his storytelling. Begin your literary adventure today and discover why Adam Silvera is hailed as a master of contemporary fiction. For more LGBTQIA+ stories, check out our LGBTQIA+ books page. 

About the author: 

Adam Silvera is an exceptionally talented author who has made a significant impact on the contemporary young adult fiction landscape. With his unique voice, poignant storytelling, and ability to tackle complex emotions, Silvera has garnered a dedicated following of readers who eagerly await each new release.

Born and raised in the Bronx, New York, Silvera's writing often reflects his personal experiences and the diverse communities he grew up in. His stories are characterized by their raw authenticity, tackling themes of love, loss, identity, and the complexities of human relationships. One of the defining aspects of Silvera's writing is his ability to weave heart-wrenching narratives with a touch of hope and resilience. He doesn't shy away from exploring the darker aspects of life, delving into themes of grief, mortality, and the fleeting nature of time. Yet, amidst the pain and heartbreak, there is always a glimmer of light, a reminder that even in the face of tragedy, there is room for growth, love, and redemption.

Silvera's storytelling prowess is evident in his bestselling novels, including They Both Die at the End, What If It's Us, and History Is All You Left Me. These books have touched the hearts of readers worldwide, earning critical acclaim for their emotional depth, diverse representation, and thought-provoking narratives. Through his characters' journeys, Silvera challenges societal norms, explores the fluidity of identity, and advocates for empathy, understanding, and acceptance.

Beyond his writing, Silvera has become a respected figure within the literary community. He actively engages with his readers, often participating in book signings, and panel discussions, and fostering connections through social media platforms. His openness and authenticity have created a strong bond between him and his fans, further enhancing the impact of his work.

Adam Silvera's contributions to contemporary young adult fiction are immeasurable. Through his powerful storytelling, he has touched the hearts of countless readers, inspiring empathy, self-reflection, and a deeper understanding of the human experience. With each new book, Silvera continues to prove himself as an author who fearlessly explores the beauty and complexity of life, leaving an indelible mark on the literary world.

title: Agatha Christie Books
description:
Agatha Christie is not only one of the most influential and respected mystery writers Britain has ever produced, but also the bestselling novelist of all time. Her books have only been outsold by The Bible and Shakespeare. During her lifetime, she wrote 74 novels, 165 short stories, plays, poems, and even a travel book. Her immortal characters, such as Poirot and Miss Marple, are regularly rediscovered and adapted into film and TV.

Christie’s most famous novel is Murder on the Orient Express. Hercule Poirot, famous Belgian detective, is travelling home to London on the cross-continental train when it’s stopped by snowfall in 1930s Yugoslavia. The body of an American businessman is discovered, and everyone on the train is a suspect for his murder. This classic work of detective fiction has thrilled readers ever since its first publication in 1934, and has been filmed many times. It's available in ﻿The World's Favourite Agatha Christie along with two more of her most popular novels, And Then There Were None and The Murder of Roger Ackroyd.

Miss Marple is one of Christie’s most beloved characters. The amateur detective appeared in twelve novels, six films, and multiple television series. The elderly spinster uses her shrewd intelligence and wealth of experience to bring the guilty parties to justice. She was created in order to give old maids a voice, and styled her after her grandmother’s friends.

Agatha Miller was born in Torquay in 1890. She started writing The Mysterious Affair at Styles in 1916 because her sister Madge bet her she couldn’t write a good detective story. It introduced the immortal Hercule Poirot, who was inspired by the Belgian soldiers and refugees she encountered during her day job as a nurse.

She married Archie Christie on Christmas Eve 1914, and he returned to the Great War in France three days after. After the war, the couple moved to London, and Christie found a publisher. They contracted her to write five more books, and her writing career was born. In 1922, the couple set out to travel the world. They returned to London, then moved out to Berkshire. Christie’s mother died in April 1926, and in August, Archie asked Agatha for a divorce. On 3 December, she disappeared for ten days, causing a national manhunt, and was found living in a hotel under an assumed name. The couple finally divorced in 1928.

Agatha Christie met and married archaeologist Max Mallowan in 1930, and accompanied him on all his expeditions. In 1934 they moved to rural Oxfordshire, where the couple lived for the rest of their lives, and Christie did most of her writing. She wrote her final novel in 1973 and died in 1976. Concluding novels for both Poirot and Marple were finished in the 1940s and published the year before and ten months after her death, respectively.

At Books2Door, we have many more mysteries waiting for you to solve. In our Crime, Thrillers and Mystery Books collection, we have box sets from classic authors like Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, to contemporary bestsellers like Elly Griffiths. For the young, we have the outrageously popular A Murder Most Unladylike series by Robin Stevens; and strictly for grown-ups, we stock the delicious Dexter series by Jeff Lindsay. Browse our collection now to find your next favourite author.

title: Akira Toriyama Manga
description:
In the vast galaxy of manga and anime, one name reigns supreme: a visionary whose creations have captured the hearts and imaginations of millions worldwide. Welcome to the captivating realm of Akira Toriyama. As you step into the digital aisles of Books2Door, prepare to embark on an exhilarating journey through his illustrious career and delve deep into the timeless classics that continue to shape the landscape of Japanese pop culture.

Born on April 5, 1955, in Nagoya, Japan, Akira Toriyama's love for manga and storytelling began to unfold at an early age. During childhood, he exhibited boundless creativity fueled by a fervent passion for art and storytelling. After honing his skills through diligent practice and unwavering dedication, Toriyama made his professional debut as a manga artist in 1978 with the one-shot Wonder Island, marking the inception of a legendary career, later creating the iconic Dragon Ball series that would revolutionise the industry.

Dragon Ball: A Manga Masterpiece
With his distinctive art style characterised by dynamic action sequences, expressive characters, and whimsical humour, Toriyama quickly rose to prominence. However, it was his groundbreaking series Dragon Ball that catapulted him to global stardom. Debuting in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1984, this epic saga follows the adventures of Son Goku, a martial artist with a heart of gold, as he embarks on a quest to find the mystical Dragon Balls.

Dragon Ball captivated audiences with its exhilarating blend of action, humour, and heartfelt moments, spawning a multimedia empire encompassing anime adaptations, movies, video games, and merchandise. Toriyama's ingenious world-building and ability to seamlessly weave together elements of Eastern mythology and Western science fiction made Dragon Ball an enduring cultural phenomenon that continues to resonate with fans of all ages.

Exploring Dragon Ball Z
Building upon the success of Dragon Ball, Toriyama went on to create its highly acclaimed sequel, Dragon Ball Z. Set several years after the events of its predecessor, this series delves deeper into Goku's journey as he defends Earth from powerful foes and confronts his inner demons. With its epic battles, intricate lore, and poignant character development, Dragon Ball Z cemented Toriyama's legacy as a titan of the manga industry, inspiring countless artists and storytellers around the globe. Find the entire 26-volume collection here at BooksDoor!

At Books2Door, you'll find an extensive selection of Akira Toriyama's manga masterpieces, meticulously curated to cater to fans old and new. Whether you're a seasoned enthusiast reliving the nostalgia of Goku's adventures or a curious newcomer eager to experience the magic for the first time, there's something for everyone within the pages of Toriyama's iconic creations.

The Author Behind the Laughter

As a self-proclaimed mischievous child with a vivid imagination, MacDonald found early inspiration in the heroics of Batman, dreaming of emulating the caped crusader's adventures. This blend of youthful curiosity and ambition laid the groundwork for his storytelling, a path humorously kick-started by winning a fountain pen in a handwriting competition. This anecdote isn't just a testament to MacDonald's early flair for creativity but serves as a reminder of the humble beginnings from which great writers often emerge. Through his stories, MacDonald hopes to ignite a spark of creativity and passion for reading in young minds, echoing the impact of that first fountain pen on his own life.

Discover Alan MacDonald at Books2Door

At Books2Door, dive into the imaginative universe crafted by Alan MacDonald, highlighted by the mischievously funny Dirty Bertie series. These tales, adored by kids and parents alike for their humour and relatable antics, offer an ideal introduction to the joy of reading. Discover a wide range of Bertie's adventures, from "Toothy," showcasing his unrivalled knack for trouble, to "Snow," where his daring exploits set new comedic standards. Each book in our collection invites young readers into Bertie's wonderfully wacky world, promising endless entertainment and laughter.

But there's more to MacDonald's genius than Dirty Bertie. Works like Queen Victoria, Her Great Empire, and Huxley and Flapjack showcase his versatility and ability to engage readers across a spectrum of interests, from historical adventures to whimsical tales of friendship and discovery.

Why Choose Books2Door?

At Books2Door, we believe in the power of stories to enrich the lives of children. Alan MacDonald's books are a testament to the joy and wonder that reading can bring. By featuring his works, we aim to inspire a new generation of readers, igniting in them a lifelong love for books, much like the way a simple fountain pen sparked a young boy's imagination many years ago.

title: Alan Titchmarsh Books
description:
British author, horticulture expert and popular TV presenter; Alan Titchmarsh first started his career in 1968 as an apprentice gardener at Ilkley Council. After which he dabbled in gardening journalism in 1974 as an assistance editor with Hamlyn Publishing. Soon after, he started writing his own gardening books.

Having acquired his experience in the field; Alan then went on to join television as a horticulture expert and shot to fame with BBC’s popular TV programmes like The Nature of Britain, British Isles: A Natural History, How to be a Gardener, Ground Force and Gardeners World. 

Now an ace gardener, established author and renowned TV presenter; he has written more than forty gardening books, as well as six best-selling novels and two memoirs. Titchmarsh was made MBE in the millennium New Year Honours List and holds a Victoria Medal of Honour, the Royal Horticultural Society's highest award. He lives with his wife and a menagerie of animals in Hampshire where he writes his books and gardens organically.

Apart from the many gardening guides, Titchmarsh has also parallelly written several fiction novels like; Only Dad amongst other Alan Titchmarsh autobiographical works like Nobbut A Lad: A Yorkshire Childhood, and Trowel & Error.

If you are someone that loves plants and is willing to learn everything there is to know about gardening then Alan Titchmarsh books are just for you. The 5 Books Collection Set about all things gardening; How to Garden Series 5 Books Collection Set by Alan Titchmarsh is perfect for those invested in organic gardening. The books will take you through all the detailed aspects and types of gardening, from greenhouse gardening to growing roses and more. Alan Titchmarsh imparts a lifetime of expertise in these definitive guides for both beginners and experienced gardeners. Step-by-step illustrations and easy-to-follow instructions will guide you through the basic gardening skills and also on to the advanced techniques, providing everything you need to create and maintain your dream garden.

In light of the organic awakening that has happened across the world; Britain too has rediscovered its passion for home produced fruits and vegetables. Just in time for this homegrown trend; the book Grow your Own Fruit and Veg by Alan Titchmarsh, is a comprehensive guide to growing your own fruits and vegetables. A gardening book for beginners by the nation’s favourite gardener himself! This guide will tell you everything you need to know about growing your own vegetables, fruits, herbs, salads to gourmet and unusual varieties. As well as providing the key facts needed to yield good results and what to do when things go wrong, the text is sprinkled with Alan's personal observations, anecdotes, culinary tips and quirky historical uses. Lavishly illustrated throughout, Grow Your Own Fruit and Veg offers inspiration, in-depth knowledge and practical advice, whether you are looking to be self-sufficient or just to grow a few items on your patio or window box. 

Alan’s writing, however earthy, is not limited to gardening guides. In a fiction collection book set of 3 novels—Alan Titchmarsh 3 Books Collection Set (The Scarlet Nightingale, Bring Me Home & Mr Gandy's Grand Tour); readers will get an opportunity to enjoy Titchmarsh’s storytelling prowess. The first book in the set; The Scarlet Nightingale is set in the 1930s. When seventeen-year-old Rosamund Hanbury leaves behind the endless summers of her coastal Devonshire home for the fast pace of high society London; adventures ensue. Under the expert guidance of her formidable aunt, the country mouse learns how to act like a lady, hosting dinner parties and rubbing shoulders with Britain's most influential. And when the enigmatic Harry Napier sweeps her off her feet at London's famous Café de Paris she could almost forget that Britain has declared war.

Whilst the second book in the collection set; Bring Me Home is a family story with a mystery at its heart. The third and the final book in the set—Mr Gandy's Grand Tour is a story of self discovery. As the protagonist embarks on a grand tour of Europe, following in the footsteps of the aristocrats of the eighteenth century, he anticipates high art, culture and pleasant weather. However, he never expects to encounter new friendships and possibly even love along the way.

title: Alastair Chisholm Books

Now, Alex must follow in his former uncle’s footsteps to complete his last mission: to investigate a multimillionaire names Herod Sayle. Other famous works by Alice Oseman

If you love Heartstopper, you'll want to dive into more of Alice Oseman's books, where Nick and Charlie make cameos.

Solitaire

Alice's debut novel, Solitaire, was published in 2014. It follows Tori Spring, an unhappy and angry teenager. This book, featuring the first appearances of Nick and Charlie, explores Tori's journey through undiagnosed depression with self-deprecating humour, finding joy along the way.

Radio Silence

Published in 2016, Radio Silence follows Frances, overwhelmed by academic pressures and losing sight of her identity. Meeting Aled, a timid genius behind her favourite podcast, helps her rediscover herself. This coming-of-age novel delves into the pressures to succeed, fandom, and the essence of true friendship.

I Was Born for This

In her third novel, I Was Born for This, Oseman follows Angel Rahimi and her favourite band, The Ark. When frontman Jimmy Kaga-Ricci's dreams become a nightmare, he and Angel find their paths unexpectedly crossing. This story explores the gap between dreams and reality, filled with rich character development and emotional depth.

Loveless

Representation is the core theme in Oseman's work. Loveless is an asexual coming-out story set at Durham University. Join Georgia as she navigates her vulnerable journey, adding to the diverse and inclusive stories Oseman is celebrated for.

Now that you're acquainted with Alice Oseman's incredible works, it's time to dive in and enjoy. Discover more heartwarming, thought-provoking stories and celebrate the diversity and representation in her books. Happy reading!

description:
The Twisted Series by Ana Huang: Where Dark Desires Meet Dangerous Secrets

Beware the man who promises forever while guarding a heart of ice. This isn’t your standard boy-meets-girl narrative; it is a high-stakes exploration of obsession, moral ambiguity, and the thin line between love and loathing.

If you’re ready to trade sweet fairytales for gritty, billionaire-led power plays and forbidden bonds, this Twisted series 4-book collection is your next visceral obsession.

The Twisted Books in Order: A Trope-Lover’s Dream

While each book can be read as a standalone, they are best enjoyed in sequence to fully grasp the interconnected lives of the core friend group. Note: The character dynamics are significantly deeper than your average romance—expect flawed heroes and heroines who fight for their happy endings.

  • Twisted Love: Meet Alex Volkov—a man cursed by a past he can't escape and driven by a cold ambition that leaves no room for love. When he’s forced to look after his best friend’s sister, Ava Chen, the ice begins to crack. This is more than a "brother's best friend" romance; it’s a story of secrets that could burn worlds down.

  • Twisted Games: Princess Bridget von Ascheberg dreams of freedom, but her life is a golden cage. Enter Rhys Larsen, the stoic, elite bodyguard with one rule: never get emotionally involved. Their forbidden "bodyguard x princess" romance is a masterclass in tension, proving that some rules are meant to be shattered.

  • Twisted Hate: Josh Chen and Jules Ambrose cannot stand each other. He’s a charming doctor; she’s an ambitious law student. Their "enemies-to-lovers" fire is fueled by a mutual dislike that masks an undeniable carnal attraction. It’s volatile, heart-wrenching, and unapologetically steamy.

  • Twisted Lies: Christian Harper is a monster in a tailored suit, and Stella Alonso is the shy social media star living in the apartment below him. When a fake dating arrangement turns into a dangerous obsession, the truth becomes a weapon. This finale is a dark, slow-burn masterpiece that redefines the "unreliable narrator."

Beyond the Twisted World: The Kings of Sin

Once you have inevitably devoured the Twisted series, your journey into Ana Huang’s world of billionaire anti-heroes continues with the Kings of Sin series. Themed around the seven deadly sins, these novels take the "alpha-male" energy and emotional stakes to even higher altitudes. description:

Her debut novel, The Hate U Give, stands out for its poignant exploration of relevant and hard-hitting topics. This book not only established Thomas as a beloved figure in literature but also inspired readers worldwide to engage deeply with her subsequent works.

Following her stunning debut, Thomas released On the Come Up, eagerly anticipated by fans and lived up to the hype. This novel focuses on the ambitions and struggles of a young aspiring rapper who battles societal expectations and personal challenges in her quest for success.

Then came Concrete Rose, a prequel to The Hate U Give, which delves into the earlier life of Maverick Carter, exploring themes of young fatherhood and the cyclical challenges of poverty and violence.

Explore Angie Thomas' captivating world of storytelling by visiting our collection, Angie Thomas Trilogy beginner, Nic Blake and the Remarkables: The Manifestor Prophecy at Books2Door. Whether you are an adult or child, reading animal stories have some wonderful benefits you may not have known. Animals in these stories are often found forming unexpected friendships even if their differences are huge, like lions, elephants, turtles, bears, pigs, zebras, dolphins and more, the animal kingdom showcasing differences will teach kids how to accept other people from different backgrounds with different beliefs. title: Anne of Green Gables Books
description:
Anne of Green Gables Stories 

Join Anne Shirley as she is adopted by siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert to live on their farm in the fictional Canadian town of Avonlea. Follow Anne as she gets to know the locals and make this town her home. Anne’s narration is imaginative, dramatic and endearing throughout making you fall in love with her and with her friends. There are a total of eight books in the series, which follows Anne as she grows into an adult. L. M. Montgomery’s revolutionary children’s classics span over the life of Anne Shirley, starting when Anne is eleven years old and then ending when she reaches fifty-three. Take a look at our breakdown of all the Anne of Green Gables books in order, below. 

Anne of Green Gables introduces the reader to Anne and her adoption by the Cuthberts. She quickly makes friends with Diana Barry and Ruby Gillis and does well in school. She soon finds herself with a school rival, Gilbert Blythe. 

Anne of Avonlea sees a sixteen-year-old Anne as she is about to start her first year of teaching at Avonlea School. Her romantic relationship with Gilbert is starting to blossom as they both teach and continue their studies. 

Anne of the Island starts as Anne is preparing to move away from Avonlea and enrol in college. Anne is getting older and is thinking about potentially settling down. She receives multiple proposals and must make a decision, tragedy also hits Anne and she must grow up very quickly and make a decision about her future.

Anne of Windy Poplars is written in a series of letters and follows Anne as she is now the headteacher of a high school and is due to be married. She continues to visit Marilla in Avonlea whilst trying to win the affection of the residents of Summerside, the town she lives in. 

Anne's House of Dreams starts with Anne’s wedding. As the title suggests, she moves into her dream house with her husband and they begin their family. Anne continues to make friends and help people out as much as she can, however, tragedy hits their family once again and Anne must turn to Marilla and Anne’s new friend Leslie Moore for support. 

Anne of Ingleside is the sixth book in the series and is set seven years after Anne’s House of Dreams and spans over six years. Anne and her husband have a large family, the book follows their children as they grow and show similarities to their parents. 

Rainbow Valley mainly focuses on Anne’s six children and their adventures with another group of siblings. They often find themselves playing in a hollow called Rainbow Valley. Anne and her husband have been married for fifteen years at the start of this instalment and are continuing to help their neighbours the best they can. 

Rilla of Ingleside is the final book in the Anne of Green Gables series and mainly focuses on Anne’s youngest daughter Bertha Marilla "Rilla" Blythe. This story follows a different theme as it is set during WW1, Anne’s three sons, Rilla’s sweetheart and two of the children’s playmates go off to fight in Europe with the Canadian Expeditionary Force. Set almost a decade after Rainbow Valley, Rilla is a fifteen-year-old girl who has to come to terms with the cruel reality of war. 

Since its publication, Anne of Green Gables has been translated into over 36 languages and has sold more than 50 million copies, making it one of the best-selling books worldwide. Take a look at our selection of Anne of Green Gables books, all with unique designs and beautiful covers. 

Lucy Maud Montgomery OBE was a Canadian author who wrote novels, essays, short stories and poetry over the course of her life. 

Suitable for all ages 


Whether you are reading them to your child as a bedtime story or if you’re reading them for the first time as an adult, Anne of Green Gables is a series enjoyed by many. Perfect for fans of wild landscapes like the Secret Garden and strong female characters like Matilda or Alice in Wonderland.

title: Anthologies
description:
This section features all of our amazing collections of anthologies. Anthologies are collections of smaller works, which can be short works of art, poems, and shorter stories. Anthologies can consist of an amalgamation of various authors that follow a particular genre or a collection of short stories by the same author. Authors can participate to be a part of an anthology book, helping them get into the world of publishing their stories. In this wonderful category of Anthologies, we have tons of delightful titles such as Poems to Live Your Life By, I Am the Seed That Grew the Tree, and An Illustrated Treasury of Scottish Folk and Fairy Tales.

What are anthologies?

Anthologies or these special excerpts can revolve around specific themes which make each title unique and different from other books, such as areas on pets, Christmas, sports, certain occupations like athletes or nurses, and the list goes on. The writing style may follow a certain guideline, the publisher then creates the guidelines for the printing, graphic design, illustrations, and distribution. 

Anthologies can incorporate many talented authors who are just starting out, when the book becomes a popular title and well known, then the author who was a part of the story can bring author awareness. Particularly if the author is trying to break into a new market or a subject that they are new to, working together on an anthology piece can really strengthen their career in that area in the beginning. Anthologies can also act as a sample or marketing strategy to showcase the writing style and skills of the author, readers who may be unfamiliar with the author can learn to love the author's writing style, which then brings the reader to research more into the author who wrote that segment.

What should I read?

If you’re not sure where to start, why not have a look at one of our bestselling anthologies, I Am The Seed That Grew The Tree, Selected by Fiona Waters (National Trust)? This beautiful hardback collection has 365 nature-themed poems, one for every day of the year. This book is the perfect bedtime read or even to read with your child to help them gain literary independence. 

If it’s something more mythical fantasy you’re after, then check out  An Illustrated Treasury of Scottish Folk and Fairy Tales. Written by award-winning children’s author Theresa Breslin, this anthology features some of the best-loved tales from all over Scotland. Retelling some of the most famed tales, each in an individual style, she presents a variety of moving, funny and enchanting fairytales. Soar with the goshawk, dive with the selkies, and battle with the Stoorworm, as each story is creatively brought to life with exquisite illustrations by Scottish fine artist Kate Leiper, brimming with otherworldly beauty.

At Books2Door, we love providing kids with the best and most affordable books. Our mission is to make books more accessible and affordable for kids, allowing for less screen time and more story time. We would love to be part of your next story, so be sure to browse our Classic Fiction and Popular section for more remarkable titles.

title: Anthony Horowitz Books
description:
Anthony Horowitz is one of the most influential and successful writers in the UK. He specialises in murder mysteries and suspense fiction, across novels and the screen. Famous for the Alex Rider series, Horowitz has also written for multiple crime television series, including Agatha Christie’s Poirot and his own creation Foyle’s War. He has also written many novels for adults, including crime fiction and new cases for Sherlock Holmes and James Bond.

The Alex Rider series has been a phenomenal success since the first book, Stormbreaker, was published in 2000. Across twelve books and counting, the teenage spy has evaded the machinations of Scorpia, made lifelong friends and defeated deadly enemies along the way. The series sold more than 19 million copies worldwide and the books are popular among the teenage age group of 9-14.

In 2006 the first book was made into a feature film by the director of 1996’s Doctor Who. Sony Pictures Television is now making it as a TV series for Prime Video. Season 1 aired in 2020, adapting the second book Point Blanc, and Season 2’s take on Eagle Strike is forthcoming. We sell collections of Alex Rider’s missions across eleven books, as well as Alex Rider graphic novels, and you can find more spy books here,

The Power of Five is a reimagining of Pentagram, a series Horowitz started in the 1980s but never finished. Across five exciting fantasy novels, you meet five teenagers, all of whom were born as Gatekeepers. They can travel freely to any of 25 Doors, dotted all over the world, and it’s their job to keep the world safe from the return of the Old Ones. Read the whole gripping adventure in The Power of Five: The Complete Collection.

The recent resurrection of The Diamond Brothers makes it Anthony Horowitz’s longest-running series. The Falcon’s Malteser was published in 1986, and a new book called Where Seagulls Dare is coming out in 2022. Across three novels and four short stories, the world’s worst private detective Tim and his intrepid teenage brother Nick fight crooks, investigate mysterious deaths, and defy time itself by not ageing once in thirty-five years. To make sure you’re up to speed, check out this five-book Diamond Brothers collection, which is also available with five other wickedly funny novels in this Anthony Horowitz Bumper Boxset.

Anthony Horowitz was born in Middlesex, and now lives in London with his wife and two sons. He went to Rugby School in Warwickshire and the University of York. His first novel was published in 1979, and has since written over fifty books. He began writing television in 1986 with the third series of Robin of Sherwood. In addition to his career as an author, Horowitz often contributes to magazines and newspapers across subjects such as education, politics and travel. He has been an advocate of the anti-bullying charity called Kidscape since 2008. He was awarded an OBE in 2014.

Find more adventures and young adult fiction, as well as adult fiction, here on Books2Door, all available at our best possible prices.

description:

title: Assassination Classroom
description:
Welcome to the Assassination Classroom manga collection at Books2Door, where you can find all the volumes of Yusei Matsui's captivating series. Whether you're a long-time manga enthusiast or a newcomer to Japanese comics, Assassination Classroom offers an enthralling experience filled with unique characters, unexpected twists, and thought-provoking themes.

Overview of Assassination Classroom
The narrative of Assassination Classroom balances intense action, adventure, heartfelt moments and humour. Each student in Class 3-E is given distinct characteristics and personal arcs, making their development and interactions highly engaging. The series delves into themes such as perseverance, the value of education, and the potential for redemption.

The story is set in Kunugigaoka Junior High School, specifically in Class 3-E, a class for students considered failures by the school's rigorous standards. The plot takes a dramatic turn when the students are introduced to their new teacher, an alien octopus-like creature with incredible powers. This creature, later named Koro-sensei, claims responsibility for destroying 70% of the moon, leaving it permanently crescent-shaped. He declares that he will destroy Earth within a year unless the students can assassinate him before then.

Despite his terrifying threat, Koro-sensei is an extraordinary teacher deeply invested in his students' education and personal growth. He uses his vast array of abilities to teach them the standard curriculum and the art of assassination. Initially frightened and confused, the students gradually develop a complex relationship with Koro-sensei, blending their mission to kill him with genuine admiration and affection for his guidance.

Yusei Matsui: The Author Behind the Series
Yusei Matsui, the brilliant mind behind Assassination Classroom, has established himself as a significant figure in the manga industry. Born on January 31, 1979, in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, Matsui started his career as an assistant to Yoshio Sawai.

Matsui debuted as a mangaka with the series Demon Detective Neuro Nōgami. However, it was Assassination Classroom that genuinely catapulted him to fame. His ability to blend unusual concepts with deep emotional storytelling has earned him a dedicated fanbase and critical acclaim. 

Matsui's work is characterised by his unique art style, sharp wit, and the ability to infuse his narratives with a sense of humanity, even in the most fantastical settings. His success with Assassination Classroom has cemented his reputation and contributed significantly to the global popularity of manga.

Explore the Collection
At Books2Door, we proudly offer the complete Assassination Classroom manga volumes collection. Dive into the world of Class 3-E and their extraordinary teacher, Koro-sensei, as they embark on a journey filled with danger, growth, and unexpected friendships. Whether you're purchasing for yourself or as a gift for a manga fan, our collection will surely provide countless hours of enjoyment.

title: Asterix Books
description:
Asterix is one of the best selling graphic novel series ever, and has fans worldwide. Find great value Asterix & Obelix collections here at Books2Door.

Asterix is the world’s bestselling comic book series. Originally written by René Goscinny and illustrated by Albert Uderzo, the French comic series follows the adventures of a Gaul warrior named Asterix, his best friend Obelix, and for the most part it is set in the Gaulish villages. Over the course of the series, the authors have described the exploits of the indomitable Gauls at the time when they resisted the forceful occupation by the Romans.

Asterix is a relatively small man, but by taking a potion made by the village druid, Getafix, he becomes strong and defeats several Romans. This infuriates the Romans who then decide to discover the secret of his strength. The Gaul’s adventures and the Romans’ chase for the secret potion make Asterix comics highly entertaining.

The Astérix le Gaulois bande dessinée began serialisation in 1959, as part of the anthology Pilote. The first album collecting the comic strip was released in 1961, and was published in English in 1969. After Goscinny died in 1977, Uderzo took over the series as the writer as well, starting with the 25th album Asterix and the Great Divide. Uderzo sold his skate in the series to publisher Hachette in December 2008, and the books are now created by Jean-Yves Ferri and Didier Conrad.

The premise of the comic books is that the Romans have conquered all of the Gauls except those in one village in the northwest. Asterix defeats four Romans who attack him in the woods. When the Romans report their defeat to their leader, Crismus Bonus wonders about the Gauls' strength and this is when the hunt for the secret of the potion begins. After much ado when the Romans finally discover the secret of the potion, Crismus Bonus drinks the potion and tests his strength but finds it unimpressive. What follows this course of events is yet another series of adventures.

The BDs are known for their uproarious comedy, outrageous puns, and pointed satire. An interesting piece of trivia about the series is that the even numbered volumes of the Asterix series take place abroad, whilst the odd numbered volumes are set in Gaul, mostly in the rural regions.

The Asterix series is one of the most famous Franco-Belgian comics in the world, alongside Tintin. The series has been translated into more than 100 foreign languages. After its tremendous success, the series has also been adapted into ten animated films and six live action movies. Several games have also been developed with the series’ characters. A theme park named Parc Asterix has also been established in Paris, and is a popular tourist attraction. By 2009, an estimated 325 million printed copies of the Asterix books have been sold worldwide. This established the authors Uderzo and Goscinny as some of the bestselling French writers.

Available in several combinations and sets, Asterix is a bestselling graphic novel series with fans worldwide. We at Books2Door have ensured you can find great value Asterix & Obelix collections here, take a look.

Overview: 
Set in a world where remnants of humanity huddle within massive walled cities, fearing the relentless Titans lurking beyond, Attack on Titan follows the journey of Eren Yeager, his adoptive sister Mikasa Ackerman, and their friend Armin Arlert. Their lives are forever changed when a colossal Titan breaches their home city's defences, shattering their illusion of safety and prompting Eren to vow revenge against the Titans for the loss of his mother.

From heart-stopping battles between humans and Titans to the political machinations within the walls, Attack on Titan weaves a complex narrative that keeps readers on the edge of their seats with each twist and turn.

About the Author:
Speaking of the creator, let's delve into the background of the visionary mind behind Attack on Titan. Hajime Isayama, born on August 29, 1986, in Ōyama, Ōita, Japan, is the talented mangaka responsible for bringing this gripping tale to life. Isayama's journey to success wasn't without challenges; he faced rejection numerous times before finally finding a publisher for Attack on Titan. His perseverance and dedication to his craft have since earned him widespread acclaim and a devoted fanbase.

Isayama's unique artistic style and ability to craft compelling characters and intricate plotlines have cemented his place as one of the most influential creators in the manga industry. Attack on Titan is a testament to his creative genius, offering readers a rich and immersive world that continues to captivate audiences worldwide.

Whether you're drawn to the series for its adrenaline-pumping action sequences, its exploration of complex moral dilemmas, or its profound themes of hope and resilience in the face of adversity, Attack on Titan has something for everyone. So why wait? Dive into the world of Attack on Titan today with Books2Door and experience the thrill of this unforgettable series.

title: Axel Scheffler Books
description:
Axel Scheffler is one of the UK’s most beloved illustrators. His collaborations with Julia Donaldson have become modern classics, and his drawings of The Gruffalo and Superworm have sparked the imaginations of children worldwide. He’s illustrated postage stamps, a book bench, the walls of children’s hospitals, and won many awards along the way.

We love illustrators here at Books2Door. Take a look at our other collections for beloved artists such as Dr. Seuss, Quentin Blake, Tony Ross and Roger Hargreaves. We also have a section dedicated to picture books, as well as pop-up and lift-the-flap books, which have many books perfect for fans of Axel Scheffler.

Biography

Axel Scheffler was born in 1957 in Hamburg, West Germany. He dropped out of the University of Hamburg and instead did national service caring for the mentally ill. He moved to England in 1982 to study Visual Communications at the Bath Academy of Art. It was during this course that he decided to become an illustrator.

Scheffler illustrated his first book, a reissue of The Piemakers by Helen Cresswell, in 1988. Since then, he’s worked with multiple authors, but his most enduring partnership is with writer and songwriter Julia Donaldson. They were put together by a publishing company that wanted to make one of Donaldson’s songs into a picture book. The result, A Squash and a Squeeze, was published in 1993. This unexpected project launched Donaldson’s children’s book career. When she had the idea for The Gruffalo in 1995, Scheffler was the person she sent it to.

The Gruffalo was published in 1999, and since then, their partnership has gone on to success after success. Their bestselling children’s books are often adapted for Christmas TV, as plays, and are constantly read and re-read by kids worldwide. Axel Scheffler also makes children’s books at Nosy Crow - his popular Pip & Posy series has been adapted for television, and the Flip Flap series is great for kids who are learning to read.

Best-Known Books

Pip & Posy are best friends. But - just like any toddlers - they have to learn what to do when life doesn’t go their way. This series is a hit for readers aged 0-5 and their parents, since it helps them learn to read as well as learn how to be in the world. The Pip & Posy 8 Book Collection is a great value way to start your Pip & Posy library.

The Flip Flap series is perfect for people tired of the same old natural history books. Each volume is spiral-bound and split down the middle. On the right, there’s a drawing of an animal. There’s a rhyme about it on the left, one on each half, and its name is written vertically across the split. You can mix and match any top half with any bottom half, so you and your child will be laughing out loud as you discover strange new hybrid creatures like the “fab” and the “squolphin” together. Each book has eleven combinations of eleven animals - that’s 121! Grab Axel Scheffler’s Flip Flap Series 8 Books Collection today.

title: Barrington Stoke Books
description:
Barrington Stoke is an independent publishing company that specialises in accessible books. Designed to be dyslexia-friendly, their books are all printed with a particular font and off-white paper and larger spacing. 

Every child can be a reader, and Barrington Stoke is driven to provide books that match a child's age and not their reading level. Aiming to keep their interest whilst they gradually improve over time. The books are expertly edited to ensure comprehension and accessibility, with shorter novels helping the reader build their confidence.

Many authors have worked with Barrington Stoke to publish work specifically for dyslexic readers. These books have also been used to encourage reluctant readers to start reading. Whether they are beginning to read with a parent or want to read independently, Barrington Stoke will have a book to suit their interests. 

Malorie Blackman 

Malorie Blackman OBE is a British author and former Children's Laureate. Her work is predominantly aimed at children and young adults. Blackman uses science fiction and dystopian themes to portray important social and racial issues. 

Barrington Stoke has worked with Malorie Blackman to create more accessible novels for different ages. For younger readers, Ellie and the Cat follows a rude and spoilt girl who is turned into a cat by her Grandma. Ellie must prove to her family that she has changed in order to be turned back into a human. This is aimed at ages 6-7 and contains clear text, which is broken up by illustrations. 

Why not check out A Dangerous Game for slightly older readers, ages 8+? A Dangerous Game follows Sam, who has sickle-cell anaemia, as he goes on a school trip, but when his friends start taking part in a challenge, Sam wants to prove that he is just as strong as them. This book is an essential read for all ages as it raises awareness of sickle-cell anaemia and the effect it can have on someone. 

Fans of Malorie Blackman's dystopian novels should check out her novella Robot Girl. Claire has been eager to learn what her dad has been working on in his lab, but Clarie soon realises her dad has created a monster! Aimed for ages 8+, this book, along with the other Barrington Stoke books, has a dyslexia-friendly layout, typeface and paper stock so that even more readers can enjoy it. 

Tom Palmer 

Tom Palmer's books are all set in either WW1 or WW2 and portray different perspectives and events over those historical periods. All books in the series are targeted for ages 10+, so they are perfect for helping young readers who may be struggling with reading independently. 

Over the line follows Jack, a professional footballer who is just about to start his career playing for his country when he is forced to enlist in the Army. This bestselling novel is based on the true story of WWI war hero and footballing legend Jack Cock. Another bestseller from Tom Palmer is Armistice Runner. This novel follows Lily as she is training for races whilst struggling with her worries and fears of losing her Gran to Alzheimer's. After Lily discovers her Gran's WW1 diaries, she forms a connection with her Gran as she learns all about her inspiring life. Why not check out our Tom Palmer Five Book Collection containing Over the line, Armistice Runner, Arctic Star, After the War and D-Day Dog.

title: Beano Books
description:
Step into a world of laughter, mischief, and endless fun with The Beano, a beloved British comic series that has captivated generations of readers. Since its debut in 1938, The Beano has been a cherished part of British culture, entertaining children and adults alike with its colourful characters and hilarious adventures. Among the numerous iconic characters that have graced its pages, none are as mischievous and lovable as Dennis and Gnasher. Join us as we delve into the misadventures of these two troublemakers, showcasing why The Beano and its dynamic duo have become such a timeless and cherished part of British comic history. Beano comics have been enjoyed by generations, they are perfect for readers aged 7-9 but can be enjoyed by younger and older readers. For more books like these, check out our children’s comic strips and graphic novels page. 

Dennis the Menace: A Classic Trouble-Maker:

Dennis the Menace, with his signature black and red striped jumper, unruly black hair, and mischievous grin, is the epitome of a lovable troublemaker. Known for his never-ending pranks and practical jokes, Dennis is always up to something that keeps readers eagerly turning the pages. From his ingenious schemes to outsmart his neighbours to his wild adventures that often leave chaos in his wake, Dennis brings a unique blend of charm, cheekiness, and creativity to The Beano. His infectious energy and rebellious spirit make him a character that readers of all ages can't help but root for. Why not check out Beanopedia: The ultimate guide to Beanotown and its inhabitants. 

Gnasher, Dennis' Loyal and Mischievous Sidekick:

No mention of Dennis would be complete without his loyal companion, Gnasher. This faithful and mischievous canine pal is always by Dennis' side, adding an extra dose of chaos to their escapades. With his distinctive snaggletooth and penchant for causing mayhem, Gnasher is a character that readers instantly fall in love with. Whether he's chasing postmen or leaving a trail of destruction in his wake, Gnasher's loyalty and boundless energy perfectly complement Dennis' adventures, making them an inseparable duo that has stood the test of time. Start your adventures with Dennis and Gnasher with our Beano Dennis & Gnasher by I. P. Daley 6 Books Collection. 

The Adventures Unleashed:

Within the pages of The Beano, Dennis and Gnasher embark on a variety of hilarious and imaginative adventures that take them from their quiet neighbourhood to distant and fantastical lands. Whether they're exploring mysterious caves, creating their own inventions, or causing chaos at school, readers are transported to a world where anything is possible. The Beano's engaging storytelling, witty dialogue, and vibrant illustrations make each escapade feel like a whirlwind of laughter and excitement, keeping readers eagerly awaiting the next instalment.

Enduring Popularity and Cultural Impact:

Throughout the years, The Beano and its iconic characters, Dennis and Gnasher, have left an indelible mark on British popular culture. The mischievous duo has become household names, inspiring TV shows, animated adaptations, merchandise, and even their own theme park attractions. The Beano's ability to capture the essence of childhood mischief and the universal appeal of its characters has ensured its longevity and continued relevance in a rapidly changing world.

For decades, The Beano has been a source of laughter, joy, and entertainment for millions of readers. At the heart of this beloved comic series are Dennis and Gnasher, two characters who have become synonymous with mischief, adventure, and timeless fun. Their misadventures continue to captivate audiences of all ages, reminding us to embrace our inner child and celebrate the joy of laughter. If you're ready to immerse yourself in a world of endless pranks and timeless humour, The Beano is the perfect companion. Discover the magic of this iconic comic series and join Dennis and Gnasher on their unforgettable escapades today.

title: Bear Books 🐻
description:
How many of us remember clinging to a stuffed teddy bear growing up? The one that had to go everywhere we went, yes the very one that sent the entire family into a frenzy if it went missing. That cuddly teddy bear we grew up with, remained our best friend for years. However, at some point, this very-loved and therefore dishevelled teddy bear was replaced by fictional bears that we continued to love through our teens and books.

Our teddy bears may have succumbed to our smothering but fictional bears continue to live on through generations in our hearts and books. Read on as we list some of our favourite, famous bears in children’s literature…

Baloo is the beloved and original papa bear who starred in Rudyard Kipling's Jungle Book. He first appeared as a strict teacher to the cubs of the Seeonee wolf pack and Mowgli, the man-cub. As the story progresses we see Baloo as one of Mowgli’s mentors, friends, and father figure. He is patient, strong, and responsible, a bear with a good heart, paternal instincts, and just one weakness, that he is ticklish! 

Winnie-the-Pooh first appears in the book Winnie-the-Pooh, a collection of stories by author A. A. Milne, in 1926. The character was named after a teddy bear owned by Milne’s son, Christopher Robin Milne, on whom the character Christopher Robin was also based. Christopher Milne had re-named his toy bear (originally called Edward) after Winnie, a Canadian black bear he often saw at London Zoo, and ‘Pooh’ a swan they had met whilst on holiday. 

Winnie the Pooh is a simple-minded, kind-hearted, lovable bear, who lacks book smarts but more than makes up for it in simple and honest emotional generosity. An endearing bear that promises to always be there for you.

Whilst Winnie the Pooh became a Disney character in 1966, we've always favoured the book version. Plus, E. H. Shepard's original illustrations, we think, are magical.

Paddington the Bear was born and raised in deepest, darkest Peru, but made his way to London and moved in with the Browns. Paddington is an innocent, friendly yet quirky bear that loves marmalade. 

Michael Bond wrote Paddington Bear based on a lonely teddy bear he once noticed on a shelf in a London store near Paddington Station on Christmas Eve in 1956. Bond, who was once a BBC cameraman, has famously said that his memories of newsreels showing trainloads of child evacuees leaving London during the Second World War with labels around their necks and possessions in a small suitcase, prompted him to do the same for Paddington’s character. This and several other touching, endearing qualities make Paddington a popular character amongst children and adults alike. 

The Paddington books have been widely published and translated into 30 languages across 70 titles and have managed to sell more than 30 million copies worldwide. Paddington was first made into a physical teddy bear in 1972. Since then, the Paddington stories have been adapted widely for both television and film. Today, Paddington is a famous movie star bear who has even had the privilege of making an audience with the queen. 

Goldilocks and the Three Bears by Axel Scheffler: The classic fairytale of Goldilocks and the Three Bears has been masterfully brought to life by Axel Scheffler, the illustrator. When Goldilocks stumbles across a little house in the woods, she finds an array of treats inside. The perfect little chair to sit on, the perfect bowl of porridge, not to mention the perfect bed for a nap—all of which belong to the Baby Bear. And when the three bears arrive home, who is in for a surprise, the bear family or Goldilocks?

title: Bear Grylls Books
description:
British author, adventurer, businessman, and television presenter—Edward Michael, also popular as Bear Grylls, wears several hats but he is most renowned for embarking on numerous adventures into the wilderness. Grylls’ ability to survive in the wild, his storytelling skills, and his ability to document his adventures have made him extremely popular across the world. Some of Bear Grylls’ most popular adventure television series include Man vs Wild, Running Wild with Bear Grylls, and The Island with Bear Grylls.

Bear Grylls’ adventures have also been illustrated into books that make excellent non-fiction reading material for kids aged 5-15. Bear Grylls’ adventure books for kids are great, for not only teaching kids about wildlife, but also providing the thrill of an adventure, whilst also helping them develop an interest in reading. Grylls’ appetite for adventure and his sheer curiosity has led him to undertake several wildlife adventures, all of which make great content for kids that share his passion for the wilderness. 

Bear Grylls the complete adventures collection 12 books is a great book series for children aged 7+. Across these twelve book titles, children are kept engaged from one exciting adventure to another. Along with young Chief Scout Bear Grylls, children face true-life challenges and learn great lessons about survival and teamwork. These are lessons that can prove beneficial for the kids in the long run. 

Sure, there are a lot of contradictory opinions about Grylls and some of his methods have been branded, for the lack of a better term, unconventional. There is no denying that the man is everyone’s favourite real-life action hero. For instance, his book Mud Sweat & Tears is an inspiring read for young readers. Grylls ability to venture into and survive dangerous environments, his passion to take up adventure sports (mountaineering, martial arts, parachuting), and his tips and safety messages around food and shelter—have got children from diverse age groups glued to his books.

Bear Grylls’ show Survival School is an action-packed tale of carefully executed adventures that challenge a group of kids between the ages of 12 and 15 to leave their beloved technology and devices behind and head for the rugged mountains of Snowdonia in Wales. Through this two-week adventure of river-crossing, fire-making, shelter-building, teamwork, perseverance, and resilience; Grylls’ will have already converted you into a fan.

Bear Grylls’ readers and viewers now range across age groups. Bear Grylls’ books for kids, The Bear Grylls Adventures – The Blizzard Challenge and The Desert Challenge, have captured the attention of children aged 5 to 8 years. We cannot help but credit Grylls for getting this gadget-crazed generation of kids interested in nature, reading, and inculcating some healthy habits in them.

If you are a parent to kids between the ages of 5 to 15; we recommend you try to look up Bear Grylls’ adventure books and get your kids hooked on some new-age adventure reading.
