title: Beatrix Potter Books
description:
Beatrix Potter is one of the most beloved authors of children's literature, best known for her charming tales of animals and their adventures. Born in London in 1866, Potter was raised in a privileged household and enjoyed a comfortable life. However, her childhood was marred by illness, and she spent much of her time at home, where she developed a love of nature and drawing.

Potter's artistic talent was evident from a young age, and she began to create her own illustrations and stories as a child. Her early works included sketches of animals and landscapes, which she created while spending summers in the countryside with her family. These sketches would later serve as the inspiration for many of her beloved tales.

Despite her passion for art and storytelling, Potter faced significant obstacles as a woman in the Victorian era. Women were not expected to pursue careers or attend university, and Potter's family discouraged her from pursuing her artistic interests. However, she persisted in her pursuits, and her determination paid off when she began to sell her illustrations to publishers and magazines.

Potter's big break came in 1901 when she published her first book, The Tale of Peter Rabbit. The book, which Potter initially self-published, was an immediate success and went on to become one of the best-selling children's books of all time. The charming story of a mischievous rabbit who disobeys his mother and gets into trouble in Mr McGregor's garden captured the hearts of children and adults alike and established Potter as a major force in children's literature. For a fantastic Peter Rabbit collection check out our Peter Rabbit Library Coloured Jackets 10 Books Box Set, which features the much-loved rabbit as well as many other beloved Beatrix Potter books. 

In the years that followed, Potter continued to write and illustrate a series of popular books featuring animal characters such as Squirrel Nutkin, Mrs Tiggy-Winkle, and Jemima Puddle-Duck. Her stories were notable for their vivid descriptions of the natural world and their gentle, humorous tone. Potter's characters were both relatable and endearing, and her stories were filled with memorable moments of humour and warmth.

Beyond her work as an author and illustrator, Potter was also a dedicated conservationist and advocate for the preservation of the British countryside. She used the proceeds from her books to purchase and protect large tracts of land in the Lake District, which she donated to the National Trust after her death. Her legacy as a champion of the natural world lives on through the Beatrix Potter Society, which works to promote her work and continue her conservation efforts.


Today, Potter's books remain beloved by children and adults around the world. Her characters and stories have become icons of children's literature and have inspired generations of readers and writers. Potter's legacy is a testament to the power of imagination, creativity, and determination, and her work continues to enchant and inspire readers of all ages. If you’re a fan of Beatrix Potter, you should check out fellow illustrators and authors Quentin Blake and Judith Kerr.

title: Bedtime Stories
description:
Building a regular reading habit from an early age carries huge developmental benefits for young minds. What better time to lock in that habit than right before sleep? You might be searching for the ideal bed time story book for a newborn, and even at that tiny age, they genuinely appreciate the calming rhythm of a familiar voice. It never takes long before they begin actively tracking the shapes and colours on the page.

As your children grow, our selection of children's fiction naturally evolves to match their shifting interests. A well-chosen bed time story book takes them on fresh adventures while they are settling down for the night. Spending just ten quiet minutes reading together each evening massively boosts their early literacy skills, increases vocabulary, and builds the confidence they need to read aloud. Every child engages with literature differently. Whether they want magical realms, animal adventures, or laugh-out-loud humour, having a fresh bed time story book ready on the nightstand keeps that love of reading alive night after night.

Beloved Bedtime Favourites

Julia Donaldson remains one of the absolute most popular authors here at Books2Door. Her rhythmic, engaging tales make for a flawless bed time story book experience. From the legendary Gruffalo to the charming The Snail and the Whale, her work perfectly balances entertaining the child while keeping the parent engaged during the read. It makes total sense that her stories hit the television screens every Christmas; they are universally loved. If you are looking for a reliable bed time story book, browse her titles or check out our page dedicated to her long-time illustrator, Axel Scheffler, for equally brilliant choices.

title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold series
description:
Step into the enchanting world of Toshikazu Kawaguchi, where time bends and the boundaries between past, present, and future blur. At Books2Door, we're delighted to introduce you to this talented Japanese author and his captivating series, Before the Coffee Gets Cold. Dive into a realm where coffee shops hold secrets, time travel is possible, and emotions transcend the ages. Purchase all four books in the Before the Coffee Gets Cold series, now available and in stock at Books2Door.

Meet the Author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi

Toshikazu Kawaguchi is a talented Japanese playwright and novelist, born in 1971. His unique storytelling style has earned him international acclaim, making him a beloved figure in the literary world. Kawaguchi's ability to blend the ordinary with the extraordinary, seamlessly weaving tales that delve into the depths of human emotions, has endeared him to readers of all ages.

Kawaguchi's background in theatre is evident in his writing, as he masterfully constructs scenes and characters that feel both authentic and emotionally resonant. His works have a timeless quality, offering readers a chance to explore the human experience in ways they never imagined.

The Before the Coffee Gets Cold Series

Toshikazu Kawaguchi's Before the Coffee Gets Cold series is a heartwarming and thought-provoking collection of books, each set in a small, cosy café named Funiculi Funicula. Within the walls of this charming establishment, customers are presented with a unique opportunity: they can travel back in time to revisit moments from their past. However, there are rules to follow, and time travel comes with its own set of challenges and limitations.

Before the Coffee Gets Cold:

In the first book of the series, Before the Coffee Gets Cold, Kawaguchi introduces us to the café's mystical time-travelling chair. Customers can sit in this chair but must return to their seats before their coffee gets cold. Each character faces personal dilemmas and regrets that lead them to take this extraordinary journey, hoping to mend their past mistakes. As they navigate the complexities of time travel, they discover that altering the past is not as simple as it seems.

The story begins in a cosy little cafe nestled in a quiet corner of Tokyo. In this cafe, there is a seat with an unusual power - it allows its occupant to travel back in time. However, there are rules to be followed: you can only meet someone who has been to the cafe before, and you must return before your coffee gets cold. As customers grapple with their regrets and longing, they embark on emotional journeys that redefine the limits of time itself. Kawaguchi's debut novel is a heartwarming exploration of love and second chances.

Before the Coffee Gets Cold: Tales from the Café 

This collection of interconnected stories revisits the magical cafe with the time-traveling chair. Each tale delves into the lives of different characters, revealing their dreams, hopes, and regrets. Readers are treated to a deeper understanding of the cafe's enigmatic owner and the underlying power of human connections. Kawaguchi weaves a tapestry of emotions, painting a vivid picture of how a simple cup of coffee can change lives forever.

Before Your Memory Fades

The sequel to the beloved series continues to unravel the mysteries of the cafe. New customers, each carrying their unique burdens and desires, embark on transformative journeys through time. Kawaguchi introduces fresh characters while bringing back familiar faces, deepening the cafe's lore and the exploration of time's impact on human existence. As the stories unfold, readers are once again enchanted by the intersection of the mundane and the miraculous.

Before we say goodbye

The regulars at Café Funiculi Funicula are well acquainted with the whimsical ability it grants them to take a trip into the past—as well as the strict rules involved, including that each traveller must return to the present in the time it takes for their coffee to get cold. In Toshikazu Kawaguchi’s previous novels, patrons have been reunited with old flames, made amends with estranged family and visited loved ones. Now readers will once again be introduced to a new set of visitors.

title: Ben MacIntyre Books
description:
Ben Macintyre, a British author and historian, specialises in crafting gripping non-fiction narratives that delve into the shadowy corners of espionage, war, and international intrigue. Known for his meticulously researched books that read like high-stakes thrillers, Macintyre transforms complex, often confidential histories into compelling stories accessible to a broad audience. His works are an impeccable blend of academic rigour and storytelling mastery. When you venture into a Ben Macintyre book, you're not just reading—you're embarking on an exhilarating journey through the annals of real-life spy games, wartime heroics, and incredible acts of valour and deception.

Non-Fiction That Reads Like Fiction

One of the most remarkable aspects of Ben Macintyre's work is his ability to construct his non-fiction books in a way that captures the essence and tension of spy thrillers or mystery novels. His storytelling ability shines through each page, making readers forget they are engrossing themselves in historical events and real-life characters. The pace, the narrative arc, the crescendo of suspense—each element is so expertly orchestrated that you'll find it hard to put the book down.

Award-Winning Works

Among his numerous accolades, Macintyre's Agent Zigzag stands out as a classic that showcases his talent at its finest. This book charts the life of Eddie Chapman, a British criminal turned double agent during World War II. Macintyre delves into the psychological complexities of a man playing both sides, with a storyline so extraordinary that you'd think it was fiction.

Operation Mincemeat—another critically acclaimed book—follows a deceptive operation that significantly influenced the outcome of World War II. It involved planting false documents on a corpse dressed as a military officer to mislead Nazi Germany about the invasion of Southern Europe. This tale of ingenuity, bravery, and high-stakes deception won Macintyre considerable acclaim and established him as a master of espionage literature. It was also made into a 2021 British war drama film directed by John Madden.

The Spy and the Traitor is another masterpiece that delves into the life of Oleg Gordievsky, a KGB officer who became a double agent for British intelligence. This book provides a vivid account of the Cold War era, filled with close calls, clandestine operations, and political brinkmanship. It offers an in-depth look into the complexities of human motives and the moral choices made under extreme circumstances.

Diverse Themes and Global Relevance

What sets Macintyre apart is his commitment to unearthing the truth, often based on exclusive interviews, classified documents, and rigorous archival research. The extensive footnotes and bibliographies in each of his books bear testament to the exhaustive research that underpins his narratives. His journalistic background—being a columnist and Associate Editor for The Times of London—shines through in the impeccable research and objective presentation of his subjects.

Macintyre's work transcends the events and people he describes, resonating with universal themes of courage, loyalty, betrayal, and the moral ambiguities inherent in espionage and war. While the geographical settings may range from war-torn Europe to the secretive corridors of Cold War-era Russia, the stories are always deeply human and relevant to any reader anywhere in the world.

Adaptations and Cultural Impact

Beyond the books, Macintyre’s works have inspired documentaries, films, and stage plays, further amplifying the impact of his storytelling. His writings have not only illuminated the often murky world of espionage but have also contributed to historical discourse, providing fresh perspectives and new information that enrich our understanding of pivotal events in modern history.

Whether you're a seasoned history buff, a lover of espionage tales, or simply someone who appreciates well-crafted stories, Ben Macintyre's collection is a treasure trove of riveting reads. Each book serves as a lens through which to view the complexities of war, politics, and human psychology.

In the world of historical writing, Ben Macintyre stands as a beacon of integrity and imagination. His books are more than just accounts of past events; they are windows into the human condition, told with the flair of a master storyteller. As you flip through the pages of any of his works, you'll find yourself not just educated but deeply moved, pondering the ever-relevant questions of loyalty, bravery, and the grey moralities that colour our world.

title: Benjamin Zephaniah Books
description:

We Sang Across the Sea: The Empire Windrush and Me:

Infused with Zephaniah's distinctive rhythm and lyrical style, these poems tackle a range of topics, from social justice and equality to self-acceptance and the power of words. Through his poetic voice, Zephaniah encourages children to explore their own creativity, challenging societal norms and inspiring them to use the written word as a tool for self-expression and positive change.

In his novels, Benjamin Zephaniah fearlessly addresses important themes that resonate with young readers. In Face, Zephaniah tackles the complex issue of facial disfigurement, exploring themes of self-acceptance, friendship, and resilience. The story follows the journey of Martin, a teenager whose journey towards self-empowerment challenges societal prejudices and stereotypes.

Gangsta Rap confronts the issue of social injustice, racism, and the power of music to bridge divides. Zephaniah weaves a compelling narrative around a talented young rapper who uses his lyrics to expose injustice and spark positive change in his community.

With Teacher's Dead, Zephaniah explores themes of education, social inequality, and the power of students' voices. Benjamin Zephaniah's books for children serve as a gateway to a world of imagination, empathy, and social consciousness. Through captivating stories, powerful poetry, and thought-provoking themes, Zephaniah encourages young minds to question the world around them, embrace diversity, and find their own unique voice. Whether it's through the picture book We Sang Across the Sea: The Empire Windrush and Me, the poetry book Talking Turkeys, or the novels Refugee Boy, Face, Gangsta Rap, and Teacher's Dead, Zephaniah's works empower young readers to navigate the complexities of life, fostering compassion, resilience, and a lifelong love for literature. Discover the transformative power of Benjamin Zephaniah's books for children and embark on a literary journey that will leave an indelible impact on young minds.

description:

With his vibrant illustrations and heartfelt storytelling, Davies has created a body of work that sparks the imagination, evokes emotion, and celebrates the power of friendship, family, and adventure. In this exploration, we will dive into some of Davies' most beloved picture books, including The Storm Whale, Tad, Grandad's Island, and The Snowflake, and discover why his works are cherished by readers around the world. With Davies' beautifully expressive illustrations, readers are transported to the rugged coastal setting, where they embark on an emotional journey of compassion, friendship, and the importance of connecting with nature. Through its gentle narrative and stunning visuals, The Storm Whale teaches young readers about empathy, resilience, and the profound impact a single act of kindness can have on both animals and humans alike.

Tad

In Tad, Davies invites readers into the extraordinary world of Tad, the smallest tadpole in a pond. As Tad yearns to grow and explore the vastness of the world beyond his pond, young readers are encouraged to embrace their own unique strengths and abilities. With Davies' captivating illustrations that capture the vibrancy of nature, Tad serves as a reminder that no dream is too big and no individual is too small to make a difference. This empowering story celebrates the courage to venture beyond one's comfort zone and the beauty of self-discovery.

Grandad's Island

Grandad's Island weaves a tale of love, loss, and the power of imagination. In this heartwarming story, young Syd embarks on an unforgettable adventure with his grandfather to a tropical island filled with wonder and magic. Davies' lush illustrations vividly bring the island to life, while the narrative explores themes of loss, grief, and the enduring bond between generations. Grandad's Island gently introduces young readers to the concept of loss and the importance of treasuring memories, offering comfort and solace in times of change.

The Snowflake

In The Snowflake, Davies introduces readers to a curious and determined little penguin named Noosh. As Noosh embarks on a journey to find the perfect gift for a loved one, readers are transported to a breathtaking winter wonderland. Davies' intricate and captivating illustrations capture the beauty and delicacy of snowflakes, while the story teaches valuable lessons about the power of giving, the beauty of individuality, and the importance of embracing one's own uniqueness. The Snowflake encourages young readers to celebrate their own special qualities and to find joy in spreading kindness.

Benji Davies is a masterful illustrator and author who has carved a place in the hearts of readers with his enchanting picture books. Through stories like The Storm Whale, Tad, Grandad's Island, and The Snowflake, Davies captivates young imaginations and imparts important life lessons. His vivid illustrations and heartfelt narratives explore themes of empathy, resilience, self-discovery, and the power of love and friendship. Each book serves as a portal to a world of wonder and offers opportunities for reflection, conversation, and connection. Discover the magic of Benji Davies' picture books and invite readers of all ages to embark on unforgettable journeys of imagination and discovery.

title: Bernard Cornwell Books
description:
Bernard Cornwell Books

Raised in Essex, Bernard Cornwell OBE is a master of historical fiction. Whether it's involving a heroic British soldier during the Napoleonic Wars or following Saxon-born Uhtred of Bebbanburg around the Anglo-Saxon Kingdom of Wessex, Cornwell continues to keep his readers hooked. Cornwell has gained a prestigious reputation for his outstanding historical epics, first with the Sharpe books, then moving on to The Last Kingdom and many other bestselling novels. 

Sharpe

The first book in the series, Sharpe’s Eagle, was released in 1981. Since then, the series has been a phenomenal success. Currently, there are twenty-two books, not including the short stories, in this adventure series based on the soldiers of a British soldier, Richard Sharpe, during the Napoleonic Wars.

The popularity of the book series continues with the TV series starring Sean Bean in the titular role, running from 1993 to 1997. With the latest book released in 2021 by Cornwell, Sharpe’s Assassin, and the twenty-third Sharpe adventure, Sharpe’s Command, due towards the end of 2022 the series maintains its popularity.  We have Sharpe by Bernard Cornwell: Books 1-20 Collection available to order, which features the first twenty books in the series.

The Last Kingdom 

The Last Kingdom, also known as the Saxon Series, has a total of thirteen books following the journey of Uhtred of Bebbanburg, who was born into a Saxon family but was captured as a child and adopted by a Danish Warlord. Cornwell takes the reader through the battle between the Saxons and the Danes for the last kingdom, Wessex. The story officially came to an end in 2020 with Cornwell’s last book of the series, War Lord. 

The TV adaptation of The Last Kingdom began in 2015 and finished in 2022, with a feature-length movie following in 2023. The series starred Alexander Dreymon as Uhtred and followed the books up to book ten, The Flame Bearer. We have The Last Kingdom by Bernard Cornwell: Books 1-6 Collection 6 Book Set available for you to order. It is a great starting point for someone getting into the series or someone wanting to re-read them as it contains the first six books in The Last Kingdom series. This collection makes for the perfect gift for fans of the TV series wanting to read the books or longstanding Cornwell fans that wish to re-read this continuing series. 

Cornwell has bought out a number of other series including, The Grail Quest Series which follows the 14th-century search for the Holy Grail, around the time of the Hundred Years' War between England and France. Cornwell has also published The Warlord Chronicles following the legend of King Arthur and his five Sailing Thrillers. 

Cornwell’s books have been a firm favourite for fans of historical fiction for many years. For books like Cornwell’s iconic series, check out The Emperor Series 5 Books Collection Set by Conn Iggulden or Eagles of the Empire Series 10 Books Collection Box Set by Simon Scarrow. We even have a historical, war and western fiction section for you to discover new titles.

title: Biff, Chip & Kipper Books
description:
Biff, Chip & Kipper - as seen on TV! Their brand new live-action show, Biff & Chip, is out now on CBeebies. The kids are joined by their Mum, Dad, Gran, best friends Wilf and Wilma, and their naughty dog Floppy. In these all-new stories, our heroes face an obstacle course, a yeti, and even a dragon! There’s all sorts going on from losing a stick insect to discovering buried treasure! Don’t forget to catch the famous book characters Biff & Chip is on CBeebies every weekday at 5.05pm, and the whole series is on iPlayer. 

For more than 30 years, the characters of Biff, Chip, Kipper and Floppy the Dog have been helping children learn how to read. These books have stood the test of time, building essential reading skills for children worldwide. Now with countless handy and helpful books and growing year by year, it is no wonder that Biff, Chip & Kipper remains one of our bestselling series.

Featuring beautiful illustrations, the Biff, Chip & Kipper books are designed by experts at Read with Oxford. The engaging books will teach readers all the basic reading skills needed in everyday life, from important phonics to common words and everyday language. The aim is to provide books that are both entertaining and educational for readers who are looking to learn but have fun at the same time. Each book is perfect for practising and perfecting skills that can prepare children for new challenges in school and life.

If you are eager to help your child develop from a struggling reader to one with confidence, we highly recommend the Biff, Chip & Kipper series - it’s a huge fan-favourite for parents and has been for over three decades. At Books2Door, we stock Biff. Chip & Kipper book packs for the entire Read with Oxford syllabus. The book sets have been carefully selected and grouped together to support children’s reading development at whatever level they’re at. Click here for the Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, Stage 4, and Stage 5 packs.

Don’t miss out on our Authors and Featured categories for more great titles. You can also shop by age to select the age group you would like to browse for your children. For other helpful reading materials to support your children’s learning at home, make sure to browse our home learning category.

 

What is Read with Oxford?

Read with Oxford is a unique range designed to help parents support their child’s reading journey. The books are packed with fun-filled stories, educational activities and much-loved characters that have been around for over 30 years. The books are favoured by schools and loved by parents.

There are six Read with Oxford Stages to help parents navigate their child’s reading journey, from first steps in phonics to reading independently. The Read with Oxford Stages can be easily matched to Oxford Levels or Book Bands used by schools. We’ve got exclusive book sets to support children with the resources and much-loved methods that parents swear by to help every child learn to read.

For nearly forty years, these loving characters and their various adventures have taken children around the world, teaching children all about language at the same time. Parents may remember these books with nostalgia - they were previously known as Oxford Reading Tree. However, they’re far from old-fashioned. Read with Oxford has continued to refresh the range with new books focused on contemporary topics. The books entertain and teach young kids about language, which helps build their interactions and relationship with friends.

Feature Specification
Series / Brand Biff, Chip and Kipper (Official Oxford Reading Tree Reading Scheme)
Creators Roderick Hunt MBE (Author) and Alex Brychta MBE (Illustrator)
Publisher Oxford University Press (OUP)
Format Architecture Graded Paperback Phonics Sets, Early Reading Collections, Durable Slipcase Box Sets
Target Academic Bracket Ages 4 to 7 Years Old (Reception, Year 1, and Year 2; EYFS and Key Stage 1)
Core Reading Levels Oxford Levels 1 to 6 (Covering Phonics Practice, Word Decoding, and First Stories)
Subject Domains Covered Synthetic phonics, high-frequency sight words, conversational English, everyday family adventures, fantasy magic key quests
Special Value Offerings Multi-book structured bundles, up to 80% off RRP, 10% BookPoints cashback rewards, direct warehouse pricing
Skills Developed Synthetic phonics decoding, independent word recognition, vocabulary expansion, reading aloud stamina

 

If you’re a little unsure about where to start, this super easy guide by Oxford University Press provides you with a short reading placement test. It’s designed to help parents determine which Stage their child is at. Check it out here.

Who are Biff, Chip and Kipper?

Kipper likes to play with Biff, Chip and Floppy, the dog. His real name is Christopher, but he couldn’t pronounce his name correctly as he was learning to talk. His dad then decided the name Kipper suited him, and since then, he’s been Kipper to everyone.

Biff and Chip are twins. Biff loves to play football and go swimming, and she is always ready to join in with games and loves to craft things. Chip likes to go cycling, enjoys sports activities and creative activities like drawing. Their real names are Elizabeth and David. Kipper couldn’t pronounce those either.

The big dog Floppy loves running around, playing with a stick and ball, digging holes and going for swims in the pond and is always covered in mud.

Together, they go on many wonderful adventures, from a trip to the beach right up to travelling in time and space. With a magic key, anything’s possible. Along the way in each story, children will learn a lot about language at a steady and manageable pace.

 

What’s in the books?

Each Biff, Chip & Kipper book is carefully designed and structured to make reading development smooth and straightforward, supporting the Read with Oxford programme as a whole. Parents can use this guide to see which books are recommended for their child’s reading age and level.

The books are designed to provide phonics-based reading practice, help support children’s reading experience and broaden their skills. The books are brimming with funny tales, drama, and charming characters that inspire, excite, and spark curiosity in children.

Many of the early stories are focused on family life. This is perfect for younger children, who can recognise the situations the characters find themselves in, and this will support their learning.

However, as the series progresses, the adventures get bigger. The characters make discoveries, go around the world and back in time, and even journey into fiction. This corresponds with the growing confidence of the reader, becoming more able to follow the stories and enthusiastic about more complex narratives. 

Children progress through five different learning levels. They start with phonics in Level 1, then move to simple words and short sentences in Level 2. These sentences get longer in Level 4, progressing to reading by themselves more in Level 4. Finally, Level 5 sees them becoming a full-fledged independent reader.

The books also contain interactive, such as fun puzzles, activities, and ‘I Spy’. These seem like ways to reward children after they have successfully completed one section, but are actually techniques to check your child’s understanding of the book, and help cement the lessons through repetition. Children will enjoy putting the letters and sounds together to make everyday and familiar words that help build their vocabulary.

Parents and teachers are huge advocates of these books because they are dedicated to teaching children phonics. This series of over 800 books has helped millions of young readers around the world, from primary school age upwards. It has become part of the National Curriculum and is used in 80% of UK primary schools. It’s available in over 130 countries, translated into more than 15 languages and read by more than 30 million children.

About the authors

The beloved Biff, Chip & Kipper series was created by writer Roderick Hunt and illustrator Alex Brychta. In a BBC interview, Hunt says that he started writing the books because he was concerned about his son’s development. He’d been a slow reader himself, so wanted reading material that could both benefit and entertain him, but couldn’t find any. So, he made some himself, writing books focused on “humour and fun and motivation” whilst encouraging reading development.

The vibrant illustrations by Brychta were designed to appeal to children in two ways. The central characters are simple, so children can draw them themselves. However, the picture as a whole is beautifully detailed, so kids can enjoy pointing out all the different things in the illustration. Brychta was born in Czechoslovakia and gre­w up around books that were “absolutely horrible… there was no humour at all, it was tedious.”

The first pack of thirty books was published in 1985 as the Oxford Reading Tree. Now known as Read with Oxford, this six-stage programme brings your child from phonics to an independent reader. They’re kept up-to-date with the changing world, as well as modern educational techniques, so you can be sure that your child is getting the best first reading experience.

The series is incredibly popular with children, parents and teachers alike. The books have been borrowed from libraries over a million times, and adapted for television on multiple occasions. The latest incarnation, Biff & Chip, premiered on CBeebies in September 2021. You may also remember the animated TV series The Magic Key, which aired on BBC Two and CBeebies way back in September 2000. These twenty-six episodes were shown right through to 2008.

 

Why Biff, Chip, & Kipper?

Let’s talk about the achievements and incredible things Read with Oxford has produced with this marvellous series. The stories don’t just focus on one particular place, but take children all around the world, across deserts, forests, the sea and in various locations in different countries. This not only teaches children about new words and sentences, but it forms new views and broadens children’s perspective on their surroundings, habitat and what goes on around them. 

Now, the entertaining series of the modern age covers all critical components like Maths, English, reading development, all filtered by age and school year. Some of the books contain activities that focus on areas around the curriculum. It’s truly a delight to find that your children could be learning times tables, phonics development, creative language or even cooking! In stage 1, stage 2 and stage 3, each collection will guide children from basic to more advanced skills. This can prepare children for all circumstances, from daily use to school exams. 

Let’s highlight some of the critical areas that the books take readers on for reading development. In the earlier books of stage 1, children will learn about alphabets. These are accompanied by alphabet games that help develop memories of letter shapes and sounds. The books will also allow children to build their recall of simple words and sentences and improve their concentration skills. In other instances, in stage 1 of the books, children will be taught to associate pictures with words and letters. There are interactive games that match letters, sounds and shapes to images helping them start reading basic words, all designed by reading experts. Children will also learn about rhyming words and linking various letters and sounds to form words fundamentally needed for spelling.

In stage 2, the adventures of Biff, Chip and Kipper takes you further to new places, for example, following Wilf on a fishing day, Floppy on a desert journey and a dress-up party with Chip. Children who are now more experienced readers and can comprehend basic language can now explore the new exciting trips the series has to offer in stage 2. In stage 3 and after, the books tackle more complex ideas and stories which further challenges readers in a fun way. 

Here at Books2Door, we want to encourage a love of reading in all children. That’s why we have been offering exceptional books at affordable prices since 2004. Shop our books by age category for more books in other age groups. 

We also stock a wide variety of educational books. These include Read it Yourself with Ladybird, a fifty book box set of fairy tales, amazing facts, and original fiction, divided into four reading levels. It’s another fantastic collection of books from Ladybird, and is highly recommended to any child learning to read.

You can also check out the nine-level Usborne Reading Programme, which starts at phonics. Then, across three series of books, your child will progress to full-length narratives. It kicks off with My First Reading Library and then goes through My Reading Library, The Usborne Reading Collection, and finishes with The Usborne Reading Collection for Confident Readers.

All of these different schemes can be used alongside each other, so you can ensure that your child is getting the most whole learning experience, and has access to a great range and variety of different stories and information. Many of our books are available in affordable box sets, so you don’t have to worry about running out halfway through. Shop our selection now, and keep checking back, as we constantly have new books listed on our site.

Roderick Hunt and Alex Brychta represent exceptionally distinguished, globally celebrated pioneers in early childhood literacy, whose Biff, Chip and Kipper stories for the Oxford Reading Tree have taught over thirty million children worldwide to read. Published by Oxford University Press, an elite academic institution universally revered for world-class educational research and strict curriculum standards, this official collection guarantees complete pedagogical accuracy. Utilising clear typography grids, color-coded level bands, and high-opacity paper stock explicitly designed to reduce eye tracking strain in young readers, this series complies seamlessly with UK National Curriculum Key Stage 1 and EYFS frameworks. Recommended by primary teachers, reading recovery specialists, and literacy coordinators across the United Kingdom, this collection serves as the gold-standard asset for early home reading support.

title: Bleach Books
description:
Authored by Tite Kubo, this iconic manga series has captured the hearts and imaginations of readers worldwide with its rich tapestry of action, intrigue, and soul-stirring drama. Join us at Books2Door on a journey through the mystical landscapes of Soul Society, where ghosts, spirits, and otherworldly beings collide in a whirlwind of supernatural battles and gripping storytelling. 

An Overview of Bleach
At the heart of Bleach lies the tale of Ichigo Kurosaki, an ordinary teenager blessed with the extraordinary ability to see spirits. His life is altered forever when he crosses paths with a Soul Reaper. Ichigo finds himself thrust into the strict world of Soul Society, where he must navigate treacherous battles against evil spirits known as Hollows and rival Soul Reapers vying for power and prestige.

As the series unfolds, viewers are drawn deeper into a web of intricate plotlines and complex characters, each harbouring their secrets, motivations, and conflicts. From the enigmatic enforcers of justice, such as the stoic Byakuya Kuchiki and the fiery Renji Abarai, to the menacing forces of darkness, every character in Bleach contributes to the rich tapestry of its narrative, adding layers of depth and intrigue to an already captivating story.

Meet the author
Beyond the pages of Bleach, Tite Kubo himself stands as a towering figure in the world of manga and anime. Born on June 26, 1977, in Hiroshima, Japan, Kubo's creative journey began young, inspired by the works of legendary mangaka, such as Akira Toriyama and Masami Kurumada. After honing his craft through various short stories and one-shot manga, Kubo's breakout success came with the serialization of Bleach in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in 2001, catapulting him to international acclaim and establishing him as one of the foremost talents in the industry.

But what truly sets Bleach apart is its seamless fusion of action-packed combat sequences and poignant character development, all underscored by Kubo's distinctive artistic style. Each panel bursts with dynamic energy and emotion as swords clash, spells are cast, and alliances are forged and shattered amid the chaos of battle. Yet, amidst the spectacle, quiet introspection and heartfelt camaraderie remind readers of humanity and vulnerability.

Get it now!
With its captivating narrative, dynamic artwork, and unforgettable characters, Bleach continues to captivate audiences of all ages. It transcends cultural boundaries to become a timeless classic in the annals of manga history. So, whether you're a seasoned fan or a newcomer to the world of Soul Reapers and Hollows, dive into the pages of Bleach, available now at Books2Door, and experience the magic for yourself.

title: Blocks Universe Books
description:
Introducing the Blocks Universe! Featuring the Numberblocks, Colourblocks, Alphablocks, and more, as seen on the BAFTA-nominated television series on CBeebies. Here at Books2Door, we have specially curated a list of the bestselling Numberblocks and Alphablocks books that are a fan-favourite among the little ones. Whether you're gift shopping for a loved one, or a little one, shop our complete Learning Blocks books collection now.

Alphablocks 

Say hello to the Alphablocks! As seen on CBeebies, check out the BAFTA-nominated television series made up of funky letters. A family of 26 living letters who discover that when they hold hands and make a word, it magically comes to life. Each Alphablock's personality revolves around the unique and memorable way they make their letter sounds. 

The Alphablocks is a step-by-step reading programme grouped into five handy colour-coordinated levels. Each level introduces new letters and "letter teams" in combination with new phonics ideas. The Alphablocks have been developed with literary experts and aligned to the EYSF (Early Years Foundation Stage) framework and the Key Stage One: 

Level One: Recognising the sounds that each letter makes. Children start to meet the letters in an order that allows them to start making words, using sounding out and blending skills.

Level Two: Introduces less common letters and rounds out the alphabet, meeting the capital letters and letter names. 

Level Three: Introduces children to letter teams- two letters that join to make one sound (e.g. sh, ch, oo and ee). 

Level Four: Introduces letter blends- two consonants that make both of their sounds when they appear together (e.g. st-, bl-, and tr-). 

Level Five: Discovering that there are different ways to make the long vowel sounds, such as the combination between a vowel and the letter E (e.g. a-e in cake and o-e in home). Children will learn to complete their journey from meeting the letters to reading words like 'alphabet' independently and confidently. 

Alphablocks Activity Books 

Children will love learning with our Alphablocks Series 3 Books Collection Set by Sweet Cherry Publishing. Perfect for ages 3-6, these books feature two wipe-clean books and a lift-the-flap book. With a free wipe-clean pen, your child can enjoy learning with the Alphablocks as the interactive books guide them to build, blend and write simple phonics.

For those little ones wanting to develop the basics of letters and numbers, why not check out the Numberblocks and Alphablocks: Let's Learn Numbers and Letters 4 Books Wipe-Clean Box Set? This spell-tacular collection of four board books each includes a free wipe-clean pen, guiding children through number bonds and letter teams. This set contains four wipe-clean books, perfect for practising and honing those pen-handling and basic maths skills. Whether they are practising writing their ABCs, counting from 0-10, basic shapes and basic words, this book set has got you covered. Practice and learn through a series of fun number and letter challenges with all of your favourite Alphablocks and Numberblocks!

Numberblocks

If you have children between the ages of 3-5 years old, you must have heard of the BAFTA-nominated show Numberblocks. The brightly coloured cubes with unique personalities are a great addition to your child's screen time as they are engaging and educational. The show strives to improve children's recognition of basic sums like adding, subtracting and timetables. This is ideal for any child who is starting school or nursery and is looking for some activities to practise their maths skills. 

Numberblocks follows a similar step-by-step tier system like Alphablocks, perfect for helping your child develop their skills and helps you monitor their progress. Numberblocks uses best-practice visual teaching techniques that is used in EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage) framework and KS1 curriculum across the UK. 

Level One: Introduction to the first five numbers and foundation skills like counting, recognising amounts of numbers, comparing and sorting numbers, and simple adding and subtraction. 

Level Two: Covers numbers up to ten and introduces bonds, odd and even numbers, square numbers, patterns and shapes. 

Level Three: This stage explores numbers up to thirty as well as looking at doubling numbers, halving, multiplication, division, factions and new number patterns. 

Level Four: The next stage takes children to numbers up to fifty and develops their skills with two-digit numbers more. 

Level Five: The final level explores using numbers up to one hundred and begins showing children how bigger numbers work and gives them an idea of what potentials there are with bigger numbers. 

Meet the Crew

The first ten Numberblocks are: 

  • One - she's the smallest and bravest 
  • Two - he loves to dance with his sparkly shoes 
  • Three - she's a bit of a clown who is always juggling 
  • Four - he's a friendly block who's solid as a rock 
  • Five - she loves giving high-fives
  • Six - she loves to role her dice 
  • Seven - he is made up of the seven colours of the rainbow and is very lucky 
  • Eight - he's the fearless Octoblock who has an evil nemesis called Octonaughty 
  • Nine - he is a square, just like four, but nine just can't stop sneezing
  • Ten - she's always ready for adventure, as she can turn herself into a rocket

Bluey Books

Bluey is the hit animated children's show that has taken the world by storm. Originating from Australia, this incredible show follows the Heeler family, specifically Bluey, an excitable pup with the imagination and energy of most six-year-olds. 

Here at Books2Door, we have a rapidly growing selection of Bluey books for you and your little pups to enjoy. Bluey and Friends Sticker Activity features over 90 stickers, games, and adventures with Bluey, Bingo, and friends. 

About the Show

The show follows six-year-old Bluey, her little sister Bingo and their parents, Bandit and Chilli. The show's creator Joe Brumm was eager to reflect modern parenting, with both adults shown to be working parents, Bandit as an archaeologist and Chilli working part-time in airport security. The show features important themes, including family, growing up, play and Australian culture. Bluey is based on the Australian Cattle Dog, also known as a Blue Heeler, hence the family's last name. There are many references to Australian culture and climate throughout the show. The show is produced in Queensland, so the climate, architecture and wildlife are what would be expected in that area of Australia. 

The show has also received praise for raising awareness of important subjects. For example, a deaf character, Dougie, who uses Auslan (Australian Sign Language) to communicate with his Mum, was introduced. Jack was introduced as a character in Bluey's class who has ADHD, highlighting that he struggles to sit still and remember things. The topic of fertility is raised when it is heavily implied that Chili's sister Brandy, cannot have children even though she would love to have them. Bluey highlights important subjects that may be difficult to discuss with children without scaring or upsetting them. The show has been praised by many parents, stating that they have found it easier to talk about certain subjects using Bluey episodes as reference points. 

The show was co-commissioned by ABC and BBC but has been released for American audiences on Disney+. The show was created in Queensland and is currently still being produced there.

title: Board Books
description:
Board books are a constant favourite for new parents of babies and toddlers and an essential part of any child’s book collection. These durable volumes are great for small ones that want to get their fingers - and mouths - on everything. They’re often the first books that kids can own themselves - there are no delicate pages to get torn, and you can usually wipe off any spills, and nothing will get crumpled up and eaten. They retain their shape even after bending and creasing. Board books are often less expensive than traditional hardcover or paperback books. We have a great selection of board books, from favourite characters to volumes that introduce children to new concepts. Whether you are looking for the first book for your baby or a special gift for a young child in your life, board books are always a great option.

Board books are great tools to encourage literacy among little learners. Since they are generally shorter and simpler than other types of books, board books are ideal for young children who have limited attention spans. While your baby may not be able to understand the story, they will still enjoy looking at the pictures and touching the pages. As your child grows older, they will appreciate being able to handle the book on their own. They are usually smaller in size, making them easier for little hands to grasp. Full-colour illustrations grab their attention and keep them glued to the page. The use of simple words and phrases helps them along the path to speaking in complete sentences. They offer a friendly and welcoming experience to new readers.

Board books are an excellent investment for parents and caregivers of young children. Starter board books will just have a word next t0 an illustration, whereas more advanced volumes will have complete sentences and are closer to picture books printed in a more durable format. 

Some have exciting textures that help to stimulate your child’s senses, and other board books also include interactive elements, such as lift the flap, puppets, or holes you can peek through. By incorporating play into reading, you can capture children's attention who’d much rather get up and do than sit down and read.

We have a range of great board books available at Books2Door. Usborne’s Peep Inside series features holes that children can look through to discover exciting new things. The That’s Not My… series is one of the bestselling books in the UK and is loved by parents for its beautiful illustrations and touchy-feely textures. We stock it in a variety of different great value box sets.

Board books are also a great way to encourage bonding between parent and child. Reading together is a special experience that you will both cherish. Whether you are looking for a traditional tale or a modern favourite, there is sure to be a board book that your child will cherish. So don’t wait, buy a board book today and start creating lasting memories with your little one.

Bonnier Books 

Bonnier Books is a British-owned family publishing company. The Bonnier family has owned the publishing house for seven generations and prides itself in publishing many stories from authors worldwide. 

Disney Reimaginations 

Autumn Publishing, an imprint of Bonnier Books, has produced various titles. This includes the increasingly popular Disney reimaginations like The Twisted Tales Series and The Queens Council series. These books take classic, and well-known stories made famous by Disney and turn them on their heads to create alternative and exciting new tales. 

Check out Disney Twisted Tales Vol. 1-3 Box Set to discover what would have happened if the villains had the upper hand. A Whole New World explores what would have happened if Aladdin had never found the magic lamp, he is just trying to survive, Jasmine is about to enter into an arranged marriage, and Jafar has the lamp. Once Upon a Dream sees the Prince kiss Aurora only for the curse to remain, she stays asleep and must fight her own way out of a dangerous world of dreams. As Old as Time follows Belle as she learns more about her family and the beast's curse. Upon touching the beast's cursed rose, she is hit with visions of her mother, and Belle soon realises that it was her mother who cursed the beast and his manors inhabitants. Belle and the beast must work together in this thrilling adventure to uncover the mystery of their families and break the curse. 

The Queens Council series continues the tales where the films left off. Rebel Rose follows Belle after she has released the beast and the inhabitants of his house from their curse and marries the Prince. But it is 1789 in Paris, and France is on the brink of revolution. Belle is now living a life of Royalty, far from her previous provincial life, and must make crucial decisions about her values, strength and political power. Feather and Flame further explores Mulan's responsibility as the heir to the throne and a strong female warrior. Feather and Flame beautifully blends Chinese history, folklore, and magic to tell the next chapter of Mulan's story. For both epic stories, check out our set, Disney Queen's Council Series 2 Books Collection By Emma Theriault & Livia Blackburne. 

Tattooist of Auschwitz

In 2018, Bonnier Books published the essential book The Tattooist of Auschwitz by Heather Morris. The book tells the story of Lale Sokolov and how he fell in love with Gita Furman while working as the concentration camp tattooist. Morris's internationally bestselling book is based on the memories of Lali Sokolov and his wife, Gita and their horrendous experiences at Auschwitz.

Morris has since published two other books, which are set at the same time and location as The Tattooist of Auschwitz but narrate the events through different prisoners' perspectives. The second book is Cilka's Journey, which follows sixteen-year-old Cilka as she is taken into Auschwitz-Birkenau and subsequently favourited by one of the SS soldiers. This leads to a horrific journey of survival and what it means to survive. The final book in the trilogy is Three Sisters. Also set in Auschwitz-Birkenau, this novel follows three sisters, Cibi, Magda and Livia, as the Nazi rule forces them into concentration camps. They promise themselves that they will stay together and survive together. For all three books, check out our collection, Tattooist of Auschwitz Collection 3 Books Set.

Here at Books2Door, we specialise in book box sets at affordable prices. By buying books in bulk, you are able to save money on the overall cost without losing out on any of the stories. title: Books by Age
description:
As the quality of children’s literature evolves faster than ever, it has become increasingly difficult for parents to find the best children’s books for every age and stage.

As your kids grow older, it will only get more difficult for you to control the literature they consume, especially teenagers. In that, you will not always be familiar with the best books available for your kid’s age group. You will soon realise that you have several factors to consider when choosing reading material. Precisely why, it is essential to get them started young on quality literature and help them pick the best books to read at every age.

Whilst several factors will influence the selection of the best children’s books for your kids at every age and stage of development—we at Books2Door believe you can start by asking some standard questions, like ‘Is this book age-appropriate for my kid?’

There are few moments in life as unique as a baby’s first introduction to books, so you must make a mindful decision. Thankfully, today there are several options at your disposal as a parent, from board books, picture books and pop-up books purpose-built for the little hands and curious minds. These touch-and-feel books, audiobooks, push, pull and slide books are an excellent way to encourage infants and babies to engage with books. These books are carefully designed and written to help babies work on their sensory development, hand-to-eye coordination, and fine motor skills. Whilst picture books work help open a world of storytelling and imagination for toddlers.

From beloved classics to the latest influx of new-age children’s literature, several books will inspire a love of reading and literature in children. As parents, all you need is to expose your kids to the books appropriate for their age group.

Why does the book need to be age appropriate?

A book should appeal to the age group and be able to hold your kid’s interest. It needs the correct number of pages, have the right vocabulary, and the content should be at the level your child is intellectually ready for.

If a book fails to achieve any of these factors, your child will lose interest and put the book down. If this happens more than once, your kid will assume they don’t like reading. It is essential, therefore, that you find a book that is age-appropriate for your child.

So how do you shortlist age-appropriate books for your kid? Here are some things that you might want to consider…

From toddlers to teens and every age in between, here is how you can pick an age-appropriate book from the classics, bestselling books, and new-age children’s literature for your child.

Read Books2Door’s book synopsis.

We at Books2Door not only list information about books under the Books By Age tab for different age groups but also present a detailed synopsis of each book under each tab. Our website navigation is designed to help you make reading choices based on all your needs and preferences. 

You can also search specific book titles by simply using the search box. If you don’t have a particular book in mind, we also have detailed descriptions and reviews that will help you make an informed decision about which book you would like for your child or yourself.

Goodreads Reviews

We at Books2Door are a big part of the book lover’s community, and Goodreads is another platform for genuine literature lovers.

Underneath every book description on Book2Door, you will find the Goodreads reviews grid. You can scroll through all the reviews, read up on what other parents thought of the said book, and make age-appropriate book choices for your kid.

Read the book yourself

Whilst we have left no stone unturned to make the decision-making process simpler for you, if you are still unsure about what qualifies as age-appropriate reading material for your kids, you can read the book yourself and decide if it is appropriate for your kid. Whilst we at Books2Door can suggest books for your child’s age group, we understand that you are the expert in what is suitable for your child.

Cater to your child’s calibre and learning speed

If your child reads books beyond their age group fluently, that’s great! You can encourage your child to read books with a higher vocabulary and complex writing. You can still censor their reading material for age-appropriate content regarding what information you expose them to.

The reverse can be done if your child struggles with reading and needs to start with more straightforward books appropriate for a younger age group. Sometimes a child simply needs to build confidence to enjoy reading. So let them read below their level to start enjoying books.

We’re here to help you find the best books suited to every age and every stage. You’ll discover an impressive range of books to inspire every eager reader regardless of age or interests. From toddlers to teens and every step in between, why not start by checking out some of our bestsellers or fiction and nonfiction titles with recommendations for each age group. At Books2Door, we like to make it easy for you to browse the most popular reads you can buy, knowing you’ve made the right choice. Whether it’s showing you the most loved kids’ books, picture books, classic collections or bestselling sets, here you’ll find unmissable prices across everyday books. 

There’s nothing quite like curling up with a good book and introducing this from a young age in a bedtime routine or for even 10-15 minutes a day will do wonders for their development skills. If you’re keen to build up your collection of books at home with various topics and interests - we’re here to nurture that love for books linked directly to childhood. Often books can have a sense of escapism packed with fun and adventure. Still, as children’s interests grow or their reading skills develop, they’ll be on the hunt for new books to fill their curious minds.

Our 0-5 collection is perfect for babies, toddlers, and kids just starting out on their reading journey. In it, you’ll find picture books, touch and feel, pop-up and lift the flap books, and all manner of great bedtime stories. From phonics to baby gift sets, find the perfect books for your child today.

If your child is between 5-7, shop our extensive range of books perfect for them. From Biff, Chip & Kipper to Mr Men and Little Miss, it’s an unbeatable selection of classic children’s books and new favourites. This is a pivotal time to make reading a habit for your children, so it’s essential that you’ve got books you know they’re going to love.

When your child reaches the age of 7-9, the whole world of reading is opened up to them. Whether it’s The Chronicles of Narnia or Diary of a Wimpy Kid, you’ll find the perfect box set to get your kids engrossed in the world of stories. Kids will be developing their own tastes by now, so whether they’re into imaginative fiction, books that are more down-to-earth, or just a good laugh, you can be sure that we’ve got the right box set for them.

Independent readers aged 9-14 can be voracious consumers of books. Luckily, we’ve got the box sets you need to keep up with them. Whether it’s Harry Potter, Alex Rider, Jacqueline Wilson or Rick Riordan, you can be sure to find a set to suit your child’s tastes.

title: Books on Death and Bereavement
description:
Grief is a complicated subject, especially when it is a child experiencing it. Dealing with the loss of a loved one or grief of any kind can be life altering for children and adults. As humans, we are all designed to feel emotions and love which also means we all have the capacity to feel pain and grief. As adults we can deal with pain and manage our emotions but children are not equipped to do the same. 

In order to help children cope with difficult emotions and experiences, you can provide them with a ton of support, positive energy and ways to channel their grief into something productive. Books on grief and loss, we think, play a pivotal role in doing so. Stories of people that have dealt with grief and loss in positive ways can help a grieving person (irrespective of age) find hope.

We at Books2Door have curated a collection of some of the best selling books on grief and loss, to help people, especially children cope with loss and grief. Whether you're looking for some help for yourself or you need a way to explain death to a child, we have a lovely selection of books for you to look through.

The Invisible String by Patrice Karst This picture book about the unbreakable connections between loved ones has healed a generation of readers—children and adults alike, and has just been updated with new illustrations and an afterword from the author. A perfect tool for coping with all kinds of separation anxiety, loss, and grief; the book is perfect for anyone that is struggling to stay afloat. 

In this relatable and reassuring contemporary classic, a mother tells her two children that they're all connected by an invisible string. "What kind of string?" the children ask! The answer is the simple truth that binds us all: An Invisible String made of love. Even though you can't see it with your eyes, you can feel it deep in your heart, and know that you are always connected to the ones you love. This heartwarming picture book for all ages explores questions about the intangible yet unbreakable connections between us, and opens up deeper conversations about love.

Let's Talk About When Someone Dies by Molly Potter, best-selling author of How Are You Feeling Today? and What's Worrying You?, comes a picture book for starting conversations with children about death, bereavement and what happens next. When someone dies, we can feel a whole host of different emotions and explaining them to a child isn't so easy. This book uses clear, easy-to-understand language to answer complex questions about death and how a child might feel when someone dies. It covers all manner of tricky subjects with sensitivity and honesty, from what death is to why people die. Each double page spread takes a child through how they might feel, what they might think and how they might behave. With engaging illustrations, gentle guidance and simple advice for parents and carers, Let's Talk About When Someone Dies fulfils an important but difficult need for starting conversations with children about death and bereavement, in an accessible and supportive way.

The Memory Tree by Britta Teckentrup is a beautiful and heartfelt picture book to help children celebrate the memories left behind when a loved one dies. Fox has lived a long and happy life in the forest, but now he is tired. He lies down in his favourite clearing, and falls asleep forever. Before long, Fox's friends begin to gather in the clearing. One by one, they tell stories of the special moments that they shared with Fox. And so, as they share their memories, a tree begins to grow, becoming bigger and stronger with each memory, sheltering and protecting all the animals in the forest, just as Fox did when he was alive. This gentle story about the loss of a loved one is a perfect grief book for adults and children, that teaches how sharing can bring comfort.

title: Brandon Sanderson Books
description:
Born in Lincoln, Nebraska in 1975; Brandon Sanderson is a popular American author of fantasy and science fiction. A biochemistry major from Brigham Young University; Brandon always found himself gravitating to writing fantasy and fiction. As a result he decided to go back to Uni, majoring in English and whilst at it, took up a job as a night desk clerk at a hotel because they allowed him to write while at work. 

During this time Sanderson went to school full time during the day, worked nights to pay for his schooling, and wrote as much as he could. He says it made for a rather dismal social life, but he finished seven novels during his undergraduate years. Brandon submitted many manuscripts for publication and accumulated quite a pile of rejection letters. In spite of this he continued to be a dedicated writer.

It was in 2003, that Brandon got a call from editor Moshe Feder at Tor, who wanted to buy one of Brandon Sanderson’s fantasy books. In May 2005 Brandon held his first, Warbreaker, and The Way of Kings, the first in a projected ten-volume series called The Stormlight Archive; this one is perfect for young adults who enjoy fantasy fiction. An epic fantasy series The Stormlight Archive is a treat for the fans of fantasy fiction and world building novels. Dive into this world that Sanderson has created and see what the novels in the series have to offer. 

The king of Alethi, Gavinar, is killed by an assassin in white who defies the rules of physics. He was hired by the Parshendi and killed on the night when the two people were about to sign a treaty. This leads both of these people to a war that is fought in the Desolated Plains. Powerful weapons such as Shardblades and Shardplates, enhanced weapons and only a few in existence, are used in battles. Dalinar, the brother of Gavinar, is leading the battle against the Parshendi but has been getting visions of Odium and the Voidbringers.

Other series like Mistborn Trilogy By Brandon Sanderson is a 3 Books Set 

This epic fantasy trilogy overturns the expectations of readers and then goes on to tell the epic story of evil overturned in a richly imagined world. A thousand years ago evil came to the land and has ruled with an iron hand ever since. The sun shines fitfully under clouds of ash that float down endlessly from the constant eruption of volcanoes. A dark lord rules through the aristocratic families and ordinary folk are condemned to lives in servitude, sold as goods, labouring in the ash fields. But now a troublemaker has arrived and there is rumour of revolt. 

The second book in the set; The Well Of Ascension starts with the impossible happening. The Ruler is dead and has been vanquished. But so too is Kelsier the man who masterminded the triumph. The awesome task of rebuilding the world has been left to his protege Vin; a one-time street urchin, now the most powerful Mistborn in the land. Adventure ensues!

The third and final book in the trilogy; The Hero Of Ages will keep young readers glued. Tricked into releasing the evil spirit Ruin while attempting to close the Well of Ascension, new emperor Elend Venture and his wife, the assassin Vin, are now hard-pressed to save the world. This adventure brings the Mistborn epic fantasy trilogy to a dramatic and surprising climax as Sanderson's saga offers complex characters and a compelling plot, asking hard questions about loyalty, faith and responsibility. Jump into the epic series from New York Times bestselling author Brandon Sanderson, The Mistborn Trilogy. 

Brandon Sanderson’s young adult books include several other fantasy series including The Reckoners Series by Brandon Sanderson 3 Books Collection Set  The Reckoners is a young adult sci-fi fantasy series, set in an undisclosed future. The series depicts a post-apocalyptic world in which the appearance of an orbiting cosmic phenomenon known as Calamity has given random people superhuman powers in apparent defiance of known physical laws. They are called Epics. With this power grows the need to destroy, rule, and kill without mercy. These Epics prey upon or enslave the rest of humanity, causing the collapse of traditional governments. Major cities fall under the tyranny of an Epic, with no one but other Epics to get in their way. One young man orphaned by a High Epic joins a group that is killing Epics.

Modern British Literature

title: Bronte Sisters Books
description:
The Bronte sisters, Emily, Charlotte, and Anne, are celebrated as three of the most significant literary figures of the 19th century. Each sister contributed to the literary canon with their unique and captivating works. Let's delve into the profound impact of the Bronte sisters' novels, focusing specifically on three masterpieces: Wuthering Heights by Emily Bronte, Jane Eyre by Charlotte Bronte, and The Tenant of Wildfell Hall by Anne Bronte. These novels continue to captivate readers with their compelling characters, vivid settings, and timeless themes.

Check out some of the amazing Bronte book sets available here at Books2Door. Whether you’re an avid reader of these iconic sisters or if you’re new to their work, a great collection for all bookshelves is The Complete Brontë Sisters Collection 7 Books Box Set. This set contains classics like Wuthering Heights and Jane Eyre as well as underappreciated masterpieces like Villette and Agnes Grey. 

Is your little bookworm desperate to read these classic Bronte novels? Perhaps you want to introduce them to your favourite stories but are worried they won’t understand the language used. If this is the case, check out Sweet Cherry Publishing’s Easy Classics! In particular The Complete Bronte Sisters 8 Books Children's Collection Set (Easy Classics) By Stephanie Baudet. Perfect for children aged 7-9 years old and comes with an easy-to-understand history of the sisters and how they took the literary world by storm. Raised on the Yorkshire moors these unlikely women went on to shape literature as we know it today. In this collection, Baudet breaks down the original texts into accessible reads without losing any of the important plot points. This book set also comes with free audiobook versions of each text, perfect for car journeys or for dyslexic readers. 

Wuthering Heights:

Wuthering Heights, written by Emily Bronte, is a novel that defies conventional storytelling and explores the darker aspects of human nature. The narrative unfolds in a non-linear manner, narrated by multiple characters, creating a complex and haunting tale. The story revolves around the intense and volatile relationship between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw. Their passionate connection transcends societal boundaries, but it is ultimately marred by vengeance, betrayal, and tragedy.

One of the remarkable aspects of Wuthering Heights is Emily Bronte's skilful depiction of complex characters. Heathcliff, a brooding and enigmatic figure, embodies the tortured soul consumed by his love for Catherine and his desire for revenge. Catherine, on the other hand, is torn between her wild, emotional attachment to Heathcliff and the expectations of societal norms. The supporting characters, such as the kind-hearted Nelly Dean and the conflicted Edgar Linton, add depth and complexity to the narrative.

Moreover, the setting of Wuthering Heights plays a vital role in shaping the atmosphere of the novel. The wild and desolate moors of Yorkshire mirror the turbulent emotions of the characters and contribute to the eerie and haunting ambience. Emily Bronte's vivid descriptions of the landscape create a sense of foreboding and intensify the emotional turmoil experienced by the characters.

Jane Eyre:

Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre is a pioneering work in the realm of Victorian literature, featuring a strong-willed and independent female protagonist who challenges societal expectations. The novel traces the life of Jane Eyre, an orphan who endures a difficult childhood under the care of her cruel aunt and at a harsh boarding school. Jane grows into a resilient and intelligent woman, eventually finding employment as a governess at Thornfield Hall.

The core of Jane Eyre lies in its exploration of Jane's quest for love, self-discovery, and personal autonomy. Charlotte Bronte subverts traditional gender roles by presenting Jane as an assertive and morally steadfast individual. Through her character, Bronte raises questions about women's rights, social class, and the importance of individuality. Jane's relationship with the brooding Mr Rochester is both captivating and controversial, as it challenges societal expectations and highlights the complexities of love and morality.

In addition to its progressive themes, Jane Eyre also stands out for its narrative structure. The novel is divided into distinct phases, each representing a different stage of Jane's life. This structure allows readers to witness Jane's personal growth, inner conflicts, and eventual triumph over adversity.

The Tenant of Wildfell Hall:

Anne Bronte's The Tenant of Wildfell Hall takes a bold stance on controversial subjects that were often avoided in Victorian literature, such as alcoholism, domestic abuse, and the rights of women. The story unfolds through a series of letters and diary entries, shedding light on the life of Helen Graham, a mysterious tenant at Wildfell Hall. As the narrative unfolds, readers learn about Helen's troubled past, her abusive marriage, and her struggle for independence.

The Tenant of Wildfell Hall challenges the societal norms of the time by portraying Helen as a strong and courageous woman who takes control of her own destiny. Anne Bronte sheds light on the realities of domestic abuse and the restrictions placed on women within marriage. Through Helen's character, Bronte emphasises the importance of self-preservation and the right of women to escape oppressive relationships.

Furthermore, The Tenant of Wildfell Hall provides a scathing critique of the destructive nature of addiction. Helen's husband, Arthur Huntingdon, embodies the consequences of alcoholism, showcasing the devastating impact it has on the individual and those around them. Bronte's portrayal of the struggles faced by Helen and her determination to protect her son make the novel a compelling and socially significant work.

The works of Emily, Charlotte, and Anne Bronte continue to captivate readers and critics alike, with their compelling narratives and exploration of complex themes. Wuthering Heights, Jane Eyre, and The Tenant of Wildfell Hall stand as a testament to the Bronte sisters' enduring literary legacy.

Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights immerses readers in a dark and turbulent world, exploring themes of love, revenge, and the destructive nature of obsession. Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre challenges societal conventions through the character of Jane, a strong and independent woman on a quest for self-discovery. Anne Bronte's The Tenant of Wildfell Hall boldly addresses issues of abuse, marriage, and women's rights, defying societal norms.

These novels not only reflect the Victorian era but also resonate with contemporary readers, providing insight into universal human experiences. The Bronte sisters' contributions to literature remain unparalleled, showcasing their mastery of storytelling and their ability to capture the depths of human emotions. Through their powerful narratives, they have left an indelible mark on the literary world, inspiring generations of readers and writers.

In contrast, Monkey, who was mistakenly shot into the forest, thinking it was outer space, is loud and mischievous and often comes up with crazy schemes to take over the forest. The series is renowned for its rich ensemble of quirky characters. Oh, let us introduce the beautiful characters to you, Skunky, a genius inventor who is Monkey's sidekick and comes up with various gadgets and gizmos; Le Fox, a charming yet cunning character; Pig, the kind-hearted and optimistic friend; Weenie, a squirrel who loves to join in the adventures; and Metal Steve, a robot with a heart.

The stories are packed with slapstick humour, witty dialogue, and exciting plot twists, making it a hit for a wide age range. Bunny vs Monkey is not just for entertainment; it is an excellent tool for education and learning. This comic book series teaches young readers the concept of problem-solving, the importance of being in harmony with nature and the wild, and friendship, as this plot is based on the core of friendship. 

This series is perfect for binge-reading or passing the time without getting bored while being informed and educated. It has several volumes perfect for this, each containing multiple short stories and building plots. Not to forget, this episodic format helps young readers follow along and stay engaged with the stories, also helping older readers break their reading episodes.

Now, if you are a parent, educator, or just somebody shopping for children who encourages readers through fun and engaging stories, this is perfect. The series captivates children's imaginations and fosters a love of reading and storytelling. It suits those transitioning from picture books to more text-heavy reading material.

Bunny vs. Monkey is an all-around must-read series that cleverly and enticingly blends humour, adventure, and meaningful life lessons. These books will surely delight and encourage young readers everywhere, whether they are used for bedtime stories, classroom reading, or individual reading sessions.

The Shardlake Series is not just a source of entertainment, but also a window into the complexities of Tudor society.
