title: C. S. Lewis Books
description:
Delve into the enchanting realm of Narnia with The Chronicles of Narnia book set, or explore the depths of his thought-provoking essays and apologetics with The Complete C. S. Lewis Signature Classics.

The Chronicles of Narnia 

Immerse yourself in the magical world of Narnia with The Chronicles of Narnia 7 book set. This exceptional collection brings together all seven books that have captured the hearts and imaginations of readers of all ages. From the wardrobe in The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe to the epic battles in The Last Battle, these timeless tales transport you to a realm where animals talk, mythical creatures roam, and adventure awaits at every turn.

In this book set, you will embark on unforgettable journeys alongside beloved characters like Lucy, Edmund, Peter, and Susan as they encounter Aslan, the great lion and the true king of Narnia. From the whimsical world of talking animals and mythical creatures to the battles between good and evil, these stories are imbued with rich symbolism and deep moral lessons. Perfect for readers young and old, The Chronicles of Narnia book set is an essential addition to any bookshelf and a gateway to a world of imagination.

For the ultimate Narnia enthusiast, we offer The Complete Chronicles of Narnia Hardback Gift Book. This exquisite edition brings together all seven books in a beautiful hardcover format. With its stunning illustrations, gilt-edged pages, and a ribbon bookmark, this edition is not only a literary treasure but also an aesthetic delight. The Complete Chronicles of Narnia Hardback Gift Book allows you to experience the entire Narnia journey in one volume. Delve into the intricate details of C.S. Lewis' vivid world as you journey from the lamp post in the snowy woods of Narnia to the majestic battles for freedom and the ultimate redemption of this magical land. This comprehensive collection is the perfect gift for Narnia fans, collectors, and those seeking a timeless escape into the realm of fantasy and wonder.

Beyond the magical realm of Narnia, C.S. Lewis also crafted a diverse body of work encompassing philosophy, theology, and literary criticism. The Complete C. S. Lewis Signature Classics brings together seven of his most influential and thought-provoking books. From the profound insights of Mere Christianity and the cleverly crafted letters of The Screwtape Letters to the introspective memoir Surprised by Joy, this collection offers a comprehensive exploration of Lewis' intellectual depth and spiritual wisdom.

C.S. Lewis Signature Classics

The Complete C. S. Lewis Signature Classics is an invitation to embark on a profound journey of self-reflection, spiritual exploration, and intellectual growth. Lewis tackles weighty topics such as faith, morality, love, pain, and the existence of God with clarity, wit, and intellectual rigour. These timeless works continue to inspire readers and provoke contemplation on life's most profound questions.

About the Author: 

Clive Staples Lewis, known as C.S. Lewis, was born on November 29, 1898, in Belfast, Ireland. From a young age, Lewis displayed a remarkable imagination and a love for storytelling. As a child, he created the fantastical world of Boxen, populated by talking animals and imaginary kingdoms—a precursor to the rich world of Narnia that would captivate readers for generations to come.

Lewis served in World War I and later studied at Oxford University, where he became a renowned scholar of English literature. His friendship with J.R.R. Tolkien, the author of The Lord of the Rings, played a significant role in shaping his literary career and fostering his creative genius. Inspired by their discussions on mythology, religion, and the power of storytelling, Lewis embarked on his own writing journey.

Throughout his life, Lewis grappled with questions of faith and reason, ultimately finding solace and conviction in Christianity. His spiritual journey greatly influenced his writings, particularly his apologetic works such as Mere Christianity and The Problem of Pain. Lewis possessed a remarkable ability to make complex theological concepts accessible to a broad audience, earning him a reputation as a brilliant thinker and a persuasive communicator.

C.S. Lewis's works continue to resonate with readers around the world. His captivating storytelling, profound insights, and unwavering faith have left an indelible mark on literature, theology, and popular culture. Whether you are seeking a captivating fantasy adventure or a deep exploration of life's most profound questions, C.S. Lewis' books offer a captivating and enriching reading experience.

Explore the realms of Narnia or dive into the intellectual depths of Lewis' signature classics. Discover the magic, wisdom, and enduring legacy of C.S. Lewis through his extraordinary body of work.

title: Canongate Books
description:
Founded back in 1973 Canongate Books is an independent British publishing house based in Edinburgh, Scotland.

Best known for nurturing and publishing new voices from across the globe, Canongate Books address several social issues and have a distinct outlook on the world. As part of their commitment to unearthing and promoting important voices and opinions; Canongate Books Edinburgh has published popular world leaders and novice writers with equal gusto. From publishing the works of an American president to new writers; the Canongate books catalogue is packed to the brim with the most coveted and unorthodox titles. 

Continuing their campaign for causes they believe in; Canongate has joined a global alliance of eleven other publishers and their international partners in their shared vision of editorial excellence, publishing original, diverse voices and their fight for causes and authors they believe in. Over the years, Canongate has given the world several bestselling, Award Winning books like Yann Martel’s Life of Pi, Alasdair Gray’s masterpiece Lanark amongst several others. Canongate Books themselves won the British Book Awards Publisher of the year in 2003 and 2009.

Whilst there are several reasons for any book lover to subscribe to the annual Canongate Books catalogue; we at Books2Door love how progressive the Canongate Myth Series is. The Myths series brings together some of the world's finest writers and commissions to each of them an ancient myth, which they then spin around and retell in a contemporary and progressive fashion. Our favourite of the Myth series is The Penelopiad by Margaret Atwood. Atwood rewrites the legend and the myth of Penelope from the perspective of Penelope and the Twelve maids and turns this story of a devoted wife waiting for her glorious husband Odysseus into a tale of lust, greed, and murder.

An award-winning Canongate gem; Homelands: The History of a Friendship by Chitra Ramaswamy brings forth the voices of immigrants and delves into sensitive themes like anti-Semitism, racism, resilience, and more. A story about an unlikely friendship between an Indian Immigrant born in 1970s Britain and another from Nazi Germany in 1939, fleeing persecution; the book is an intriguing read about common grounds, homelands, and more.

Yet another important voice that Canongate Books has given the world is My Name Is Why by Lemn Sissay. The book follows a seventeen-year-old orphan through his childhood years with a foster family and in care homes. Until the day when Norman Greenwood is given his birth certificate and his real identity is revealed. Lemn Sissay, upon learning of his British heritage and his mother, sets out on a journey of self-discovery. Through Sissay’s journey, the book explores the institutional care system, race, and most importantly the meaning of home and family. A powerful memoir by a foster kid, the book is one of the many diverse voices brought forth by Canongate Books.

Whilst Canongate Books are all for encouraging new authors and voices; the Canongate Books submissions department does not accept unsolicited submissions and makes it a point to work with a lot of brilliant literary agents. They value the work of literary agents in the UK no less than the writers and are known to follow stringent and ethical editorial practices.

title: Cartoons & Comic Strips
description:
A comic strip is a series of panels with cartoon drawings and sequential art in them, that tell a story. Sometimes comic strips are humorous, sometimes they are simply telling a story and sometimes they are serious but they are always short, easy to read, and they always provide immediate satisfaction to the reader. These comic strips put together in a sequence tell stories that make perfect reading material and comic strip books for children and adults alike. Reluctant readers or voracious readers—comic strip books are loved by anyone that enjoys a well-told story and interesting narrative.

It's important to note however that these books do not read like graphic novels or old-school superhero comic books. Comic Strip books are curated, in a short panel-format (like those in newspapers!) comic strips in book format, or a series of books to tell stories that can interest readers across age groups.

In this collection of comic strip books we bring together both classics and contemporary comic strips. Some of the most popular being Peanuts by Charles Schulz and Calvin and Hobbes by Bill Watterson.

Yukon Ho! : Calvin & Hobbes Series: Book Four by Bill Watterson is unquestionably one of the most popular comic strips of all time. One of the best comic strip books for adults and children alike; Calvin and Hobbes is a popular classic. The imaginative world of a boy and his real-only-to-him tiger was first syndicated in 1985 and appeared in more than 2,400 newspapers when Bill Watterson retired in January, 1996. This classic comic strip is the treasure that all Calvin and Hobbes fans seek. Amidst the discussions of morality, consumerism, and existentialism, Calvin and Hobbes is an escapist story of a six-year-old boy and his ambiguously imaginary friend the tiger. The relatability of Calvin’s attempts to escape from reality appeals not just to childhood memories but also to present experiences of the real world.

Plus a rare opportunity to see what Pig-pen looks clean!

The Mortal Instruments

The Mortal Instruments is where the series all began. In 2007 Clare's first novel and the first book in the series, City of Bones, was published. The book starts as fifteen-year-old Clary witnesses a brutal crime in the middle of New York City. She soon discovers that the attackers are invisible to other humans, but she can see them. As she learns more and more about this group of tattooed teens, she discovers more about her past. The series has a total of six books, starting with City of Bones and followed by City of Ashes, City of Glass, City of Lost Souls, City of Fallen Angels and City of Heavenly Fire. 

Now a major motion picture starring Lily Collins and Jamie Campbell Bower, The Mortal Instruments has taken the world by storm. This set contains all six books from The Mortal Instruments series plus The Shadow Hunters Codex. 

The Infernal Devices series is a prequel to The Mortal Instruments series and is set in 1878 London and follows Tessa Grey as she enters the Shadow World and that she is not a mundane. There are a total of three books in The Infernal Devices series, starting with Clockwork Angel, then Clockwork Prince and ending with Clockwork Princess. The entire Infernal Devices trilogy is available in our Shadowhunters by Cassandra Clare - The Infernal Devices 3 Books Box Set.

Clare is currently writing a trilogy sequel to The Internal Devices called The Last Hours. The series is set in 1903 and follows Tessa's children. The Dark Artifices is the third set of books published by Cassandra Clare and is the sequel to The Mortal Instruments series. CBeebies Bedtime Stories series

You may recognise lots of famous faces that join in on your evening routine to read to your little ones before they go to sleep. Read by award-winning English actor Tom Hardy, this board book aimed at children aged 0-5 contains colourful illustrations integrated with a heart-warming story of taking the time to overcome your fears and building up the courage to try something new with a support of a loved one. The winner of the Indie Book Award 2020, this book follows the story of Very Big Crab and Little Crab living in the rockpool above the sea. If you loved this book, check out the Oh No, George! Collection by Chris Haughton 5 Book Series. This five-book collection contains more heartfelt and encouraging stories such as A Bit Lost, Oh No, George!, Shh! We Have a Plan, Goodnight Everyone and Don’t Worry, Little Crab. Check out our other board books here. 

Another great read is I Talk Like a River by Jordan Scott. Read by Engish singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran, this book is perfect for children aged 7-9. The book is a powerfully moving and personal story of a boy’s struggle with a stammer. What if words got stuck in the back of your mouth whenever you tried to speak? After a day of being unable to speak, a boy and his father spend some quiet time near the river. Despite everything, the boy can’t stop thinking about all the eyes watching his lips twisting and twirling. That is until his father points to the river bubbling and churning, crashing and whirling. Even the river stutters. Just like him. This incredibly moving picture book masterfully offers solace and understanding rather than a solution to resonate with readers young and old.

title: Cecelia Ahern Books
description:
Cecelia Ahern is a highly acclaimed Irish author and screenwriter with over 25 million Books sold across 40 countries, with her works translated into over 50 languages. Born and raised in Malahide, a coastal town in north County Dublin; Ahern attended Griffith College Dublin and earned a degree in journalism and media communications. At the age of 21, after she completed her education, Cecelia went on to write her first book P.S I love You in 2004, through which she shot to fame. 

P.S I Love You was an instant success, becoming a bestseller in Ireland, the UK, the US, and other countries. It was later adapted into a film starring Hilary Swank and Gerard Butler. Cecelia has since published a novel every year and to date she has published over 18 successful novels including Love, Rosie, If You Could See Me Now, A Place Called Here, and The Gift. Popular for their heartwarming stories, relatable characters and poetic language; Ahern’s novels explore themes such as love, friendship, family, self-discovery, and the human experience. Ahern has a way of capturing the complexity of human emotions and experiences with sensitivity and nuance. Her writing style is poetic and evocative, making her stories relatable for the readers. 

Despite her phenomenal success as a writer, Ahern remains grounded and continues to be actively involved in various charitable causes. And advocates mental health awareness. This apart from the significant impact she has had on the literary world. Ahern’s books have touched the hearts of millions of readers worldwide and her writing has been praised for its beauty and sensitivity. Ahern continues to be a prominent figure in the world of literature and is dearly loved by her readers.

Cecelia Ahern and her books have won numerous awards, including the Irish Book Award for Popular Fiction for The Year I Met You. She has published several novels and contributed a number of short stories to various anthologies. Alongside writing novels, Cecelia has also established herself as a screenwriter in the recent past. She has created and produced the ABC comedy Samantha Who? starring Christina Applegate. Two of her books have been adapted as major motion films. Whilst her short story collection Roar has been adapted as a series for AppleTV+. Cecelia has also written a TV series currently in development with Picturestart, and a feature film sequel to PS I Love You titled Postscript with Alcon Entertainment is also in development.

Following Celelia Ahern’s phenomenal success and popularity with the Young Adult readers; we have curated this collection with all of her bestselling works. Read on and enjoy with a hot cuppa of cocoa. 

Two of Celelia Ahern’s popular books, The Year I Met You and How to Fall in Love are brought together in this Cecelia Ahern Collection 2 Books Set for young adults. 

The Year I Met You is a poignant novel that explores the themes of friendship, love, and self-discovery. The story centres around two characters, Jasmine and Matt, who are forced to spend New Year's Eve alone due to different circumstances. Jasmine is a successful businesswoman who has been suspended from work for a month, while Matt is a freelance journalist who has been laid off. They are neighbours but have never really spoken to each other until that fateful night. The novel follows their journey as they become friends and support each other through their respective struggles and discover a deep connection that they both cannot ignore. What makes The Year I Met You a must-read is its beautiful portrayal of human relationships and the relatable characters with inspiring journeys.

How to Fall in Love is another touching novel that explores the themes of love and self-discovery. The story revolves around Christine, a woman who is feeling lost. She meets a stranger named Adam, who is determined to help her find her way back to happiness. Adam challenges her to complete a list of tasks that he believes will help her rediscover her true self and fall in love with life again. As Christine embarks on this journey of self-discovery, she starts to unravel the secrets of Adam's past and discovers that he has his own reasons for wanting to help her. As they get closer, she realises that she might be falling in love with him, but wonders if it's too late to start over. You must read How to Fall in Love for its uplifting and inspiring message. The novel encourages readers to take a step back and reflect on their lives, and to have the courage to make the changes necessary to find happiness.

Flawed By Celelia Ahern is yet another stunning YA novel by the bestselling author Cecelia Ahern. Celestine North lives a perfect life. She's a model daughter and sister, she's well-liked by her classmates and teachers, and she's dating the impossibly charming Art Crevan. But then Celestine encounters a situation in which she makes an instinctive decision. She breaks a rule and now faces life-changing repercussions. She could be imprisoned. She could be branded. She could be found FLAWED. The book delves into the complexities of how our society makes perfection paramount and mistakes are punished. And where one young woman decides to take a stand that could cost her everything.

To round up Cecelia Ahern's books in order of why they make great reads; her writing we think is a testament to the power of skilled storytelling. Her novels are not only entertaining and engaging but also offer valuable insights into the human experience. If you're looking for a heartwarming and inspiring read that will stay with you long after you've finished the last page, then Ahern’s books are definitely worth your while.

title: Celebrating Asexual and Aromantic Voices
description:
Asexuality and aromanticism are often overlooked or misrepresented in mainstream storytelling. This collection shines a light on these identities, offering books that reflect the reality and diversity of life without sexual or romantic attraction.

These characters live full and satisfying lives outside of conventional love narratives. You’ll find thoughtful explorations of friendship, personal discovery, chosen family, and self-worth. Some stories challenge societal expectations of love, while others embrace identities with confidence and pride.

Our selection includes contemporary fiction, fantasy, and non-fiction that educate and demystify what it means to be ace or aro. These stories provide essential representation, especially for readers who rarely see themselves in books.

For allies, parents, and educators, this collection offers a new lens on connection, showing that love takes many forms, all of them worthy of celebration.

title: Celebrating Bisexual & Pansexual Voices
description:
Looking to explore bisexuality and pansexuality through powerful storytelling or insightful non-fiction? This collection centres books that reflect these identities with honesty, care, and joy.

From teens navigating attraction across genders to adults reclaiming their identities later in life, these stories celebrate the richness of bisexual and pansexual experience. You’ll find contemporary romances, speculative fiction, heartfelt memoirs, and practical guides like Bisexuality: The Basics by Lewis Oakley.

This collection challenges common myths like the idea that bisexuality is “just a phase” or that pansexuality is “confusing”and instead presents characters whose identities are valid, nuanced, and empowering.

With intersectional perspectives on culture, gender, mental health, and community, these books reflect the beautiful diversity within bi and pan communities. Whether you're exploring your identity or seeking to understand others better, these stories offer connection, visibility, and pride.

title: Celebrating Black Voices & Stories
description:
Celebrating Black voices and stories all year round is essential, and we are thrilled to share this journey with you, our dear readers. We hold these writers in high regard and invite you to join us as we explore our favourite Black authors. We hope to inspire you, and who knows, perhaps you might even feature in our collection someday!

It’s time to focus on agency, and we’re fully committed to this mission. So, let’s dive in and get started, shall we? For more recommendations and to discover incredible reads, check out our blog, Black History Month: A Guide to Must-Read Books by Black Authors, for a deeper exploration of Black authors and their powerful stories.

Young Readers

We believe starting young is crucial for nurturing a love of literature and shaping young minds. By introducing diverse perspectives and powerful stories early on, we can help instil important morals and ideologies from a young age. So, here are some books we think are perfect to build a foundation for them to grow into thoughtful, informed individuals.

Marv Collection by Alex Falase-Koya

Let’s kick things off with the Marv Collection by Alex Falase-Koya—a fun, action-packed series that will have your little ones glued to the pages! Join Marv, a comic-loving ordinary boy, as he discovers a superhero suit that transforms him into the next big hero. Perfect for reluctant readers, this award-nominated series teaches resilience, kindness, and courage through exciting, two-colour illustrations.

Anna Hibiscus Series by Atinuke

Are your children accustomed to stories set in the West? It might be time to transport them to a different part of the world—Nigeria, to be precise—with the Anna Hibiscus series by Atinuke.

Join Anna as she splashes in the sea, prepares for exciting parties, sells oranges, and even dreams of tasting snow! Through Anna’s big family and her adventures, young readers will be introduced to a rich, vibrant life in Nigeria. This series is a must-read, offering a beautiful blend of African culture and universal childhood experiences.

By introducing your children to books like Anna Hibiscus, you’re expanding their reading horizons and opening their minds to different cultures and experiences. Diverse stories like these foster empathy and understanding, crucial for shaping thoughtful, well-rounded individuals from a young age.

Onyeka Series By Tolá Okogwu

Now, here’s another superhero you’ve all been waiting for! Tolá Okogwu's Onyeka series follows a Nigerian girl with extraordinary powers. These exciting tales are filled with courage, friendship, and the magic of African heritage. Okogwu herself describes it as Black Panther meets Percy Jackson, and we couldn’t agree more!

Encouraging teens to explore stories like Onyeka not only sparks their imaginations but also introduces them to cultural narratives and perspectives. By reading diverse stories, they’re developing an essential understanding of the world around them—beyond their immediate surroundings.

Older readers

Now that we've explored some fantastic stories for young readers, let’s move on to captivating books for teens and adults. These are packed with complexity, imagination, and themes that will challenge and inspire older readers.

The Legendborn Cycle By Tracy Deonn

Teens craving a blend of mystery, magic, and a bold protagonist will be captivated by the Legendborn Cycle by Tracy Deonn. Filled with secret societies and ancient legacies, this thrilling series is perfect for those ready to dive into a world where courage, identity, and magic collide.

Angie Thomas Collector's 2 Book Box Set (The Hate U Give & On the Come Up, Age 14+)

Angie Thomas transcends the typical themes found in young adult literature. She boldly tackles racism, privilege, police brutality, and other pressing societal issues.

Her debut novel, The Hate U Give, stands out for its powerful exploration of these topics, solidifying her as a literary icon. Following this triumph, Thomas released On the Come Up, the compelling story of a young aspiring rapper grappling with societal expectations and personal challenges in her quest for success.

Noughts & Crosses Collection (6 Book Set) by Malorie Blackman

For those who enjoy dystopian worlds, Malorie Blackman’s Noughts & Crosses series flips racial power structures on their head, creating a world where racial hierarchy is reversed. This gripping series explores themes of love, inequality, and resistance, making it essential reading for both teens and adults alike.

FictionAdults:

Lilith's Brood Trilogy by Octavia E. Butler

For adult readers seeking a captivating gift or indulgent read, look no further than Octavia E. Butler's Lilith's Brood Trilogy. This sci-fi masterpiece blends thought-provoking social commentary with alien encounters, delving deep into questions of identity, survival, and what it means to be human.

Candice Carty-Williams 3 Books Collection Set

Candice Carty-Williams, the author of the acclaimed Queenie, offers a brilliant collection of works that explore the complexity of modern life. With wit, charm, and honesty, her characters grapple with identity, love, and the often messy reality of relationships.

Percival Everett's Dr. No, The Trees & James: 3 Books Collection Set

Percival Everett’s novels challenge perceptions and dig into complex themes of race, justice, and human nature. With works like Dr. No, The Trees, and James, Everett's storytelling stretches the boundaries of traditional narratives, making his collection a must-read for lovers of thought-provoking fiction.

At Books2Door, we believe that representation in literature is crucial for shaping a more inclusive world. By celebrating Black authors and introducing readers to diverse voices, we help build a future where empathy, understanding, and creativity thrive. With our Celebrating Black Voices & Stories collection, you’ll find the strength, resilience, and creativity of Black authors on full display.

Don’t miss the chance to discover these powerful stories. Browse our Celebrating Black Voices collection today and add these must-reads to your bookshelf!

title: Celebrating Gay Voices
description:
From global favourites like Heartstopper by Alice Oseman to the heartfelt Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda by Becky Albertalli, these stories explore gay love, friendship, and identity with warmth and honesty.

For too long, gay characters were pushed to the margins. Today, literature offers authentic portrayals across age groups- stories filled with joy, resilience, humour, and vulnerability. This collection features romantic comedies, powerful coming-of-age narratives, fantastical adventures, and intimate portrayals of everyday life- all told through the lens of gay protagonists.

These characters are not side notes, they're complex, fully realised individuals navigating the world with courage and heart. Many of these books also embrace intersectionality, offering layered narratives that explore race, disability, faith, mental health, found family, activism, and more.

Whether you’re exploring your identity, supporting a loved one, or simply seeking meaningful stories, this collection offers a dynamic and affirming range of reads.

title: Celebrating Lesbian Voices
description:
At Books2Door, we believe in the power of stories to build empathy, foster visibility, and honour the diverse experiences within the LGBTQIA+ community. Our Celebrating Lesbian Voices collection highlights stories by and about lesbian characters and authors- stories rich in heart, resilience, and identity.

Lesbian representation in literature has come a long way- from coded subtext to unapologetically bold narratives. This collection spans genres and age ranges, reflecting the true depth of sapphic experiences. Whether you're looking for heartfelt coming-of-age tales, deeply romantic novels, or thoughtful reflections on identity, you’ll find stories that speak to all kinds of readers.

Expect themes of first love, chosen family, and the complexities of coming out, alongside vibrant celebrations of queer joy, self-expression, and love in all its forms. With inclusive titles across young adult fiction, adult novels, and children’s books, we aim to ensure every reader has access to stories that reflect the world they live in.

These books don’t just offer representation- they affirm, uplift, and inspire. Whether you’re a young person looking for mirrors in fiction, a parent or educator expanding your bookshelf, or simply someone who values diverse storytelling, this collection makes space for lesbian voices to be heard and celebrated.

title: Celebrating Non-binary Voices
description:
Non-binary people have always existed, but their voices remain underrepresented in mainstream literature. This collection seeks to change that.

Spanning fiction and non-fiction, these books centre stories beyond the binary—tales that are thoughtful, joyful, and real. From bold fantasy adventures to quiet coming-of-age journeys, graphic novels to educational resources, these books reflect the many ways non-binary people move through the world.

These aren’t just narratives about struggle or confusion. While some books do explore the challenges of identity and societal expectation, many others highlight themes of love, belonging, humour, and simply existing as whole, multidimensional people.

We’ve also included stories from neurodiverse and racially diverse non-binary authors and characters, to reflect the richness and variety of real-world experiences. Whether you’re exploring your identity or expanding your understanding, these stories offer affirmation, empathy, and inspiration.

title: Celebrating Racial Diversity and Inclusion
description:
This collection is made to celebrate racial diversity, the wide range of authors from different backgrounds we stock at Books2Door, and recommend some best-selling titles that feature diverse characters. Books that celebrate racial diversity and promote cultural inclusion are integral when it comes to the broader publishing industry as they help to introduce diversity within underrepresented cultures into children’s fiction. These writers present an intriguing look into the stereotypes existing in cultures that come from being from a minority background, offering a unique perspective into a lifestyle often different from ours. 

For some avid readers, being able to identify with characters from backgrounds like theirs is not only representative but also inclusive of the cultural differences celebrated within literature and children’s fiction. Books with diverse characters allow Black, Hispanic, Asian and Native students to see themselves and their experiences reflected by characters within the books. Similarly, for children of other backgrounds, these books allow an opportunity to learn about the practices and cultural beliefs of others worldwide. We have so many amazingly diverse books to choose from by so many brilliant authors! On this page, you can filter by author or age group by using the left-hand side to find the right collections to tailor the page to your own personal needs. It’s quick and easy to find the right books for your child.

For those little ones starting to read, why not introduce them to My Hair by Hanna Lee? This fun and vibrant book has a strong message about self-esteem and celebrates Black afro hair in all its glorious versatility! 

If you’re unsure where to start, why not try the Sam Wu 6 Books Collection Box Set by Katie and Kevin Tsang, perfect for ages 7-9? This series is inspired by Kevin and Katie’s aspiration to see more children’s books featuring children from Asian heritage backgrounds that are accessible and enjoyable to all children. Kevin’s own childhood experiences are told through Sam Wu’s adventures as he overcomes a new fear with the help of his family and friends by his side. This hilarious and fast-paced chapter book is filled with rib-tickling black and white illustrations alongside wacky plots, which are also ideal for reluctant readers who enjoy chapter plots and illustrated books. 

Another brilliantly diverse collection that highlights the individuality of other cultures is the Onjali Q. Raúf 4 Books set. This series features four outstanding books, including The Boy at the Back of the Class, The Day We Met the Queen, The Star Outside my Window and The Night Bus Hero. Her debut novel, The Boy at the Back of the Class, follows the story of nine-year-old Ahmet, who comes to a school as a refugee from Syria. This inspiring and sweet tale has an important message of not judging people before getting to know them. 

For some YA recommendations, why not have a look at some of the hit TikTok sensations, including the likes of To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before Series by Jenny Han, Crazy Rich Asians Trilogy by Kevin Kwan and the Noughts & Crosses 5 Book Collection set by Malorie Blackman.

title: Celebrating Trans Voices
description:
Celebrate transgender voices with books that centre real, affirming experiences across genres and age groups. From tender middle-grade reads to bold young adult novels and insightful adult memoirs, this collection honours the journey of discovery, courage, and transformation.

Trans characters are not defined solely by their transitions. These stories highlight full, complex lives, exploring love, friendship, activism, family, and identity in all its depth. Fiction and non-fiction alike offer insight into the joys and challenges of being seen and accepted.

Representation is especially vital for young readers. Seeing oneself reflected in a story can offer life-changing validation and clarity. For trans readers, these books affirm identity. For allies, educators, and families, they provide meaningful tools for understanding and support.

This collection also celebrates the diversity within the trans community, including trans men, trans women, non-binary individuals, and those who don’t fit into a single label. With characters of varying racial, cultural, and economic backgrounds, these stories reflect the full spectrum of trans experience.

title: Chainsaw Man Books
description:
Are you ready to embark on a thrilling journey into a world where Demons lurk in the shadows and a chainsaw-wielding hero is the last hope? Look no further than the Chainsaw Man series, now available in all its spine-chilling glory at Books2Door. Created by the talented manga artist Tatsuki Fujimoto, Chainsaw Man has taken the manga world by storm, captivating readers with its unique blend of horror, action, and dark humour.

Chainsaw Man: An Overview
In the Chainsaw Man series, you'll follow the adventures of Denji, a young man living a miserable life drowning in debt and struggling to make ends meet. But Denji's life takes a shocking turn when he merges with a Devil, granting him the powers of a Chainsaw. With a chainsaw blade for a head and the ability to regenerate, Denji is transformed into a weapon against the terrifying creatures known as Devils.

Tatsuki Fujimoto's storytelling is relentless and unapologetic, drawing readers into a world where the line between human and monster blurs. With relentless action scenes, unpredictable plot twists, and a cast of morally ambiguous characters, Chainsaw Man keeps you on the edge of your seat from the very first page. It's a rollercoaster ride through a nightmarish landscape, and you won't be able to put it down until you've devoured every thrilling chapter.

Chainsaw Man is more than just blood and guts; it delves into complex themes of identity, power, and the human condition. Fujimoto's masterful narrative invites readers to contemplate the price of survival in a world filled with supernatural horrors.

The entirety of Chainsaw Man Part 1 is available in a box set containing stunning artwork and volumes 1-11 of the series. You can also get the collection broken up into two sets, one containing volumes 1-5 and the other containing volumes 6-10. Finally, the volumes are also available to be bought individually.  

The Man Behind It All: Tatsuki Fujimoto
To fully appreciate the Chainsaw Man series, it's essential to understand the creative genius behind it – Tatsuki Fujimoto. Born in Shizuoka, Japan, in 1989, Fujimoto began his journey as a manga artist with a deep passion for storytelling. His early works showcased his unique style and knack for blending horror and comedy in an unsettling and entertaining way.

It was Chainsaw Man that truly catapulted him into the manga elite. His ability to take the supernatural and the absurd and weave them seamlessly into a gripping narrative is extraordinary. What sets Fujimoto apart is his willingness to tackle dark and challenging subject matter fearlessly. 

In Chainsaw Man, Tatsuki Fujimoto has created a manga series that is a testament to his incredible talent and dedication to his craft. His ability to craft compelling characters, build immersive worlds, and deliver gut-punching emotional moments has earned him a devoted fan base worldwide.

title: Champion’s Picks
description:
The Lionesses are Euros 2025 champions!

We’re celebrating their amazing win with a collection full of fun, sporty, and empowering reads for all ages. From football adventures to stories about confidence and teamwork, these books are perfect for young fans and future stars.

title: Chapter Books
description:
The Chapter Books Collection: Building Bridges to Independent Reading

The bridge between "read to me" and "I can read it myself" is built with a single, short chapter. The Chapter Books collection at Books2Door is specifically curated for the most critical milestone in a child's literacy journey. This is where "looking at pictures" evolves into "visualizing stories," as young readers develop the stamina to tackle multi-page narratives. Our selection moves beyond the basic sentence structures of early phonics, offering rich plots, relatable characters, and the addictive pull of a long-running series.

Whether your child is a fan of sparkling magic or mud-splattered mischief, these independent reading sets are designed to turn "I have to read" into "I can't put this down."

1. The Sparkle and the Shadow: Perfect First Series

At the beginning of the chapter book journey (typically ages 5–8), familiarity is the ultimate motivator. By offering complete series box sets, we ensure that once a child falls in love with a character, the next "win" is already waiting on the shelf.

  • Isadora Moon by Harriet Muncaster: Half fairy, half vampire, and totally unique. This series is a masterclass in "transitional" fiction, using striking pink-and-black illustrations to support the text, making it perfect for readers moving up from picture books.

  • Rainbow Magic by Daisy Meadows: With hundreds of fairies to discover, this series is the ultimate "stamina builder." The predictable yet enchanting structure allows children to master vocabulary through repetition while exploring a vast, interconnected world of magic.

2. Mischief and Mayhem: Engaging Reluctant Readers

For many children, the jump to chapter books feels like a chore. We dismantle that intimidation factor by championing "Funny Fiction"—books where the humor is high and the text is broken up by expressive, kinetic art.

  • Horrid Henry by Francesca Simon: Henry is the anti-hero every child understands. These short, punchy chapters are legendary for engaging boys and girls who prefer their stories with a side of rebellion.

  • Dirty Bertie by Alan MacDonald: As we’ve noted before, Bertie is the king of the "gross-out" chapter book. His antics are a primary gateway for reluctant readers, proving that reading can be just as chaotic as real life.

3. Visual Literacy: The Hybrid Chapter Book

The modern chapter book often blurs the line between a novel and a comic. For children in the 7–10 age bracket, these hybrid books are vital for developing "visual literacy"—the ability to decode meaning from both text and art simultaneously.

  • The Graphic Novel Influence: Series like Dog Man or The Bad Guys use heavy illustration and dialogue bubbles to keep the pace fast. This "hybrid" style reduces the cognitive load on the reader, allowing them to focus on the plot and humor without getting bogged down in dense paragraphs.

  • Topic Clusters: Our collection includes imprints from Oxford University Press and Usborne, ensuring that every set is pedagogically sound while remaining high-energy.

title: Charles Dickens Books
description:
Check out our fantastic range of Charles Dickens's books that capture the essence of his timeless literary genius. With his captivating storytelling and vivid characters, Dickens has cemented his place in literary history as one of the most influential and celebrated authors of all time. Immerse yourself in the enchanting world of Dickens as you explore our curated selection of his bestselling works.

For a classic gift set check out our fantastic Major Works of Charles Dickens 5 Books Box Set. This set contains A Christmas Carol, Great Expectations, A Tale of Two Cities, Hard Times and Oliver Twist. Making it an ideal gift for any bookworm or a treat for yourself if you’re wanting to explore the classics. 

Bestselling Books by Charles Dickens:

Step into the tumultuous era of the French Revolution through the pages of A Tale of Two Cities. This unforgettable tale weaves together the lives of characters from London and Paris, encompassing themes of love, sacrifice, and redemption. Dickens' evocative prose transports readers to a bygone era, capturing the spirit of the time and leaving an indelible impact on their hearts.

Embark on a journey of self-discovery with the young orphan Pip in Great Expectations. This masterful coming-of-age story explores themes of social class, identity, and ambition. Through Dickens' intricate plot twists and memorable characters like Miss Havisham and the enigmatic Magwitch, readers are taken on a rollercoaster of emotions that will leave them pondering the power of forgiveness and personal growth.

Delve into the dark underbelly of Victorian London as you follow the adventures of the orphaned Oliver Twist. From the merciless workhouses to the seedy criminal underworld, Dickens' vivid descriptions shed light on the harsh realities faced by the impoverished. This timeless tale of survival and justice remains a poignant critique of social inequality, making it an essential read for all.

Immerse yourself in the semi-autobiographical narrative of David Copperfield. Through the eyes of the titular character, readers witness a vivid panorama of Victorian England, where Dickens expertly intertwines themes of love, loss, and resilience. With an array of memorable characters, including the charming and eccentric Mr Micawber, this bildungsroman is hailed as one of Dickens' greatest achievements.

Experience the atmospheric and intricate world of Bleak House, where Dickens seamlessly intertwines multiple plotlines. From the never-ending legal case of Jarndyce and Jarndyce to the gripping mysteries surrounding Lady Dedlock, this novel is a scathing critique of the legal system and the social injustices prevalent in Victorian society. Through his keen observations and sharp wit, Dickens crafts a multi-layered narrative that captivates readers until the very last page.

For little bookworms, don’t forget to check out Sweet Cherry Publishing Easy Classics. In their Charles Dickens Easy Classics 10 Books Collection the classic stories are shortened and simplified with beautiful illustrations to break up the writing. This book set is ideal for Children aged 7-9 years who are confident independent readers. 

Biography of Charles Dickens:

Born on February 7, 1812, in Portsmouth, England, Charles Dickens was a literary prodigy whose works continue to resonate with readers worldwide. Coming from a modest background, Dickens' early experiences of poverty and hardship deeply influenced his writing and fostered his commitment to social reform.

His literary career began in 1836 with the serialisation of his first novel, The Pickwick Papers, which garnered widespread acclaim. This success was followed by a series of groundbreaking novels that solidified his reputation as a literary giant. Dickens' unique ability to create memorable characters, combined with his vivid descriptions of Victorian society, earned him a dedicated readership.

Beyond his literary accomplishments, Dickens was a passionate social advocate. His novels often exposed the harsh realities of life for the working class, shedding light on issues such as child labour, poverty, and inequality. His activism extended to public readings of his works, where he fervently championed social change.

Charles Dickens' impact on literature and society cannot be overstated. His works continue to be studied in schools and universities, and adaptations of his novels have graced both stage and screen. Dickens' legacy as a literary luminary endures, enchanting new generations of readers with his timeless tales and thought-provoking themes.

From his bestselling classics to lesser-known gems, each book offers a captivating glimpse into the extraordinary mind of one of history's greatest authors. Discover the enduring magic of Charles Dickens and let his words transport you to a world that will leave an indelible mark on your literary journey.

title: Children's Fiction & True Stories
description:
We cannot stress enough the importance of Children’s literature. Reading is an important aspect of every child’s life. Unfortunately for most tech-savvy children today, reading is limited to academics and educational books. We at Books2Door firmly believe that every child deserves access to books beyond just their academic curriculum. We want to ensure every child has the opportunity to enjoy great literature.

Fortunately, there is a wealth of children’s literature books available today for every age group. The list of popular children’s fiction books online and offline is rich with some brilliant titles and we believe every child deserves access to classic and contemporary children’s literature. Whilst there are several sub-genres when speaking of the types of children’s literature, children’s fiction we believe is the most popular; when trying to inculcate a love of reading in children.

Within children’s fiction, there is an extensive body of written works, written-accompanied by illustrations—produced to entertain and inform little readers. This genre encompasses everything; from picture books to classics like Alice in Wonderland, easy-to-read storybooks for young learners, fairy tales, fables, poetry, and more based on the child’s age group. Let’s take a look at some of the most popular children’s books that your kids cannot miss.

Some timeless children’s classics (fiction and true stories) that have enchanted generations and continue to remain hot favourites include; The Diary of a Young Girl by Anne Frank, Roald Dahl’s Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, A Bear called Paddington by Michael Bond, amongst several others. Children’s classics like these have accompanied several generations through their crucial teen years and growth journeys. 

Enid Blyton’s adventures like The Secret Seven and The Famous Five on the other hand have kept children aged 6 + entertained and hooked for generations (since the 1940s to be precise). The suspense, the disguises, the suspects, friendships and outdoor adventures that unfold in Blyton’s classic children’s books and mystery novels have managed to get several young readers hooked on children’s fiction.

Rudyard Kipling’s The Jungle Book is yet another popular Children’s book that has managed to stay etched into the hearts and minds of young readers through its most loveable characters—read, Mowgli, Baloo, and Bhageera. A tale of survival, friendships, and the triumph of good over evil; Jungle Book may have originally been written for children but the book has a major fan following amongst adults and has managed to bag several cinematic and live adaptations. Making it one of the most popular children’s storybooks ever.

The Diary of a Young Girl: by Anne Frank is arguably the most famous diary/memoir ever published. An account of a thirteen-year-old Jewish girl living under the Nazi regime; the book is a true story that has been discovered and rediscovered by several generations. This is a thought-provoking, moving insight into the world of a thirteen-year-old; surviving extraordinary conditions like hunger, the threat of being captured by the enemy, death, and worse (a life isolated from the real world). The book is a good read for children aged 14 and up.

It is known by all that reading has endless possibilities and benefits, it helps children develop essential reading skills and it helps adults develop important new skills which can be practically applied to day to day life. One of the key benefits of reading fiction books is that the talented authors of this genre have written detailed and creative storylines which introduce new concepts and circumstances that readers may not have thought about or experienced currently, these new suggestions could improve the social awareness of readers. Reading Fiction books can create empathy, you will have improved capacity to understand one another, and studies have suggested that reading Fiction can improve on the area of the brain which is responsible for understanding the world from new perspectives. A study has shown that reading is one of the most effective ways to beat stress, done by research at the University of Sussex. 

Reading Fiction may also serve as a way or technique to improve relationships in real life. You may think of reading as like a reality simulator, by reading Fiction books and its various situations in different scenarios, not only is it fun and expected for readers but readers may learn from how to deal with life's’ certain relational scenarios. Whether these are close relationships with family and friends or challenging relationships with strangers and new people, fiction titles can help us in these areas. Reading story books and fiction titles can even help readers open their minds as well as accept inclusivity for all people. Reading fiction starting from a young age will help kids develop new perspectives, empathy and acceptance of all people and from different backgrounds. In this exciting collection of books, we have Isadora Moon Puts on a Show, Isadora is special and unique from everyone else because her father is a vampire and her mother is a fairy. It is time for the vampire ball, a time for all vampire childrens to perform their vampire skills however Isadora is concerned she is unable to show off her vampire side in this show! This fun story is supported with amazing artwork in black and pink by the talented illustrator Harriet Muncaster. In this collection, we also have hundreds and hundreds of more lively titles! title: Children's Mental Health Books
description:
In today's fast-paced digital world, nurturing your child's mental well-being is more crucial than ever. Amidst this chaos, reading stands as a beacon of hope. By cultivating a positive mental space early on, children are primed for success and equipped with a healthy mindset to support them throughout their lives. Whether your little one is facing challenges or thriving, we're here for you every step of the way at Books2Door. Join us as we explore Mental Health for Children and how mindful reading can cultivate a positive mental space for them.

How can mindful reading cultivate a positive mental space for children and its benefits?

Mindful reading celebrates the joy of reading and introduces children to books that promote mindfulness, empathy, communication, self-esteem, and emotional well-being. It enhances emotional intelligence by helping children understand and manage their own emotions and those of others. It enriches vocabulary and communication skills, fostering better behaviour and stronger relationships. 

Additionally, reading improves focus and attention span, which is crucial in an age dominated by technology, and boosts self-esteem by encouraging independent reading. This practice also contributes to physical health, as positive emotions enhance the immune system and overall well-being, helping children mentally and physically thrive.

Here are some book recommendations to get started!

My First Books of Happiness 4 Books Collection Box Set by Patricia Hegarty

Crafted to inspire joy and positivity in your child, this collection of four enchanting books is perfect for laying the foundation of life's key concepts. With vibrant illustrations and short stories, this collection teaches valuable lessons in kindness, gratitude, mindfulness, and optimism. These engaging stories encompass fun storytelling, perfect for introducing key concepts to children aged 0-5. 

My Behaviour and Emotions Library By Jasmine Brooke 20 Books Collection Box Set

These 20 stories guide children through everything from jealousy to excitement, anxiety to bullying, and everything in between. With engaging characters and compelling tales, this collection teaches essential lessons in empathy, confidence, resilience, patience, and more. It's the perfect toolkit for helping children aged 3+ handle their emotions with fun and flair!

Mula and the Fly Series by Lauren Hoffmeier 3 Books Collection Set

With each delightful tale in this collection, your child will be guaranteed to embark on a journey filled with friendship, bravery, confidence and kindness. Perfect for children aged 4-6, this series encompasses yoga whilst tackling concepts such as making dreams come true, not worrying about what others think, and so much more.

The Good Thing About Bad Days

Packed with advice, activities, and uplifting messages helping your little one express and manage their feelings, this heartwarming and practical guide is perfect for children aged 5- 9. With a reassuring mantra that "The good thing about bad days is that they come to an end," this book empowers children to cope with tough situations and boost their self-esteem. Plus, with plenty of space for them to jot down their thoughts and doodle, it is a super interactive and engaging experience!

Judy Moody by Megan McDonald: Books 1-15 Box Set Collection

Bad moods, good moods, even back-to-school moods – Judy has them all! Introduce your children to Judy Moody, her little "bother" Stink, her best friend Rocky and her "pest" friend Frank Pearl. Judy has a mood for every occasion, and I'm sure she often struggles to handle them like all our children. Let your children join Judy in learning to control her moods and approach life's challenges positively. As this book encompasses Judy's life at school, this book is perfect for children aged 6-12.

Let us unlock the power of literature to shape our children's futures. Watch as our children's world becomes brighter with every turn of the page!

title: Children's, Teenage & Young Adult Poetry
description:
Reading to or with children is really important for their intellectual well-being. Children sometimes struggle with longer stories so introducing them to poems and nursery rhymes is a great way to encourage their love of reading early on. Poetry is also said to create pathways in children's brains that listening to other types of languages simply does not. With teens, poetry helps them process and express their conflicting emotions in a more controlled and creative way. 

In fact, exposing them to poems and rhymes can help children develop three really critical pre-reading and communication skills—phonological awareness, rich vocabulary and background knowledge. Not only can poems and rhyming words help a child develop a good vocabulary, it can also help your child develop phonological awareness. Phonological awareness is the ability to consciously tune in to the sounds of spoken language, to understand them and to talk about them. For example, a three-year-old whose phonological awareness is developing might say something like: "Hey, cat-bat: they sound the same!"

Background knowledge on the other hand is considered a strong predictor of how easily your child will learn to read and write. Several studies have confirmed that a child’s awareness and knowledge of their background will strongly impact their social and academic success. Teachers, speech-language therapists and linguists; unanimously agree that it is vital for babies and young children to hear the kind of language used in poems and rhymes. This is because the sometimes unusual words, repetitions and speech patterns contained in poems written for children help enrich your child's intellect.

Here are some poetry books that we think will move your child, stir something within them and whilst at it; also inculcate the love of poetry in their hearts. What Are Little Girls Made of? If you are a parent raising a feminist little girl, then this poetry book by Award-winning author, Jeanne Willis is just what she needs. Think you know your favourite classic nursery rhymes? Read this picture book and think again! In this witty reworking of popular nursery rhymes, Georgie Porgie doesn't dare to make the girls cry, Little Bo-Peep's sheep are all present and correct, thank you, and it's the queen, of course, who fixes Humpty Dumpty. With the combination of Jeanne Willis's brilliantly funny poems and Isabelle Follath’s charming, witty illustrations; these nursery rhymes prove that girls can be the heroes of any story. This remixed nursery rhyme collection is the perfect gift book for any child (or adult!), to read aloud or enjoy alone.

Hot Like Fire Bind-up by Valerie Bloom is a book of beautifully crafted poetry that covers a wide range of subjects from global pollution, maths homework problems to dealing with the death of a beloved pet. Full of sunshine and fire; Bloom’s poetry is fun and energetic with the mixed use of standard English and other dialects; that come together to make delightful poetry for kids.

title: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie Books
description:
Explore the importance of diverse narratives on our Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie collection page at Books2Door. Renowned for challenging the "single story" that simplifies complex characters into one-dimensional stereotypes, celebrated Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie champions a richer, more varied tapestry of human experiences. Discover her compelling works that encourage a broader worldview and deeper understanding.

Starting her journey with British children's books, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's early writings were shaped by characters and scenes far removed from her own reality in Nigeria. In her novel Purple Hibiscus, she delves into themes of identity and freedom, challenging her formative influences and inviting readers into more prosperous, resonant worlds.

The Impact of Single Stories on Identity and Perception

Witnessing the dangers of a narrowed perspective, Adichie addresses the misrepresentation and marginalisation caused by singular narratives in her book, The Thing Around Your Neck. This collection of stories brings to life the varied experiences of Nigerians navigating their identities across different contexts, urging a reconsideration of the stories we tell and hear.

Embracing Authenticity Through Diverse Narratives

Adichie's pivotal encounter with Nigerian literature broadened her narrative scope, inspiring her to pen Half of a Yellow Sun. This novel profoundly examines the Nigerian-Biafran War, weaving personal and political narratives that challenge and engage readers globally.

Adichie encourages embracing a multitude of stories to avoid the pitfalls of stereotyping. Her novel Americanah serves as a manifesto for this belief, exploring themes of race, identity, and love across continents with depth and nuance.

Why Stories Matter

As Adichie and literary icon Chinua Achebe remind us, stories form the essence of human experience. Engaging with diverse narratives counters harmful stereotypes and fosters empathy and understanding. Dive into Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's world at Books2Door, featuring titles like We Should All Be Feminists and Notes on Grief, and expand your literary horizons while embracing the complexity of human stories.

Achebe, a pillar of modern African literature, deserves a showcase of nothing but his finest creations. Our collection offers a guided journey through his trilogy, inviting you to immerse yourself in the richness of his prose and the depth of his themes.

Things Fall Apart: This seminal work, the first in the trilogy, stands out for its compelling narrative and deep cultural insights. It keeps readers engaged to the very end. It sparks a keen interest in the unfolding generational stories in the following books. Achebe's deliberate use of language, which includes preserving indigenous expressions, brings readers close to the narrative, enhancing the impact of his storytelling. 

The novel centres on Okonkwo, an Igbo community leader, as he contends with the clash between traditional African values and encroaching Western influences, offering a vital perspective on cultural resilience.

No Longer at Ease: Building on the success of its predecessor, this novel elevates Achebe's narrative art. We meet Obi Okonkwo, the grandson of Okonkwo, grappling with his identity amid the pressures of Western education and traditional values. This book explores the challenges faced by post-colonial African societies, with themes of identity, corruption, and moral complexity urging readers to ponder the nuanced realities of these communities.

Arrow of God: The final instalment of the Trilogy shifts focus to Ezeulu, a chief priest facing British administrative overreach into his community's cultural practices. Achebe wraps up his trilogy by showcasing the struggles of indigenous leaders to maintain artistic integrity and faith amidst external pressures.

Why Chinua Achebe Matters Today: 

Achebe's narratives are more than literary masterpieces; they serve as educational tools that foster a greater appreciation for diverse stories and authentic African history narrated by its people. His works counter the often one-dimensional portrayal of Africa, offering a vibrant, multi-dimensional tableau of African life.

At Books2Door, we proudly feature Achebe alongside other distinguished writers like Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, promoting a rich diversity of voices and perspectives in literature. Through our collection, we encourage readers to explore these essential perspectives and join us in learning, understanding, and appreciating the complexities of human experience through the potent words of these remarkable storytellers.

Embark on this literary journey with Books2Door to discover, dissect, and cherish the legacy of Chinua Achebe, whose works continue to inspire and educate today, tomorrow, and forever.

title: Chris Riddell Books
description:
Chris Riddell is the illustrator of many fabulous books, including the works of Neil Gaiman and multiple collections of poetry. He co-created The Edge Chronicles with Paul Stewart and is the author of Goth Girl and Ottoline. Alongside this, he’s the political cartoonist for The Observer. He’s won three Kate Greenaway Medals, three Nestlé Smarties Book Prizes, and was appointed as Children’s Laureate 2015-2017.

We have a great selection of Chris Riddell books in stock here at Books2Door. You may also be interested in other Children’s Laureates such as Quentin Blake, Julia Donaldson, and Jacqueline Wilson.

Biography

Chris Riddell was born in 1962 in Cape Town, South Africa, to a vicar and his wife. The family moved back to England when he was one. His mother used to give him a pen and paper to keep him occupied during his dad’s sermons, which eventually led to him studying illustration at Brighton Polytechnic. He was an illustrator for The Economist during the 80s and began working at The Observer in 1995. Riddell now lives in Brighton with his wife and children. He was awarded an OBE in 2019 to recognise his services to illustration and charity.

Best-Known Books

The Edge Chronicles was born from a map drawn by Chris Riddell in 1994. It depicted a fantasy world, all on the edge of a cliff. He challenged Paul Stewart to write a story about it, and four years later, Beyond the Deepwoods was published. The book turned into a trilogy, then a quintet, then a trilogy of trilogies. The series was concluded in 2009 with a supersized tenth book, The Immortals, set hundreds of years later. But the pair couldn’t resist making one final trilogy, which was published between 2014 and 2019, for a total of thirteen books. The first six books, now incorporating two World Book Day novellas initially published alongside the series, are available in The Edge Chronicles 6 Book Collection.

The Ottoline series follows Ottoline Brown, Mistress of Disguise, who lives with her hairy friend Mr Munroe in a city apartment. The pair love puzzles and mysteries and are attendants of the Brown family’s eclectic collections. Across the four-book series, they use their undercover detective skills to unmask the Yellow Cat, expose the ghost at the Alice B. Smith School for the Differently Gifted, get lost at sea, and go on a nighttime safari with a purple fox. These adventures are perfect for children between six and eight to read by themselves and are great bedtime stories for younger ones.

Ada Goth, the only lonely child of Lord Goth, lives in Ghastly-Gorm Hall. When William and Emily Cabbage and their ghostly mouse Ishmael come to stay, they begin to unravel gamekeeper Maltravers’ dastardly plot. So begins Chris Riddell’s Goth Girl and the Ghost of a Mouse, winner of the Costa Children’s Book Award. In the series that follows, Ada’s adventures take her to a Fete Worse Than Death, a Wuthering Fright at Lord Goth’s literary dog show, and a Sinister Symphony at Ghastly-Gorm Hall music festival.

title: Classic Children's Books
description:
Some classic children’s books are so memorable that they’ve lasted decades in the popular imagination, getting passed down from generation to generation and still being enjoyed by kids. In this collection, we’ve gathered together some children’s classic books that are still being read in bedrooms and classrooms up and down the country more than half a century from the day they came out. Our children’s classic book selection includes everything from timeless tales like The Very Hungry Caterpillar to modern classics like When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit.

Many children’s classic stories have been retold in simpler forms to help kids learn how to read. They’re often part of a reading scheme that develops your ability from phonics up to independent reading. An example of this is My First Reading Library from Usborne, which contains versions of Aesop’s Fables and nursery rhymes. These schemes lead to sets such as The Usborne Reading Collection for Confident Readers, which includes children’s versions of Robinson Crusoe and Frankenstein. Find more in our reading libraries collection.

Once your child’s a confident reader of classic fiction books, there’s nothing like the original versions of the text. The Puffin Classics Story Collection contains authoritative versions of ten essential children’s books. This instant library includes the magical Peter Pan, the lyrical The Wind in the Willows, the heartbreaking The Railway Children, and many more unbelievable novels. This great value box set makes a fantastic gift for any kid pushing on into broader reading.

Some classic children’s authors like Beatrix Potter and A.A. Milne have survived the test of time, with several books getting passed on to the next generation. However, few can rival Enid Blyton as one of the most popular children’s authors of all time. Her classic series like The Famous Five and The Secret Seven are still widely read today, and who could forget the iconic Noddy? We sell a wide range of Enid Blyton books, including complete series box sets like Malory Towers: 12 Book Collection. They’re perfect for your kid or a nostalgic trip down memory lane for yourself!

Colleen Hoover Books
description:
Colleen Hoover is an American author who has gained fame for her Romance and YA fiction. Before she was a bestselling author, Hoover worked as a social worker and a teacher. She has twenty-two published fiction books so far and has received numerous awards and accolades for her work. 

In 2021, Hoover experienced a lot of attention from TikTok for her 2016 book It Ends With Us. As a result, in January 2022, It Ends with Us was #1 on The New York Times best sellers list. The book follows Lily, who witnesses and experiences domestic violence as a child and then, as an adult, gets into a violent relationship herself. Hoover stated that it was based on her own life experiences and wrote the book to advocate for domestic violence victims and raise awareness of the subject. The sequel, It Starts With Us, is due to be released in October 2022, and a movie adaptation of It Ends With Us is currently being discussed. 

If you are just getting started with Colleen Hoover books, our Colleen Hoover 4 Book Collection Set is perfect. Whether it's a gift for a friend or a treat for yourself, this collection is an excellent addition to any bookshelf. The collection contains It Ends With Us, Verity, Ugly Love and November 9. For more of her standalone books, check out Reminders of Him, All Your Perfects, Without Merit, Regretting You and Confess. For the first instalment of the Maybe series, check out Maybe Someday. 

Hopeless Series 

The Hopeless Series follows seventeen-year-old Sky as she falls for a guy she knows is wrong for her. As the truth about his past starts to unravel, both Sky and Dean must begin to heal their emotional scars and find a way to live and love without boundaries. The series is targeted at Young Adults but has been very popular with adults. 

There are four books in this series: Hopeless, Losing Hope, Finding Cinderella and Finding Perfect. All are available to buy in our Hopeless Series Collection by Colleen Hoover. 

Slammed Series

The Slammed series is centred around eighteen-year-old Layken. After her father's death, her mother and little brother rely on her to hold them all together. When Layken meets Will, a handsome twenty-one-year-old who has a passion for poetry, her life is changed again. This series encapsulates the emotions and intensity of falling in love for the first time. 

Slammed is Hoover's debut novel, published in 2012; it has gone on to have global success. The second instalment, Point of Retreat, was also published in 2012, and the final book, This Girl, was published in 2013. For all three books together, check out our Slammed Series Three Book Boxset. 


Colleen Hoover's books are perfect for fans of Taylor Jenkins Reid, Jojo Moyes and Gillian Flynn. Perhaps you are a fan of Colleen Hoover and are looking for your next big read, then check out some of the above authors. Colleen Hoover gained popularity through Tiktok, for more books popular on Tiktok, check out our BookTok Made me Buy it collection.

Collins, a renowned publishing company with a rich history spanning over two centuries, has been committed to providing high-quality educational materials and literary works since its inception. The roots of Collins can be traced back to 1819 when printer William Collins established a printing and publishing business in Glasgow, Scotland. The company flourished and grew over the years, becoming a household name for its commitment to excellence in publishing.

In 1990, Collins merged with Harper & Row, an American publishing company, forming HarperCollins Publishers. This collaboration brought together the strengths and expertise of both companies, establishing HarperCollins as one of the world's largest and most respected publishers. Today, the Collins imprint remains an integral part of HarperCollins, continuing its legacy of producing outstanding books that inspire and educate.

At Books2Door, we are thrilled to offer a collection of Colson Whitehead's modern and contemporary works, which focus on American society, history, and the human condition. We believe Whitehead's contribution through his series of novels has significantly impacted storytelling today, and we eagerly invite our beloved readers to immerse themselves in his narratives. 

His works shed light on contemporary issues such as race, identity, and social justice. This establishes them as exceptional literary works and as profoundly resonant readings that echo the complexities of our times.

Celebrating Colson Whitehead's Literary Journey

Whitehead's language shines through his body of work, from the vivid landscapes of The Underground Railroad to the Fun towns in The Nickel Boys. His unparalleled ability to blend complex narratives with historical depth and imaginative flair makes his books essential studies of past and contemporary issues.

The Underground Railroad, with its innovative reimagining of the historical escape network as a literal railroad, has not only elevated Whitehead to new fame but also secured a spot in Oprah's Book Club, reflecting its broad acclaim and influence. Equally, The Nickel Boys tackles the grim realities of a reform school in Jim Crow-era Florida, shedding light on systemic injustices that echo through time.

Accolades and Digital Engagement

The multiple Pulitzer Prizes awarded to Whitehead for The Underground Railroad and The Nickel Boys underscore the significance of his times: freedom, oppression, and justice. These accolades affirm the powerful impact of his work.

In today's digital era, Whitehead's significance extends beyond the classic. His thought-provoking narratives have ignited discussions across social media, book clubs, and academic forums, broadening his reach and opening new avenues for exploring his central themes.

Discover Colson Whitehead's World with Books2Door

We invite you to join us as we explore the worlds crafted by Colson Whitehead, an author whose stories enlighten and inspire and help you navigate life with a profound understanding of society.
