title: Cormac McCarthy Books
description:
This page is dedicated to the brilliant works of Cormac McCarthy. Here, we present an exquisite collection of his masterpieces that have captivated readers with their immersive narratives, profound themes, and mesmerising prose. Discover the following books and delve deep into the extraordinary literary world crafted by McCarthy. 

A fantastic gift idea for a fan of McCarthy’s work would be Cormac McCarthy 3 Books Collection Set (The Road, Blood Meridian & No Country for Old Men). All three of these novels are a tour de force in modern American literature. Whether it’s a gift or maybe you're looking to broaden your literary horizon, this is the perfect way to introduce these American classics. 

The Road takes us on a harrowing journey through a post-apocalyptic landscape, where a nameless father and his young son struggle to survive amidst the remnants of a devastated world. McCarthy's haunting prose paints a bleak yet poignant picture of humanity's resilience in the face of despair. As they navigate the barren and dangerous terrain, the father and son grapple with existential questions, moral choices, and the unbreakable bond between them. This profoundly moving tale explores themes of love, hope, and the inherent goodness that can survive even in the darkest of times.

Blood Meridian transports us to the American West of the mid-1800s, where violence, savagery, and the relentless pursuit of power prevail. Through the eyes of a young runaway known only as "the kid," we are thrust into a merciless world of lawlessness, inhabited by a band of ruthless outlaws led by the enigmatic and malevolent Judge Holden. McCarthy's vivid and unflinching prose vividly captures the brutality and rawness of the era, while delving into profound questions about the nature of evil, the human capacity for violence, and the thin line that separates civilization from savagery.

Set against the backdrop of the Texan desert, No Country for Old Men unravels a suspenseful tale of greed, fate, and moral dilemmas. When Llewelyn Moss stumbles upon a drug deal gone wrong and discovers a briefcase filled with money, he becomes entangled in a deadly cat-and-mouse game with the relentless and psychopathic hitman, Anton Chigurh. McCarthy's masterful storytelling builds tension with every page, exploring themes of chance, consequence, and the frailty of human existence. With its terse dialogue, memorable characters, and philosophical undertones, this novel offers a gripping exploration of morality and the consequences of our actions. You may have seen the gripping 2007 movie adaption starring Javier Bardem and Tommy Lee Jones. 

Another fantastic book set is The Border Trilogy Series by Cormac McCarthy: 3 Books Collection Set. McCarthy's Border Trilogy is a literary triumph, comprising three interconnected novels that celebrate the vastness of the American Southwest while exploring themes of identity, love, and the clash of cultures.

In the first instalment of the trilogy, All the Pretty Horses, we embark on a coming-of-age journey with John Grady Cole, a young Texan whose restless spirit leads him to seek adventure and a connection to the disappearing cowboy way of life. As he travels to Mexico with his best friend, Lacey Rawlins, and encounters danger, romance, and betrayal, McCarthy's evocative prose vividly captures the allure and hardships of the cowboy ethos.

Continuing the saga, The Crossing introduces us to Billy Parham, a teenager who sets out on a transformative quest to return a stolen wolf to its native Mexican mountains. Along the way, he encounters trials, loss, and encounters with both human and natural forces that shape his understanding of the world. McCarthy's poetic language and introspective exploration of nature, solitude, and the human spirit make this novel a profound and meditative experience.

In the final chapter of the trilogy, Cities of the Plain, McCarthy reunites two protagonists from the previous novels, John Grady Cole and Billy Parham, as they work on a ranch near the U.S.-Mexico border. As their lives intertwine and they confront love, loyalty, and the passage of time, McCarthy's lyrical prose captures the beauty and harshness of the land, painting a poignant portrait of friendship and the end of an era.

These exemplary books by Cormac McCarthy, showcased on our webpage, offer readers a profound literary journey. Immerse yourself in McCarthy's unparalleled storytelling, and be prepared to be moved, challenged, and forever changed by his extraordinary works.

About the Author: 

Cormac McCarthy, an esteemed American author, is widely regarded as one of the most significant literary voices of our time. Born Charles McCarthy Jr. on July 20, 1933, in Providence, Rhode Island, McCarthy's writing career spans several decades and encompasses a diverse range of themes, styles, and settings. Renowned for his distinctive prose, powerful storytelling, and philosophical depth, McCarthy has left an indelible mark on the literary landscape.

McCarthy's early works, such as The Orchard Keeper (1965) and Outer Dark (1968), established his reputation as a formidable writer with a penchant for exploring the dark corners of human existence. However, it was his novel "Blood Meridian" (1985) that catapulted him to international acclaim. Set against the backdrop of the American West, Blood Meridian delves into the themes of violence, morality, and the human capacity for savagery. McCarthy's evocative descriptions and unflinching portrayal of the harsh landscapes and brutal characters make the novel a haunting and challenging read.

In 1992, McCarthy published All the Pretty Horses, the first volume of his Border Trilogy. This epic tale follows the journey of John Grady Cole, a young Texan cowboy, as he seeks adventure and meaning in the changing American Southwest. The trilogy, which also includes The Crossing (1994) and Cities of the Plain (1998), showcases McCarthy's lyrical prose, deep exploration of human nature, and his ability to weave intricate narratives that span generations.

Perhaps McCarthy's most widely known work is The Road (2006), a post-apocalyptic novel that tells the story of a father and son struggling to survive in a devastated world. This hauntingly beautiful tale explores themes of love, resilience, and the human spirit's will to endure while examining the depths of despair and the search for hope in a bleak landscape.

Throughout his career, McCarthy has received numerous accolades, including the National Book Award for Fiction and the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novel "The Road." His contributions to literature have earned him a devoted readership and critical acclaim.

Cormac McCarthy's writings are characterised by their poetic language, profound philosophical reflections, and unflinching exploration of the human condition. His works resonate with readers on a deep level, challenging them to confront the complexities of existence and the choices that shape our lives. McCarthy's ability to craft powerful narratives that transcend time and place solidifies his status as an iconic figure in American literature.

description:
Cressida Cowell is an author, illustrator, and the current Children’s Laureate. She’s most famous for writing the How to Train Your Dragon series, which has since been adapted into blockbuster movies and TV shows. Her latest series is The Wizards of Once, and she’s also written the Emily Brown series for younger children. Cressida Cowell’s books are perfect for children with a wild imagination, who love fantasy, and want to get stuck into a whole series of books. Find our selection of her books here at Books2Door, and check out the other Children’s Laureates like Chris Riddell, Jacqueline Wilson, and Quentin Blake.

Biography

Cressida Hare was born in London in 1966, the daughter of Michael Hare, 2nd Viscount Blakenham. Her brother Caspar, 3rd Viscount Blakenham, is second in line to be Earl of Listowel. She grew up between London and Little Colonsay, an uninhabited island in the Scottish Hebrides. Her time on the island was the inspiration for How to Train Your Dragon. 

Cressida studied English at Oxford University and Illustration at Brighton University and Saint Martin’s School of Art. She lives in London with her husband Simon, former director and CEO of Save the Children Internation, and has three children. She wrote and illustrated her first picture book in 1998, and her first novel in 2003.

Cressida has won the Nestle Smarties Children’s Book Prize and the Blue Peter Book Award. She was appointed Children’s Laureate in 2019, and her two-year tenure was extended to 2022 due to COVID-19. She was appointed MBE in 2020 for services to children’s literature and elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in 2021.

Best-Known Books

How to Train Your Dragon is best known as an animated film trilogy from DreamWorks, complete with merchandising and multiple spin-off TV series. However, it all began with a 2003 book by Cressida Cowell. The series follows Hiccup Horrendous Haddock The Third, one of the only people ever who can speak and understand the language of the dragons. Across the twelve book series, Hiccup and his friends Toothless the dragon and Fishlegs navigate the unstable relationship between Vikings and dragons.

The Wizards of Once follows Wizard boy Xar, who sets out to steal a witch’s magic because his own never arrived. Instead, he captures a Warrior girl called Wish. Although they’ve been taught to hate each other, the two must team up to defeat the evil queen. This series is a must for all fantasy fans, and the whole series is available in The Wizards of Once 4 Book Collection.

The Emily Brown series of picture books are illustrated by Neal Layton. They’re about Emily and her adventures with her toy rabbit Stanley. There are five books in the award-winning series, published between 2006 and 2018. Emily meets the Queen, Father Christmas, an unhappy teddy bear, a Thing, and Matilda the Elephant. These charming tales are perfect bedtime stories for 0-5-year-olds and are available in a great five book bundle.

Danny, our super-inventor, joined by his best buddy Percy is going to join the SCOUTS (SCOUTS stands for Spy Club Only for Ultra-Terrific Spies). Together they are faced with the prospect of a perilous camping trip to sunny Scotland and while at it, Danny and Percy want to build the coolest super-sonic submarine ever! Will they make it to the camping trip? Will they build the submarine? The book only gets more interesting as the adventure unfolds.

The Jet of Justice, is a hot favourite Danny Dingle book as it takes the young readers through the excitement of heading off to a summer camp. It’s finally time for the summer holidays and Danny Dingle can now be a full-time super-inventor! He no longer has to deal with boring schoolwork. Instead, Danny and Percy have a sci-fi convention and a flying machine competition on the horizon. The mission is to get noticed by Metal Face but mum is plotting against all the fun! The immersive storytelling and creatively written characters, the visual explanation, and the suspense all make it one of the best books in the series. 

The Farts of Gratitude is yet another book in the series that will manage to tickle young readers whilst also keeping them engaged through the book. In Farts of Gratitude, Danny Dingle is seen trying to hide a super-secret spy operation whilst trying to use his boring family holiday as a cover. Amidst all that, Metal Face has a super-cool new band called G.A.G, and Danny and Percy now want to copy their idol and make some noise themselves. Together, the duo wants to put up a show of a lifetime but will they win the school’s Battle of the Bands?

title: Daphne Du Maurier
description:
Daphne Du Maurier, an iconic British author, captivated readers around the world with her mesmerising storytelling and unparalleled ability to weave tales of suspense, romance, and psychological intrigue. Born on May 13, 1907, in London, Du Maurier hailed from a talented artistic family, with her father, Sir Gerald Du Maurier, being a renowned actor and her grandfather, George Du Maurier, a celebrated author and cartoonist.

From an early age, Du Maurier demonstrated an extraordinary talent for writing, which she nurtured and honed throughout her life. Her novels transcended genres, delving into the depths of human emotions and exploring the darkest corners of the human psyche. With her keen eye for detail and the ability to create atmospheric settings, Du Maurier's works continue to leave an indelible mark on the literary world.

Rebecca

Rebecca, a timeless classic, remains one of Du Maurier's most celebrated and beloved works. Published in 1938, this haunting tale of love, jealousy, and secrets enthrals readers to this day. Set against the backdrop of a grand estate called Manderley, the story follows an unnamed narrator who marries the enigmatic widower Maxim de Winter. But as the new mistress of Manderley, she finds herself haunted by the pervasive presence of Rebecca, Maxim's deceased first wife. With its haunting atmosphere and unforgettable characters, Rebecca is a mesmerising exploration of power, identity, and the enduring power of love.

Rebecca has been adapted into numerous films and TV shows. Most famously is the 1940s film starring Joan Fontaine and Laurence Olivier directed by Alfred Hitchcock. Rebecca was also adapted into a Netflix movie starring Lily James and Armie Hammer in 2020. Check out our As Seen on Screen page for more Netflix adaptations and so much more. 

Jamaica Inn

Immerse yourself in the dark and mysterious world of Jamaica Inn, a gripping tale of adventure and suspense. Set in the desolate moors of Cornwall, this novel takes readers on a thrilling journey into the heart of darkness. Young Mary Yellan finds herself in a web of deceit and treachery when she arrives at Jamaica Inn to live with her aunt and uncle. As she uncovers the inn's grim secrets, she becomes entangled with a band of smugglers and faces grave danger. Jamaica Inn showcases Du Maurier's unparalleled ability to create an eerie and atmospheric setting that adds depth to the already riveting plot.

You can visit the real Jamaica Inn in Cornwall and step into the history of this world-famous smugglers inn. A film adaptation of the novel was produced in 1939, directed by Alfred Hitchcock, and starring Charles Laughton and Maureen O'Hara. As well as the film adaptations, there have been numerous TV and radio adaptations of Jamacia Inn. 

My Cousin Rachel

In the novel My Cousin Rachel, Du Maurier once again demonstrates her mastery of psychological suspense. The story revolves around Philip Ashley, a young Englishman who is haunted by the memory of his cousin Ambrose's mysterious death. When Ambrose's widow, the beguiling Rachel, arrives at the family estate in Cornwall, Philip is both fascinated and suspicious of her intentions. As their relationship unfolds, Philip is drawn into a web of desire, manipulation, and uncertainty. My Cousin Rachel is a gripping exploration of obsession, trust, and the complexities of human nature.

My Cousin Rachel was adapted into a movie in 2017 starring Rachel Weisz and Sam Claflin. The first adaptation was released in 1952 and starred Richard Burton and Olivia de Havilland. 

Each of these literary gems showcases Du Maurier's ability to transport readers to vivid and atmospheric settings while delving into the depths of human emotions and motivations. Her stories continue to resonate with readers of all generations, standing the test of time and solidifying her status as one of the most influential writers of the 20th century.

Indulge yourself in the spellbinding worlds created by Daphne Du Maurier, and experience the magic that has captivated readers for decades. With her timeless storytelling and remarkable characters, these books are sure to enthral and leave an indelible mark on your literary journey. Step into the mysteries of Rebecca, the secrets of Jamaica Inn, and the enigmatic My Cousin Rachel, and discover the brilliance of Daphne Du Maurier's unparalleled literary genius.

What is Dark Academia?

The subculture of dark academia is concerned with the arts, classic greek and gothic architecture, and the prominence of knowledge and education. In literature, Dark Academic Books are most recognisable for their particularly dark and heavy themes of existentialism and death against a mystery and thrilling academic setting. These books are often classed as moody and mysterious, with narratives taking place within the confines of an esteemed boarding school or university. For more information on Dark Academia books check out our blog post: The Allure of Dark Academia: A Curated List of 10 Must-Read Books.

Dark Academia Books Recommendations

Considered one of the most definitive dark academic novels, Donna Tartt’s The Secret History has been described as compelling and elegant, dramatic and playful. This murder mystery novel follows the perspective of Richard Papen, who studies literature at the elite Hampden College in Vermont. Under the influence of their charismatic classics professor, Richard and five other eccentric misfits discover a new way of thinking that goes against their mundane existence leading them to corruption, betrayal and evil. The Secret History is a story of two parts; the chain of events that led to the death of a classmate- and what happens next. 

Our next recommendation is a more subtle Dark Academia book but nonetheless should not be left out of our list. Published in 2005, Kazuo Ishiguro’s Never Let Me Go is set in a darkly dystopic version of contemporary England. The book follows Kathy’s perspective as she attempts to come to terms with her childhood and upbringing and towards a bleak fate that awaits her and her closest friends. Ishiguro masterfully presents the fragility of life, identity, empathy and friendship in this novel against the prominence of boarding schools harbouring dark secrets. Time named it the best novel of 2005 and one of the top 100 novels published since 1923. The book has also been adapted into the 2010 film of the same name, directed by Mark Romanek and starring Cary Milligan, Andrew Garfield and Keira Knightley. 

No Dark Academia list would be complete without mentioning Ninth House by Leigh Bardugo. From the author of the Shadow and Bone series, this book has become a TikTok sensation. This paranormal fantasy series follows Galaxy “Alex” Stern, who is the sole survivor of a horrific, unsolved homicide. At her hospital bed, she is offered a second chance: to attend one of the world’s most elite universities. But what’s the catch, and why her? As Alex struggles to search for answers to these questions herself, she arrives in New Haven, tasked by her mysterious benefactors with monitoring the activities of Yale’s secret societies- whose occult activities turn out to be rather more sinister than any imagination might conceive.

title: Darren Shan Books
description:
Watch out readers, these books are not for the faint-hearted…Find true horror in our collection of box sets from bestselling young adult horror writer Darren Shan. He is best known for his young adult fiction series with works such as The Cirque Du Freak, The Demonata and Zom-B.

With each series in a convenient and affordable box set, this collection would make the perfect gift for any young horror fan. Whether it’s freaky zombies, creepy vampires or devilish demons, Darren Shan’s books are guaranteed to keep your children both spooked and entertained for hours on end.

Best-Known Books:

The Cirque Du Freak: The Saga of Darren Shan series is a twelve-part book collection about the titular character’s experiences of being transformed into a half-human half-vampire whilst trying to save his best friend, Steve. As the story progresses, the reader will identify Shan’s ordeals whilst dealing with being part vampire and how he adapts to his newfound life-changing powers. The vampires are much stronger than the average human, running at speeds too fast for normal people to see. With super senses being able to see in the dark and track scents like a predator, Shan must adapt to his powers quickly…

In 2009 the series was brought to life in the movie Cirque du Freak: The Vampire's Assistant. The book has been published in 33 countries around the world, in 30 different languages. Described as “Stephen King for kids”, the Cirque Du Freak Saga is sure to be a hit with horror fanatics. This horrifying collection is aimed at children aged 9+.

If spooky vampires don’t scare you enough, try The Demonata series, perfect for young adults. The three protagonists, Grubbs Grady, Kernel Fleck and Bec MacConn, each from different time periods throughout human history, must delve into the frightening world of demons. They must each fight the demon master Lord Loss and his many familiars who promise to destroy the human universe and even to stop death. In this graphically violent saga, the trio must come together to attempt to defeat Demonata and his plans of destroying the world.

For those zombie lovers, the Zom-B series will definitely give you a good scare. The master of horror spins another frightful tale in this series, narrative in the first-person perspective of “Becky “B” Smith, a teenager turned Zombie. Eighteen months after rejecting her racist father, B wakes up as a zombie and must explore this new world amidst the ongoing battle between Dr Oystein and his Angels and Mr Dowling and his mutant-controlled zombies.

This book is aimed at older readers aged 13+, with the series dealing with themes of racism and opposing beliefs.

About the Author:

Darren O'Shaughnessy is an Irish writer and young adult novelist born on 2 July 1972. His works have been published under a variety of pen names including Darren Shan, D. B. Shan and Darren Dash. His most popular works surround the fantastical and the horror, the perfect collection of books for older readers looking for spooky fast-paced and action-packed thrillers combined with spooky vampires or killer zombies.

title: Dav Pilkey Books
description:
Dav Pilkey is an American author, illustrator and cartoonist that is behind some of the most well-known children's book series, Captain Underpants and Dog-Man. Pilkey was diagnosed with ADHD and dyslexia and often would disrupt the classroom, resulting in him being sent out of class a lot. During these times, he would often write stories or draw cartoons for his own entertainment. Pilkey has channelled his vivid imagination with creative storytelling to create some of the most beloved characters in children's literature. 

Pilkey's books provide humour with the overall kind-hearted nature of humanity. His books are designed to be easy to read and follow whilst keeping children entertained throughout. The books encourage children to use their imagination and unlock their own creative potential, as well as encourage them to read in their spare time. 

Captain Underpants Books

Since the first book was published in 1997, Captain Underpants has gone on to be an international bestseller and has been translated into over twenty languages. The success of the series may be down to the relatability of the two main characters, best friends Harold and George. The two boys are fourth graders, 9-10-year-olds, from Ohio who create an underpants-wearing superhero out of their mean school principal. 

There are a total of twelve books in the series, as well as additional activity books and spin-offs. Captain Underpants books are aimed at readers aged 7+. However, they continue to be enjoyed by children of all ages. For a bumper box set of Captain Underpants books, check out our Captain Underpants 10 Book Set. This set contains ten books and jam-packed full of comic strips, toilet humour and fun. 

The award-winning series was even made into a movie called Captain Underpants: The First Epic Movie. The film was released in 2017 and starred Kevin Hart, Ed Helms and Jordan Peele. 

Dog-Man Graphic Novels 

As well as the infamous Captain Underpants, Dav Pilkey is also responsible for creating Dog-Man, the crime-fighting policeman with a dog's head. The books continue with the adventures of George and Harold as they look back on an old comic strip they made together in Kindergarten and decide to continue the adventure. A great gift idea for fans of Dog-Man or Captain Underpants is our Dog Man 1-10: The Supa Buddies Mega Collection 10 Books Box Set. This set features some hilarious adventures, including Dog Man Unleashed, A Tale of Two Kitties, Grime and Punishment and Mothering Heights.

As of 2022, there are eleven Dog-Man comic books. There is also a spin-off series which features Cat-Kid, a character introduced in the main series. We have a selection available for Cat-Kid books, including Cat Kid Comic Club, Cat Kid Comic Club: Perspectives and Cat Kid Comic Club: On Purpose. 


Pilkey's books are great for fans of Diary of a Wimpy Kid, Big Nate and Roald Dahl's books. Ideally, the books are aimed at ages 7-9, but they are also enjoyed by children older and younger. For more for your mischievous little ones, check out our range of funny children's books.

title: David Baldacci Books
description:
The name David Baldacci is synonymous with riveting storytelling, intricately designed plots, and characters that linger in your thoughts long after you've turned the last page. Over the years, Baldacci has become one of the most respected and sought-after authors in the genres of thriller, mystery, and suspense. This collection of David Baldacci's works is a treasure trove of storytelling mastery, an essential compilation for devoted fans and newcomers alike. Here, in one comprehensive package, are the stories that have captivated millions, cementing Baldacci's reputation as a luminary in modern fiction.

For those new to the world of David Baldacci, each book serves as a gateway to a complex universe of political intrigue, legal drama, and human emotion. His books frequently explore the inner workings of the U.S. government, delving into the secretive realms of espionage, conspiracy theories, and the ethical grey zones that characters must navigate. With series like 'Camel Club,' 'King and Maxwell,' and 'Amos Decker,' Baldacci showcases his remarkable ability to sustain multifaceted story arcs that span multiple volumes without sacrificing the depth or integrity of individual titles.

About the King and Maxwell Series:

The "King and Maxwell" series by David Baldacci is a popular sequence of thriller novels featuring Sean King and Michelle Maxwell, two former Secret Service agents who turn into private investigators. Known for their sharp intellect, tactical skills, and unyielding commitment to solving complex cases, King and Maxwell make for a dynamic and compelling duo. The series combines elements of crime, mystery, suspense, and political intrigue, and it has garnered a large following due to its fast-paced storytelling, intricate plots, and well-developed characters.

Sean King is an ex-Secret Service agent who left the service under a cloud of controversy, leading him to start his own law practice. Michelle Maxwell, on the other hand, is a former elite athlete who also left the Secret Service under complicated circumstances. They both find a second chance at professional redemption when they form their private investigation firm. Together, they take on cases that often involve high stakes and dangerous players, from political scandals to international espionage.

King and Maxwell Books in order:

  • Split Second 
  • Hour Game
  • Simple Genius
  • First Family 
  • The Sixth Man
  • King and Maxwell

The King and Maxwell series has also been adapted into a television series, further extending its reach and popularity. However, fans of the books often find that the depth and intricacy of the original stories offer an experience that is hard to replicate in any other format. This series stands as an exemplar of modern thriller writing. The books are not just page-turners but also thought-provoking narratives that delve into the complexities of morality, duty and the human psyche. For anyone interested in suspenseful stories with intricate plots and multi-dimensional characters, this series is a must-read.

About the Author:

David Baldacci is an American author best known for his thriller and mystery novels. Born on August 5, 1960, in Richmond, Virginia, he has become one of the most popular and prolific writers in these genres, with numerous bestsellers to his name. Baldacci's books have been translated into more than 45 languages and sold in over 80 countries, with more than 130 million copies in print worldwide.

Beyond his work as a writer, Baldacci is involved in philanthropic activities, particularly in promoting literacy and fostering a love for reading. He and his wife, Michelle, have founded the Wish You Well Foundation, an organisation that supports family and adult literacy programs in the United States.

Baldacci is known for his meticulous research, which lends authenticity to his narratives. He frequently consults with experts in various fields, including law enforcement and the military, to ensure the accuracy of the technical and procedural aspects of his stories. This attention to detail has been one of the hallmarks of his writing, adding a layer of realism to his intricate and suspense-filled plots.

title: David Litchfield
description:
David Litchfield, author of some highly acclaimed children’s literature, is an award winning writer and illustrator of picture books and novels, by himself and other authors. David loves to illustrate and has created art works for several fiction covers, non-fiction and full-colour picture books. His clients span across genres and publications including Francis Lincoln, Faber and Faber, Penguin Random House amongst many others. 

David’s love of illustrating and drawing dates back to when he was very young. He first started to draw when he was a child, creating Star Wars and Indiana Jones ‘mash up’ comics for his older brother and sister. Since then David’s work has appeared in several publications; magazines, newspapers, books and even on T-shirts. He has also exhibited his illustrations in both solo and group shows across the U.K, Europe and America.

Amongst his illustration gigs for other authors; David Litchfield has also managed to author bestselling children’s books of his own like The Bear & The Piano trilogy, Lights On Cotton Rock and Kid Christmas: Of The Claus Brothers Toyshop amongst others. Given his creativity, his imaginative art works and storytelling prowess; his books make engrossing reading material for children. 

Some of our favourite David Litchfield children’s books are part of this dedicated collection…

The Bear and the Piano by David Litchfield is the first book in the best-selling, award-winning 'Bear and the Piano' trilogy; the book has won several awards in the illustrated book category. The premise of the book being, a young bear who stumbles upon an instrument in the woods and teaches himself to play it. Eventually the beautiful music is heard by a father and son who are picnicking in the woods. The bear goes with them on an incredible journey to New York, where his piano playing makes him a huge star. He has fame, fortune and all the music in the world, but he misses the friends and family he has left behind. A moving tale of exploration and belonging from the best-selling and critically-acclaimed author David Litchfield; along with his breath-taking and stunning illustrations of the forest and the New York skyline—together make this book a rich experience for young readers (aged between 5-7). 

Centred around Heather, a little girl who wants to go to Outer Space, where the stars sparkle with magic and wonder—Lights on Cotton Rock is an out-of-this-world picture book by David Litchfield. A magical, heartwarming story told through stunning illustrations with a powerful message; this is just the book you want to get your little one to enjoy and learn from. When a spaceship lands at Cotton Rock, it seems that all of Heather’s dreams have come true. But soon the alien has to leave. Will the spaceship ever come back? And if it does, is Heather ready to leave everything on Earth behind? This beautiful story (for children between the age of 4 to 7) about family and dreams, travels through space and time to show us that what we are looking for might be closer than we think. 

Grandad's Secret Giant by David Litchfield is a funny, touching and visually stunning storybook that will teach your child valuable lessons whilst also making for a great storytime. "He has hands the size of tables," Grandad said, "legs as long as drainpipes and feet as big as rowing boats. Do you know who I mean?" "Yes," sighed Billy. "The Secret Giant. But he's not real!" Billy doesn't believe his Grandad when he tells him there's a giant living in his town, doing good deeds for everyone. He knows that a giant is too big to keep himself hidden. And why would he want to keep himself a secret? But as time goes on, Billy learns that some secrets are too BIG to stay secret for long... This delightful heartfelt story of belonging and friendship teaches the importance of tolerance and acceptance to young children (aged between 5 -7).

title: David Walliams Books
description:
Welcome to the world of David Walliams.

Join us at Books2Door as we explore the fantastic collection of books by David Walliams. Born in Wimbledon, London, in 1971, Walliams gained popularity as a comedian, writer, and television personality. However, he is best known for his bestselling children's books. Since his first publication in 2008, he has sold over 35 million books worldwide, and his works have been translated into more than 50 languages. David Walliams and his books have taken the children's literary world by storm, often holding the number one spot for weeks. Some of his books have even won the National Book Awards - Children's Book of the Year category.

At Books2Door, we strive to ensure you and your little ones have the best books delivered to your doorstep. David Walliams' books are a fantastic choice. His works are among the best and will leave your children in awe. His beloved children's comedy fiction not only entertains but also imparts valuable life lessons in an engaging and accessible way. His books have been bringing light and laughter to children worldwide for over two decades. Written for children aged 7 to 14, his fantasy fiction books are a great way to build up your child's library.

David Walliams has published over thirty children's novels, picture books, and short story collections. His books have been widely adapted for television, often airing during the prestigious Christmas primetime slots. His novels have also been made into plays, musicals, and even a ride at Alton Towers, making them even more appealing to children who recognise the characters.

Not sure where to start? We're here to help!

Walliams published his first trendy book, The Boy in the Dress, in 2008, marking the beginning of his literary success. title: Death Note Manga
description:
About the Series:

Death Note follows the extraordinary story of Light Yagami, a brilliant high school student who stumbles upon a supernatural tool capable of shaping the fate of mankind. When Light discovers the Death Note, a mysterious notebook that grants its owner the power to kill anyone by writing their name within its pages, he becomes consumed by a godlike desire to rid the world of evil.

Driven by an unwavering belief in his own sense of justice, Light embarks on a dangerous path, adopting the moniker "Kira" to strike fear into the hearts of criminals. As his reign of terror unfolds, the world becomes divided between those who worship Kira as a righteous deity and those who see him as an unforgivable murderer.

However, Light's actions do not go unnoticed. Enter L, an enigmatic and eccentric detective whose extraordinary intellect poses a formidable challenge to Kira's reign. A deadly game of cat and mouse ensues as L relentlessly pursues the truth behind Kira's identity, leading to a battle of wits that pushes both men to their limits.

At its core, Death Note examines the dark underbelly of humanity, exploring themes of justice, morality, and the abuse of power. As Light grapples with the immense power he wields, the series forces readers to confront complex questions about the nature of right and wrong. Is it justified to kill criminals in the name of justice? Where do we draw the line between vengeance and the pursuit of a better world? The series challenges readers to examine their own values and confront the consequences of their actions.

One of the greatest strengths of Death Note lies in its complex and multifaceted characters. Light Yagami's transformation from an idealistic young man to a power-hungry megalomaniac is a fascinating exploration of the human psyche. L, with his enigmatic persona and unorthodox investigative techniques, captivates readers as he matches wits with Light, showcasing the lengths one can go to unravel the truth.

Secondary characters such as Misa Amane, a devoted follower of Kira, and Ryuk, the shinigami who owns the Death Note, add further depth and complexity to the narrative, providing unique perspectives on the events unfolding around them.

The Death Note  Manga Series is that it offers an enthralling reading experience, drawing readers into a world where morality blurs and the pursuit of justice takes on a twisted form. With its compelling narrative, intricate artwork, and thought-provoking themes, this manga series is a must-read for fans of psychological thrillers, crime dramas, and captivating storytelling. Step into the world of Death Note, and prepare to question your own sense of justice and the consequences of playing with powers beyond our understanding.

title: Demon Slayer Books
description:
Dive into the World of Demons with Demon Slayer
Demon Slayer, known as Kimetsu no Yaiba in Japanese, is an enthralling manga series that combines action, fantasy, and heart-wrenching drama. The story is set in Taisho-era Japan and follows the life of Tanjiro Kamado, a young and kind-hearted boy who becomes a demon slayer after a tragic encounter leaves his family slaughtered and his sister, Nezuko, turned into a demon.

Determined to avenge his family and find a cure for Nezuko's condition, Tanjiro joins the Demon Slayer Corps, an organisation dedicated to eradicating demons and protecting humanity. The series chronicles his journey as he trains to become a formidable swordsman, battles terrifying demons, and uncovers the mysteries of his world.

One of the standout features of Demon Slayer is its breathtaking artwork and meticulously choreographed fight scenes. Koyoharu Gotouge's attention to detail brings each character and their unique abilities to life, making every battle a visual feast for readers. The intricate character development also adds depth to the story, making you care deeply for Tanjiro and his companions as they face increasingly powerful and sinister demons.

As the series progresses, Tanjiro's quest for revenge evolves into a mission to uncover the truth about demons, their origins, and their connections to his past. Along the way, he encounters a diverse cast of fellow demon slayers, each with their own tragic pasts and motivations, and they form a tight-knit family bound by their common goal.

If you're a fan of spine-tingling adventures, breathtaking battles, and captivating characters, then look no further than the Demon Slayer series, now available in stock for purchase at Books2Door.  

The Enigma Behind Demon Slayer: Koyoharu Gotouge
Koyoharu Gotouge, the brilliant mind behind Demon Slayer, is a renowned mangaka who hails from Japan. While the author is famously private, their work has garnered immense popularity and critical acclaim worldwide.

Demon Slayer is Gotouge's magnum opus, showcasing their extraordinary storytelling skills and artistic prowess. The series debuted in February 2016 and quickly gained a massive following due to its compelling narrative, captivating characters, and stunning artwork. Gotouge's ability to craft a narrative that seamlessly blends action, emotion, and mythology has earned them a special place in the world of manga. 

The Anime
This breathtaking series has also been transformed on screen into a multi-season anime and movie, breaking countless records worldwide. The Demon Slayer anime is a visual feast, bringing Gotouge's intricate artwork to life with breathtaking animation and meticulously choreographed battles. Demon Slayer has become a global sensation with rich storytelling, unforgettable characters, and a perfect blend of action and emotion. Dive into this extraordinary world and experience the epic battles and heartfelt moments that have captured the hearts of millions.

title: Diana Wynne Jones Books
description:
Diana Wynne Jones is the master of fantasy fiction for ages 10+. She is most famous for her collection of children and young adult series, most notably The Land of Ingary. The series, also known as the Howl or Moving Castle series, consists of three titles: Howl’s Moving Castle (1986), Castle in the Air (1990) and House of Many Ways (2008). Find all of her most popular books in this collection now.

She is also the author of the bestselling Chrestomanci Series, which follows Gwendolen Chant, a gifted witch with astonishing powers, and her brother on magical adventures across a series of twelve worlds. 

The Moving Castle Series

Published in 1986, Howl’s Moving Castle is the first book in the series, following the story of a young woman named Sophie Hatter, who leaves her life of servitude in her mother’s hat shop after being cursed by the Wicked Witch of the Waste. To her misfortune, Sophie finds herself under a horrid spell that transforms her to look like an elderly woman.

Her only chance at breaking this curse is at the Wizard Howl’s Castle. There she is to deal with the heartless Howl, strike a bargain with a dangerous fire demon and get caught in the crossfire of both political and love affairs if she is to untangle her own enchantment.

The novel was adapted into a 2004 animated film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki and produced by Studio Ghibli, which was critically acclaimed and nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

The second book in this charming series is Castle in the Air, published in 1990. Though the story is set in the same fantasy world as the first book, the sequel focuses on Abdullah's adventures based on the tales from Arabian Nights.

Set in the land of Ingary, Abdullah is a carpet dealer who sits in his booth and spends his time daydreaming about being the long-lost son of a prince. One day he purchases a carpet from a man who claims that the carpet possesses magical properties. Soon enough, Abdullah has been whisked away on an adventure to replicate his dreams into reality by meeting dangerous djinns and beautiful princesses.

With a few familiar characters from Howl’s Moving Castle, fans of the series are in for another whimsical and enchanting adventure. 

The last book in the trilogy is House of Many Ways which is labelled as the direct sequel to the first book in the series, Howl’s Moving Castle. In this stunning finale, the story tells of Charmain Baker, who lives a sheltered life and spends her days with her nose in a book, never learning how to do the simplest of household chores.

When her Great Uncle William is overcome with sickness, Charmaine is tasked with cleaning and looking after the house- except this is no ordinary house, but one that bends space and time. When Charmain gets caught up in resolving the kingdom’s financial troubles, she encounters Sophie Pendragon and her magical family, her eccentric husband Howl, their son Morgan and the brilliant fire-demon Calcifer. With this magical family involved, there’s bound to be much chaos and unexpected revelations. 

About the Author:

Diana Wynne Jones was a British novelist who wrote fantasy and speculative fiction for children and young adults. Her work often explores themes of time travel or parallel universes.

Her work has been nominated for several awards, including being a twice finalist for the Hugo Award and being nominated fourteen times for the Locus Award, among many others. 

Jones died in early 2011 as a result of Lung Cancer. Before her death, she was working on a novel that was completed by her sister Ursula Jones in 2014.

title: Dictionaries
description:
Dictionaries and Thesauruses 

Are you often left hunting for the right word? Or maybe you have overused a word in your essay and need an alternative? If these sound like a regular problem for you, then it is time to invest in a dictionary or a thesaurus! 

Before we get into the different variations of dictionaries and explore all the different types available, let's highlight some classic dictionaries. Starting off with Collins, English Gem Dictionary and English Gem Thesaurus, these two resources both come in mini sizes for easy transportation. There is also the classic Oxford English Dictionary which has been a reference text and is the most widely-referenced historical dictionary of the English language. Oxford English Dictionaries come in many different variations

Dictionaries for Children 

Whether your little ones are preparing to start their first day at school or if you’re sending them off to University, it is always handy to have a dictionary to help with their studies. For young children, we recommend Oxford Phonics Spelling Dictionary. This little book makes for a great home and school resource. With this dictionary, it is easy to explain how 'sun' and 'Cinderella' both start with the 's' sound and how 'dance' has the same 's' sound at the end. 

Other great dictionaries for young children are The Oxford First Dictionary and The Oxford Illustrated Children’s Dictionary. Both of these books are a great introduction to dictionaries, and using them in schools and at home will help further your child’s literary progression. 

Standard Dictionaries 

Whether you’re buying your child’s first ‘grown-up’ dictionary or you’re purchasing it for yourself, it can be overwhelming at times to know what to look for. There are so many brands, sizes and variations in prices, which makes it difficult when shopping for a dictionary. That is why we have highlighted our bestselling dictionaries to make it a little clearer for you. For a brief and comprehensive dictionary, you should check out Concise Oxford English Dictionary, great for on-the-go and studying away from home. Another fantastic pocket dictionary is the Oxford Mini Dictionary and Thesaurus. Not only does it carry essential and everyday vocabulary, but it also contains 65,000 synonyms and antonyms! 

Foreign Language Dictionaries 

Learning a new language is always a daunting project, especially if you are starting from scratch. Therefore, having a dictionary to hand can often help with your skill development and language progression. Here at Books2Door, we have a varied selection of different language dictionaries, including Spanish, German, Italian, Korean, Irish and Latin. As well as verbal language, we also have a fantastic book to help you learn British Sign Language, Let's Sign Dictionary: Everyday BSL for Learners.

In the Discworld series, Terry Pratchett invites you into a flat, disc-shaped world balanced on the backs of four giant elephants, who, in turn, stand on the back of Great A'Tuin, a cosmic turtle. This unusual setting is the stage for a wildly imaginative and hilarious collection of stories that traverse genres and themes, all the while poking fun at the quirks of our own world. From the bustling city of Ankh-Morpork to the perilous journeys across the Disc, you'll meet an array of memorable characters, including the bumbling wizard Rincewind, the indomitable Granny Weatherwax, and the lovable anthropomorphic personification of Death himself.

There are many ways to embark on a journey through Discworld. 

  • You can start at the very beginning with the adventures of Rincewind and Twoflower in The Colour of Magic and The Light Fantastic, which take you across the Discworld. 
  • If you enjoy tales of witches and the supernatural, with a hefty dose of cultural satire, you'll love the Witches series, set principally in the folkloric region of Lancre where Granny Weatherwax lives. This sequence includes novels such as Equal Rites, Wyrd Sisters (Pratchett’s take on Macbeth), and Witches Abroad.
  • Alternatively, you can dive into the fan-favourite stories of Captain Sam Vimes of Ankh-Morpork’s City Watch with books like Guards! Guards! and Men at Arms. 
  • Don't dismiss the unforgettable stories of perhaps the most popular character, Death. Death is around the corner in nearly every novel, but you can learn more about him in Mort.
  • Moist von Lipwig is a conman, spared from execution by Ankh-Morpork’s leader (dictator) Lord Vetinari on the condition that he spearhead the Discworld’s Industrial Revolution. This sequence of books begins with Going Postal.

If you can’t decide, you can grab the first 5 books of each sequence in the Enter the Discworld Box Set, now available at Books2Door!

There are also several Discworld books suitable for younger readers. The Amazing Maurice and his Educated Rodents, a send-up of the Pied Piper of Hamelin, was recently adapted into an animated movie starring Hugh Laurie. The Tiffany Aching books are perfect for fans of Diane Wynne Jones, and are another great jumping-on point for readers of all ages. Tiffany is a trainee witch, learning the ropes from characters like Granny Weatherwax, whose adventures start in The Wee Free Men.

About the Author:

Terry Pratchett, the creative genius behind the Discworld series, was a true literary legend. Known for his sharp wit, clever wordplay, and insightful commentary on the human condition, Pratchett's writing has captured the hearts of millions of readers worldwide. He received numerous awards throughout his career, including the prestigious Carnegie Medal for his novel The Amazing Maurice and His Educated Rodents. Beyond his writing, Pratchett was an advocate for Alzheimer's awareness, having been diagnosed with the disease himself. His courage and determination in the face of adversity continue to inspire his fans.

So, whether you're a seasoned Discworld aficionado or a newcomer eager to explore this fantastical realm for the first time, Books2Door has the entire Terry Pratchett Discworld series in stock, waiting for you to dive in. Get ready to embark on a journey filled with laughter, wisdom, and unforgettable characters.

The series starts with Dork Diaries: Tales from a Not-So-Fabulous Life, where we meet Nikki and follow her hilarious diary entries as she tries to survive the trials and tribulations of Westchester Country Day Middle School. Nikki's journey is anything but ordinary, from the school talent show to holiday adventures and even a trip to Paris. Rachel Renée Russell's engaging storytelling and captivating illustrations bring Nikki's world to life, making each book a delightful and immersive experience for readers of all ages.

Rachel Renée Russell: A Biography
Let's look at the creative genius behind the Dork Diaries series, Rachel Renée Russell. Born in St. Joseph, Michigan, Rachel had a passion for art and writing from a young age. She attended Michigan State University, where she studied graphic arts and continued to nurture her love for storytelling.

After working as an attorney for several years, Rachel decided to pursue her dream of becoming a writer and illustrator. Her breakthrough moment came with the creation of Dork Diaries, a series inspired by her own experiences and those of her two daughters. Rachel's ability to tap into the authentic voice of a teenage girl and infuse it with humour, heart, and relatability has made her a beloved author among readers worldwide.

So, whether you're a longtime fan of the Dork Diaries series or just discovering it for the first time, Books2Door is your gateway to this enchanting world created by the talented Rachel Renée Russell.

Explore our collection today and empower yourself with the knowledge and strategies to support your brain health through every stage of life. Whether you're looking to prevent dementia, understand the impact of menopause, or simply enhance your cognitive well-being, Dr Mosconi's books are essential.

The XX Brain: The Groundbreaking Science Empowering Women to Prevent Dementia

The XX Brain by Dr. Lisa Mosconi is a pivotal work that empowers women with actionable insights and evidence-based strategies to prevent dementia and cognitive decline. Written by a leading expert in women's brain health, this book is tailored specifically for women and addresses the gender-specific factors that influence brain health. 

Dr. Mosconi presents cutting-edge scientific research in an accessible format, making complex concepts understandable for readers of all backgrounds. Suitable for women of all ages, The XX Brain focuses on self-development and self-care, aligning with current trends and providing practical recommendations to enhance cognitive function and overall brain health.

The Menopause Brain: Understanding the Impact of Menopause on Cognitive Health

In The Menopause Brain, Dr Lisa Mosconi explores the intricate relationship between menopause and brain health, shedding light on how hormonal changes can significantly impact cognitive functions and overall mental well-being. 

This groundbreaking book discusses how the decline of oestrogen and other hormones during menopause affects brain function, contributing to symptoms like memory lapses, brain fog, and an increased risk of neurological conditions. Dr. Mosconi explains why women are more susceptible to anxiety, depression, migraines, brain injuries, strokes, and Alzheimer's disease during and after menopause. She presents evidence-based research highlighting the differences in how men's and women's brains age, emphasising the need for specialised approaches to women's brain health. 

The book offers practical, scientifically-backed methods for protecting and enhancing brain health, including dietary recommendations, stress reduction techniques, sleep optimisation, and hormone replacement therapy. Additionally, Dr. Mosconi examines the dangers of environmental toxins and the significant role of the microbiome in maintaining brain health.

description:
Theodor Seuss Geisel, an American children’s author and cartoonist that made numerous timeless classics, is one of the major influential creators of the past century. He is best known for writing under the pen name Dr. Seuss and illustrating over 60 books that have sold over 600 million copies and has been translated into over 20 languages. His works remain a longstanding and well-loved children’s favourite for generations, particularly due to his use of nonsensical and silly made-up names, creatures stories and distinctive rhyming structure. 

In this collection, we have included some of the bestselling Dr. Seuss books and titles to add to any kids' bookshelf. When read aloud, rhymes help children to help identify rhythm and repetition for words, creating a secure foundation for early learning and literacy development. 

If you’re not sure where to look, let us help you find a good book! The perfect collection for beginner or longstanding Dr. Seuss fans is A Classic Case of Dr. Seuss 20 Books Collection Set. You may know the stories from movies and television, but nothing compares to the originals! With 20 paperback books in a sturdy box for easy storage, these books are the perfect addition to any child’s bookshelf. This edition is particularly useful for children aged 0-5 who are learning to read. Each book is colour-coded:

  • Blue backs- contain simple rhymes and repetition with pictures to help understand meaning. 
  • Green backs- for kids beginning to read on their own. The rhythm and rhyme helps to build confidence and independence.
  • Yellow backs- for fluent readers and particularly great for reading aloud. They also make for excellent bedtime stories. 

About the Author

The great author had his first book rejected by 27 publishers in his early career, but he

soon found success and became a legendary author, and in 1957 his book The Cat in the Hat was an instant hit! Dr. Seuss was proficient in writing, illustrating and making new creatures with wonderful names and personas, which all rhyme and flow tastefully through the story. Author Beatrix Potter even made a statement about his early work: “The cleverest book I have met with for many years.” Dr. Seuss’s artwork and creation can be seen in theme parks, paintings, sculptures and movies such as How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, which appears every Christmas. Dr. Seuss’s commitment to his work is well respected and appreciated; he has won several awards for numerous entertainment projects like the 1984 Pulitzer Prize, which involved his great contributions to education for children.

Did you know there are some correlations between Dr. Seuss with his lovely childhood memories with his mother connected to his rhyming style? When he was just a kid, his mother would often entertain him with rhymes based on various pie flavours. Did you know that it was reported Dr. Seuss would write roughly 8 hours a day and throw away, on average, 500-1000 pages during the initial draft of a picture book? From the thrilling search for the Dragon Balls to the epic confrontation with the Red Ribbon Army, and the legendary battles against powerful foes like Frieza and Cell, each volume presents a mesmerising blend of action, humour, and heartfelt moments that captivate readers of all ages.

Akira Toriyama's distinctive art style brings the vibrant world of Dragon Ball to life. With meticulous detail and dynamic illustrations, Toriyama seamlessly captures the intensity of battles, the intricacies of martial arts techniques, and the essence of each character's personality. Every panel bursts with energy, showcasing the sheer power and excitement that has made Dragon Ball a cultural phenomenon. Akira Toriyama's artistic prowess shines through in every panel of Dragon Ball. The distinctive character designs, dynamic action sequences, and detailed backgrounds bring the story to life, immersing readers in the world of Dragon Ball. Toriyama's ability to blend intense battles with comedic moments adds depth to the characters and showcases the versatility of his storytelling.

Dragon Ball is not just about thrilling battles and fantastical adventures; it is also a story of personal growth, friendship, and the power of determination. As Goku and his companions face insurmountable odds, they learn valuable life lessons, discover the strength within themselves, and inspire readers to never give up, no matter the challenges they may face.

Dragon Ball Anime adaptation: 

Dragon Ball is not just limited to the manga world; it has also made a significant impact as an anime series. The Dragon Ball anime adaptation brings Akira Toriyama's dynamic storytelling and vibrant characters to life with stunning visuals, exhilarating action sequences, and a captivating soundtrack.

The Dragon Ball anime series consists of multiple arcs, each encompassing different storylines and introducing new challenges for the characters. The anime faithfully adapts the manga, retaining its humour, intense battles, and character development while adding its own visual flair and sound design.

The original Dragon Ball anime aired from 1986 to 1989 and covered the adventures of a young Goku, from his early encounters with Bulma to his training under Master Roshi and his participation in the World Martial Arts Tournament. This part of the series focuses on light-hearted adventures, martial arts tournaments, and the search for the Dragon Balls.

Following the success of the original series, the sequel, Dragon Ball Z, premiered in 1989 and continued the story, showcasing Goku's growth into adulthood, the introduction of new allies and enemies, and an expansion of the series' power scaling and epic battles. Dragon Ball Z is known for its iconic moments such as Goku's transformation into a Super Saiyan, the intense fights against villains like Vegeta, Frieza, Cell, and Majin Buu, and the exploration of the Saiyan race and their intergalactic origins.

title: Dune Books
description:
Frank Herbert's Dune book series stands as a monumental achievement in science fiction literature, revered for its intricate world-building, political intrigue, and profound exploration of complex themes. Spanning six novels, this epic saga has captivated readers for decades, leaving an indelible mark on the genre and influencing countless works that followed. Buy the six books that started it all in our Dune by Frank Herbert complete series four book collection with six titles included. 

The series begins with the eponymous novel, Dune. Set in a distant future, it introduces us to a universe dominated by powerful noble houses, interstellar travel, and a valuable resource known as melange, or spice. The story primarily follows the young protagonist, Paul Atreides, as his family takes control of the desert planet Arrakis, the sole source of the spice. Through Herbert's masterful prose, readers are immersed in a richly detailed universe, complete with intricate political machinations, religious sects, and a vividly realised desert environment.

Original Dune book series: 

  • Dune
  • Dune Messiah
  • Children of Dune
  • God Emperor of Dune
  • Heretics of Dune
  • Chapterhouse: Dune

One of the defining aspects of the Dune series is Herbert's world-building. He meticulously crafts a complex and believable future society, delving into the intricacies of politics, ecology, religion, and philosophy. The planet Arrakis itself becomes a character, with its harsh desert landscape, giant sandworms, and intricate ecology shaped by the presence of spice. Herbert's attention to detail and his ability to create a fully realised universe are unmatched, drawing readers into a world that feels both alien and familiar.

The exploration of power and politics lies at the heart of the Dune series. Herbert delves into the complexities of governance, examining the delicate balance of power and the consequences of its abuse. The noble houses, the Emperor, and the secretive Bene Gesserit sisterhood engage in intricate power struggles, manipulating events to further their own agendas. The character of Paul Atreides undergoes a transformative journey, grappling with his own destiny as a messianic figure, and the weight of the decisions he must make to shape the future of the universe. The series challenges readers to consider the implications of power and the moral responsibilities that come with it.

The Dune series also explores themes of ecology, religion, and the human condition. Herbert explores the interconnectedness of all things through the lens of the desert planet and its fragile ecosystem. He delves into the power of belief systems and the impact of religion on society, examining the rise and fall of messianic figures and the influence of religious dogma on individual and collective behaviour. The human condition is laid bare, as characters wrestle with their desires, fears, and the complexities of navigating a vast and ever-changing universe.

Herbert's writing style is immersive and thought-provoking, blending poetic prose with philosophical musings. His intricate plotting and multi-layered narrative keep readers engaged, while his vivid descriptions transport them to the vastness of the Dune universe. The series is a masterclass in storytelling, deftly balancing action, political intrigue, and introspection.

All Dune books in chronological order: 

  • The Butlerian Jihad (2002)
  • The Machine Crusade (2003)
  • The Battle of Corrin (2004)
  • Sisterhood of Dune (2011)
  • Mentats of Dune (2014)
  • Navigators of Dune (2016)
  • House Atreides (1999)
  • House Harkonnen (2000)
  • House Corrino (2001)
  • The Duke of Caladan (2020)
  • The Lady of Caladan (2021)
  • The Heir of Caladan (2022)
  • Dune (1965)

*Books in bold written by series creator Frank Herbert; all other books written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Frank Herbert's Dune book series stands as a landmark in science fiction literature. It’s expansive world-building, intricate plotting and exploration of complex themes have solidified its place as a masterpiece of the genre. Herbert's vision of a future universe, populated with captivating characters and filled with political manoeuvring, ecological intricacies, and philosophical depth, continues to captivate readers and inspire new generations of science fiction authors. The Dune series remains an essential read for anyone seeking a richly crafted and thought-provoking journey into the realm of science fiction.

title: Dyslexia Friendly Books
description:

Dyslexia is a learning difficulty that affects reading and spelling, often including the individual's awareness of language patterns, verbal memory, and processing speed. Therefore, reading can be difficult for a dyslexic person, which can often result in people with dyslexia being reluctant readers. Whether you're shopping for yourself or a family member, here at Book2Door, we have a wide range of books that are more accessible to dyslexic readers.

Barrington Stoke Books 

Barrington Stoke Publishers focuses on providing more accessible books for dyslexic and reluctant readers. They have published books written with dyslexic and reluctant readers in mind by fantastic authors such as Malorie Blackman, Nick Sharratt, Tom Palmer, and so many more. This Scottish-based publishing company has been responsible for encouraging children of all ages and abilities to get into reading, helping every child experience the joy of reading and the feeling of getting lost in a book. Barrington Stoke is driven to provide books that match a child's age and not their reading level. Aiming to keep their interest whilst they gradually improve over time. The books are expertly edited to ensure comprehension and accessibility, with shorter novels helping the reader build their confidence. 

There is an excellent range of books available from Barrington Stoke for a wide range of ages. For ages 7-9-year-olds, check out this fantastic five-book collection by Tom Palmer. This set features World War-based fiction stories D-Day Dog, Over the Line, After the War, Armistice Runner, and Arctic Star. These stories have gained popularity since their release due to Palmer's unique exploration of World War narratives. 

For fans of Stranger Things and The Goonies, check out The Crooked Oak Mysteries Series by Dan Smith. This three-book collection features thrilling unexplainable mysteries that this group of friends tries to solve. The series is printed in a dyslexia-friendly font and on yellow paper which makes it more accessible. This series is excellent for 7-9-year-olds who are fans of sci-fi and horror. 

For more Barrington Stoke books, check out our Barrington Stoke page! We also have a blog page, great books for dyslexic readers, to help point out some titles for your little readers. 

Books about Dyslexia 

Whether you have recently been diagnosed or want to learn more about it to help a loved one, we've got a wide range of books to make it a little easier for you. For children and tweens, check Dyslexia and Me by Amy Rainbow, a dyslexia specialist. Perfect for helping children understand the difficulty and what techniques could help them in school, exams, daily life, and mindfulness activities. 

For advice and information for adults with dyslexia, check out Kate Grigg's This is Dyslexia: The definitive guide to the untapped power of dyslexic thinking and its vital role in our future. Griggs is CEO of the charity Made by Dyslexia and is driven to help people understand the advantages and disadvantages of dyslexia, reframing it into strengths rather than weaknesses.

The story follows the sixteen-year-old protagonist, Thomas, who wakes up with no recollection of his past memories other than his own name. But he is not alone. His memories have been wiped, just like the other Gladers- a group of teenage boys who inhabit the Maze. They all have no idea why they’re there or what’s happened to the world outside. All they know is that every single morning, like clockwork, the walls open at sunrise and close at dusk. With danger at every turn, do the boys risk escaping through the Maze, or should they live out the rest of their lives trapped in their new home? 

Now a series of popular major motion pictures starring Thomas Brodie-Sangster, Dylan O’Brien and Kaya Scodelario, this unique storyline brings a fresh perspective to the teen Dystopian theme. The original trilogy follows the protagonist Katniss Everdeen who lives in District Twelve, one of the twelve districts surrounding the shining Capitol in a region of North America known as Panem. The Capitol is harsh and maintains order over the districts by forcing one boy and girl between the ages of twelve and eighteen to participate in the annual Hunger Games- a fight to the death on live TV. Katniss takes her sister’s place in the Games, but if she is to win, she will have to start making choices that weigh survival against humanity. 

The prequel, A Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, follows former president Coriolanus Snow in his youth as he prepares for his one shot at glory as a mentor for the Games. But the odds are against him. He’s been given the humiliating task of mentoring the female tribute from District Twelve, the lowest of the low. With their fates now completely intertwined, every choice Coriolanus makes could lead to his favour or failure, triumph or ruin.

The Chaos Walking Trilogy by Patrick Ness has been praised for its unique narration style and gritty action. The trilogy includes all three books in the series, including The Knife of Never Letting Go, The Ask and the Answer and Monsters of Men, all included in a beautiful slipcase for easy storage. 

This series has been highly regarded for its white-knuckle journey of identity, power and acceptance. Now a major motion picture starring Tom Holland, Daisy Ridley and Mads Mikkelsen, read the book that started it all in this intriguing and action-packed series. 

The story follows young Todd Hewitt, the last boy living in a town of men. In this world, a race of alien species has landed, bringing with them a disease known as the Germ, which killed all the women and has altered the brains of the remaining men so that everyone can hear each other’s thoughts constantly. That is until Todd randomly stumbles upon a rare patch of silence and, with it, a girl. Where has she come from? Why wasn’t she killed with the rest of the women? Why can Todd not hear her thoughts? With all these questions buzzing in Todd’s mind, he knows the town has been hiding a sinister secret from him- something so awful that Todd is forced to flee with only his dog as company and now this mystery girl.

description:
The Early Readers Collection: From First Sounds to Fluent Stories

Reading isn't just a skill; it’s the moment the world finally starts to make sense. The Early Readers collection at Books2Door is designed to capture that electric "click" when a child realizes they are no longer just looking at pictures, but decoding a narrative. These are the essential stepping stones—pedagogically structured to bridge the gap between shared picture books and independent chapter books.

Featuring the "gold standard" of reading schemes, this collection utilizes a systematic, leveled approach to build phonics confidence, vocabulary stamina, and a lifelong love for storytelling.

1. The Power of Phonics: Early Reader Schemes

At this foundational stage, decodability is everything. We stock the most trusted names in early literacy to ensure that every "new reader" win is supported by expert pedagogy.

  • Read with Oxford Biff, Chip and Kipper: The definitive UK reading scheme. By following the familiar adventures of Biff, Chip, Kipper, and Floppy the dog, children build familiarity and confidence across meticulously leveled stages.

  • Julia Donaldson’s Early Readers: Even the stars of modern classics like The Smeds and Smoos have been adapted into early reader formats. These versions maintain the rhythmic magic of Julia Donaldson while simplifying the text for independent decoding.

2. Colour-Coded Progress: Stepping Stones to Fluency

Many of our early readers use a color-coded leveling system (Blue, Red, Yellow, etc.) to help parents and teachers track a child’s progress through the National Curriculum milestones.

  • Horrid Henry Early Readers: Francesca Simon’s iconic anti-hero is a primary tool for engaging reluctant readers. These "stepping stone" books use shorter chapters and expressive art to make the leap into independent fiction feel like a game rather than a chore.

  • Maverick Early Readers: From Gold to White levels, these sets focus on high-interest themes like space, magic, and monsters, ensuring that while the vocabulary is controlled, the imagination is limitless.

3. Why Variety Matters in Early Literacy

A child shouldn't just read one type of story. Our collection balances fiction with non-fiction early readers, helping children develop "reading for information" skills early on.

  • Visual Literacy: By blending vibrant illustrations from artists like Tony Ross with structured text, these books teach children to use visual cues to decode meaning—a vital skill in modern literacy.

  • Value-First Reading: At Books2Door, we believe literacy shouldn't be a luxury. We offer these Early Reader Box Sets at significant discounts, allowing you to stock an entire "reading level" for the price of a few high-street volumes.

Moving far beyond the "monolith" stereotype, this curated selection spans the neon-lit streets of modern Tokyo to the mythic landscapes of ancient China and the bustling family kitchens of the diaspora.

Whether you are looking for #OwnVoices narratives that reflect your own upbringing or seeking a window into a culture different from your own, these books offer unfiltered, powerful perspectives from the region's most influential writers.


1. The Heavyweights: Modern Masterpieces & Global Sensations

The global appetite for ESEA literature has reached a fever pitch, driven by authors who blend cultural specificity with universal emotional truths. This section of our collection features the writers currently defining the literary landscape.

  • Ana Huang: A powerhouse in the contemporary romance world, Huang’s Twisted Series has become a staple for readers who crave high-stakes emotion and billionaire intrigue with a modern Asian-American perspective.

  • Contemporary Classics: Dive into stories that explore the complexities of the immigrant experience, generational trauma, and the evolving face of modern Asia. From satirical social commentaries to heart-wrenching family sagas, these books challenge and captivate in equal measure.

2. Myth, Magic, and History: Historical Epics & YA Fantasy

East and South East Asian history and folklore provide a limitless well of inspiration for fantasy and historical fiction. Our collection brings these legends to life for a new generation.

  • Reimagined Folklore: Discover YA titles that weave traditional spirits, demons, and deities into modern settings, offering a fresh take on ancient magic.

  • Historical Box Sets: Why settle for one volume when you can immerse yourself in an entire era? Our Fiction Box Sets allow readers to follow sprawling dynasties and revolutionary movements from start to finish.

3. Culture on a Plate: Food, Family, and Identity

In many ESEA cultures, love is spoken through food. Many of the titles in this collection use the kitchen as a central stage for exploring identity. These stories are as much about the recipes passed down through generations as they are about the people who cook them, making for a truly sensory reading experience.

In the vast world of manga and anime, few names shine as brightly as that of Eiichiro Oda. Born on January 1, 1975, in Kumamoto, Japan, Oda's journey from a young dreamer to the legendary creator of the internationally acclaimed manga series One Piece. His work has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. At Books2Door, we are proud to celebrate the genius of Eiichiro Oda and his magnum opus, One Piece.

Eiichiro Oda's journey into the world of manga began at a tender age when he was captivated by the works of Akira Toriyama, the creator of Dragon Ball. His fascination with Toriyama's artistry and storytelling ignited a spark within him, setting him on a path to become a mangaka 

Oda's art style is as distinctive as his storytelling. His characters are instantly recognisable, with their exaggerated features, unique quirks, and outlandish costumes. The world he has crafted is teeming with fantastical islands, mythical creatures, and eccentric characters, all brought to life with meticulous attention to detail. Oda's ability to blend humour, emotion, and action seamlessly keeps readers on the edge of their seats and laughing heartily.

The Birth of One Piece:
Oda's creative genius and determination culminated in the birth of One Piece in 1997. The series, serialised in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, quickly became a cultural phenomenon in Japan. It wasn't long before its impact spread across the globe, enchanting readers and viewers of all ages with its epic tale of adventure, friendship, and the pursuit of the ultimate treasure, the One Piece.

One Piece:
One Piece follows the adventures of Monkey D. Luffy, a young and ambitious pirate with a stretchy body, after eating a Devil Fruit. Along with his diverse and lovable crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, Luffy embarks on a quest to find the fabled One Piece treasure and become the Pirate King. Their journey takes them to the ends of the Grand Line, a treacherous and mysterious sea, where they encounter powerful foes, form unbreakable bonds, and unveil the world's secrets.

One Piece's success knows no bounds. With over a thousand chapters and a staggering 100+ volumes, the series has sold over 480 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series in history. The anime adaptation has also garnered a massive following with its vibrant animation and unforgettable moments.

Eiichiro Oda's remarkable journey from a young manga enthusiast to a manga icon is a testament to the power of dreams and dedication. His work in One Piece has left an indelible mark on the world of manga and anime, inspiring countless artists and storytellers to follow their passions. So, join us at Books2Door in celebrating the genius of Eiichiro Oda and embark on an epic adventure with One Piece, a series that will continue to enthral generations to come.
