title: Enid Blyton Books
description:
Enid Blyton is one of England’s most-remembered children’s writers. She is the creator of The Famous Five, The Secret Seven, Malory Towers and the unforgettable Noddy, as well as many other great stories. She was a prolific writer, and she wrote about all sorts of topics, including adventure, mystery and fantasy. Her books have sold more than 600 million copies worldwide, been translated into more than 90 languages, and they have been bestsellers since the 1930s.

If you’ve got a child who loves to read but is getting too old for picture books, they might love an Enid Blyton book. We’ve got jam-packed box sets of some of her most popular titles. They’re perfect for readers aged seven and upwards who are seeking a little maturity in their next book and love to follow the same characters across a series. Among them are The Complete Faraway Tree Collection, which includes four magical adventures, and The Naughtiest Girl 10 Book Collection. They’re perfect for confident, independent readers ready to get stuck into a great series.

Famous series, great-value sets

The Famous Five is one of Enid Blyton’s well-known sequences. It’s a classic children’s book series that has been loved by generations of readers. The first book, 1941’s Five on a Treasure Island, introduced Julian, Dick, Anne, Georgina and their faithful dog Timmy. Their rural adventures in the school holidays were so popular that a new one had to come out every year. Their final adventure, Five Are Together Again, came out in 1963. These books encourage readers to look at the world around them with the intent to explore, observe, discover and learn. We stock The Famous Five Collection, which includes all 21 novels in the series.

If you’re into mysteries, you’ll thrill to the adventures of The Secret Seven Society. Across fifteen novels and several short stories, Peter, Janet, Pam, Barbara, Jack, Colin and George investigate various mysteries, from a mail heist to missing medals. Find their adventures in The Secret Seven: Complete Collection, featuring 16 books, which will keep your kids entertained for hours on end.

The Malory Towers series is perfect for fans of boarding school adventures. Darrell Rivers and her girl gang grow up in the castle-like grounds, the books following their experience from their first year to the end of Sixth Form. Our Malory Towers 12 Book Collection also include the follow-up series from Pamela Cox, following Darrell’s younger sister Felicity.

If you can’t get enough of schooldays, you need to make a visit to St. Clare’s. The first volume follows The Twins at St. Clare’s, Pat and Isabel O’Sullivan, settling into the school and making new friends. The original six books by Enid Blyton were bolstered by three more by Pamela Cox so that you can follow the twins all the way to sixth form. All are available in the St Clare’s Collection - enrol today!

The Mystery Series, previously known as The Five Find-Outers and Dog, may be less well-known than Enid Blyton’s other series, but it’s of the same high standard. Fatty, Larry, Daisy, Pip and Bets, along with their faithful dog Buster, solve mysteries on their holiday breaks from boarding school. Across the series, you can follow Fatty and the gang from the age of twelve to seventeen, as they beat Mr Goon, the village policeman, to the solution every time. The Mystery Series: Complete Collection features all fifteen adventures from The Find-Outers in one great-value box set.

If you’re jonesing for a holiday, check out The Adventure Series. It follows Phillip, Jack, Dinah and Lucy-Ann as they break out on their own and explore various landscapes in the UK and across the world. Along the way, they encounter a prince, a fugitive, a crook, and lost treasure. The gang stumble on sinister plots and strange mysteries, all available in The Adventure Series: Complete Collection, which sports magnificent 70th-anniversary covers on all the books.

About the author

Enid Blyton was born in London in 1897 and died there in 1968. In between, she married twice, lived variously in Suffolk, Kent, Buckinghamshire, and across Greater London, and published over 750 books. Many of her books remain in print, with some of her series, like The Naughtiest Girl, continuing under other authors after her death. They have been adapted for theatre, film, and TV, including a recent Malory Towers series on CBBC.

Blyton’s books have been bestsellers for over eighty years. She wrote so many books so quickly, some people thought she had an army of ghostwriters - which has never been proved. She started out writing poetry but found commercial success with her children’s books Adventures of the Wishing-Chair and The Enchanted Wood.

Enid Blyton wrote her stories with simple language, making them easy for even very young children to understand. Her work is fun and engaging but still teaches important lessons about life. Enid Blyton’s books feature cleanly depicted goodies and baddies and have dramatic plots that illustrate traditional moral lessons. Her approach to story makes her work is accessible to a wide variety of readers. Enid Blyton’s legacy lives on, and her works continue to inspire, entertain, and educate children worldwide. 

With her imaginative characters and exciting plots, Enid Blyton will keep readers entertained for hours on end! Whether it is a rainy day or just a Monday afternoon when nothing seems right with the world — let our collection of Enid Blyton's classic children's books take care of everything. You can buy these books for your kids or even yourself on our website today! They make great gifts for any occasion. So if you want to discover some great new reads, look no further than this collection of classic stories from an iconic author that everyone knows and loves.

You can trust Books2Door to provide the best and encourage the love of reading in all children. We have children’s books in stock range from young readers aged 5-7, right up to young adults. Don’t forget to check out our bestsellers for more great books.

title: Faber & Faber Books
description:
Founded in 1929, Faber and Faber is an independent publishing house in London. Since their establishment, poetry has been at the heart of their publishing, with T. S. Eliot as their first Poetry Editor. Since then, they have sought to publish the foremost voices in fiction, non-fiction, poetry, drama, film and children’s books. They have an extensive list of published authors and poets, including William Golding, Samuel Beckett, Kazuo Ishiguro, Sally Rooney and more. 

Here at Books2Door, we have curated a list of the latest and bestselling Faber and Faber Books. This page is dedicated to our extensive collection of books for all ages ranging from ages 0-5 all the way to YA and even adult fiction. 

Books for 0-5

Have you ever wondered what your fruit and veggies get up to while you sleep? Or how

your toothbrushes and bathroom essentials spend the day when the children go off to school, and the adults go to work? Well, look no further than the Kitchen Disco by Clare Foges & Al Murphy 3 Picture Books Collection Set. This collection includes Kitchen Disco, Bathroom Boogie and Veg Patch Party. This book contains everything from break-dancing lemons to twirling tangerines, from backflipping mouthwash to toothbrush raves and even dancing veggies! The repetitive rhymes and choruses will get even the most reluctant of fussy eaters to try something new (no promises, though!). 

Books for 9-14

William Golding’s dystopian novel Lord of the Flies has remained a popular classic for over 60 years since its publication in 1954. The novel demonstrates the baseness of human nature through its characterisation and heavy symbolism. The novel starts with a plane crash on a desert island, leaving only a group of schoolboys as the sole survivors and explores their disastrous attempt to govern themselves without the presence of adults. By day they discover fantastic wildlife, but by night, they are haunted by the nightmare of a primitive beast. This book is perfect for easing older kids that are fans of Suzanne Collins's The Hunger Games Trilogy and want to delve into the classics. 

Books for YA and Adults 

Kazuo Ishiguro is considered to be one of the most critically acclaimed and praised contemporary fiction writers. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2017. His works convey the yearning for life and the struggle against ignorance and brute force. His works remain popular among the YA and adult community, with his most popular titles including Never Let Me Go, The Remains of the Day, Klara and the Sun and more. His latest publication Klara and the Sun, released in 2021, follows the story of Klara, a solar-powered Artificial Friend (AF), who is chosen by Josie, a sickly child, to be her companion. Perfect for fans of science fiction and fantasy, readers can delve into the mind of an artificial robot, exploring human nature. 

Sally Rooney has taken the fiction genre by storm lately with her notable works, including Normal People, which gained its own BBC Three adaptation. In this Irish psychological and romantic drama, the novel follows the complex friendship and relationship between two teenagers, Connell and Marianne, who both attend the same secondary school. Her most recent work, Beautiful World, Where Are You, published in 2021, follows two best friends on the cusp of 30, repeatedly grappling with their struggle to find meaning in a troubled world. 

At Books2Door, we aim to make reading affordable and accessible to everyone, regardless of age, interest or budget. Whether you’re shopping for a loved one or a little one, we have the perfect selection of books for you to choose from.

title: Fairy Books 🧚
description:
Since the beginning of time, civilisations and cultures have told stories of fairies in various different forms. Stories of fairies date back all the way to the 13th century—from Greek Mythology to European and English folklore; fairies have been a part of most civilisations and cultures. Except of course, each culture has seen fairies in their own unique light.

A fairy (also called faery, faerie, fay, fae) is perceived as a type of mythical being or legendary creature, a form of spirit, often described as metaphysical, supernatural or preternatural. The term ‘fairy’ encapsulates many members of the fae family, including goblins, gnomes, elves, and more. However, the one thing that is consistent about fairies across the globe; is that they are all part of amazing stories, tales and literary works.

In this collection therefore, we are shifting the spotlight to books with fairy characters and not just fairy tales. Whilst not all fairy tales are about fairies, they sure do make most fairy tales come alive. A sprinkle of fairy dust and magic fairy books—we believe, are all it takes to trigger a child’s imagination and draw them towards fiction literature early on. A great series filled with the magic of fairies is Daisy Meadow's Rainbow Magic series.

If the bestselling charts (children’s literature) are to be believed, the fairies seem to have quite the fan following with little children, especially girls. We at Books2Door have had our own share of love for the fairies. There was something so fascinating about being able to read a book and transport ourselves into a fantasy world and to believe in fairies and their magic. Not only was it fun to read fairy books but it was also fun to get our hands on the fairy merchandise, dolls and more.

We suggest you share this precious childhood memory with your child and introduce them to fairies and their magical world early on. Here are some children’s books to help your child blossom a friendship with the fairies…

A great series filled with the magic of fairies is Daisy Meadow's Rainbow Magic series, as the name suggests, is the A to Z of fairies. Whilst Rainbow Magic Books are available in sets suitable for early readers that is children aged 3 + they also have a magical adventures collection set for older kids aged 6 and above.

Get the set for your child and allow them to join the fairies and their friends on their magical adventures. The Rainbow Magic books are jam-packed with magical facts and figures from the world of the fairies and their friends! It's just the book you must get for your child, if you want them to make friends with the fairies in fiction and believe in magic.

The Twinkly Twinkly Fairies is a book that little children will love. A peekaboo into the world of fairies’ and their sparkling life; this one is a magical novelty book. Albert the unicorn doesn't like the dark, but the fairies light the way for him and help him feel better in this heart-warming story. The number of lights gradually increase as you turn the pages, until you find ten lights at the end. Such a beautiful way to teach your kids about the light at the end of the tunnel.

A Natural History of Fairies by Emily Hawkins is an enchantingly illustrated natural history of fairies, compiled in the 1920s by the botanist Professor Elsie Arbour for her niece, and is filled with colourful sketches and precise notes detailing the secret life of fairies and their important role in the natural world. Inside, you will discover the wide and wonderful array of different species of fairies around the globe and explore where and how they live. Get this book for your kids and allow them to revel in this hidden world and learn about: The anatomy of a fairy, the life cycle of a fairy and more.

title: Fairy Tales and Legends 🏰
description:
Fairy Tales, Myths and Legends 

For as long as people have been on this earth to say them, stories have been told. Whether they were stories of knights battling dragons, the search for the fountain of youth or gods fighting each other, our fascination has continued to grow. There are a phenomenal amount of fairy tales, myths and legends throughout the world, meaning that there is always something new to read about them. Here at Book2Door, we have highlighted some of our favourites that we think you will enjoy. Now sit back, relax and dive into some fantastical other worlds and cultures with our fairy tales, myths and legends collection. 

Classic Fairy Tales 

There are many different fairy tales that have been past down to us since we were young children. Many of these classic stories originated from Hans Christian Anderson and The Brothers Grimm, Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm. These pioneers of modern storytelling paved the way for a vast amount of writers, artists and musicians. If you would like to check out the original dark warning tales by these classic authors, check out Grimm's Complete Fairy Tales by The Brothers Grimm and Hans Andersen's Fairy Tales: Retold by Naomi Lewis. 

If you are looking for lighter retellings of classic fairy tales, check out Ladybird Tales My Once Upon A Time Library 24 Books Collection. This wonderful collection contains classic tales like Beauty and the Beast, Cinderella, Puss in Boots, and so many more. Many children have grown up seeing these stories on the big screen. However, it is always an enjoyable activity for you to read the stories with them. Perfect for bedtime stories, this book collection also makes a great gift. 

Mythology books 

There are so many different mythologies out there it can be hard to know where to start! Here at Books2Door, we have a great selection of mythologies from across the globe for you to look through. Starting with the UK is Arthurian Mythology. The main story originates from Welsh mythology about a great warrior defending Britain from human and supernatural enemies. This then turned to the story of the legendary king of Britain, King Arthur. Sweet Cherry Publishing has released an easy classics series called The Legend of King Arthur, perfect for introducing your 7-9-year-old to mythology. 

Turning to our Scandinavian neighbours for our next exploration of different cultures' mythology. Norse mythology features some of the craziest and creepiest stories, creatures and lands. Many Hollywood films have taken inspiration from Nordic mythology, including, Midsommar, The Ritual and The Northman. Not to mention the comic book retelling of the Gods Thor and Loki in Marvel. Once you dive into Norse mythology, it is easy to see why so many writers have taken inspiration from it. For a great retelling of Norse Mythology, focusing on Ragnarok and the antics of Loki, the God of Mischief, check out Neil Gaiman’s Norse Mythology. For a beautiful collection of illustrated Norse myths and legends, check out Norse Myths by Matt Ralphs. 

Another famous collection of mythology is Egyptian. Originating from Ancient Egypt, these stories describe the actions of Gods, the order of the Universe (Maat) and various frightening creatures. Ancient Egyptian mythology largely influenced modern-day Egyptian culture, with scenes and symbols from myth appearing in art in tombs, temples, and amulets. For a fantastic illustrated guide to Egyptian mythology, check out Treasury Of Egyptian Mythology: Classic Stories of Gods, Goddesses, Monsters & Mortals By Donna Jo Napoli. For a factual but child-friendly resource, check out Stars of Mythology: Egyptian by Hachette publishing. This is part of a series, so don’t forget to check out Stars of Mythology: Greek. 

Want FREE DELIVERY for a whole year round? Well, you can with Book2Door plus+. Check out Books2Door Plus+ here. Don’t forget to subscribe to our newsletters to keep up to date with our new releases, offers and news in one place. Subscribe here.

title: Family & Home Stories Books
description:
In this splendid collection of stories, we have books about family, relationships, bonds, belonging, journeys of self-discovery, and individual identities. Amongst all our other collections of books and genres; this one is the closest to our hearts. Here we have a collection of books that matter beyond genres—creative, contemporary, literary nonfiction, or fiction. The books in this section cover a range of themes; from family issues to coming-of-age adventures. Stories about relationships with your grandparents, siblings, and even yourselves.

Some stories chase the question of the protagonist’s identity whilst some follow them through their journeys and relationships. Let’s take a look at some books that delve into these very sensitive yet relevant themes.

If All the World Were... by the poet and playwright Joseph Coelho is a moving picture book about a young girl coping with the loss of her beloved grandfather. A beautifully illustrated, moving, and yet uplifting book, this one is an ideal way to introduce children to the concept of the loss of a loved one. Following this story of love and loss of a grandparent; through spring, summer and autumn are Allison Colpoys' brilliant artworks. As the grandfather teaches the young girl to live without him, to create, and to imagine—the reader too will experience a flood of emotions. Soothing, moving, and finally uplifting; If All the World Were... is a beautiful approach to surviving love and loss. 

Winner of several literary awards, The Bone Sparrow is a beautiful, vivid, and deeply moving story about a refugee boy who has lived his entire life in a detention centre. The book is a reminder of the importance of freedom, hope, and home. Subhi the protagonist has only ever known life behind the fences. But as he grows, so does his imagination, until it reaches the brink of his world. The Night Sea brings him gifts, the faraway whales sing to him, and the birds tell their stories. One night however the sea brings him Jimmie, a scruffy, impatient girl who appears from the other side of the wires, and brings a notebook written by the mother she lost. Unable to read it, she relies on Subhi to unravel her own family’s love songs and tragedies. A vivid tale of sorrow, self-discovery, and survival—this book is an interesting children’s story about family, relationships, and self.

A family storybook; No Ballet Shoes in Syria by Catherine Bruton is a story about self-discovery and identity. Aya is an eleven-year-old Syrian refugee who has arrived in Britain with her mum and brother seeking asylum. As Aya starts to discover her life in Britain, she stumbles across a local ballet class where her dance teacher recognises her exceptional talent and sees her potential to win the ballet scholarship. But winning the ballet scholarship is the least of Aya’s concerns. She must, at the same time, fight to be allowed to remain in Britain, make a home in a new country and find her father who was separated from them in Syria. Through Aya’s life story as a refugee in Britain; the book tells a captivating account of authentic ballet detail and in the process becomes a piece of literature championing the rights of refugees. A story of hope, humanity, and the undying human spirit; the book is all heart and all feels.

title: Family Saga Books
description:
Family Saga Books: Multi-Generational Epics & Heart-Wrenching Legacies

Families aren't just built on blood; they are built on the secrets, triumphs, and heartbreaks of those who came before. The Family Saga collection at Books2Door is a curated archive of the world’s most sweeping narratives. These aren't just "once-upon-a-time" stories—they are sprawling, multi-generational journeys that explore how legacy, war, and love shape the human spirit over decades.

Whether you're looking for the gritty realism of post-war London or the gothic shadows of a hidden attic, these collections offer a permanent seat at the family table.

1. The Titans of the Family Saga: Modern & Historical Classics

The power of a family saga lies in its depth. At Books2Door, we specialize in bringing you the complete journey via Fiction Box Sets, ensuring you never have to wait for the next generation's story to unfold.

  • The Cazalet Chronicles by Elizabeth Jane Howard: Set against the encroaching shadows of World War II, this 5-book masterpiece is the definitive British family saga. It follows the Cazalet family through their loves, losses, and the slow erosion of their world, offering an intimate look at a family caught in the gears of history.

  • The Dollanganger Family Series by V.C. Andrews: For those who prefer their sagas with a dark, gothic edge, this 5-book collection is a cult classic. Beginning with Flowers in the Attic, it explores a legacy of twisted secrets and forbidden love that spans generations.

  • Little Women Series by Louisa May Alcott: The ultimate celebration of sisterhood. Join the March sisters as they navigate the American Civil War and the transition from girlhood to womanhood. This timeless Louisa May Alcott collection remains a foundational entry in the genre.

2. Grit, Grace, and The East End: Contemporary Sagas

Not all sagas are ancient history. Many of our most popular sets explore the resilience of families in the face of modern struggle and social change.

  • Call the Midwife Series by Jennifer Worth: Step into post-war London with the memoirs that inspired the global hit TV show. This series is a raw, beautiful exploration of community, childbirth, and the families—both biological and chosen—that define the East End.

  • The Ration Book Series by Jean Fullerton: Known as the queen of the East End saga, Jean Fullerton crafts stories that feel "deliciously readable." From A Ration Book Victory to her wider family chronicles, her work is perfect for readers who love a blend of historical accuracy and heartwarming drama.

3. The Enduring Power of Friendship: Chosen Family Sagas

Modern literature has expanded the definition of "family" to include the lifelong bonds of friendship.

  • Firefly Lane Series by Kristin Hannah: This collection follows Tully and Kate over thirty years. It is a saga of loyalty and ambition that proves some sisters aren't born—they are found.

title: Fantasy Books
description:

Fantasy fiction is a subgenre of speculative fiction that transports readers to otherworldly realms filled with magical creatures, epic adventures, and fantastical landscapes. It encompasses a wide array of themes, from high fantasy featuring intricate world-building and intricate magic systems to urban fantasy, blending the supernatural with our everyday world. What makes fantasy fiction so beloved is its ability to ignite the reader's imagination and offer an escape from the mundane into a world where anything is possible.

Let's dive into some must-read fantasy series available in stock at Books2Door:

  • A Court of Thorns and Roses Series by Sarah J. Maas: Follow the journey of Feyre Archeron as she navigates a world of beauty and danger, love and betrayal, and an intricate web of political intrigue and magic.
  • The Chronicles of Narnia by C.S. Lewis: Venture into the wardrobe and discover the magical land of Narnia, where talking animals, mythical creatures, and epic battles between good and evil await.
  • The All Souls Trilogy by Deborah Harkness: Dive into a world where witches, vampires, and daemons coexist in secret. Follow the journey of historian Diana Bishop as she unravels the mysteries of a hidden manuscript and her own supernatural abilities.
  • The Skulduggery Pleasant Series by Derek Landy: Join the wisecracking skeleton detective Skulduggery Pleasant and his apprentice, Stephanie Edgley, as they battle dark forces and uncover hidden conspiracies in a world of magic and mayhem.

Whether you're looking for epic quests, magical romance, or whimsical adventures, you'll find a treasure trove of fantastical stories to immerse yourself in. We invite you to explore our collection and embark on a journey into the realms of fantasy that will transport you to places beyond your wildest dreams.

title: Fantasy Romance Books
description:
Welcome to Books2Door's enchanting collection of fantasy romance books. At Books2Door, you'll find these captivating fantasy romance series and many more. Whether you're in the mood for epic adventures, sizzling romances, or tales of love that defy the boundaries of reality, our collection has something to offer every romantic at heart. Immerse yourself in these enchanting worlds, where love knows no bounds and magic is just a turn of the page away. Discover your next favourite fantasy romance today!

title: Farshore Books
description:
A year after HarperCollins UK’s acquisition of Egmont UK Books in 2019 (formerly Egmont UK Ltd) from the Danish media group, Egmont, they announced their new identity: Farshore. Powered by a new brand identity and name; Farshore continued to remain firmly committed to their initial mission which is to make every child a happy reader.

Now an established children’s book publisher, Farshore owns imprints for Electric Monkey, Red Shed and more. Electric Monkey is one of the young adult fiction imprints of Farshore books, that features a range of bestselling and award-winning books for readers of 13+ age that are inclusive, immersive, surprising and page-turning reads to appeal to today’s children, teens and young adults.

Through their broad and inclusive portfolio of children’s books, fiction and nonfiction, Farshore Books’ one true purpose is to inspire reading for pleasure amongst children of all ages. Their books are hand-picked for all children; from the most reluctant to the most enthusiastic of readers and bookworms. Farshore Books range between a diverse spectrum of stories for children and teens—from popular established brands to brilliant new series by debutant authors.

Farshore are firm believers of the fact that reading for a hobby can also improve a child’s academic attainment, social skills and their intellectual and emotional health at large; Farshore Books publish titles that are sure to delight children of all ages—from early years to primary, secondary, and beyond. Whatever your child’s age and interest, they’ve got titles that will inspire, challenge, and make them laugh out loud. The Farshore website even has the resources that can help both parents and teachers inspire a love of reading amongst kids at home and in the classroom.

A publication house powered by a unique research machinery and consumer insights; Farshore Books know what children love, and they make sure their books reflect the same. Having published some of the hottest book brands in the world like—Winnie-the-Pooh, TinTin, The Little Princes, The Velveteen Rabbit and The Hundred and One Dalmatians. 

For older readers the Farshore Catalogue has some bestselling titles from authors like Michael Morpurgo, Lemony Snicket, Jim Smith, Andy Stanton, Laura Ellen Anderson, B.B. Alston and Jenny McLachlan. Their list of YA fiction includes award-winners and genre game-changers like Holly Jackson, Michael Grant, David Levithan, Laura Steven, Tahereh Mafi, and Elizabeth Acevedo.

Little Miss 36 Books My Complete Collection Box Set By Roger Hargreaves for children Aged between 5 and 7 is a Farshore book set that is sure to delight your child with their charming antics. Unless you have been living under a rock, you have seen the Little Miss social media trend that took over the internet recently. Clearly, these endearing Little Miss characters are popular with kids and adults alike. The character illustrations are bold, funny and the stories woven around them make The Mr Men and Little Miss books a fun experience for its readers.

All the Little Miss characters; from Little Miss Bossy to Little Miss Naughty—the characters show traits that are fun, relatable and also make good life lessons, which will help you inculcate life values in your child. For instance, Little Miss Bossy likes to boss everybody around, which nobody likes. When the wizard named Wilfred saw how bossy she was, he decided something ought to be done and he introduced her to something even bossier than her. A lesson you might want your kid to learn early in life.

Amelia Fang Series 7 Books Collection Set by Laura Ellen Anderson is yet another Farshore Publication that explores the dark world of Amelia Fang. The series is set in a utopian place called Nocturnia where all things dark reign. Whilst Amelia Fang the vampiress protagonist and her friends take on adventures that are sure to keep the readers intrigued. This is just the book your child needs to trigger their creativity and imagination. For more books by Laura Ellen Anderson check out our extensive range here.

title: Feminism and Feminist Theory
description:
Must-Read Books by Women Writers

Think You Know These Famous Quotes? Think Again.

Some of the most powerful lines in literature have been misattributed, overlooked, or forgotten. But not today! Let’s give these words and the women behind them, the spotlight they deserve.

“There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you.”
Maya Angelou, I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings

“After all, tomorrow is another day.”
Margaret Mitchell, Gone with the Wind

For too long, women’s voices in literature have been sidelined. It’s time to reclaim the words, the writers, and the impact they’ve had on shaping history and the future.

The Feminist Books You NEED on Your Shelf

This isn’t just about reading; it’s about immersing yourself in stories that have shaken the world, challenged the status quo, and sparked conversations that still matter today.

Literary Powerhouses

A Room of One’s Own– Virginia Woolf
Frankenstein– Mary Shelley
I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings– Maya Angelou
The Handmaid’s Tale– Margaret Atwood

Modern Feminist Must-Reads

We Should All Be Feminists– Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
Hood Feminism– Mikki Kendall
The God of Small Things– Arundhati Roy
Invisible Women: Data Bias in a World Designed for Men– Caroline Criado Perez

And because inspiring young readers early is just as important, we’ve got book sets for little ones, too. We’ve partnered with Sweet Cherry Publishing to bring you an exclusive International Women's Day Special: Easy Classics By Sweet Cherry Publishing 10 Books Collection Set of iconic classics written by and about remarkable women. This specially curated Easy Classics set is designed to introduce young readers to these iconic stories in an accessible way. 

Join the Conversation

Women’s words have shaped literature, politics, and culture for centuries; even when they weren’t given credit for it. This collection is for readers who want to:

  • Uncover the real voices behind history-making quotes
  • Explore feminist perspectives through groundbreaking storytelling
  • Read books that challenge, empower, and inspire

Feminist literature isn’t just about looking back, it’s about what comes next. Explore the Collection Now!

title: Fitness and Diet Books
description:
As underrated as this segment is, fitness and diet books are worth the investment and here is why. Contrary to popular belief, the one-size-fits-all approach does not work in fitness. We each have a different body type and each body has different needs with regard to fitness, nutrition and health. What works for one individual might not always work for another. Precisely why, it is important to read up, educate yourselves and get your facts straight before you start following any trending fitness regimen or diet for yourself. 

It is important to keep a check on your body, its functions and its requirements before you indulge yourselves in any particular fitness regimen. For instance if your body has a calcium deficiency your dietary needs will be different. You will have to ensure you are consuming enough of the nutrients your body is deficient in and not just the foods that may be trending at the moment. Similarly, if you have any particular physical ailment you must avoid certain exercises and not just blindly follow the newest fitness trends. 

To make sure you are treating your body right and consuming what it needs without doing it any harm; we have curated a selection of books to help get you into shape and to help you manage what you are eating.

Read on as we list some of the best books on fitness and nutrition that we have found most helpful… 

Lean In 15 The Body Coach Collection 4 Books Set By Joe Wicks All four books in this collection set are focused on different aspects of fitness. The first book; Lean in 15 - The Shift Plan; Joe Wicks, aka The Body Coach, reveals how to shift your body fat to the desired places by eating more and exercising less. The book features a hundred recipes for nutritious, quick-to-prepare meals – including his bad-boy burrito and oaty chicken. Whilst the second book of the set is one of the best workout books for beginners; Lean in 15 - The Shape Plan focuses on building lean muscles and burning fat with 100 delicious recipes and four new workouts to take your fitness to the next level. The next book in this collection; Lean in 15 - The Sustain Plan reveals how to SUSTAIN incredible results while still seeing progress week on week. The book comes fully illustrated with quick-fix healthy meal ideas and workouts for busy people who need to maintain fitness whilst on the go. The last book of the set, Cooking for Family and Friends is a beautifully photographed collection of Joe's easy favourite recipes that are big on flavour and packed with the hero ingredients you need to impress your mates, fuel your workout and burn fat.

Tiny Habits: Why Starting Small Makes Lasting Change Easy by BJ Fogg is all about improving your lifestyle and doing it with ease. Whether it's losing weight, sleeping more, or restoring your work/life balance—the secret is to start small. Tiny Habits advocates starting with quick wins and embedding new, tiny habits into our everyday routines in order to initiate big lifestyle and lasting changes in your life and routine. BJ Fogg has based this theory on twenty years of research and his experience of coaching over 40,000 people to crack the code of habit formation. 

The Slimming Foodie by Pip Payne is one of the best weight loss books based on an award winning blog with the same name. The Slimming Foodie is all about delicious, hearty, home-cooked meals that can work for anyone who is on a slimming journey. The Slimming Foodie philosophy is simple. First and foremost, the recipes have to taste great! But also important is that they use fresh, nourishing, healthy ingredients that are easily available and can be prepared by anyone on a budget.

title: Five Nights at Freddy's Books
description:
The Five Nights at Freddy's book collection, written by Scott Cawthon and Kira Breed-Wrisley, is a series of young adult horror novels based on the popular video game franchise. The books explore the sinister world of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, a fictional restaurant where animatronic animals come to life at night and terrorize the security guard. With a dark and suspenseful plot, vivid descriptions, and unforgettable characters, the Five Nights at Freddy's book collection will leave readers on the edge of their seats.

Another standout feature of the series is its use of suspense and horror to create a truly terrifying experience. The animatronics are presented as more than just machines but as living, breathing creatures that are both fascinating and horrifying. The tension and dread build steadily throughout the series, keeping readers on the edge of their seats and unable to put the books down.

Not sure where to start? Let us give you a few recommendations to help you get started! Or check out our FNaF for beginners blog article. 

To start with, why not check out the Five Nights at Freddy’s 3 Books Collection by Scott Cawthon? During the day, it's a place of joy... But you aren't here during the day. You have the night watch. The first book in the series, Five Nights at Freddy's: The Silver Eyes, follows the story of Charlie, a teenager who returns to her hometown to attend a memorial for her childhood friend, who was murdered at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza years ago. Along with her friends, Charlie decides to explore the abandoned restaurant, but they soon discover that the animatronics are still active and more dangerous than ever. title: Folk of the Air Books
description:
The Folk of the Air series is an enchanting trilogy of books written by the talented author Holly Black. It consists of three books, each of which follows the story of Jude, a mortal girl who finds herself immersed in the magical and treacherous world of the fae.

The first book in the series is called The Cruel Prince, and it introduces readers to the world of the fae and the complex politics and power dynamics that exist within it. Jude is a human who was raised in the faerie world, and she dreams of one day earning a place among the fae despite their prejudice against mortals. Her life changes when she finds herself embroiled in a dangerous power struggle that threatens to tear the faerie realm apart.

The second book, The Wicked King, continues Jude's story as she navigates the treacherous waters of faerie politics and tries to keep her hold on power. The stakes are higher than ever in this book, as Jude is forced to make difficult choices and confront the true nature of the fae.

The final book in the series, The Queen of Nothing, brings the story to a thrilling conclusion as Jude faces off against her most dangerous enemies and fights to protect the people she loves. Throughout the series, readers are treated to a thrilling blend of political intrigue, romance, and magic as they explore the faerie world alongside Jude.

How the King of Elfhame Learned to Hate Stories is a companion novel to the Folk of the Air series, written by Holly Black. The book tells the story of Cardan, the charismatic but cruel king of the faeries, and how he came to be the way he is. Through a series of interconnected stories, readers are given a glimpse into Cardan's past and the events that shaped him into the enigmatic and complex character that he is in the main series. With its richly detailed world-building and compelling characters, How the King of Elfhame Learned to Hate Stories is a must-read for fans of the Folk of the Air series.

One of the things that make the Folk of the Air series so compelling is the way that Holly Black brings the world of the fae to life. Her writing is immersive and richly detailed, painting a vivid picture of the faerie realm and the creatures that inhabit it. From the glittering courts of the fae to the dark and dangerous forests that surround them, the world of the Folk of the Air is one that readers won't soon forget.

Another strength of the series is the characters that populate it. Jude is a complex and compelling protagonist who is both strong-willed and vulnerable, and her struggles to navigate the world of the fae while staying true to her mortal roots are at the heart of the story. The supporting cast is equally well-drawn, with a range of characters that run the gamut from scheming and manipulative to loyal and brave.

In addition to its compelling story and characters, the Folk of the Air series has also been praised for its exploration of themes like power, identity, and belonging. As Jude navigates the treacherous waters of faerie politics, she is forced to confront the true nature of power and the lengths to which people will go to obtain it. Her struggle to find her place in a world that doesn't fully accept her is also a theme that will resonate with many readers.

Overall, the Folk of the Air series is a must-read for fans of fantasy and YA literature. With its richly detailed world-building, compelling characters, and gripping storylines, it's a series that will keep readers on the edge of their seats from beginning to end.

About the Author: Holly Black

Holly Black was born in West Long Branch, New Jersey, in 1971, and she has been writing since she was a child. She studied English and American literature at The College of New Jersey, and she later went on to earn an MFA in fiction from Rutgers University.

Holly's career as a writer began in earnest in the early 2000s, when she started publishing books for children and young adults. Some of her early works include Tithe, Valiant, and Ironside, which are all part of the Modern Faerie Tales series. She also wrote the Spiderwick Chronicles with Tony DiTerlizzi, which went on to become a bestselling series and was adapted into a movie.

What are Folklore & Mythology and How Are They Different?

If you're excited about this genre but need to become more familiar with folkloristics, don't worry—we've got you covered! 

Folklore refers to the traditional knowledge and beliefs passed down through generations, usually by word of mouth. Often recognised as fictional tales, these stories serve as commentary on a culture's customs and beliefs. A few famous works that can help you follow are Pandora's Box, The Arthurian Legends, Sleeping Beauty, and The Hare and Tortoise.

On the other hand, mythology is closely tied to a culture's religion and can be considered sacred by some. Myths are narratives a society regards as true stories explaining the natural world, human nature, and the divine. They often feature gods, goddesses, and supernatural beings, reflecting the spiritual beliefs of a culture. Also, unlike folklore, myths are seen as profound and venerable.

title: Frances Lincoln Children's Books
description:
An independent English publisher based in the UK; Frances Elisabeth Rosemary Lincoln first began to publish books for children in 1977. She went out on her own as an independent publisher, publishing both under her own name and in co-editions. The firm she founded continued as Frances Lincoln Publishers, based in London, until 2018.

In August 2011, The Quarto Group acquired Frances Lincoln Publishers, making it the Frances Lincoln Children's Book imprint. The firm has always been known for the list of illustrated gardening books it published, and for its illustrated children's books. Among these are David Litchfield's The Bear and the Piano, which won the 2016 Waterstones Children's Book Prize for Illustrated Books, and Lizzy Stewart's There's a Tiger in the Garden, which won the same prize in 2017.

Today, FLCB boasts of having sold over a multimillion copies of bestselling titles like; Little People, Big Dreams series and the New York Times Best Seller, This Book Is Anti-Racist. FLCB is regarded as one of the world’s most respected creators of picture books, illustrated books and gift titles that celebrate cultural diversity, as well as narrative nonfiction. 

Given its reputation for quality literature, Frances Lincoln Children’s Books, UK is known to work only with the world’s most innovative illustrators and (visual) storytellers and the same is evident in the books they publish. From high-quality picture books, multicultural books, poetry, and information books, FLCB has some of the best illustrated children’s literature to their credit. 

Needless to say, the FLCB’s bestselling book list finds strong support from bookshops, libraries, international institutions and also us at Books2Door. Precisely why we have stocked up on all of FLCB’s books for children and young adults. Here are three of our absolute favourites…

A New York Times’ Bestseller that’s perfect for young adults to learn about racism and tolerance; This Book Is Anti-Racist : 20 lessons on how to wake up, take action, and do the work is a guided journal with more than 50 activities to support the reader’s anti-racism journey. 

Allow your soon-to-be young adult to learn about social identities, the history of racism and resistance against it, and how they can use their anti-racist lens and voice to move the world toward equity and liberation. The book allows the readers to gain a deeper understanding of their anti-racist self as they progress through 20 chapters that spark introspection, reveal the origins of racism that we are still experiencing and gives its readers the courage and power to undo it. Each chapter builds on the previous one as the readers learn more about themselves and racial oppression. 20 activities get the reader thinking whilst also helping ‘em grow their knowledge. All one needs is a pen and paper. 

Another great FLCB book to teach your child about the history of travel, migration and how it has impacted our world is A World Full of Journeys and Migrations by Quarto Generic. Since the dawn of time, people have travelled to distant lands for many different reasons; to escape war, famine or injustice, to find work, or to simply see new sights and have an adventure. But everyone who migrates does it to seek a brighter future. A World Full of Journeys is an illustrated book which tells some of the most fascinating stories of migration throughout history. From the very first humans who left Africa almost 70,000 years ago and moved around the world, to immigrants welcomed to America at Ellis Island, this book is packed with fascinating tales of human triumph told through beautiful illustrations. 


The first book in the best-selling, award-winning 'Bear and the Piano' trilogy; The Bear and the Piano by David Litchfield is a great book to teach your child the values of home and family. Get the trilogy for your child and allow them to learn important life lessons from the protagonist bear. One day, a young bear stumbles upon something he has never seen before in the forest. As time passes, he teaches himself how to play the strange instrument, and eventually the beautiful sounds are heard by a father and son who are picnicking in the woods. The bear goes with them on an incredible journey to New York, where his piano playing makes him a huge star. He has fame, fortune and all the music in the world, but he misses the friends and family he has left behind. A moving tale of exploration and belonging from best-selling and critically acclaimed author David Litchfield.

description:
Discover the Magic of Frank Cottrell-Boyce: Children's Laureate 2024

At Books2Door, we are passionate about celebrating the world of books and publishing. We're excited to introduce you to our special collection page dedicated to Frank Cottrell-Boyce, the Children's Laureate of 2024.

Join us as we dive into the dreamy world of one of the most beloved authors in children's literature, renowned for his captivating storytelling and unforgettable characters.

But first, what is the Children's Laureate?

The Children's Laureate is a prestigious title awarded biennially to an eminent writer or illustrator of children's books. This role aims to promote the importance of literacy, reading, and children's literature through various initiatives and public engagements. The laureate's mission is to inspire young readers and foster a love for books among children. Simply put, it is like a national ambassador, like Malala Yousafzai. Although she is not an official ambassador in the diplomatic sense, she is a well-known advocate for education and children's rights globally.

What Do They Do?

Children's Laureates engage in numerous activities, including:

- Advocating for children's literature and literacy.

- Conducting school visits, workshops, and public readings.

- Creating programmes and campaigns to encourage reading.

- Collaborating with libraries, schools, and literary organisations.

Why Frank Cottrell-Boyce is the Children's Laureate 2024

Frank Cottrell-Boyce, renowned for his innovative storytelling and engaging narratives, has been honoured as the Children's Laureate for 2024. It's no surprise, but a well-deserved choice. His words resonate with young readers, combining humour, adventure, and heartfelt moments that leave a lasting impact. Frank's dedication to inspiring children through his books and his commitment to promoting literacy make him a perfect fit for this esteemed role.

Who is Frank, and where do you know him from? 

Frank Cottrell-Boyce, the renowned author, is not just that! He is also a screenwriter who is celebrated for his innovative storytelling and engaging narratives. You might know him from his acclaimed books such as Millions, adapted into a successful film, and Cosmic. This thrilling adventure has captivated young readers. He also wrote the screenplay for the opening ceremony of the London 2012 Olympics, the spectacular event watched by millions worldwide. Also, HE PENNED AN EPISODE FOR THE BELOVED SERIES DOCTOR WHO!

At the Books2Door office, we had a real 'awe' moment when we realised it was him!

title: Game of Thrones Books
description:
A Song of Ice and Fire Series 
Welcome to Westeros, where you will face a cruel and violent battle between families for the throne. George R.R. Martin’s fantasy epic is arguably one of the most iconic and influential since J R.R. Tolkien’s Lord of the Rings series. 

HBO’s groundbreaking adaptation of George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire series started in 2011 and ended in 2019. The series eventually overtook the books as George R.R. Martin is yet to finish writing them. Many fans were left unhappy with how the show ended and so are eagerly awaiting Martin’s conclusion to A Song of Ice and Fire, which he has said will end over two books called The Winds of Winter and A Dream of Spring. 

The Books in Order 
The first book in the series, A Game of Thrones, was published in 1996 and sets the scene for the horror to come. King Robert Baratheon calls forth his friend and warden of The North, Eddard Stark, to become his advisor, hand of the king. From this, a series of events result in the three main houses Stark, Lannister and Targaryen fighting for their right to the throne of the seven kingdoms. 

A Clash of Kings (1998) was the next to be released and saw the civil war unleashed in the seven kingdoms of Westeros. Robert Baratheon’s son, Joffrey, currently sits on the Iron throne, but Robert's two brothers, Renly and Stannis, have a claim to the throne. Meanwhile, two regions attempt to withdraw themselves from Westeros, with Robb Stark being declared King of the North and Balon Greyjoy declared himself King of the Iron Islands. 

A Storm of Swords (2000) tensions are rising as Robbs' army returns to Riverrun after a successful battle against the Lannisters’ army in the west, Jaime and Brienne are captured by the Boltons all while the Lannisters have new allies, the Tyrells. This book builds up to even more anguish, including the catastrophic red wedding. 

The fourth book in the series is A Feast for Crows (2005). At this point, The War of the Five Kings is slowly coming to an end. The book journeys through the different kingdoms with Sansa hiding in The Vale with LittleFinger, Arya training with The Faceless Men in Braavos and Cersei facing difficulty as she tries to help her young son, the newly appointed King. The tensions are rising as the aftermath of the war begins. 

The fifth instalment A Dance with Dragons (2011) sees The Wall occupied by Stannis Baratheon and Jon Snow as the newly appointed Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. With a total of eighteen different points of view, A Dance with Dragons is able to show the slow build-up to the eventual final battle for the throne. 

About the Author 
George R.R. Martin is an American novelist, screenwriter, producer and short story writer. His work is highly regarded and greatly appreciated by fans across the world. He is currently writing the final two instalments of A Song of Ice and Fire series. 

For fans of Game of Thrones, be sure to check out our range of J.R.R Tolkien books and Robin Hobb books.

title: Garfield Books
description:
Introducing the purr-fect collection of Garfield books, where laughter and mischief collide in the delightful world of everyone's favourite lasagna-loving cat. Join Garfield, Odie, Jon Arbuckle, and a colourful cast of characters in a series of hilarious adventures that will tickle your funny bone and warm your heart. This collection is a must-have for Garfield fans of all ages, bringing together the beloved comic strips and stories that have entertained millions around the world.

At the centre of the Garfield series is the lovable and lazy orange tabby cat, Garfield. Known for his insatiable appetite for lasagna and disdain for Mondays, Garfield's witty one-liners and sarcastic remarks have made him an iconic figure in the comic strip world. With his unique blend of humour and charm, Garfield delights readers as he navigates the ups and downs of his daily life, often taking naps, avoiding exercise, and outsmarting his hapless owner, Jon Arbuckle.

Speaking of Jon Arbuckle, he is Garfield's well-meaning but often bumbling owner. Jon's attempts to win the heart of the lovely veterinarian, Liz, are frequently foiled by Garfield's mischievous antics. Jon's eternal optimism and unwavering love for his pets make him endearing, and his interactions with Garfield and Odie provide many comedic moments throughout the series. Read all about the thrilling adventures of everyone’s favourite orange tabby in the Garfield Fat Cat Pack (Volume 20) by Jim Davis.

Odie, the lovable but dim-witted dog, is Garfield's loyal sidekick and the source of much amusement. Garfield often takes advantage of Odie's naivety, resulting in hilarious pranks and slapstick humour. Despite their differences, the unlikely duo forms an amusing and heartwarming friendship, adding depth and warmth to the series.

The Garfield books collection brings together a treasure trove of comic strips and stories that showcase the humour and wit of creator Jim Davis. From Garfield's witty observations on life to his hilarious encounters with other animals, each page is filled with laughter and relatable moments that will resonate with readers of all ages. Check out how the loveable tabby because so popular, entertaining millions of people with The Creation of Garfield Book by Rodney McCance.  This book explores our relationship with Garfield, Jon and Odie and how Davis' characters have become such an integral part of American pop culture over the decades. The Garfield series encompasses various themes, including Garfield's obsession with food, his disdain for exercise, and his quest for the perfect nap. Whether he's battling against the scale, plotting against his loathed neighbour, Nermal, or dreaming up elaborate schemes to outwit Odie, Garfield's escapades never fail to entertain.

Garfield's popularity lies not only in the amusing scenarios but also in the relatable and endearing aspects of his character. Readers of all ages can identify with his love of comfort, his aversion to Mondays, and his knack for finding humour in everyday situations. With his quick wit and laid-back attitude, Garfield has become an iconic figure that has captured the hearts of millions worldwide.

In this collection, readers will find volumes of Garfield's comic strips, showcasing the timeless humour that has made the series a classic. Dive into the hilarious world of Garfield as you flip through page after page of side-splitting gags, clever wordplay, and Garfield's indomitable charm.

Whether you're a long-time fan or discovering Garfield for the first time, this collection is a delightful addition to any bookshelf. Join Garfield and his companions on their comical escapades and let their antics brighten your day. The Garfield books collection is a guaranteed recipe for laughter and enjoyment that will leave you hungry for more.

title: Gege Akutami Manga
description:
In the vast landscape of manga and anime, certain creators emerge as titans, shaping the industry with their unparalleled imagination and storytelling prowess. Among these luminaries stands Gege Akutami, a pen name for the visionary and mysterious mangaka whose creative genius has captivated millions around the globe.  At Books2Door, we are proud to offer a curated selection of Gege Akutami's works

 Born on August 23, 1992, in Tokyo, Japan, Akutami embarked on his journey into the world of manga with a passion that would ultimately redefine the genre. From a young age, Akutami displayed an insatiable appetite for storytelling, often immersing himself in the rich tapestry of Japanese folklore and mythology. These early influences would become the cornerstone of his distinctive narrative style, blending the supernatural with elements of horror, action, and profound philosophical inquiry.

Jujutsu Kaisen
Akutami's meteoric rise to prominence began with the serialisation of his debut work, Jujutsu Kaisen, in the pages of Weekly Shonen Jump in 2018. Set in a world where cursed spirits lurk in the shadows, waiting to prey on the unsuspecting, Jujutsu Kaisen follows the journey of Yuji Itadori, a high school student thrust into a perilous battle against the forces of darkness. Fueled by a potent blend of intricate world-building, dynamic character development, and pulse-pounding action sequences, the series quickly amassed a devoted following, propelling Akutami to the forefront of the manga scene.

What sets Akutami apart as a storyteller is his ability to imbue his characters with depth and complexity, grappling with themes of morality, sacrifice, and the inherent darkness of the human psyche. Whether it's the enigmatic sorcerer Gojo Satoru, whose unyielding resolve masks a profound sense of loneliness, or the tormented antagonist Sukuna, whose insatiable thirst for power belies a tragic past, each character in Jujutsu Kaisen is rendered with nuance and empathy, inviting readers to ponder the true nature of heroism and villainy.

Beyond its captivating narrative, Jujutsu Kaisen has garnered widespread acclaim for its stunning artwork, courtesy of Akutami's masterful penmanship. From the visceral intensity of its battle scenes to the haunting beauty of its supernatural entities, every panel is a testament to Akutami's boundless creativity and meticulous attention to detail.

Today, Akutami stands as one of the most influential figures in contemporary manga, inspiring a new generation of creators to push the boundaries of storytelling and artistic expression. As his magnum opus continues to enthral audiences worldwide, one thing remains abundantly clear: Gege Akutami's indelible legacy is only just beginning.

title: George R.R. Martin Books
description:
George R.R. Martin: A Literary Journey
When it comes to epic fantasy literature, few names stand as tall as George R.R. Martin. A modern-day literary maestro, Martin has captivated the world with his vivid imagination and intricately woven tales, most notably with his A Song of Ice and Fire series, better known as Game Of Thrones. Purchase George R.R. Martin's work here at Books2Door and immerse yourself in the genius of this legendary author and the gripping world he has crafted.

George Raymond Richard Martin, born on September 20, 1948, in Bayonne, New Jersey, began his journey as a writer at an early age. He was an avid reader, devouring the works of fantasy giants like J.R.R. Tolkien, which would later inspire his storytelling.

With the release of The A Song of Ice and Fire series, Martin truly made his mark. The series began with Game of Thrones in 1996, introducing readers to the sprawling, complex world of Westeros, where noble houses vied for power, and a looming threat of winter and darkness lay just beyond the Wall. 

Martin's distinctive storytelling style is a revelation, defying traditional fantasy tropes and delivering a narrative where no character, no matter how beloved, is safe from the cruel twists of fate. Over the years, George R.R. Martin has become renowned for his meticulous world-building and his ability to breathe life into a vast array of characters, each with their own motives and complexities. His ability to blur the lines between good and evil makes us question the morality of his characters.

Game of Thrones: A World of Intrigue and Betrayal
The Game of Thrones series, adapted for television by HBO, has become a cultural phenomenon, and for good reason. At Books2Door, we're thrilled to offer the complete collection of Martin's epic saga.

Set in the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos, Game of Thrones is a tale of political machinations, brutal power struggles, and supernatural forces. It features a sprawling cast of characters, including the ambitious Starks, the cunning Lannisters, the exiled Targaryens, and many more. As each house vies for the Iron Throne, alliances are formed and betrayed, secrets are unveiled, and unexpected heroes and villains emerge.

The series is not just a story of epic battles and dragons but also a profound exploration of human nature, morality, and the consequences of power. The depth of Martin's storytelling shines through on every page, making it impossible to predict who will survive and who will meet a gruesome end.

With our Game of Thrones books collection, you can dive into this richly detailed world and experience the story as it was initially conceived by George R.R. Martin, complete with intricate plot twists and morally grey characters. Whether you're a fan of the TV series or new to the world of Westeros, these books offer a fresh perspective and a deeper understanding of the complex narrative.
