title: Granta
description:
Granta, the magazine and Granta Books, the publisher share their mission to discover and publish the best of new literary voices—fiction, memoirs, reportage and poetry—from across the world.

Whilst the magazine was founded in 1889 by students at Cambridge University as The Granta, a periodical of student politics, it was transformed into a literary quarterly in 1979 and ten years later into, Granta Books, the publication. Which had originally set out to publish six books a year, distributed and promoted by Penguin. 

In 1997 however, Granta Books was expanded by its previous owner, Rea Hederman, publisher of the New York Review of Books. Following which, the publication saw exponential growth. Today, Granta Books publishes around thirty new titles a year, providing authors with the intimacy of a small, passionate and creative team, while consistently punching above its weight in review coverage, prizes, cultural impact and sales.

Most celebrated for its focus on issues of the young and for publishing the most important voices of our generation—Granta has managed to make a deep impact on the world’s literary landscape. The Granta books catalogue has twenty-seven Nobel Prize laureates.

A journey into the soul of a nation; A Passage North by Anuk Arudpragasam begins with a message informing Krishan that his grandmother's former caregiver has died. As Krishan makes the train journey from the Sri Lankan capital into the war-torn Northern Province for the funeral, he travels into the soul of a country devastated by civil war. Written with precision and grace, the book is a luminous meditation on time and consciousness, race and national identity, and a poignant exploration of the unattainable distances between who we are and what we seek. 

My Phantoms by Gwendoline Riley is an insightful, compelling and painfully funny account of a family strained to breaking point; a reckoning with the damage we do over the course of a life. Helen Grant has always been a mystery to her daughter. Twice-divorced, with few friends, her desire to join in is matched only by her need to stand apart. As Bridget looks back over their fractious relationship, she is forced to confront the cruelties inflicted on both sides. 

In yet another gritty tale by Granta Books—Convenience Store Woman by Sayaka Murata is an unconventional story of a woman with unconventional choices. Keiko is 36 years old. She's never had a boyfriend, and she's been working in the same supermarket for eighteen years. Keiko's family wishes she'd get a proper job. Her friends wonder why she won't get married. But Keiko knows what makes her happy, and she's not going to let anyone come between her and her convenience store. 

*Convenience Store Woman comes in three different colours; the colour you receive will be chosen at random*

title: Graphic Non-Fiction & True Stories
description:
Graphic nonfiction and true stories are a rich sub-genre within creative nonfiction. An exciting new literary genre that tells real-world stories in the creative, graphic format.

Packed to the brim with artsy illustrations and real stories; non-fiction graphic novels are a league of their own. From creatively metaphoric memoirs with emotional and political subtexts to graphic adaptations of history—the genre is rich with varied subject matter, sensitive emotional subjects, clever political satires and of course stunningly immersive artwork.

If you are a nonfiction reader and someone that enjoys storytelling through sequential art; then graphic nonfiction will certainly be your thing. Now that we know this is in fact the genre for you; let’s find you something that will reflect your taste.

Sapiens A Graphic History, Volume 2: The Pillars of Civilization by Yuval Noah Harari If you are a fan of the Harari books then this 2nd Volume of a beautifully illustrated graphic history of humankind, based on Yuval Noah Harari's multi-million copy bestselling phenomenon, is just for you. When nomadic Homo sapiens settled to live in one place, they started working harder and harder. But why didn't they get a better life in return? In The Pillars of Civilization, Yuval Noah Harari and his companions including Prof. Saraswati and Dr. Fiction travel the length and breadth of human history to investigate how the Agricultural Revolution changed the course of human evolution and society forever. Discover how wheat took over the world, how war, famine, disease and inequality became a part of the human condition, and why we might only have ourselves to blame. A radical, witty and colourful retelling of the story of humankind, adapted from Yuval Noah Harari's Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind, Volume 2 can be read as a standalone or as a follow-up to Volume 1, The Birth of Humankind.

Palestine by Joe Sacco In late l991 and early 1992, at the time of the first Intifada, Joe Sacco spent two months with the Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, travelling and taking notes. Upon returning to the United States he started writing and drawing Palestine, which combines the journalistic techniques of eyewitness reportage with the medium of graphic storytelling to explore this complex, emotionally hefty situation. He captures the heart of the Palestinian experience in one unforgettable image after another, with great insights and remarkable humour. The nine-issue comics series won a 1996 American Book Award. It is now published for the first time in one volume, befitting its status as one of the great classics in graphic non-fiction. If you are a nonfiction reader that is intrigued by the Palestinian condition and want to read up every journalistic account of the suffrage then this is the book you cannot miss.

If you are someone that has been conflicted about the subject; Queer: A Graphic History by Meg-John Barker may just be the book you need. From identity politics and gender roles to privilege and exclusion, Queer is a ground-breaking graphic novel for adults that explores how we came to view sex, gender and sexuality in the ways that we do. How these ideas get tangled up with our culture and our understanding of biology, psychology and sexology; and how these views have been disputed and challenged. Along the way we look at key landmarks that shift our perspective of what qualifies as 'normal'—Alfred Kinsey's view of sexuality as a spectrum, Judith Butler's view of gendered behaviour as a performance, the play Wicked, or moments in Casino Royale when we're invited to view James Bond with the kind of desiring gaze usually directed at female bodies in mainstream media. Presented in a brilliantly engaging and witty style, this is a unique portrait of the universe of queer thinking and the many theories about gender and sexuality.

title: Graphic Novels - Genre Fiction
description:
There are many types of Graphic Novels across several genres— fiction, non-fiction, history, fantasy fiction et al. If we were to analyse graphic novel vs comics: graphic novels are fairly similar to comic books in that they also use sequential art and illustrations to tell stories along with the craft of storytelling and character of prose text. Unlike comic books however, graphic novels are stand-alone stories with more complex plots. Although collections of short stories that have been previously published as individual comic books can also qualify as a graphic novel.

Whilst there are several genres and subgenres within Graphic Novels; we have dedicated this collection to the rich genre that is Graphic Novels genre fiction. Which has several sub-genres like superhero fantasy fiction stories, historic fiction and science fiction amongst others. 

Take a look at our selection of recommended, new and bestselling graphic novels, genre fiction—from sitcom adaptations to must-read essential classics like Heartstopper. Innovative, artsy and unlike anything else; here are some of the best Graphic novels, genre fiction…

Scott Pilgrim 6 Books Collection by Bryan Lee O'Malley for young adults is a graphic novel, fiction series with 6 volumes. Scott Pilgrim's Precious Little Life: Volume 1 sees Scott living his best life. He's 23 years old, he's in a rock band, he's "between jobs," and he's dating a cute high school girl. Nothing could possibly go wrong, unless a seriously mind-blowing, dangerously fashionable, rollerblading delivery girl named Ramona Flowers starts cruising through his dreams and sailing by him at parties. Will Scott Pilgrim's awesome life get turned upside-down? Will he have to face Ramona's seven evil ex-boyfriends in battle? The short answer is yes. The long answer is Scott Pilgrim’s 6 steller volumes. In the second volume Scott Pilgrim Vs The World; Scott Pilgrim is seen with two girls on the go. When he's with Knives Chau, he feels like he can erase his past and start over. When he's with Ramona Flowers, he's ready to accept all that, grow up and move on. But like all adult relationships, Ramona comes with baggage and in her case, seven evil ex-boyfriends, showing up one by one to challenge Scott for the right to date her. What happens when Knives and Ramona meet? What happens when Scott's own ex-flames get thrown in? How will Scott deal? Which girl will he choose? Fights, drama ensue as secrets get revealed in the following four volumes. 

The Sandman Complete Collection by Neil Gaiman & Others 4 Books Set for young adults aged Age 17+ Enter the beautiful and poignant world of Neil Gaiman's The Sandman. From the mind that brought us Coraline, American Gods, and, along with Sir Terry Pratchett, Good Omens. This fiction graphic novel series explores the lives of seven metaphysical entities, collectively called The Endless. The main character of The Sandman is Dream, also known as Morpheus, and over the course of the series, you meet the rest of The Endless, Destiny, Death, Desire, Despair, Delirium, and Destruction. The series takes inspiration from different mythologies, folklore, and religions. Making it the perfect combination of fantasy, horror, and sci-fi. These beautifully illustrated graphic novels would make the perfect gift for any fan of Gaiman's work or fans of the DC comic universe. The artists that helped shape this world into the visual masterpiece we see today are Sam Kieth, Mike Dringenberg, Kelley Jones, and so many more. Combined with Gaiman's writing, these creative minds have created a literary world beyond our imaginations.

title: Graphic Novels History & Criticism
description:
Graphic Novels History and Criticism is a subgenre of graphic literature which has books that give an overview of the history and cultural impact of graphic novels and comic books on the social fabric including analysis and criticism of the artistic and graphic narrative .

Since graphic novels rose to prominence some 50 odd years ago, it has become one of the fastest growing literary/artistic genres globally. The evolution of comic books into graphic novels and the consequent development of this art form into several diverse subgenres like anime comics, superhero comics, memoirs, nonfiction graphic novels amongst others has made it an immensely popular literary genre worldwide.

Comic books and graphic novels were once considered a form of lowbrow popular culture. Today however they are a global phenomenon and have Hollywood blockbusters adapted from them and have some of the best selling video games made after them. Literary scholars have immersed themselves in this creative discourse, the practices of this art and its subculture to provide a social history of the genre in the past few decades. Several writers have used a theoretical framework to examine the construction of comic book culture and its cult following—analysing a wide range of texts, subtexts, artistic representation, and narrative strategies from both theoretical and historical perspectives. 

As a result, us comic book nerds now have books on the history and criticism of graphic novels that examine the theories and histories of the graphic narrative as one of the most versatile forms of storytelling in contemporary literature. Here are a select few books that have managed to give us analytical and theoretical insights into this very intriguing genre.

Scott McCloud's Understanding Comics is one such seminal examination of comic art: its rich history, surprising technical components, and major cultural significance. Highly reviewed by industry luminaries like Neil Gaiman and Art Spiegelman; Understanding Comics is an international bestseller classic on storytelling and visual communication. A book, we think you should definitely read if you are an avid reader and follower of the graphic novels and comic books genre.

The Comics of Charles Schulz : The Good Grief of Modern Life by Jared Gardner is another theoretical examination and collection of essays on the work of the creator of the immensely popular Peanuts comic strip. Despite Schulz's celebrity, few scholarly books on his work and career have been published. This collection serves as a foundation for future study not only of Charles Schulz (1922-2000) but, more broadly, of the understudied medium of newspaper comics. Schulz's Peanuts ran for a half century, during which time he drew the strip and its characters to express keen observations on postwar American life and culture. As Peanuts' popularity grew, Schulz had opportunities to shape the iconography, style, and philosophy of modern life in ways he never could have imagined when he began the strip in 1950. Edited by leading scholars Jared Gardner and Ian Gordon, this volume ranges over a spectrum of Schulz's accomplishments and influence, touching on everything from cartoon aesthetics to the marketing of global fast food. Philosophy, ethics, and cultural history all come into play. As the broad interdisciplinary range of this volume makes clear, Peanuts offers countless possibilities for study and analysis. From many perspectives-including childhood studies, ethnic studies, health and exercise studies, as well as sociology. The Comics of Charles Schulz offers the most comprehensive and diverse study of the most influential cartoonist during the second half of the twentieth century. 

Gender and the Superhero Narrative by Michael Goodrum

The contributions assembled in this book question the applicability of the gender narrative within the subgenre that is superhero comics. The explosive popularity of San Diego's Comic-Con, Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Rogue One, and Netflix's Jessica Jones and Luke Cage all signal the tidal change in superhero narratives and mainstreaming of what were once considered niche interests. Yet just as these areas have become more openly inclusive to an audience beyond heterosexual white men, there has also been an intense backlash, most famously in 2015's Gamergate controversy, when the tension between feminist bloggers, misogynistic gamers, and internet journalists came forth. 

The place for gender in superhero narratives now represents a sort of battleground, with important changes in the industry at stake. These seismic shifts-both in the creation of superhero media and in their critical and reader reception-need reassessment not only of the role of women in comics, but also of how society conceives masculinity. Gender and the Superhero Narrative launches ten essays that explore the point where social justice meets the Justice League. Ranging from comics such as Ms. Marvel, Batwoman: Elegy, and Bitch Planet to video games, Netflix, and cosplay, this volume builds a platform for important voices in comics research, engaging with controversy and community to provide deeper insight and thus inspire change.

title: Graphic Novels, Manga, Comic Books & Strips
description:
Did you know the modern form of comics has been traced back to the nineteenth century? However, we’ve arguably been creating stories using images since the first cave paintings. Manga, newspaper cartoons, comic strips, comic books, graphic novels, webcomics- across the years, sequential art have taken several forms. They can be fictional, factual, or somewhere in between. Some are serious, some are hilarious, and they can cater to a wide range of reading abilities.

We’ve pulled together some of the very best manga, comic books and graphic novels from North America, Europe, the UK and Japan in this collection. Whether you're a dedicated anime fan, superhero stan, or looking to read your first comic, we've got something for you here.

Graphic novels

Everything is bigger in North America, and that includes comics. The comic book has evolved from a disposable commodity to the cornerstone of billion-dollar companies. Comic artists and writers have flocked from all over the world to be a part of the industry. The superhero was invented there, a character-type that has taken over popular culture.

It’s not all business. The form and term graphic novel was invented in the USA as a way to help legitimize serious, groundbreaking work like the Pulitzer Prize-winning Maus by Art Spiegelman. America’s also the home of underground, alternative, and independent comics that challenge and redefine the mainstream.

One of the most popular indie comics of recent years is actually Canadian. The Complete Scott Pilgrim by Bryan Lee O’Malley is heavily influenced by manga and video games culture but is entirely original. Scott Pilgrim is 23 years old. He’s in a band, doesn’t have a job, and his girlfriend’s in high school. His precious little life is turned upside down when he meets delivery girl Ramona Flowers. To win her love, he must defeat her seven evil exes and maybe even grow up. The series was filmed as Scott Pilgrim vs. the World by superstar director Edgar Wright, and it’s turning out to be a modern classic.

Manga

The term manga first came into use right at the end of the eighteenth century. Before World War II, the illustrations followed Japanese artistic traditions. However, the influence of the US occupation immediately after the war revolutionised the art form. Cinematic techniques, American culture, and television led to popular characters and series such as Astro Boy. Popular manga series are regularly turned into anime - film and television cartoons - which completes the circle of influence.

Manga is loved not only for its dynamic art style, but the wide range of stories produced for audiences of all ages and genders. The works trickled into the west through the twentieth century, with popular series such as Akira, Dragon Ball, Sailor Moon and Ghost in the Shell leading the charge. The popularity of Japanese culture exploded after the international success of Pokemon, and now many manga series are international bestsellers. Right now we're selling the hilarious Assassination Classroom: Complete Box Set. Grab it now before it sells out!

British comic strips & characters

The first comic magazine is reported to have been published in Glasgow in 1826. Since then, the UK has had a fine tradition of comics that have become global phenomenons. From The Beano to 2000AD, Bunty to Commando, Eagle to The Phoenix, Britain has published a wide range of different styles and genres in comic form. Many of the most highly regarded writers and illustrators come from Britain, including Alan Moore, Neil Gaiman, Grant Morrison, and Posy Simmonds.

The UK is also home to many memorable comics characters, like Dennis the Menace and Judge Dredd. One of these is Roy Race, better known as Roy of the Rovers. Originally appearing in Tiger in September 1954, he was published in various magazines for nearly sixty years. Now, Roy is back. Roy of the Rovers: 3 Book Collection by Rob Williams and Ben Willsher features a modern Melchester Rovers, broke and languishing at the bottom of League Two. Can Roy help turn the club around?

Bandes dessinées albums

Mainland Europe brought the world Rodolphe Töpffer, the man dubbed “the father of comic strips.” 175 years after his death, it’s still the home of some of the world’s best comics art. This is particularly true of the Francophone sphere, which calls the medium Bandes dessinées, sold in books called albums.

France brings us Asterix, which was created by Goscinny & Uderzo. In these hilarious adventures, Asterix, Obelix, and the warriors of his Gaulish tribe are the last hold-out against the Roman Empire. The Complete Asterix contains 39 albums, which should keep you busy until the Romans come back.

Belgium is most famous for master cartoonist Hergé, who is best known for The Adventures of Tintin. We stock the boy reporter's most famous adventures individually and in two box sets. The Adventures of Tintin: 90th Anniversary is a box set of twenty-three paperback books, printed close to their original size. The Tintin Collection: The Adventures of Tintin (Compact Edition) reprints the series in eight hardback volumes.

Comics are some of our bestsellers at Book2Door. We’re always bringing in new stock, so keep an eye out for our latest products.

title: Greek Mythology Books 🔱
description:
Greek mythology in essence is the body of ancient myths and teachings that belong to the ancient Greeks, concerning their gods, legends and heroes, their culture and their ritual practices. This body of ancient Greek myths and legends together form Greek Mythology literature. The genre includes books varying from non-fiction to fiction. However, there are two main kinds of Greek Mythology Books available for readers who enjoy this genre. Retellings of the ancient Greek Myths that have become modern classics and legends by some of the most renowned authorities on classic writing.

What are Ancient Greek Myths?

Ancient Greek Myths were basically a way of explaining the world to a more primitive people who did not have access to science and as a result didn’t understand the happenings of the world. The primitive people did not have any explanation for the sun rising, the moon changing its size, the natural disasters like earthquakes and floods. So it was easier for them to make up myths about these occurrences and blame them on God. These Greek myths give us fascinating insights into the beliefs and culture of ancient Greece.

What is most fascinating about Greek mythology and their literature however is how their perception of God is terribly human. For instance; Zeus cheats and lies and he is the most appalling serial adulterer. Another fascinating aspect about Greek Mythology is how their stories also tend to set out the ideal behaviour commandments and the consequences of certain actions. It is the same as the Ten Commandments—”Thou Shalt not…” or something terrible will happen. So, for instance, Ixion, who committed the murder, ends up in a fiery pit, tied to a wheel, forever revolving, as a punishment. 

Greek Myths therefore also serve as a guide to life as well as make interesting cultural tales. If you are the kind of reader that wants to immerse yourself into historic fiction that draws from the rich heritage, tales and legends of ancient Greece; here is a collection that you are going to love. In the collection below we have gathered the best of Greek Mythology books—from spellbinding myths retold that have become bestselling modern classics to mesmerising anthologies and mythical adventures for readers of all ages and preferences. 

Books2Door’s Greek Mythology Recommendations

Ancient Myths 16 Books Collection by McCaurhrean Ross - for children aged between 7-9 Sixteen highly rated Greek Mythology Books for kids, each dedicated to an ancient myth from Greece; this collection is all things Greek Mythology. From Zeus to Odysseus, from Icarus to Medusa; this collection set has everything you want to know about Greek literature.

Hopeless Heroes: The Greek God 10 Books Collection Set By Stella Tarakson - for children aged 7-9 is a fun-filled series about Greek mythology, adventure and what it means to be a hero. This ten book collection follows the adventures of Tim Baker as he travels back in time and meets legendary Greek Gods. Only, sometimes they make his life a little complicated. Perfect for young readers aged between 7+ Hopeless Heroes The Greek God collection is packed full of brilliant kids’ books that make familiar historical characters, modern-day heroes and whilst at it, also makes history fun to learn!

Mythos: The Greek Myths Retold by Stephen Fry is a romp through the lives of ancient Greek gods. Fry is at his story-telling best through the book; the gods will be pleased! No one loves and quarrels, desires and deceives as boldly or brilliantly as Greek gods and goddesses. In Stephen Fry's vivid retelling, we gaze in wonder as wise Athena is born from the cracking open of the great head of Zeus and follows doomed Persephone into the dark and lonely realm of the Underworld. We shiver in fear when Pandora opens her jar of evil torments and watch with joy as the legendary love affair between Eros and Psyche unfolds. Mythos captures these extraordinary myths for the modern age reader in all their dazzling and deeply human relevance. Perfect for the YA readers of today with a thing for historic Greek literature. 

Want some more great Greek mythology recommendations? We have plenty! From re-tellings of Medusa to Hecules we have it all, from romantic reads to action-packed books! Check out our blog post on Greek Mythology recommendations for young readers right here at Books2Door!

title: Grishaverse Books - Shadow and Bone Novels
description:
The Grishaverse is a fantasy book series by bestselling author Leigh Bardugo that takes place in a world filled with magic, adventure, and danger. The series includes multiple books that follow different characters as they navigate their way through this mystical world. Find all the series reading order below: 

Shadow and Bone Series

The Shadow and Bone trilogy is a captivating journey through a mystical world full of magic and adventure. The books in the trilogy consist of: Shadow and Bone, Siege and Storm and Ruin and Rising. From the powerful Grisha to the darkness that threatens to consume Ravka, readers are immersed in a world that is both beautiful and dangerous. With the help of a dynamic cast of characters, including the strong-willed Alina Starkov and the enigmatic Darkling, readers are taken on a thrilling ride that will keep them on the edge of their seats. The popularity of the trilogy led to the creation of a Netflix series, which has brought the world of the Grishaverse to life in a whole new way for fans to enjoy.

Shadow and Bone is the first book in the Grishaverse series. The story follows Alina Starkov, an orphan who discovers that she possesses a rare and powerful magic that can save her country, Ravka, from the darkness that has engulfed it. Along with the help of the Darkling, a powerful Grisha who guides her through her new world, Alina must navigate the dangers of the Grisha court, the darkness that threatens to consume her, and her growing feelings for the Darkling. 

Siege and Storm is the second book in the Grishaverse series. The story picks up where Shadow and Bone left off, with Alina and Mal on the run from the Darkling. They are soon captured by the Darkling's forces and brought to his palace, where Alina must use her powers to help the Darkling create a new kind of magic. As Alina struggles to control her powers and her feelings for both Mal and the Darkling, she must also contend with the threat of a new enemy who seeks to destroy Ravka.

Ruin and Rising is the third and final book in the Grishaverse series. The story follows Alina as she fights to bring down the Darkling and save Ravka from destruction. Along the way, she must confront her own fears and insecurities, as well as her growing feelings for Mal. With the help of her friends and allies, Alina must face the ultimate test of her power and her will to survive.

Six of Crows Duology

The Six of Crows duology is a spin-off book set in the Grishaverse world but with new characters and a new storyline. The story follows a group of six outcasts, led by Kaz Brekker, as they attempt to pull off the biggest heist in history. Along the way, they must confront their own pasts and inner demons, as well as the dangers of the world around them.

Crooked Kingdom is the second and final book in the Six of Crows duology. The story picks up where Six of Crows left off, with Kaz and his crew reeling from the aftermath of their heist. As they struggle to stay alive and out of the hands of their enemies, they must also contend with their own personal demons and the growing tensions within their group.

King of Scars Duology

The King of Scars duology is an enthralling addition to Leigh Bardugo's Grishaverse series. The two books, King of Scars and Rule of Wolves follow the story of Nikolai Lantsov, the young and charismatic king of Ravka, as he tries to navigate the political and personal challenges of his reign. With the help of his friends, including the Grisha healer Zoya Nazyalensky, Nikolai must confront the threats to his kingdom and to his own inner demons. The duology is a masterful continuation of the Grishaverse series, filled with Bardugo's signature complex characters and rich world-building that will captivate readers until the very end.

The Language of Thorns

The Language of Thorns is a collection of short stories set in the Grishaverse world. Each story is a fairytale-like retelling of a classic fable or myth, with a twist of Grishaverse magic and mythology. The stories explore themes of love, betrayal, courage, and the power of words.

Leigh Bardugo, the Author of the Grishaverse

Leigh Bardugo is a talented American author who has made a name for herself in the world of young adult fiction. Her work is known for its captivating world-building, complex characters, and intricate plotlines. Bardugo has a unique talent for creating dark, atmospheric stories that keep readers on the edge of their seats, and her ability to craft compelling narratives has won her a devoted following of fans. With numerous bestselling books and a hit Netflix series based on her Grishaverse novels, Bardugo's work has made a significant impact on the world of young adult literature and continues to capture the hearts of readers everywhere.

Leigh Bardugo is an American author who was born in Jerusalem and raised in Los Angeles. She began her writing career as a journalist and copywriter before turning to fiction. Her debut novel, Shadow and Bone, was published in 2012 and quickly became a New York Times bestseller. Since then, she has written multiple books in the Grishaverse series, as well as the Six of Crows duology and the King of Scars duology.

title: H. P. Lovecraft
description:
Step into the eerie world of H.P. Lovecraft, where ancient cosmic entities lurk in the shadows and madness dances at the edges of human comprehension. At Books2Door, we invite you to explore the spine-tingling tales penned by one of the most influential authors in the realm of horror fiction.

The Enigmatic Life of H.P. Lovecraft
Born in 1890, Howard Phillips Lovecraft was a master of the weird and the macabre. His life was as enigmatic as his stories, marked by a reclusive nature and a deep fascination with the unknown. Lovecraft's upbringing in Providence, Rhode Island, a city steeped in history and haunted by its own dark legends, undoubtedly influenced his literary imagination. 

Despite facing numerous personal struggles and financial hardships throughout his life, Lovecraft's literary legacy remains an enduring testament to his boundless creativity and unparalleled storytelling prowess.

Delving into the Depths: The H.P. Lovecraft Collection 6 Books
Immerse yourself in the chilling landscapes of Lovecraft's imagination with The H.P. Lovecraft Collection: 6 Books. This comprehensive anthology features some of his most iconic works, including Stories of the Dreamlands, At the Mountains of Madness and The Call of Cthulhu. These tales transport readers to a universe teeming with eldritch horrors and forbidden knowledge, where humanity is a speck amidst the vast cosmic forces that govern the universe.

At the Mountains of Madness plunges readers into the frigid expanses of Antarctica, where a scientific expedition uncovers ancient ruins and encounters unfathomable horrors that defy rational explanation. title: Harlan Coben Books
description:
Harlan Coben's Books: Captivating Thrillers and Unforgettable Mysteries

Welcome to the captivating world of Harlan Coben, where thrilling suspense and unforgettable mysteries come to life. With his signature blend of intricate plots, compelling characters, and unexpected twists, Coben has cemented his position as one of the most popular and prolific authors of our time. We invite you to explore the works of this master storyteller, delve into his gripping novels, and discover why Harlan Coben continues to enthral readers around the globe.

Harlan Coben is a highly acclaimed and bestselling author known for his mastery of suspense and gripping storytelling. Born on January 4, 1962, in Newark, New Jersey, Coben developed a passion for writing at a young age. He attended Amherst College, where he studied political science, but his love for storytelling led him to pursue a career as a novelist.

He is renowned for his ability to craft gripping suspense that keeps readers on the edge of their seats, making him a master of suspense. Whether it's a missing person, a dark secret, or a seemingly ordinary life turned upside down, Coben knows how to build tension and create an atmosphere that leaves you guessing until the very last page. With each book, he masterfully weaves together multiple plotlines, leaving no loose ends and delivering a satisfying resolution.

One of Coben's greatest strengths lies in his ability to create complex and relatable characters. From flawed heroes to enigmatic villains, his protagonists are ordinary people thrust into extraordinary circumstances. They grapple with moral dilemmas, face personal demons, and embark on journeys of self-discovery. Coben's characters resonate with readers, as they mirror the complexities and contradictions of real life.

At the heart of Coben's extensive bibliography lies the beloved Myron Bolitar series. Myron, a sports agent turned detective, takes centre stage in this thrilling collection of novels. With his sharp wit and unwavering determination, Myron tackles cases that blend sports, crime, and intense personal drama. Each instalment reveals more about Myron's past, making readers feel invested in his journey as both a detective and a human being. Check out the series 1-5 in our Myron Bolitar series 1 to 5 collection by Harlan Coben. 

While the Myron Bolitar series brought Coben widespread acclaim, his standalone novels have garnered equal praise and a dedicated fan base. These books explore a wide range of themes, from family secrets to buried pasts, and they showcase Coben's versatility as a writer. Some of the best Harlan Coben books include Stay Close, The Boy from the Woods, Run Away and many more. No matter which standalone novel you pick up, you can expect a rollercoaster ride of suspense and an exploration of the darkest corners of the human psyche.

Coben's books are notorious for their addictive quality. Once you start reading, it's nearly impossible to put them down. The plots are intricately constructed, with layers upon layers of mystery that unravel at just the right pace. Coben seamlessly combines pulse-pounding action, shocking revelations, and emotionally charged moments to create a reading experience that will keep you hooked from the first page to the last.

Prepare to be astonished, as Coben is a master of the unexpected twist. Just when you think you have it all figured out, he throws a curveball that leaves you reeling. These twists are never gratuitous; instead, they deepen the intrigue and challenge your assumptions. Coben's ability to surprise and defy expectations is what sets his books apart and keeps readers coming back for more.

Harlan Coben's books transcend genre boundaries, attracting readers from various backgrounds. While firmly rooted in the thriller and mystery genres, his novels also incorporate elements of family drama, psychological suspense, and even elements of romance. This wide appeal has contributed to his immense popularity and made him a favourite among readers who crave a blend of heart-pounding action and emotional depth.

Coben's captivating storytelling has not only captured the hearts of readers but has also found its way onto screens both big and small. Several of his novels have been adapted into successful television series, bringing his compelling narratives to life with the help of talented actors and production teams. These adaptations have introduced a new generation of fans to Coben's work and further solidified his reputation as a master of suspense.

Harlan Coben's books have enjoyed unparalleled success both in his home country, the United States, and internationally. With over 75 million copies sold worldwide and his books translated into numerous languages, Coben's storytelling prowess has captivated readers across the globe. His novels consistently top bestseller lists, and his dedicated fan base eagerly awaits each new release, hungry for another enthralling journey into the unknown.

Whether you're a long-time fan or new to the world of Harlan Coben's books, this web page serves as your gateway to adventure. Dive into his extensive bibliography, choose your starting point, and prepare to embark on a thrilling literary journey. With Harlan Coben as your guide, you can expect heart-stopping suspense, unforgettable characters, and a reading experience that will stay with you long after you've turned the final page.

Harlan Coben has carved a niche for himself in the literary world with his gripping thrillers and unforgettable mysteries. His ability to create suspenseful plots, complex characters, and unexpected twists has made him a household name and a favourite among readers of all backgrounds. Whether you're delving into the Myron Bolitar series or exploring his standalone novels, you're guaranteed a rollercoaster ride of emotions and an enthralling reading experience. So, pick up one of Harlan Coben's books, and get ready to be swept away into a world of suspense, mystery, and unputdownable storytelling.

title: HarperCollins Books
description:
In the glorious two hundred years of its existence; HarperCollins has managed to position itself as one of the world’s top English-language publishers. Headquartered in New York and having set up publishing operations across 17 countries; they have more than 120 branded imprints around the world. HarperCollins publishes on average 10,000 new books every year in 16 languages and has a print and digital catalogue of more than 200,000 titles. For two hundred extensive years (and counting), HarperCollins has been an inseparable part of the world’s literary history.

With a long, rich history that dates back to the 19th century; HarperCollins books boast the most incredible list of writers. HarperCollins is one publication house that credits itself for having published world-class writers like Mark Twain, the Brontë sisters, Thackeray, Dickens, John F. Kennedy, Martin Luther King Jr., Maurice Sendak, Shel Silverstein, Margaret Wise Brown amongst several others. With books published across dozens of genres; the prestigious HarperCollins author list includes Nobel Prize winners, Pulitzer Prize winners, and more.

At HarperCollins publishing, authors are at the centre of everything they do. They provide authors with a platform to voice relevant opinions and tell important stories about pressing causes. To the authors they represent, they extend world-class and unprecedented editorial support, marketing reach, long-standing connections with booksellers, and industry-leading insight into reader and consumer behaviour. 

As the second largest consumer book publisher in the world; HarperCollins UK publishes books for readers of all ages, cultures, and interests. Their bestsellers include memoirs of British prime ministers. Hilary Mantel’s Wolf Hall trilogy. George R. R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire series and legendary titles by legacy authors J.R.R. Tolkien, Agatha Christie mysteries, and The Chronicles of Narnia by C.S. Lewis. Apart from world-class non-fiction and fiction titles to their credit; Harper Collins is also home to the most iconic bears in literary fiction. They can single-handedly take credit for blessing the world’s young readers with bear characters like Paddington, Rupert, Winnie-the-Pooh, Judith Kerr, Rob Biddulph, Michael Morpurgo, Mr. Men & Little Miss, Thomas & Friends, and Minecraft.

HarperCollins publishers are also the only UK publishers to release audio versions of all their new fiction, narrative nonfiction, and children’s books at the same time as their print publication. They publish as many as 700 audiobooks every year. And whilst they explore all new and old, digital and print avenues of publishing literature, HarperCollins also has a social conscience. They have a unique partnership with the Royal National Institute for the Blind, where their complete catalogue is free for the members of the institute. As part of the HarperCollins Learning and Education division; the publication house has also pioneered reference publishing. They develop market-leading dictionaries, atlases, and other academic books for school students.

On their mission to bring only the best authors to their readers; HarperCollins is a publication house that has championed core human values like diversity and inclusivity in their work and not just in their company policy. As part of its mission to publish diverse and culturally inclusive books; HarperCollins submissions desk hires only the best literary agents to scout out and represent only the best writers and voices from across the globe.

title: Harriet Tyce Books
description:
A Scottish barrister, author and novelist—Harriet Tyce grew up in Edinburgh and studied at the prestigious Oxford University. She studied English Literature at Oxford before doing a law conversion course at City university and subsequently completed an MA in Creative Writing - Crime Fiction at the University of East Anglia. 

Tyce worked as a criminal barrister for nearly a decade before she retired to become a full time writer. Once she escaped law, Tyce started writing, and her first novel, Blood Orange, published in 2019 to huge critical acclaim followed by her second novel, The Lies You Told, published in summer 2020 and her third It Ends at Midnight in April 2022.

With three critically acclaimed novels to her credit; Harriet (in the very first few years of her becoming an author) already established herself in the league of bestselling, psychological suspense authors. Tyce’s psychological suspense novels take the readers into a bleak world characterised by poor decision making, violence and sexual danger so spooky they will make anyone consider celibacy. 

Harriet Tyce’s best psychological suspense works… 

Harriet Tyce’s Blood Orange tells the story of Alison Bailey, a United Kingdom-based lawyer, the wife to Carl, mistress to Patrick Saunders and mother to Matilda. It’s clear from the beginning that Alison wants to end things with Patrick to make her marriage much better and be a better mom to her daughter but the difference between desire and action can at times be a wide chasm. Unlike most other crime novels where the narrative is centred around one case; Tyce does not refrain from speaking blatantly of the different litigations that her main character faces alongside the main case. Even as Alison is awarded her first murder case; she is not spared of her other cases and the novel documents them as Alison juggles with the demands of a murder case along with her other professional responsibilities. Things become even more tricky as Alison is assigned a mentor, tasked with helping her prepare for this murder trial. This mentor is none other than the man she wants to end things with—making things even more challenging for Alison. A feminist crime novel that delves into the sensitive themes of domestic violence, workplace sexual misconduct, toxic masculinity and manages to be brutally realistic about it all.

The Lies You Told by Harriet Tyce is another jaw dropping intelligent thriller by the author. Sadie the protagonist loves her daughter and will do anything to keep her safe. She can't tell her why they had to leave home so quickly - or why Robin's father won't be coming with them to London. She can't tell her why she hates being back in her dead mother's house, with its ivy-covered walls and its poisonous memories. Sadie just wants to get their lives back on track. But even lies with the best intentions can have deadly consequences. An intriguing tale with a gripping plot and a layered narrative; the novel will have you glued till the very last page. 

It Ends At Midnight by Harriet Tyce is the author’s third novel and like her other works, the book lives up to the expectation of being a nail biting thriller with complex and compelling characters. The novel revolves around three friends, two bodies and a lavish party in one of Edinbrugh’s best postcodes. It’s a splendid party, the night sky is alive with fireworks and the champagne is flowing but the celebration is about to fail. Someone is about to die. An absolute page turner with a twist you'll read twice; this suspense novel is another treat for those who enjoy the genre.

In Norwegian Wood, Murakami explores themes of love, loss, and coming of age. Set in 1960s Tokyo, the novel follows the introspective protagonist, Toru Watanabe, as he navigates the complexities of his relationships against the backdrop of a society in turmoil. Murakami's delicate prose and introspective musings create a poignant atmosphere, drawing readers into a world filled with emotional depth and introspection. This novel was adapted into a film directed by Tran Anh Hung starring Kenichi Matsuyama and Rinko Kikuchi. 

A Wild Sheep Chase takes readers on a mind-bending journey as an unnamed protagonist becomes entangled in a quest to find a peculiar sheep. As the narrative unfolds, Murakami seamlessly blends elements of mystery, fantasy, and social commentary, crafting a surreal tale that defies conventions. With his distinct blend of humour and introspection, Murakami challenges readers to question the nature of reality and the boundaries of perception.

The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle stands as one of Murakami's most ambitious and intricate works. Centred around Toru Okada, a man searching for his missing wife, the novel immerses readers in a labyrinthine narrative that traverses different realms and intertwines multiple storylines. Murakami's masterful storytelling weaves together themes of memory, identity, and the human psyche, creating a mesmerizing tapestry that blurs the lines between the conscious and the subconscious.

In Hard-Boiled Wonderland And The End Of The World, Murakami presents a dual narrative that alternates between a futuristic, Kafkaesque city and a mystical, isolated village. The novel follows a "Calcutec" whose mind has been divided into two separate entities, each navigating its own strange and surreal worlds. Murakami's distinct ability to merge the mundane with the fantastical takes readers on an existential journey that explores themes of consciousness, identity, and the nature of existence.

Across these four novels and all of his books, Murakami showcases his mastery in crafting intricate narratives that transcend traditional genre boundaries. His writing is characterized by a surreal blend of realism and fantasy, where mundane settings become portals to extraordinary experiences. Murakami's prose flows effortlessly, painting vivid landscapes of emotion and introspection while tackling universal themes that resonate deeply with readers.

The allure of Murakami's works lies not only in their intricate plots and vivid imagery but also in their profound philosophical underpinnings. Through his characters' introspection and existential dilemmas, Murakami invites readers to question the nature of reality, the complexities of human existence, and the interconnectedness of our experiences.

Haruki Murakami has become a literary icon, capturing the hearts and minds of readers worldwide with his thought-provoking narratives. His unique blend of magical realism, introspection, and social commentary creates a literary experience like no other. Whether you are a longtime fan or a newcomer to his works, immersing yourself in the worlds he creates in Norwegian Wood, A Wild Sheep Chase, The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle, and Hard-Boiled Wonderland And The End Of The World is an invitation to embark on an extraordinary journey of self-discovery and contemplation.

title: Heartstopper Books
description:
Originally released as a webcomic, Heartstopper is now an award-winning and internationally bestselling, YA, LGBTQ+ graphic novel series that tells a touching boy-meets-boy queer love story; written and illustrated by popular British YA author Alice Oseman. The series follows the lives of protagonists Nick Nelson and Charlie Spring as they meet, become friends and fall in love. The Heartstopper series is an expanded adaptation of Oseman's 2015 novella, Nick and Charlie, although the characters first appeared in her 2014 novel Solitaire. 

Given its popularity with the YA readers; the Heartstopper graphic novel series has now been adapted into a major live-action Netflix television show starring Kit Connor and newcomer Joe Locke as Nick and Charlie. The books follow the blossoming romance between Charlie and Nick whilst also touching upon other sensitive themes that are very relevant and relatable for teenagers and young adults. The series is a gorgeous coming of age story about love, friendship, loyalty, sexuality and mental illness. 

Despite the highly relatable content for teens and young adults; the sensitive content in some of the later books means we recommend them for readers 13/14+. However we suggest you read them in the order of their release from Volumes One to Four so you enjoy the development of the story in the best way possible. 

Now an award-winning author; the 28-year-old Alice Oseman, of the Heartstopper graphic novels series has written four volumes as part of the series and the next book is scheduled for a release in the year 2023. Oseman has also written several other novels and won several awards; however the four volumes of the Heartstopper graphic novel series still continue to top the bestselling children’s book charts. 

The Heartstopper Series revolves around the relationship between the two protagonist school boys Charlie Spring (year 10) and Nick Nelson (year 11). Whilst Charlie has already ‘come out’ as gay; he is in a difficult, controlling and abusive situation with another boy called Ben who masquerades as straight. Charlie meets Nick when the school experiments with ‘vertical form times’, which include kids from multiple year groups. Charlie immediately develops a crush. Nick is lovely, but he is sporty and popular, everything Charlie is not. Given his athletic personality everyone assumes Nick is straight, including himself! However, as his friendship with Charlie develops they start to feel an undeniable attraction towards each other which leads to a kiss.  

This is where volume 1 ends leaving the YA readers in a moment of anticipation and utmost curiosity about what is to become of their new favourite teen couple. In the following three volumes, Oseman manages to meet the expectations she set in the first book with her sensitivity as a YA LGBTQ+ author. The same is evident in the popularity of the Heartstopper series across the bestselling book charts and now a popular Netflix series.

Through highly relatable experiences, sensitive teen emotions and relevant themes written in the graphic novel format; Oseman has managed to explore an unconventional format with a Young Adult LGBTQ+ novel. Thus making the Heartstopper Series perfect for teens who find it hard to read books in their conventional format. The expressive and warm graphic illustrations make the novels far more easy to savour and manage to appeal to a wider; often reluctant; reader base.

title: His Dark Materials Books
description:
His Dark Materials

His Dark Materials is a coming-of-age story set within many parallel universes. The book's main protagonists are Lyra Belacqua and Will Parry. The book series is fantasy and was written with no particular genre in mind, however, it has been increasingly popular with children and young adults. The trilogy includes witches, armoured polar bears and a truth-telling compass which all create unique and thrilling adventures for Lyra and Will. 

The first book in this epic series is Northern Lights which follows Lyra Belacqua and her animal Daemon Pantalaimon (Pan for short) in an alternate world very similar to Earth. Lyra lives amongst the scholars at Jordon College, Oxford, raised by the scholars and her uncle Lord Asriel. Whilst at the college Lyra overhears her uncle talking about a mysterious substance he is researching called ‘Dust’. Lyra becomes increasingly curious about ‘Dust’ and must know more; doing so causes her to be catapulted into a world beyond anything she should have imagined.

The next title in the series is The Subtle Knife. The adventure continues for Lyra as she runs into Will Parry, a young boy without a Daemon who is in a lot of trouble. She has never seen anyone without a Daemon before, and Will has never seen a Daemon before. They both embark on a journey to learn more about each other and the mysterious city they find themselves in. All while this is happening, Mrs Coulter is trying to track down Lyra.

The final book in the trilogy is The Amber Spyglass. Lyra and Will have been separated, Lyra is being held captive, and Will is desperately trying to find her with the help of two Angels. Will must find a way to get to Lyra, but he needs help, so one of the Angels seeks out Lord Asriel for help. 

Philip Pullman also released companion books that fit alongside the main trilogy novels. These short stories and novellas include Lyra’s Oxford, Once Upon a Time in the North, The Collectors, Serpentine and The Imagination Chamber. 

His Dark Materials is now a hit TV show on BBC and HBO, produced by Bad Wolf. In 2007 a film adaptation was released starring Daniel Craig and Nicole Kidman; the film was titled The Golden Compass. 

Further Reading 

Pullman has released many other literary series over the years. The Sally Lockheart series began with The Ruby in the Smoke (1985) and ended with The Tin Princess (1994). He has also released The New Cut Gang series and The Book of Dust Series, which is in the same world as His Dark Materials. 

As well as the His Dark Materials companion books and other series, Pullman has also released a collection of Grimm Tales For Young and Old. He has also released various standalone novels, such as I Was a Rat! Or, the Scarlet Slippers, The firework Maker’s Daughter, Clockwork and Spring-Heeled Jack, all of which are available in this Four Fairy Tales by Philip Pullman 4 Books Collection Set. 

About the Author 

Philip Pullman is an English fantasy writer. From a young age, he travelled with his family, living in places like Zimbabwe and Australia before settling in Wales. By age 25, Pullman had gained an English degree and taught in Middle schools. He has remained passionate about education but often voices his dedication to encouraging creativity instead of exams and grades. 

Take a look at our range of Philip Pullman Books. Alternatively, fans of His Dark Materials may enjoy Stranger Things, Two Novels Suspicious Minds and Darkness on the Edge of Town or Neil Gaiman’s Books like Coraline and The Graveyard Book.

title: Hodder Books
description:
Hodder Publishing is a book publisher from Hachette UK with a rich history of classic titles and legendary authors to their credit. They have published a wide range of fiction and non-fiction titles over hundreds of years and are renowned for passion, quality and delivering bestselling books across many different literary formats.

First founded in 1868 by Matthew Henry Hodder and Thomas Wilberforce Stoughton on Paternoster Row, London; the Hodder & Stoughton publishing house is one of Britain’s oldest, most elitist publishers. Their publishing in the early years included books from Winston Churchill, JM Barrie and GK Chesterton, and The Bible. The 1920s ‘Yellow Jacket’ series were the precursors to the first paperbacks and included bestsellers from John Buchan, Sapper and Edgar Wallace. In 1921 Hodder & Stoughton also took over ownership of the soon-to-be world-famous medical journal, The Lancet.

After the First World War, Hodder & Stoughton published landmark non-fiction bestsellers like Anthony Sampson’s Anatomy of Britain. The second half of the twentieth century held in store one of the most successful publishing events in the company’s history with the phenomenal reception of Sir John Hunt’s The Ascent of Everest in 1953. Other notable publications include David Niven’s much-celebrated autobiography The Moon’s a Balloon in 1973 and John le Carré’s Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy in 1974. In 1986, Hodder & Stoughton set up Sceptre as a literary imprint to sit alongside mass-market imprints Coronet and NEL (New English Library). 

By 1993, a company called Headline acquired Hodder & Stoughton and the company became Hodder Headline Ltd. Following which Hodder Headline acquired John Murray in 2002 and two years later the company was bought by Hachette Livre which already owned British publishers Orion and Octopus (and now also Little, Brown and Company). Hodder Headline was restructured and a single Hodder & Stoughton publishing division was created.

Since then the Hodder Books Publishing Catalogue has had big non-fiction names such as Sir Ranulph Fiennes, Clarissa Dickson Wright, James Bowen and Street Cat Bob, Hans Rosling and Michael Caine. Their cookery and lifestyle titles include Gordon Ramsay, Gino D’Acampo and Deliciously Ella, whilst the non-fiction list covers many areas including biographies, memoirs, sports books, humour, health, lifestyle and cookery and is home to the million-copy bestselling The Power of Now.

The crime and thriller list of the publication house boasts some of the best writers in the genre with the likes of John Connolly, Stephen Leather, Erin Kelly, Antonia Hodgson and Peter Robinson, whilst their fiction publishing continues to expand with authors such as Holly Bourne, Becky Chambers and Laini Taylor.

For younger children and early teens between the ages of 7 to 11; Hodder Books have fiction titles like Planet Omar 4 Books Collection Set By Zanib Mian. A beautiful lesson in kindness and facing fears; this one is perfect for when you want your child to develop a reading habit and also pick up good values whilst at it. One of Omar's best friends, Daniel, has a little sister who goes to hospital regularly. He usually finds it easy to cheer her up when she's there, but this time he feels he needs to do something extra special. Enter Omar and their other best friend Charlie to help with Operation Kind! The boys try to come up with the perfect surprise for Suzy, and when they find out her favourite author is in the UK for just one day it feels like it was meant to be. Can the boys overcome all of the ridiculous obstacles that get thrown in their path and face their fears, in a race against time to get a signed copy of the book for Suzy?

One of our favourites from the Hodder Books fiction list for children is this Alice Oseman Four-Book Box Set (Solitaire, Radio Silence, I Was Born For This, Loveless) by Alice Oseman. A set of acclaimed novels by a young and dynamic British author Alice Oseman, who was recently awarded the 2021 YA Book Prize. Alice published her first book when she was all of 19 and she has since written several books and illustrated a graphic novel series, of which has been produced into a Netflix series that she wrote the screenplay for.

Her first book (also a part of this set) Solitaire is about Tori Spring, a Year 12 student who doesn’t really have any close friends. She spends most of her time keeping to herself, reading blogs and doing worse on her coursework than she should be. For someone so unfriended, though, Tori has no shortage of people in her orbit. A teenage drama the book is engaging and makes for a fun read. Another award winning book in the set is Loveless, the fourth novel from the phenomenally talented Alice Oseman. It was all sinking in. Georgia had never had a crush on anyone. No boys, no girls, not a single person she had ever met. What did that mean? Georgia has never been in love, never kissed anyone, never even had a crush - but as a fanfic-obsessed romantic she's sure she'll find her person one day. As she starts university with her best friends, Pip and Jason, in a whole new town far from home, Georgia's ready to find romance. What follows makes for another one of Alice Oseman’s incredible teenage fiction.

title: Holly Jackson Books
description:
Join us at Books2Door as we celebrate Holly Jackson, the author who has cemented her name as a leading voice in the world of young adult fiction, specialising in teen mysteries and thrillers that meld the intricacies of adolescent life with compelling, edge-of-your-seat narratives. 

Each book she pens invites readers into a labyrinth of emotion, mystery, and human intricacy, providing an experience that captivates and challenges. This collection of Holly Jackson's works is an invaluable cornerstone for both fans and newcomers, offering the complete set of stories that have made her a household name in modern storytelling. Let us dive in, shall we?

A Good Girl's Guide to Murder Series

One of Jackson's flagship titles, A Good Girl's Guide to Murder, is a remarkable foray into crime and investigation with a teenage twist. The story captures the essence of small-town dynamics, high school social hierarchies, and the quest for justice. High school senior Pippa (Pip) Fitz-Amobi takes on a murder investigation for her final year project. Five years earlier, Andie Bell, a high school student, was believed to have been murdered by her boyfriend, Sal Singh, who then committed suicide. Pip doubts Sal's guilt and thinks the case was prematurely closed.

As Pip uncovers clues and follows leads, she finds herself in increasingly dangerous situations. Her determination to uncover the truth only intensifies, evolving the story into a complex web of revelations through traditional prose and multimedia elements like interview transcripts, text messages, and charts. 

Jackson's sequels, Good Girl, Bad Blood and As Good as Dead, further explore these elements, adding new dimensions to familiar characters and solidifying her reputation for masterful character development and plot progression.

About Holly Jackson

Born and raised in the United Kingdom, Holly Jackson developed a love for storytelling from a young age, voraciously reading a wide range of books. She attended the University of Nottingham, where she honed her skills in English and Creative Writing. During her time at university, she began shaping ideas that would culminate in her debut novel, blending mystery, suspense, and drama into narratives that capture the complexities of adolescence. 

A defining quality of Jackson's work is her commitment to inclusivity. Her books feature diverse characters that reflect the multifaceted nature of contemporary society, with characters of various ethnicities, orientations, and backgrounds. This dedication to diversity adds depth and realism to her fictional worlds.

Holly Jackson's books offer rich material for discussing essential themes such as justice, ethics, and societal norms. Often included in school curricula, her work engages with issues relevant to young adults in a manner that is both enlightening and entertaining. Her books have been used in educational settings to spark interest in forensic science and psychology, proving her storytelling has applications far beyond leisurely reading.

A Literary Treasure Trove

We want this collection to testify to Holly Jackson's ingenuity and talent. We invite you to immerse yourself in a universe where suspense meets substance; every page is a journey into the human psyche. Whether you're a dedicated fan looking to complete your collection or a newcomer eager to dive into her captivating world, this compilation of Holly Jackson's books is a literary treasure trove that promises countless hours of exhilarating reading.

At Books2Door, we are passionate about bringing you the best in young adult fiction. Holly Jackson's collection is a prime example of the high-quality, engaging stories we offer. Explore our selection today and discover why Holly Jackson is a beacon of storytelling brilliance in young adult literature.

title: HomeEd
description:
Homeschooling is on the rise in the UK, with 111,700 children in elective home education as of autumn 2024- a significant 21.4% increase from the previous year, according to The Times, 2024. As more families turn to home education, parents and caregivers must have the right resources to make informed decisions. That’s where we come in!

We’ve curated a comprehensive collection of homeschooling books designed to support both parents and children on their educational journey. Whether you're new to homeschooling, also known as alternative schools, self-learning, and unschooling, or already deep into your routine, you'll find many titles to help make learning at home fun, effective, and budget-friendly.

Why Home Learning Matters

There’s no shortage of opinions on homeschooling, but one thing’s clear: growing up surrounded by books is a beautiful thing. Easy access to books in the home can spark curiosity, develop a love of reading, and improve learning outcomes for kids and adults alike.

Creating a small home library in your living space can encourage children to pick up books more often and reduce unnecessary screen time. From early years phonics to Key Stage 4 science and geography, there are endless opportunities to engage your child with age-appropriate educational content that nurtures their development.

We offer a broad selection of Curriculum-aligned workbooks, Children’s storybooks, STEM learning resources, Activity and puzzle books… all aimed at making home learning enjoyable and enriching.

More Story Time, Less Screen Time

With books tailored to your child’s interests, they’re more likely to stay engaged, develop independent learning skills, and spend less time glued to a screen. Reading regularly helps improve vocabulary, boosts cognitive thinking, strengthens emotional intelligence, and even supports better sleep routines. It’s not just about academics- it’s about building confident, curious, and well-rounded learners.

There are also plenty of homeschooling communities and learning clubs you can get involved in, which give children the chance to build friendships and grow their social skills outside of a traditional classroom setting.

Explore Our Homeschooling Book Range by Age and Key Stage.

Whether you're starting with toddlers or supporting teens, we’ve got you covered:

  • Ages 3–5 (Early Years): Fun and colourful books on phonics, counting, shapes, and early storytelling.
  • Key Stage 1 (Ages 5–7): Reading practice, handwriting workbooks, basic maths, and simple science.
  • Key Stage 2 (Ages 7–11): More in-depth comprehension, multiplication, grammar, geography, and science projects.
  • Ages 11+: Revision guides, English literature texts, and subject-specific textbooks to support independent study and exam prep.

You can also browse by subject- English, maths, science, geography, history, and more. Whether you're looking for structured curriculum workbooks, creative learning tools, or topic-specific study guides, our home education range is designed to make homeschooling accessible, affordable, and stress-free.

Start building your home library today, because learning doesn’t just happen in a classroom.

It starts with curiosity, a good book, and a little help from us.

If you have an infant or toddler and you want to expose your child to early reading, the Biff, Chip and Kipper Phonics Stories & Activities: Read with Oxford Stages (1-3) 6 Books Collection Set - Roderick Hunt Ages 0-5 may be just the book you are looking for. Each book has two engaging stories, ideal for children who are developing early reading skills. These activity books are packed to the brim with fun phonics activities and stickers linked to the stories, at just the right level for your child. The book also has word games, colouring, puzzles, rhymes, matching, and more, that make reading, writing, and spelling fun.

Ready to get started? Browse our full homeschooling range and find the perfect mix of learning and fun, all at pocket-friendly prices.

title: Horrible Histories Books
description:
Terry Deary – the author of Horrible Histories, said: “I’m not a historian, but I want to change the world, attack the elite. Overturn the hierarchy, look at my stories, and you’ll notice that the villains are always those in power. The heroes are the little people.” In his Horrible Histories series, Deary states that he doesn’t just want to create history books but simply stories about people in dramatic scenarios combined with jokes. When Deary’s son was asked about his opinions on the books, he stated: “They’re brilliant. Because you learn stuff, and you laugh at the same time.” The aim of the books is to educate but also entertain. The books are filled with silly jokes and humorous stories, which makes the facts much more memorable. 

Deary is known as a very straightforward writer that paints an accurate picture with objective facts of the terrible and tragic history of different regions of the world. Even though you can see Deary’s personality portrayed in his work that brings forth humour and silliness, his goal was always to portray the terrible acts of past evil aristocracies. The books themselves are filled with gore and gruesome details, they are not for the faint-hearted. The series details historical facts and don’t gloss over particularly horrific events that they don’t always teach you at school. Don’t forget to check out our page for more Terry Deary books. 

In our Horrible Histories Savage 8 Book Collection, children will learn about the Terrifying Tudors and their terrible publishments, relentless royal family and long-suffering subjects. Also included in this set are The Awful Egyptians, Rotten Romans, Vicious Vikings, Measly Middle Ages, Vile Victorians, Frightful First World War and Woeful Second World War. Deary’s books not only educate but are also incredibly entertaining, combining facts with hilarious jokes and quizzes to test your knowledge. These books are much loved by children, teachers and adults alike. Making them an excellent read for anyone interested in the subject areas or for reading with your children as extracurricular activities! 

In 2009, CBBC produced a live-action sketch comedy musical series based on the bestselling novels. Horrible Histories became an incredibly popular tv series and ran until 2014, it has since been relaunched in 2015 with a different cast. The show remains one of the most-watched children’s tv shows, taking inspiration from iconic British comedies like Blackadder and Monty Python. The show has been used in schools and to help with exam revision, making it very popular with all ages. 

As well as the fantastically written Horrible Histories, Scholastic has also published the dreadfully good Horrible Geography series. With facts about Earth-Shattering Earthquakes, Monster Lakes, Violent Volcanoes, and so many more fascinating occurrences from around the world. Check out our Horrible Geography 10 Books Collection for a bumper box set. 

There are so many different subjects covered in Deary’s Horrible Histories and the Horrible Geography series, written by Anita Ganeri, there is bound to be something for all interests! We hope you enjoy, Horrible Histories.

title: Horrid Henry Books
description:
Horrid Henry is the ultimate antihero, and his adventures have brought delight to children the world over through these fantastic kids fiction books. Horrid Henry is a fun-filled, larger-than-life series about child iconoclast Henry. He knows that life’s not fair. The teachers are after you, your neighbours hate you, and it’s always one rule for the grown-ups and another rule for you. You know the score! As the leader of the Purple Hand Gang, Henry’s determined to get his own back on everyone - no matter the cost.

Henry's pranks delight kids and parents alike as he puts down the bullies, outwits the grown-ups, and causes havoc for his family. There's never a dull moment where Horrid Henry is involved, and his clever ideas for getting back at those who upset him often lead to unpleasant results for everyone. These kids fiction books aimed at children aged between 7-9 are wonderfully written by Francesca Simon and hilariously illustrated by Tony Ross, this series is perfect for reluctant readers and fans of Dennis the Menace and Diary of a Wimpy Kid. If you haven’t already, you need to get on board with Horrid Henry.

Who’s it for?

The Horrid Henry books are perfect for readers aged 7-9 who like stories filled with mayhem, wicked deeds, and outrageous humour. Filled with memorable characters such as Perfect Peter, Moody Margaret, Rude Ralph, and more, children will laugh their socks off at Henry’s horrible adventures.

Horrid Henry has been a publishing phenomenon since 1994, and there’s no stopping him any time soon. The books have been published in 27 languages, selling over 21 million copies worldwide. This collection includes Horrid Henry and the Abominable Snowman, which won the Children’s Book of the Year Award in 2008. The Bafta-nominated TV series began on CITV in 2006 and ran for 250 episodes over thirteen years. The series has now moved to Netflix, which are producing new one-hour specials due to its continued popularity. The live-action Horrid Henry: The Movie was released in 2011, and there has also been video games and a stage play.

About the authors

Francesca Simon is an American author who lives in North London with her family. Having previously worked as a journalist for publications from The Sunday Times to Vogue, she began writing children’s books after reading them to her son Joshua. Now, she’s one of the UK’s most popular children’s authors and has written over fifty books for kids of every age. In 2019, she was the third most borrowed author from libraries and the fifth most borrowed overall. She’s been a judge for literary prizes, been involved in many literacy charities, and was awarded a Gold Blue Peter badge.

Tony Ross is the award-winning illustrator of over two thousand books. He is most famous for his work for children the Horrid Henry and Little Princess series, as well as for illustrating the works of David Walliams. Born in 1938 in Wandsworth, South London, Ross previously worked in teaching and advertising.
