title: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga Books
description:
Few authors have made as profound an impact as Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga in the realm of self-help and personal growth literature. Their collaborative work, the Courage To series, has become a beacon of enlightenment for readers worldwide, offering a unique blend of philosophy and practical guidance for navigating the complexities of life. Dive into the world of these remarkable authors and explore the empowering wisdom they offer in the pages of their books, all available at Books2Door.

Ichiro Kishimi: A Journey of Wisdom
Ichiro Kishimi, born in Japan, is a philosopher and the co-author of the Courage To series, which has gained international acclaim. Kishimi's fascination with the teachings of Alfred Adler, the renowned Austrian psychiatrist and founder of individual psychology, laid the foundation for his collaborative work with Fumitake Koga.

Drawing from Adler's philosophy, Kishimi delves into the intricate workings of the human psyche, addressing issues such as self-worth, relationships, and the pursuit of happiness. His writing style is insightful and accessible, making complex concepts relatable to readers from all walks of life. Kishimi's background in philosophy and his deep understanding of Adlerian psychology shines through in each book of The Courage To series, offering readers the tools they need to lead more fulfilled lives.

Fumitake Koga: A Collaborator in Wisdom
Fumitake Koga, a Japanese author and co-author of the "Courage To" series alongside Ichiro Kishimi, brings his unique perspective and storytelling skills to the partnership. Koga's ability to blend philosophy with real-life anecdotes creates a compelling narrative that resonates with readers on a personal level.

Koga's collaboration with Kishimi has produced a series of books that explore the profound ideas of Alfred Adler through relatable stories and practical advice. This dynamic duo has created a powerful synergy that makes Adler's philosophy accessible to a wide audience, allowing readers to apply these timeless principles to their own lives.

About the series 
The Courage To series, a collection of books authored by Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga, offers a roadmap for personal growth and self-improvement. Each book in the series focuses on a specific aspect of life, giving readers the courage and wisdom to overcome challenges and find meaning in their journeys.

Whether you're seeking the courage to be disliked, to be yourself, or to find happiness, Kishimi and Koga have you covered. The series explores various topics, including the psychology of happiness or the ability to be disliked. Each book offers valuable insights and actionable advice, empowering readers to make positive changes in their lives.

In a world filled with self-help literature, Ichiro Kishimi and Fumitake Koga stand out for their unique blend of philosophy, storytelling, and practical wisdom. Their Courage To series has touched the lives of countless readers, offering a transformative journey towards self-discovery and personal growth. Dive into their work today and embark on a path of courage, wisdom, and lasting change here at Books2Door.

title: Icon Books
description:
Icon Books is an independent British publisher founded in 1992—which makes 2022 their 30th anniversary. For 30 years, Icon books, UK have specialised in publishing intelligent, quality non-fiction for audiences across age groups.

The Icon Books publishing catalogue includes their Graphic Guide series alongside a list of other books in science, history, politics, sport, language, humour and more. Based primarily in north London, they publish books across all English-speaking markets of the world—and many non-English speaking ones too. Icon Books’ graphic guides are their most famous published works including the illustrated series and titles like the bestselling, ‘Why Do People Hate America?'.

A part of the Independent Alliance sales grouping in the UK and other markets, Icon books are also sold by leading distributors around the world, such as PGW in the USA, PGC in Canada, Allen & Unwin in Australasia, Jonathan Ball in South Africa and Penguin Random House in Singapore, Malaysia and India. Their translation rights sales are managed by the Marsh Agency in London.

As publishers of intellectual, non-fiction content, world-class graphic guides and illustrated series; Icon Books publishing have created the very popular Graphic Guide Introduction to Big Ideas 8 Books Collection Set. A set of 8 spectacular graphic guides; with each book in the set focused on one world-defining idea. Every book focuses on an idea that has either helped redefine the world as we know it or changed the course of world events.

From complicated socio-economic theories like Marxism and Capitalism to provocative concepts by philosophers and ideas around psychology and world economics; this set of graphic guides covers it all.

The Marmalade Diaries: The True Story of an Odd Couple by Ben Aitken Charming, touching and funny; this one by Icon books is perfect for millennial readers. When hunting for a room in London, Ben Aitken comes across a room for a great price in a lovely part of town. There had to be a catch. And there was. The catch was Winnie: an 85-year-old widow who doesn't suffer fools. Full of warmth, wit and candour, The Marmalade Diaries tells the story of an unlikely friendship during an unlikely time. Imagine an intergenerational version of Big Brother, but with only two contestants. One of the pair is a grieving and inflexible former aristocrat in her mid-eighties. The other a working-class millennial snowflake. What could possibly go wrong? What could possibly go right? Out of the most inauspicious of soils—and from the author of The Gran Tour—comes a book about grief, family, friendship, loneliness, life, love, lockdown and marmalade.

Queer: A Graphic History by Meg-John Barker Activist Meg-John Barker and cartoonist Jules Scheele; together illuminate the histories of queer thought and LGBTQ+ action in this ground-breaking nonfiction graphic novel. From identity politics and gender roles to privilege and exclusion, Queer explores how we came to view sex, gender and sexuality in the ways that we do. How these ideas get tangled up with our culture and our understanding of biology, psychology and sexology; and how these views have been disputed and challenged. Along the way we look at key landmarks which shift our perspective of what's 'normal'—Alfred Kinsey's view of sexuality as a spectrum, Judith Butler's view of gendered behaviour as a performance, the play Wicked, or moments in Casino Royale when we're invited to view James Bond with the kind of desiring gaze usually directed at female bodies in mainstream media. Presented in a brilliantly engaging and witty writing style, this is a unique portrait of the universe of queer thinking.

title: Irish Books
description:
Ireland, a land of captivating beauty and rich cultural heritage, enchants visitors with its lush green landscapes, rugged coastlines, and ancient ruins steeped in history. From the bustling streets of Dublin to the serene countryside dotted with quaint villages, Ireland offers a tapestry of experiences. Its vibrant music and dance traditions, embodied in lively pubs and spirited festivals, reflect the warmth and friendliness of its people. 

Explore the rich literary tradition of Ireland with us at Books2Door. Irish literature boasts a wealth of talent, with authors who have captured the imagination of readers worldwide. Among them are the legendary Oscar Wilde, novelist James Joyce, storyteller Sally Rooney, Darren Shan, acclaimed for his Cirque du Freak series and Derek Landy, creator of the Skulduggery Pleasant novels.

The country's mythology and folklore are woven into its stunning scenery, evoking a sense of magic and mystique. Ireland's charm lies not only in its picturesque views but also in the warmth and hospitality of its inhabitants.

Irish authors:
James Joyce was a groundbreaking figure in modernist literature who reshaped the literary landscape. His masterpiece, Ulysses, offers a kaleidoscopic view of Dublin on a single day. He is also known for the short story collection Dubliners, which delves into the complexities of everyday life. A century on, these works continue to inspire readers and writers alike.

Sally Rooney has emerged as one of Ireland's most celebrated contemporary writers. She is known for her insightful explorations of modern relationships and social dynamics. With novels like Normal People and Conversations with Friends, Rooney has earned praise for her nuanced characterisations and deft handling of complex themes. We also have a three-book collection of her works. 

Darren Shan's Cirque du Freak transports readers into a dark and fantastical world where vampires, werewolves, and other supernatural beings lurk in the shadows. With its gripping narrative and memorable characters, Shan's writing captivates audiences of all ages and offers a thrilling escape into the unknown. Find the 22-book box set here!

Derek Landy's Skulduggery Pleasant series follows the adventures of a wisecracking detective who is also a skeleton. Blending humour, mystery, and magic, Landy's novels are a testament to his imaginative storytelling prowess, earning him a dedicated following of readers eager for each new instalment.

title: J. K. Rowling Books
description:
It all started with the “Boy Who Lived” and the magical adventures of the most famous wizard of our generation - Harry Potter, of course!

J.K. Rowling is the author of the much-loved and best-selling children’s book series Harry Potter. The series has sold over 500 million copies worldwide and has been translated into at least 70 languages.

But the magical adventures don’t stop there! There are also several spin-off prequel series such as Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, all forming the Wizarding World transmedia franchise. In 2016, Rowling announced a new story in the original Harry Potter Series with Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, a two-part play written by Rowling, John Tiffany and Jack Thorne.

She is also the writer of the popular crime-fiction series Cormoran Strike, writing under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. 

Biography 

Joanne Kathleen Rowling is a British author and philanthropist, best known as the author of the Harry Potter series, which was published between 1997 and 2007. She was born on 31st July 1965 and grew up in Yate, Gloucestershire in England and in Chepstow in south-east Wales. 

Rowling graduated from the University of Exeter in 1987 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in French and Classics. She recalls preferring to read the work of Dickens and Tolkein during her time at university, which went on to inspire her own work later on. After university, Rowling had several jobs working as a bilingual secretary and a researcher at Amnesty International’s London offices. 

Most people are familiar with J. K. Rowling’s rise to fame of how she went from being a single mother to becoming one of the most highest-paid children’s author in the world. She wrote most of the Harry Potter books in Edinburgh, Scotland after moving there in 1993, in the Elephant House cafe. 

However, it was on a delayed train travelling from Manchester to London King’s Cross that Rowling first had the idea for Harry Potter in 1990. With the train being delayed by four hours, the famous trio Harry Potter, Hermione Granger and Ron Weasely sprung into her mind allowing her to fully explore the characters in her imagination before reaching her flat where she began to write. 

Best-Known Books

Whether it's reading the books, or watching the on-screen adaptation, the name Harry Potter is known by children and adults worldwide. Rowling’s much-loved Harry Potter series follows the titular character of an 11-year-old orphan who was brought up by his horrible aunt and uncle. 

On the day of his birthday, everything changed when he is told that he comes from a family of wizards and is to be enrolled at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry- the most famous British boarding school of magic. But life isn’t ever easy for Harry - each year brings new trials and dangers that Harry must face, with the help of his best friends Ron Weasely and Hermione Granger, until he must defeat Lord Voldermort in a final battle 

Those children too young yet to delve into the adventures of Harry Potter and his friends will instead enjoy Rowling’s collection of children’s books such as The Ickabog and The Christmas Pig perfect for readers aged 7-9.

Rowling has also written a series of books for adults under the pen name Robert Galbraith. The story follows the cases of Cormoran Strike, a private detective and his partner Robin Ellacott. There are five novels in the series, with the sixth novel titled The Ink Black Heart to be released in August 2022. Her novel Casual Vacancy was her first novel for adults under her own name, which has now been adapted for TV in 2015.

title: J. R. R. Tolkien Books
description:
John Ronald Reuel Tolkien was an English fantasy writer, novelist, artist, scholar, linguist and professor who was most renowned around the world as the author of The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit trilogy. Tolkien spent most of his life teaching at Universities as a distinguished academic. He was a professor at the Universities of Leeds and Oxford for almost forty years, teaching Old and Middle English, as well as Old Norse and Gothic. His illuminating lectures on works such as the Old English epic poem, Beowulf, illustrate his deep knowledge of ancient languages and at the same time provide new insights into peoples and legends from a remote past. His creativity, confined to his spare time, found its outlet in fantasy works, stories for children, poetry, illustration and invented languages and alphabets.

Tolkien’s most popular fantasy novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings trilogy have both had a devoted international fan base and have been adapted into award-winning blockbuster films. If however you are a parent that is raising a reader who enjoys fantasy fiction, Tolkien’s fantasy novels and characters are best enjoyed through Tolkien’s books first and films second. Here are some of Tolkien’s books that any ardent fan must own.

The Monsters and the Critics by J. R. R. Tolkien A comprehensive and complete collection of Tolkien's essays, including two on Beowulf, which span three decades beginning six years before The Hobbit to five years after The Lord of the Rings—this book is just what you need to get your teenager or young adult hooked to quality fiction literature. 

The seven 'essays' by J.R.R. Tolkien assembled in this new paperback edition were with one exception delivered as general lectures on particular occasions; and while they mostly arose out of Tolkien's work in mediaeval literature, they are accessible to all. Two of them are concerned with Beowulf, including the well-known lecture whose title is taken for this book, and one with Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, given in the University of Glasgow in 1953. Also included in this volume is the lecture English and Welsh; the Valedictory Address to the University of Oxford in 1959; and a paper on Invented Languages delivered in 1931, with exemplification from poems in the Elvish tongues. Most famous of all is On Fairy-Stories, a discussion of the nature of fairy-tales and fantasy, which gives insight into Tolkien's approach to the whole genre. 

After the release of The Hobbit, the classic children's story, readers clamoured for a sequel, but Tolkien was trying—and failing—to get his mythological Eä stories into print. Eventually, the two ideas came together, and became the internationally successful The Lord of the Rings. This story, told across a trilogy of books, invented modern fantasy, and inspired everything from Game of Thrones to Dungeons & Dragons. Tolkien's work has since been adapted many times, most notably Peter Jackson's Middle-Earth cycle of films. Fans across the globe are now looking forward to the upcoming series The Rings of Power with the books about where it all began. For those inclined to re-read the complete works before the new releases, we’ve got a complete box set of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings available at a great price.

Whilst The Lord of the Rings is set at the end of the Third Age, The Rings of Power will tell the story of the Second Age. It’s adapted from the references sprinkled throughout The Lord of the Rings, and its extensive appendices. You can read a more complete account of the history of Middle-Earth in J.R.R Tolkien’s middle-earth books published after Tolkien’s death such as The Silmarillion, Unfinished Tales, The Children of Hurin and The Fall of Gondolin. Or you can purchase this curated box set with all four titles—Tales of Middle-earth by J.R.R. Tolkien 5 Books Collection Set.

title: Jack Reacher Books
description:
The Jack Reacher series is a popular book franchise created by British author Lee Child. It revolves around the adventures of the eponymous character, a former United States Army Military Police Corps officer who now wanders the country as a drifter. The series consists of thirty books, with each novel telling a self-contained story.

The first book in the series, Killing Floor, was published in 1997 and introduced readers to Jack Reacher, a character who quickly became a fan favorite. In the book, Reacher is arrested for a crime he didn't commit and ends up getting embroiled in a complex and dangerous conspiracy. From then on, Reacher becomes a lone wolf, wandering from town to town and using his considerable military training to help those in need and right wrongs.

One of the reasons that the Jack Reacher series has been so successful is the character of Jack Reacher himself. Reacher is a complex and enigmatic figure, with a sharp mind and a seemingly inexhaustible array of skills. He's a man of few words and little attachment, but he has a strong moral code and will stop at nothing to protect the innocent and punish the guilty. This makes him a fascinating character to follow, as readers never quite know what he's going to do next.

Another reason for the success of the series is the writing style of Lee Child. Child has a knack for crafting tight, suspenseful plots that keep readers on the edge of their seats. His prose is spare and straightforward, but also evocative and powerful. He's a master of pacing, slowly building the tension until the explosive conclusion.

Throughout the series, Reacher faces a wide variety of adversaries, from corrupt government officials to powerful criminal organizations. He also has a number of recurring allies, including a tough-as-nails female cop named Susan Turner, and a computer expert named Frances Neagley. These characters add depth and richness to the series, making it feel like a fully-realized world.

In addition to the books, the Jack Reacher series has also been adapted into a number of successful movies and a television show. The movies star Tom Cruise as Jack Reacher, and while they've been criticized for not staying true to the character's physical description (Reacher is described as being over six feet tall in the books, while Cruise is only five foot seven), they've still been popular with fans of the series.

In conclusion, the Jack Reacher series is a thrilling, action-packed adventure series that has captured the imaginations of readers all over the world. Lee Child's writing is taut and suspenseful, and Jack Reacher himself is one of the most compelling characters in modern fiction. With over twenty books in the series, there's plenty of material for fans to dive into, and with the recent addition of a television show, it's clear that Jack Reacher isn't going anywhere anytime soon.

title: Jacqueline Wilson Books
description:
Jacqueline Wilson is one of the most beloved children's authors of her generation. She’s written over a hundred books, and in 1991 created the famous character Tracy Beaker, played by Dani Harmer on TV for twenty years. Four of her books were ranked among the 100 most popular books in the UK in 2003’s The Big Read: Double Act, Girls In Love, Vicky Angel, and The Story of Tracy Beaker. Some of her other famous books include The Illustrated Mum, Dustbin Baby, and Hetty Feather. Her memoir for children Jacky Daydream was published in 2007. Long-term collaborator Nick Sharrat usually illustrates her books.

Biography

Wilson was born in Bath in 1945, and grew up in a council flat in Kinston-upon-Thames. She helped launch legendary magazine Jackie when she was seventeen and married a policeman when she was nineteen in 1965. They had one daughter, Emma, and divorced in 2004. She now lives in Sussex with her partner of eighteen years, Trish. She was appointed an OBE in 2002 and became a Dame in 2008. Between these dates, she was the most read author in British libraries. To keep to two novels a year, Wilson makes sure to write 500 words a day before she’s even got out of bed.

Best-Known Books

The Story of Tracy Beaker was published in 1991 and launched Jacqueline Wilson into the stratosphere. It’s told from Tracy’s point of view, who’s been placed in the residential care home “The Dumping Ground” due to her mother’s neglect. She uses her imagination to deal with her unhappiness due to her lot in life. There have been several sequels to the book, and they were adapted into the popular CBBC series Tracy Beaker and its spinoffs.

Dustbin Baby follows April on her fourteenth birthday as she runs through the events of her life and seeks out people from her past. She was found behind a pizza restaurant in the bin and had a tumultuous childhood cycling through foster homes, residential care, and a school for problem girls. It was adapted into a BBC film starring Dakota Blue Richards in 2008.

The Illustrated Mum is about Dolphin, her half-sister Star, and their bipolar alcoholic mum Marigold. Dolphin loves Marigold, but Star is embarrassed by her. After Star’s father comes back onto the scene, their family life becomes increasingly complicated. Dolphin tries to find her old father amid Marigold’s mental breakdown and Star’s desertion to her father.

At Books2Door, we stock several box sets and collections of Jacqueline Wilson’s books. You may also be interested in our pages for other Children’s Laureates, including Michael Morpurgo, Julia Donaldson, and Quentin Blake.

title: James Bond Books
description:
James Bond is a literary franchise that consists of a series of novels and short stories that were first published in 1953 by the British author and journalist Lan Fleming. The protagonist of the series, James Bond, is a British Secret Service agent, often referred to by his code name 007. Lan Fleming himself was a former naval intelligence officer before he turned to writing, which we believe adds an interesting edge to his protagonist James Bond.

James Bond first appeared in Fleming’s 1953 novel Casino Royale following which the character and the books became popular across the world. The books are set in a contemporary period during Fleming's lifetime between 1951 to 1964. Fleming wrote twelve novels and two collections of short stories in the series and published annually. Two of the books were even published after Fleming's death in 1964.

By then James Bond was already an iconic literary character and continued his adventures through several authors that wrote continuation works (books and films) for the franchise. The first in the long list of James Bond literary series authors was Kingsley Amis, who wrote under the pseudonym of Robert Markham. However, John Gardner was the one who was invited to continue the series by Ian Fleming Publications, the copyright holders to the franchise. He wrote fourteen novels and two novelisations between 1981 and 1996. Since Gardner retired due to ill health; many other authors have written James Bond. The most recent novel being the one by Anthony Horowitz which was released more recently on 26th May 2022.

Young Bond: Strike Lightning by Steve Cole Third in this three-part series (also available as a box set) by Steve Cole, this thrilling Young Bond adventure brings back James Bond. If you are a James Bond fan that is keen on getting your child hooked on to the series, this may be a good start for your youngster to become interested in the franchise.

The British chef, television personality, and author has been a ubiquitous presence in kitchens around the globe for more than two decades. Known for his casual, relatable demeanour and passion for simple, delicious food, Jamie Oliver's collection of cookbooks has redefined the way we approach cooking and eating. This collection page at Books2Door serves as your gateway to the world of Jamie Oliver, a world filled with vibrant flavours, easy-to-follow recipes, and a philosophy that champions good food as a cornerstone of good living.

Approachable Cooking For All

If you are new to cooking or feel overwhelmed by the thought of preparing meals, Jamie Oliver’s collection is the perfect starting point. His books like 5 Ingredients: Quick & Easy Food or Jamie’s 30-Minute Meals offer recipes that are not only quick to prepare but also require a minimal list of ingredients. These works break down the barriers to cooking, proving that anyone can create a scrumptious meal without elaborate techniques or a pantry full of exotic ingredients.

From Farm to Table

One of the most compelling aspects of Jamie Oliver’s philosophy is his commitment to using high-quality, sustainable ingredients. His book Jamie Oliver Together is a testament to this approach, focusing on seasonal recipes that emphasise locally sourced produce and meats to produce memorable meals. Oliver doesn’t just offer recipes; he offers an education about the origins of food and the impact that our choices can have on both our bodies and the planet.

A World of Flavors

Jamie Oliver’s culinary adventures have taken him far beyond his native England, and his collection reflects a global palate. Whether it’s exploring the rustic cuisines of Italy in Jamie Cooks Italy or savouring the spicy, vibrant dishes in Jamie’s Food Tube: The BBQ Book, Oliver’s books serve as both cookbooks and travelogues. They invite readers to expand their culinary horizons, encouraging them to step out of their comfort zones and experiment with new flavours and techniques.

Social Impact & Food Education

Jamie Oliver is not just a chef; he's a global advocate for food education. His various campaigns, like the Jamie Oliver Food Foundation, aim to instil a love for cooking and an understanding of nutrition from a young age. Oliver’s collection often includes educational materials aimed at parents and schools, with the intent to transform how societies approach food and health. His books like "Super Food Family Classics" focus on nutritional meals that the whole family can enjoy, seamlessly blending taste and health.

For Food Lovers of Every Stripe

Whether you are a seasoned home cook, a foodie, or someone who has never boiled water successfully, the Jamie Oliver collection has something for you. His books not only make cooking accessible but also turn it into an act of joy and creativity. They embody Oliver’s philosophy that good food is not just about recipes and techniques; it’s about bringing people together and celebrating life’s moments, big and small, around the dining table. Explore this collection and invite the spirit of Jamie Oliver into your kitchen today.

title: Jane Austen Books
description:
Jane Austen Books

Jane Austen is a world-renowned author and a pioneer of literature and paved the way for generations of authors, in particular female authors. Austen was born in Hampshire, England, in 1775 and is primarily known for her six key novels: Pride and Prejudice, Sense and Sensibility, Emma, Mansfield Park, Northanger Abbey and Persuasion. wo of these books were published after her death. Austen had a short life, but her legacy and the impact she made on literature have changed the course of history. 

All of her novels contain heavy criticism of high society at the time and the expectations of women. Austen regularly wrote about the expectations of marriage and the demand for women to be married by a certain age. Jane Austen herself never married but was able to live independently on the profits earned from her writing, so she didn’t need to.

title: Jewish Books
description:
The Jewish culture is rich and the Jewish spirit is unbreakable. It is the resilience of the Jewish people that has kept the community alive and blessed the world with the renowned Jewish sense of humour. Their food, their intellectual prowess, their rich culture and painful history—together make Jews an interesting people with some of the most interesting and moving stories. 

Jewish books therefore are a treasure trove of good quality literature and details about their faith. Jewish writers have an interesting way of delving into details about their beliefs regarding life and death. Precisely why we at Books2Door have curated a collection of the best Jewish books to read; perfect for anyone that is interested in learning about Judaism, the Jewish lifestyle, religion and history. We have tried to pack this collection to the brim with books suitable for every age range too.

For children

Out Of The Hitler Time by Judith Kerr is a set of 3 semi-autobiographical books for children aged 9 plus. The titles in the set include; When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit, Bombs on Aunt Dainty and A Small Person Far Away. Each book in the set is about the plight of jews during war and their respective struggles as refugees.

The first book in the set; When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit is an unforgettable story of a Jewish family fleeing from Germany before the start of the Second World War. This internationally acclaimed story of one Jewish family’s flight from Hitler’s Germany has become a much-loved classic, and has been in print since its debut 45 years ago. 

Bombs on Aunt Dainty follows the life of Anna through a war-torn Germany, to London during the Blitz and her return to Berlin to discover the past. If it wasn’t hard enough being a teenager in London during the Blitz, Anna also finds herself wondering every waking second; whether she will survive the bombs. Can she and her beloved refugee family possibly survive? 

A Small Person Far Away is the third book in the set and is yet another story of survival against all odds during Hitler’s reign and the life of refugees in London. Berlin is where Anna lived before Hitler, when she was still a German child; before she spoke a word of English, before her family had all become refugees. Long before her happy new existence in London. But her mama is there, dangerously ill. Anna is forced to go back, to deal with questions of life and death, to face old fears, and to discover the past which she has so long shut away.

For Young Adults 

Maus I & II Paperback Box Set by Art Spiegelman is a special-edition box set created to celebrate the Pulitzer-Prize winning Graphic Novel’s 40th anniversary. Arguably the best jewish book for young adults; Maus is also widely hailed as the greatest graphic novel ever written and the most famous jewish book to read. MAUS recounts the chilling experiences of the author's father during the Holocaust, with Jews drawn as wide-eyed mice and Nazis as menacing cats. Maus is a haunting tale within a tale, weaving the author's account of his tortured relationship with his ageing father into an astonishing retelling of one of history's most unspeakable tragedies. If you are a Maus fanatic or someone that has thoroughly enjoyed reading Maus; this box set will make a treasured addition to your bookshelf.

For adults

3 Books Collection Set by Joseph Roth This collection of Peter Owen modern classics by Joseph Roth contains—Flight Without End, Weights and Measures and The Silent Prophet. All these books by Joseph Roth, an Austrian-Jewish journalist and novelist, delve into very dark themes about the complexity of life in a war-torn world. 

Flight Without End tells the story of a young ex-officer of the Austro-Hungarian army in the 1914-18 War, who makes his way back from captivity in Siberia, only to find that the old order that shaped him has crumbled and there is no place for him in the new "European" culture. Whilst the second book in the series; Weights and Measures follows the life and experiences of Eibenschütz who leaves his job as an artilleryman in the Austro-Hungarian army for a civilian job as the Inspector of Weights and Measures. Now in a remote territory near the Russian border, he finds his principles at odds with a host of smugglers and crooks. A fable about the disintegration of a good man, Weights and Measures deep dives into moral dilemmas and conflicts.

title: Jigsaw Puzzles
description:
Jigsaw puzzles come in a set of varied, irregularly shaped pieces that when properly assembled, form a complete picture or a map. The Jigsaw puzzles are so named because the original picture attached to wood or paperboard is cut into random pieces using a jigsaw, which cuts intricate lines and curves. These cut-out pieces are carefully and intricately cut in a way such that when put together; they complete a picture.

Jigsaw puzzles however are a lot more than this simple definition. Jigsaw puzzles are an important piece of most of our childhoods. A piece of our childhood that has tickled our brains as children and also helped us develop our cognitive skills. Jigsaw puzzless are like a childhood friend that we all cherish and a childhood memory that your child also deserves to have in their lives.

When you give your kid a jigsaw puzzle; you are not just giving them a simple puzzle game or board game. You are giving them hours of creative thinking, the gift of hand and eye coordination and, of course, hours of fun.

Here are some jigsaw puzzles for children derived from children’s favourite books, games, nature, animals and even maps. Browse through our Jigsaw puzzles collection as we have managed to stock up on some of the most fun and challenging jigsaw puzzles for each age group…

Usborne Book and Jigsaw Animals of the World by Sam Smith for children aged 7+. Give your child the opportunity to travel across the world through this jigsaw puzzle of the world map. Through this puzzle you can allow your kid to explore amazing facts about our planet and its creatures. With this colourful book and 200-piece jigsaw puzzle; give your child hours of fun and also a chance to learn fun facts and fascinating details about this planet we inhabit. 

Adult Jigsaw Puzzle Moomins on the Riviera: 1000-piece Jigsaw Puzzles by Flame Tree Studio If your child is a Moomin fan; then this is the jigsaw puzzle for them. If you are a Moomin fan; this is still the jigsaw puzzle you want to get for your child so they develop a love for the Moomins and good literature at large. 

A 1000-piece jigsaw puzzle in a square box; this one is part of an exciting series from the very popular Flame Tree, featuring powerful works of art. Intended as a jigsaw puzzle for adults and children aged 13+ this jigsaw is designed to satisfy your need for a challenge, with your favourite charming Moomin characters. P.S; this set is not suitable for children under 3 years due to small parts. 

In the event that you are not familiar with the Moomins; here is why you need to familiarise yourself and your child with the series and its endearing characters. Tove Jansson was a Finnish-Swedish writer and artist who created the Moomin characters in 1935 and her last Moomin book was published in 1970. However, the Moomin series and its characters have out-lived their creator and continue to be adapted and enjoyed by several generations even today.

Usborne Book and Jigsaw: Tree of Life by Alice James A colourful 300-piece puzzle featuring a graphic illustration of the tree of life, this jigsaw puzzle features everything from microscopic bacteria to towering trees and sleepy sloths. Accompanied by a book packed with information about the tree of life, the plants and creatures in it—one of the best jigsaw puzzles available; this one is perfect for children 5 and up.

The Fault In Our Stars

Printz Award for excellence in young adult literature and continues to be a beloved choice for book clubs and classrooms.

title: John Grisham Books
description:
An award-winning American novelist; John Grisham is an expert storyteller who writes unforgettable characters that are determined to fight for justice in a world that isn’t always fair.

Bestselling author, former lawyer and member of the 7th district of the Mississippi House of Representatives—John Ray Grisham is popular for his legal thrillers and has managed to author forty-seven consecutive #1 bestselling titles that have been translated into nearly fifty languages. Widely read and celebrated for his writing prowess; Grisham is also a two-time winner of the Harper Lee Prize for Legal Fiction and was honoured with the Library of Congress Creative Achievement Award for Fiction.

When he’s not writing, Grisham is known to serve on the board of directors of the Innocence Project and of Centurion Ministries, two national US organisations dedicated to exonerating those who have been wrongfully convicted. Not surprising then, much of Grisham’s work explores deep-seated problems in the US criminal justice system and many of Grisham’s stories are inspired by true stories. John Grisham’s characters and protagonists strive for justice. Grisham practised criminal law for nearly a decade before his first novel; A Time to Kill was published in June 1989. Grisham’s first bestseller The Firm, managed to sell more than 7 million copies and was adapted into a feature film by the same name starring Tom Cruise. After which several of his novels were adapted into films. 

For anyone that enjoys reading crime thrillers; you are going to love Grisham’s brand of criminal justice novels.

Here are some of our favourite John Grisham books…

Theodore Boone Series Collection 5 Books Box Set By John Grisham A set of 5 stellar young adult books—these smart, fast-paced legal thrillers for young readers all feature the clever and determined kid lawyer Theodore Boone and his newest adventures. Theodore Boone is all of thirteen but he wants nothing more than to swap homeroom for the courtroom. Theodore lives for big trials and wants nothing more than to bring the killer to justice. Overview of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, penned by the acclaimed Hirohiko Araki, is a monumental manga series that has enthralled readers since its inception in 1987. The series is renowned for its distinctive art style, intricate plotlines, and deep character development. It spans multiple generations of the Joestar family, each part featuring a new protagonist nicknamed JoJo. The narrative explores supernatural forces and beings, with protagonists often endowed with unique powers like Stands or the martial arts technique Hamon.

The manga, which began serialisation in Weekly Shōnen Jump and later moved to Ultra Jump, is divided into nine distinct story arcs. It introduces us to a world where characters battle foes using their Stands—psycho-spiritual manifestations with unique supernatural abilities. The series covers a wide range of themes and settings, from 19th-century England to modern Japan and even alternative universes, each part enriching the overarching saga with new conflicts and characters.

JoJo's Bizarre Adventure incorporates multiple genres: action, supernatural, adventure, and fantasy. Its unique narrative blends horror, psychological thriller, and humour. The series is known for its distinctive art style, dramatic character poses, and deep exploration of themes like family, legacy, and the battle between good and evil.

The man behind it all:
Hirohiko Araki, born in Sendai, Japan, in 1960, is a manga artist whose work has left an indelible mark on the manga industry. His journey into the world of manga began early, inspired by a father who was an avid reader. Araki's passion for drawing manifested in his youth, leading him to pursue a career in manga soon after high school. His professional debut came with the one-shot Poker Under Arms; he quickly established a distinctive style that would become his signature.

Araki's breakthrough came with JoJo's Bizarre Adventure in 1986, a series showcasing his storytelling prowess and ability to blend Western pop culture with intricate character designs and dynamic plotlines. His work often features muscular characters and a unique blend of horror, fantasy, and adventure, making his style instantly recognisable.

In addition to JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Araki has worked on various other projects, including collaborating with high-profile brands like Gucci and contributing artwork to international exhibitions, such as at the Musée du Louvre. His book Manga in Theory and Practice offers insights into his creative process, further cementing his status as a manga luminary.

Hirohiko Araki represents an exceptionally distinguished, globally celebrated pioneer in graphic fiction and contemporary manga, whose iconic JoJo's Bizarre Adventure franchise has sold over 120 million copies worldwide and achieved prestigious museum features, including exhibits at the Louvre in Paris. title: Judith Kerr Books
description:
An Iconic Children's Author 

Judith Kerr is a celebrated children's author and illustrator. Her works have been published in many languages and adapted for the big screen.

Born in Berlin in 1923, she and her family fled Germany just as the Nazi party came into power. They eventually settled in England in 1936, but her childhood experience from this period has been published in her trilogy, Out of the Hitler Time. Her children's picture books have been essential to children's nurseries for many years. The light-hearted adventures the characters all experience were all stories she used to tell to her children. For more Picture Books, be sure to check out our full range. 

The Tiger that Came to Tea 

The book follows a young girl called Sophie and her mother as a well-spoken Tiger appears at their door. The Tiger invites himself in for afternoon tea and proceeds to eat and drink everything they have.

Written and illustrated by Kerr, the book was initially created as a bedtime story for her daughter, but fifty years on from its publication, it is still one of the most popular children's books. The Tiger Who Came to Tea is available to purchase on our website. Perfect for The Gruffalo and Julia Donaldson fans, The Tiger Who Came to Tea is the ideal book for reading together. 

Mog the Cat 

Written and illustrated by Kerr, the seventeen-book series contains many adventures from the mischievous cat. Our Mog the Cat 8 Books Collection is the perfect gift for any child. These picture books are beautifully illustrated and set out in an easy-to-read format, making them ideal for bedtime stories. 

We also have Mog the Forgetful Cat available to order separately. In 2002 Judith Kerr published the final book in the series, Goodbye Mog, in which the beloved character passes away. This book has been a sad but excellent source for helping children cope with loss and grief. 

Out of the Hilter Time 

When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit has quickly become an essential modern classic. This semi-autobiographical count tells the story of a Jewish family fleeing from Germany just before WW2, just like Kerr's family did. The Out of the Hilter Time Trilogy has been critically acclaimed and praised for its portrayal of the Nazis' takeover of Germany and the experience of being a refugee through the eyes of a nine-year-old girl. The fact that the books reflect on Kerr's own experiences makes the books even more essential and heartbreaking to read. 

We have the trilogy available to order here, Out of Hilter Time 3 Book Set. This series is aimed at ages 9+ due to the reading level. The books are at a much higher reading level than her picture books; with a handful of illustrations and chapters, it is an excellent series for any child wanting to broaden their reading library. For more books like When Hitler Stole Pink Rabbit series check out Michael Morpurgo Books or Goodnight Mister Tom by Michelle Magorian.

title: Julia Donaldson Books
description:
Julia Donaldson is one of our top-selling authors. With iconic books like The Gruffalo and Cave Baby, it’s not hard to see why. Her picture books with illustrators like Lydia Monks, Nick Sharrat, and particularly long-time collaborator Axel Scheffler have been bestsellers for over twenty years - and with good reason.

With their wonderful rhymes and delightful stories, Julia Donaldson’s books are a great choice if you want to read aloud with your child. The illustrations are always funny and imaginative and bring the fantastical characters to life. Once you’ve met Zog and The Highway Rat, you’ll never forget them. If you’ve watched the films, or gone to see the stage shows, you must get the books.

At Books2Door, we stock a wide range of Julia Donaldson’s books, essential for any picture book library. We’ve got everything from The Scarecrow’s Wedding to Tyrannosaurus Drip. Our comprehensive selection will ensure that you’ll be able to find the right Julia Donaldson book for your child.

 

Picture books

Julia Donaldson’s most famous story is The Gruffalo. A mouse walking through the forest has to evade being eaten by some fearsome predators. To scare them off, he tells each in turn that he’s on his way to eat with his friend, the fearsome Gruffalo. The mouse doesn’t think the Gruffalo exists, or does it? Children across the world love this modern classic. It’s been made into a hit BBC One animated film, a stage play, and a ride at Chessington World of Adventures.

Find The Gruffalo and more in The Julia Donaldson Story Collection. It contains ten of her most famous books, including Room on the Broom, Charlie Cook’s Favourite Book, The Snail and the Whale and The Gruffalo’s Child. Seven of these are collaborations with Axel Scheffler, and there’s one book each with David Roberts, Emily Gravett and Rebecca Cobb.

The Julia Donaldson & Axel Scheffler 10 Book Collection includes their most recent collaborations. Remarkable stories like Stick Man, The Highway Rat, Superworm, The Smeeds and the Smoos, and Zog and the Flying Doctors feature in this great value pack. There’s no overlap between these two collections, so why not get both?

You can also get The Julia Donaldson Collection across 10 CDs. It features readings of some of her best-loved stories, as well as her album The Gruffalo Song and Other Songs. It’s a perfect accompaniment for car journeys, bedtimes, and many other occasions.

We stock many of her other picture books, either individually or in packs. What the Ladybird Heard, Sugarlump and the Unicorn, and her other collaborations with Lydia Monks are very popular with young readers. There’s Spinderella, the spider with a passion for football. Or how about Night Monkey Day Monkey, which is perfect for toddlers?

There’s Julia Donaldson’s Songbirds for children learning to read, part of the Read with Oxford line. Part of the bestselling reading scheme, these books will take children from phonics right up to becoming confident, independent readers. They’re the perfect accompaniment to the Biff, Chip & Kipper series.

There’s a Julia Donaldson book for every child aged 0-5. It’s not really a case of which one should you choose, but which one first?

 

About the author

Julia Donaldson was born Julia Shields in 1948 in Hampstead, London. It was a musical household - both of her parents were in the Hampstead Music Club. Her mother sang, and her father played the cello. During her childhood, Donaldson acted at the Old Vic, played the piano, and sang with the Children’s Opera Group. By the age of 19, she was conversant in French, German and Italian. During her studies in the 60s, she lived in Bristol and Paris and met her future husband, Malcolm Donaldson.

After graduating from Bristol University in 1970 with a 2:1 in Drama and French, Donaldson had various jobs throughout the 70s, sometimes simultaneously. Primarily she wrote songs for BBC Children’s Television, for shows such as Play Away, Play School and Watch With Mother. She also worked as an editor for publishers including Michael Joseph and Robert Tyndall. In 1974 she moved to Brighton and performed in the local folk club scene with Malcolm. She devised plays for children, ran a Saturday-morning workshop, and composed two children’s musicals. She worked for Radio Bristol and for two years as a teacher until 1978 - her last full-time employment. Their first son, Hamish, was born in 1978.

Work was slow during the 1980s. Alastair was born in 1981, and the family moved to Bristol in 1983. Donaldson wrote topical songs for the radio, did street theatre and amateur acting, and volunteered in Hamish’s primary school by devising plays for the reading group. Jerry came along in 1987, and they moved near Glasgow in 1989.

Julia Donaldson was commissioned for more songs for BBC programmes in the 1990s. More significantly, she was asked to adapt her 1975 song “A Squash and a Squeeze” as a picture book with illustrator Axel Scheffler. It was published in 1993 and led to Donaldson’s writing career. She published her plays for children from the 80s and wrote extensively for educational publishers.

In 1999 Donaldson and Scheffler published The Gruffalo, which was an overnight success. The duo has since published over 25 books together, some of which have been made into films, plays, and musicals. The Gruffalo was a life-changing success and completely altered the course of Donaldson’s career. She has since won multiple awards, served as children’s laureate, and written many more books for her legion of fans worldwide.

Donaldson has also published CDs, plays, picture books, books for older children and teenagers, poetry books, and educational books. She’s written over 200 books - over half for educational use in schools and at home. Donaldson often performs her work at book festivals and theatres, encouraging children to join in with the storytelling. New books are coming out every year, and Donaldson is as enthusiastic as ever about children’s literacy and the value of a good story. So we’ll hopefully be enjoying her singular creative talent for some time yet.

title: Kazuo Ishiguro Books
description:
This collection has been curated to showcase the work of the bestselling author Kazuo Ishiguro. He’s one of the leading authors of literary fiction in the UK and appeals to both adult and young adult audiences. The central themes of his novels surround abstract concepts such as time, memory, loss and lifelong deception - particularly its unreliability in narratives. A lot of his work focuses on the manipulation of human desire and how human beings reinterpret their own world from which they are estranged. His work moves freely across genres, including fantasy, magical realism and SF.

At Books2Door, we want to highlight and celebrate a range of different authors to give you the best selection of books. Browse our full Authors page to view our full list of bestselling authors, artists and illustrators to discover your next favourite read. 

Biography

Sir Kazuo Ishiguro is a British novelist, screenwriter and musician born in Nagasaki, Japan, in 1954. He moved to Britain in 1960 with his parents when he was five years old. Ishiguro is one of the most critically acclaimed contemporary English fiction writers of this century, being awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature. He won the Booker Prize for the 1989 novel The Remains of the Day, which was soon adapted into an Oscar-nominated movie starring Anthony Hopkins.

Kazuo Ishiguro’s most notable works

If you’re not sure where to start, let us help to give you a few handy recommendations to get you going. Why not check out his latest dystopian science fiction work, Klara and the Sun? Published in 2021, the book is told from the viewpoint of the titular character, Klara, a solar-powered AF (Artificial Friend). 

Klara has been chosen by Josie, a sickly child, to be her android companion and caretaker. Through the window of a store for which she is for sale, Klara learns about the world through outstanding observation qualities and watches the Sun, often referring to it as a physical entity. In the growing days, as Josie almost reaches the brink of death, she implores the Sun to heal and save her. Ishiguro presents an accurate insight into the human experience through the eyes of an unforgettable narrator to answer the fundamental question: what does it mean to love?

One of Ishiguro’s most popular books is Never Let Me Go. In a dystopian version of late 1990s England. The book follows Kathy’s perspective as she attempts to come to terms with her childhood and upbringing and towards a bleak fate that awaits her and her closest friends. Ishiguro masterfully presents the fragility of life, identity, empathy and friendship in this novel. Time named it the best novel of 2005 and one of the top 100 novels published since 1923. The book has also been adapted into the 2010 film of the same name, directed by Mark Romanek and starring Cary Milligan, Andrew Garfield and Keira Knightley.

Oi Dog! by Kes Gray The laughter never ends with the Oi Frog and Friends series! Packed to the brim with silly animals this absurdly funny sequel to the bestselling Oi Frog, is a hilarious rhyming story that will have children rolling around with laughter.

Winner of the Laugh Out Loud Picture Book Award and shortlisted for the Sainsbury's Book Award; this one is a laughter riot throughout. Cat is a stickler for rules: cats sit on mats, hares sit on chairs and, however irritating, dogs must sit on frogs. That's until Frog decides to change the status quo. But will Cat want to sit on gnats instead of cushy mats? Will spiders like sitting on gliders? Will whales like sitting on nails? And, most importantly, where is FROG going to sit? The book is a giggling delight, a perfect match of words and pictures to entertain kids again and again.

Younger children will enjoy reading the book because of the rhyme scheme as the frog lists different things that each animal should sit on. Additionally, the illustrations in this book paint an imaginative picture for the younger kids to learn about different animals.

With the Oi Frog and Friends book, you can have your child point out several rhyming phrases as they read these books. You can have the children find out what makes these words rhyming words. title: Khaled Hosseini Books
description:
Khaled Hosseini is a name that echoes in the literary world as an emblem of poignant storytelling, rich cultural exposition, and deeply intricate character development. His books are not mere compilations of printed words; they are curated experiences that delve into the human psyche, sociopolitical landscapes, and intricate webs of relationships. Born in Kabul, Afghanistan, and later relocating to the United States, Hosseini draws from a well of experiences and cultures that infuse his writing with unparalleled depth. Purchase all three books in this masterful Khaled Hosseini collection with the Khaled Hosseini 3 Book Collection now available and in stock at Books2Door! 

The Kite Runner— Hosseini's debut novel—has become a modern classic. Published in 2003, this riveting story focuses on Amir, a young boy from Kabul, and his complicated friendship with Hassan, his father's servant's son. Set against the backdrop of Afghanistan's turbulent history, from the fall of the monarchy to the rise of the Taliban, the story explores themes of guilt, betrayal, and the quest for atonement. The kite-fighting scenes serve as a brilliant metaphor, entwining the fate of the characters with the kites they fly, cut, and chase. If you're new to Hosseini's works, this is often the starting point—and for a good reason.

A Thousand Splendid Suns takes us back to Afghanistan but shifts its focus to the intricacies of women’s lives under oppressive regimes. Following the stories of Mariam and Laila, two women from different backgrounds but similar fates, the book captures the essence of sacrifice, resilience, and the unbreakable bond that forms in the face of immense adversity. For anyone interested in understanding the lives of women in the Middle East or those who simply love a tale of indomitable spirit against all odds, this book is a must-read.

And the Mountains Echoed is a tapestry of interconnected stories laid out over continents and generations. A departure from the single, linear narrative, this book resembles a collection of short stories that are brilliantly woven together. With themes ranging from love, sacrifice, and betrayal to the complexities of family relationships, the book showcases Hosseini's narrative versatility. Every character feels lived-in and authentic, making you invest emotionally in their individual journeys as much as in their interconnected destinies.

The appeal of Hosseini's works is not solely confined to the narrative brilliance. He employs a host of literary devices—from evocative metaphors to striking imagery—to craft a story that resonates emotionally and intellectually. His narrative style accommodates different viewpoints, allowing readers to immerse themselves in the world he's created. This level of emotional engagement is why so many readers have claimed that Hosseini's books have changed their perspectives on life, empathy, and the collective human experience.

Moreover, his books are often accompanied by thought-provoking discussion questions, making them ideal picks for book clubs and classroom settings. They are not just stories to be read but experiences to be discussed, dissected, and absorbed.

The magic of Khaled Hosseini's books lies in their universality. While they bring to light the cultural, historical, and social nuances of Afghanistan, their themes are universally relatable. They are about us—about our frailties, our desires, our relationships, and our ceaseless quest for a place we can call 'home'.

So, whether you're a voracious reader on the hunt for your next great read or someone looking to delve into a story that offers more than just a beginning, middle, and end, Khaled Hosseini’s books are not just a choice; they are imperative. These are not mere books; they are journeys that enrich the soul, question our prejudices, and embrace our shared humanity. Prepare to be not just entertained but profoundly moved.

Alongside these practical benefits, there are also numerous benefits of using audiobooks to enhance your child’s reading ability and help them gain confidence and independence as they continue to read. By listening to skilled narrators, children are exposed to rich vocabularies, diverse sentence structures, and various accents. This exposure to different speech patterns and styles helps enhance their language skills, vocabulary, and comprehension. Ladybird Books UK is a renowned London-based children’s publishing company, trading as a stand-alone imprint within the Penguin Group. The Ladybird imprint publishes an extensive range of children's books for all ages. From new-borns to toddlers up to primary aged children. Ladybird Books children’s classics feature everything from classic fairy tales to early learning books to TV adaptations of classics.

Originally founded in 1867, this British publisher has been producing mass-market books for children for over 100 years. They have mastered the art of publishing for children and know exactly what kids like to read, from cover to cover. Ladybird Books recommend reading in stages, with a tried and tested method that has continued to stand the test of time. The iconic little ladybird appears on every single children’s book and library collection, something that young book lovers will come to recognise and love as they work their way up the Ladybird Books’ many collections.

We at Books2Door have heard parents and schools rave about Ladybird Books for their solid understanding of how to approach reading with children of all ages. They are popular for producing big box sets as well as individual titles that not only encourage children to pick up the books but also guides them through their journey of becoming confident readers. From practising phonics to stunning and engaging picture books to reading aloud—Ladybird Books cover every stage of reading. Plus, they cover a huge range of interests to suit your child.

Ladybird Books for children offers some of the absolute best books in children’s fiction with phenomenal stories and literature that your child is going to love having on their bookshelf. Here are some of our favourites from their extensive range…

Early Learning Ladybird Head Start 18 Books & 52 Flashcards Collection. This set of paperback books and flashcards for children aged 4 to 8 years has everything you could possibly need to give your child a head-start with early learning. Providing structured practice of phonics, handwriting and essential maths concepts—these bright, motivating books and flash cards help to reinforce learning in a fun way. Titles in this Set include: 12 Phonics readers, 4 Maths sticker books, 2 Handwriting sticker books 52 Flash cards. Get your hands on these and give your child the gift of a head-start on school learning. For more phonics, check out our dedicated phonics books page.

A Baby Ladybird Library - Children's 10 Books Collection Set this one has 10 spectacular books, each prefect for children aged 0 to 5. Each board book adorned in bold, bright colours and simple text covers an important subject like shapes, animal sounds, On the farm, Things that go, colours, At the zoo, numbers, animals, faces and first words; respectively. For more board books, check out our dedicated board books page here. 

These fabulous books are the perfect way to introduce your little one to their reading journey whilst also allowing their sensory development. These books help stimulate the development of your child’s senses whilst also encouraging interaction and play between the parent and child.

Ladybird I'm Ready 8 Books Collection Set is a set of Ladybird books for children aged 5 to 7 years is a comprehensive set of workbooks packed to the brim with activities that will ensure cognitive and sensory development of your child. The phonics activity books are a great way for children to learn and practise their phonics skills. The series of phonic readers and their accompanying activity workbooks have been carefully written to give gradual, structured practice of the synthetic phonics to your child. The 4 titles in the collection set include—Adding and Subtracting: Ladybird I'm Ready for Maths, Time, Shapes and Seasons: Ladybird I'm Ready for Maths, Times Tables: Ladybird I'm Ready for Maths, Multiplying and Dividing: Ladybird I'm Ready for Maths; each focused on a different maths function to ensure your child gets enough and more practice with each.

title: Laura Ellen Anderson Books
description:
A page dedicated to books written by British Children's author and illustrator Laura Ellen Anderson. She is behind many unique series', including Amelia Fang and Rainbow Grey.

Laura Ellen Anderson is a British children's author and illustrator best known for her quirky and imaginative books that capture the hearts and minds of young readers. With a range of captivating characters and vivid illustrations, Anderson's work is beloved by both children and adults alike, making her a highly respected figure in the world of children's literature.

Born in the UK in 1988, Anderson spent much of her childhood drawing and creating stories, leading her to study illustration at the University of Falmouth. Since then, she has worked on numerous successful children's book series, including Amelia Fang and Evil Emperor Penguin.

One of Anderson's most popular series, the Amelia Fang books, follows the adventures of a young vampire girl named Amelia, her pet pumpkin Squashy, and her friends in Nocturnia. The books are a unique blend of humour, adventure, and friendship, making them popular among children of all ages. With its charming illustrations and engaging storytelling, the Amelia Fang series has won multiple awards and has been translated into numerous languages. These books are perfect for children aged 7-9 years old. 

Another popular series by Anderson is Evil Emperor Penguin, which tells the story of an evil penguin who is determined to take over the world. The books are filled with hilarious jokes and witty puns, making them enjoyable for both children and adults. Anderson's illustrations are full of intricate details, bringing the story to life in a fun and engaging way. In addition to her book series, Anderson has also worked on other projects, including creating book covers for other authors and illustrating activity books for children. Her unique style and colourful illustrations have made her a highly sought-after illustrator in the industry, and prestigious organizations like the Society of Illustrators have recognized her work.

Anderson's success is a testament to her talent, hard work, and dedication to creating memorable and inspiring stories for children. Her books have sparked a love of reading in countless young readers and have helped to cultivate a new generation of book lovers.

In addition to her work as an author and illustrator, Anderson is also an advocate for diversity in children's literature. She has spoken out about the importance of representing diverse characters in children's books, and her own books feature a wide range of characters from different backgrounds.

Overall, Laura Ellen Anderson is a talented and innovative author and illustrator who has significantly impacted the world of children's literature. With her engaging stories and stunning illustrations, she has captured the hearts of children and adults alike and has inspired a love of reading in countless young readers. Her work is sure to continue to delight and inspire for years to come.

Anderson's books are perfect for fans of Isadora Moon by Harriet Muncaster, the Bad Mermaids series by Sibeal Pounder, the Toto the Ninja Cat Series By Dermot O'Leary and the Sam Wu Is NOT Afraid of…series by Katie and Kevin Tsang.

title: Laura Thalassa Books
description:
Join us at Books2Door as we celebrate Laura Thalassa and explore her works. 

Let us enter her worlds, which will capture us with a blend of fantasy, romance, and, without fail, spice! Let us look at the works of this author, who is bestselling and has her novels as a testament to her passion for storytelling.

With a range of themes under her belt, Thalassa's books are a treat for readers who are all in when it comes to captivating plots, dynamic characters, and a good amount of heat. Thalassa's writing transports us to worlds filled with mystery, magic, and passion, helping us escape into alternate realities.

The Four Horsemen series, one of her most popular, is a saga that delves into her recurring themes of love and destiny in an apocalyptic world, suitable for readers 18 and up. Set in a world where the four horsemen of the apocalypse roam freely, these books blend fantasy and romance, keeping us on the edge of our seats. 

Another significant aspect of The Four Horsemen series is that it can be read out of order and enjoyed in every way we want. While there is an overarching plot, each book can still be read as a standalone story without leaving us, her avid readers, feeling lost or confused. This allows us to dive into Thalassa's world at any point and immerse ourselves in the thrilling adventures of her characters.

Thalassa's storytelling extends to The Bargainer series, a mesmerising collection that delves into the realms of fae and magic also for adult readers. With four books in this captivating series, we are invited to join protagonist Callie as she navigates a world of danger, intrigue, and forbidden romance. Set against the backdrop of the mystical Otherworld, this series promises to enthral us with its spellbinding plot and irresistible characters.

What makes Thalassa's works unique is her ability to add a lot of spice to her storylines, which makes readers who like heat in their romance novels want more. Even if Thalassa's earlier works were perhaps less passionate, her writing has enhanced over time, and her more recent books include more intimate sequences guaranteed to make your heart race.

title: Learn to Read Books
description:
If we haven’t said it already, we will say it again—reading is extremely important for children! Exposure to good, age-appropriate books is crucial for younglings who are learning to read, through their formative years. 

Books expose children to new worlds and new words, improve their vocabulary and help them discover new ways of using language. Books also help children learn general information about the world, which makes it easier for them to navigate the world and learn about new subjects and objects.

It is important that you give your children access to the best, most age-appropriate books available. Precisely why, we at Books2Door have curated this collection of learning to read books for children starting at 0-years-of-age right up to 9-years-old where they can be independent readers. 

Usborne First Phonics Reading Library 20 Books Set for children between the ages 0 to 5. My First Phonics Reading Library from Usborne is a fantastic introduction for your child to the world of reading. These books use simple rhyming language and essential vocabulary to help kids learn how the sounds they make relate to the words on the page. Every volume in this twenty book collection set is fully illustrated, with fourteen books by David Semple and six books by Fred Blunt. Children in the age bracket will love the charming illustrations and vibrant use of colour, and this in turn will make them want to learn.

Among the many funny stories are Underpants for Ants, where a mouse has to knit underwear for the chilly ants. There’s also Spider in a Glider, where the intelligent arachnid inventor has to turn her many hands to heroism. And who could forget Seal at the Wheel, where a speeding seal learns the hard way about careful driving. Children are going to love these unforgettable tales; that will help them learn how words work together in sentences. They'll be able to build their vocabulary while learning about animals, colours, shapes and more. Your child will love each story as they learn in an engaging manner that keeps them entertained throughout the entire book. This collection is perfect for parents who want their kids to grow up loving books as much as they do. And it's never too early to start building those lifelong skills!

Julia Donaldson's Songbirds Phonics: Read with Oxford Stages 1-4 is a 36 Books Collection Set has learning to read books for 3-year-olds (for children aged between 0 to 5) Julia Donaldson Songbirds collection is one that comes with the most amazing books which are designed to help kids around the world develop important reading skills. Produced by Oxford University Press, each book and phonic story is carefully crafted with words, sounds, spelling patterns and phonology to teach children the fundamentals of reading. Some words are rhymes and some tell a fun story to help kids engage with the story. The 36 books packed together neatly in a wallet, contain exciting titles which are carefully levelled to help readers gain reading confidence step by step. This collection can truly help ease children’s minds and help them develop their reading skills. Kids can gradually level up their reading skills to prepare them for classes in school, especially as children move on from class to class, year to year. 

Reading Ladder My First Read-Along Library 30 Books Box Set for children aged 5-7 is a book set that every child needs if you as parents want to ensure development of their reading knowledge. A great help in learning to read in a fun and easy way with plenty of support, this particular set is fantastic for ages 5-7. This particular Reading Ladder collection was designed by literacy experts and professionals like Nikki Gamble to make learning straightforward for kids. Furthermore Reading Ladder will make reading fun, providing them a positive and bright beginning to their literary journey. 

Perfect for home studying and an essential part of your child’s book collection. Learning to read Level 1 Reading Ladder books are designed for new readers, and help kids begin their reading life, with letters and sounds. There are fun ways to engage with your kids when reading these books, ask questions and get their opinions on what they think the books is about based on illustrations and titles. 

Learning to read Level 2 is best for young readers who have gained some confidence in reading basic words and sentences. Books in Level 2 therefore contain longer and more interesting conversations and pages, so kids will need to learn to read more challenging words, scenarios as well as absorb and take in more complicated story-lines. Level 2 covers bands Orange, Turquoise, Purple, these books will have a wide array of sentence structures, and a range of vocabulary that might not be found in Level 1. However just like Level 1, Level 2 books also come accompanied with illustrations that lend themselves to the stories, the characters and ensure the children stay interested in the books.

Learning to read Level 3 obviously is the most challenging Level in this collection and will be best suited for readers who are completely confident with independent reading, readers are now fluent and can comprehend a variety of themes and stories. Books in Level 3 therefore are divided into chapters, and the sentence structures are different from page to page. Vocabulary is more evolved compared to Level 2 and Level 1, the story-lines are designed to push children to think on their own and give them the chance to try and grasp these new found concepts. Languages have now become technical, kids are now reading aloud quickly and confidently without needing help from parents!

title: Lee Child Books
description:
Lee Child is a British author, most famous for his thrill-seeking and crime-fighting Jack Reacher series. As of 2022, there are a total of 27 books in the Jack Reacher series, with many more planned. The series follows a former major in the United States Army Military Police Corps as he travels across America and the rest of the world to investigate suspicious activity. Since the release of the first book, Killing Floor, in 1997, Child has published at least one new Reacher book each year. They are now written with his brother Andrew Child.

The Jack Reacher books have sold over 100 million copies across 49 languages and continue to be among the highest-grossing series. Child was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in the 2019 Queen's Birthday Honours List for services to literature.

Jack Reacher

As mentioned above, there are currently 27 books in the Jack Reacher series and counting. As the series stands, here is a breakdown of all Jack Reacher titles in the order they were published. 

  1. Killing Floor
  2. Die Trying
  3. Tripwire
  4. The Visitor

  10. The Hard Way
  11. Bad Luck and Trouble
  12. Nothing To Lose
  13. Gone Tomorrow
  14. 61 Hours

  16. The Affair

  18. Never Go Back

  23. Past Tense

In 2012, Hollywood came for a slice of Reacher and a movie adaptation was made starring Tom Cruise in the titular role. The movie is an adaptation of the ninth novel in the series, One Shot. A sequel to the film was released in 2016 following the eighteenth novel, Never Go Back. 

However, Jack Reacher has recently been turned into a TV series with Amazon Prime. The series is said by fans to follow the original source material more strictly,even down to casting of Jack Reacher with of 6'2 American actor Alan Ritchson. 

In January 2020, Child announced that he would be retiring from writing the Jack Reacher books, and handing it to his brother Andrew Grant. His brother will continue to write further books in the series under the surname Child. The first book written in collaboration was the 25th installment, The Sentinel, and since then books in the series has beeb credited to both brothers.

Child has managed to maintain the same high-level crime thriller novels packed full of action and suspense for twenty-five years and counting. Trained under the wise guidance of Sensei Wu, they are not your average warriors. They are defenders of peace, protectors of sacred artefacts, and warriors of immense skill and courage. With every flip, kick, and elemental burst, they captivate hearts and inspire awe. But don't let their youth fool you—each holds incredible powers that can both create and destroy!

Meet our fearless heroes, each a Master of an elemental power. There's Kai, the Master of Fire, whose fiery personality is as vibrant as the flames he controls. Then we have Jay, the Master of Lightning, whose quick wit is as electrifying as his abilities. Don't forget Cole, the Master of Earth, as solid and dependable as the ground we walk on. Zane, the Master of Ice, is the group's strategist, always keeping a cool head. Nya, Kai’s sister and the Master of Water brings a tidal wave of determination to the team. And finally, there’s Lloyd, the Green Ninja, who is destined to be the most powerful of them all. Led by Master Wu, a wise, ancient ninja and the brother of the villainous Lord Garmadon, they form an unbreakable team.

An Adventure for Every Age

Our collection is designed to cater to a wide audience, including young readers taking their first steps into the world of Ninjago, as well as seasoned fans looking for advanced narratives and comprehensive world-building. We offer books in various formats: storybooks for younger children, chapter books for intermediate readers, and detailed encyclopedias for those wanting to dive deep into the Ninjago universe.
