title: Leigh Bardugo Books
description:
Leigh Bardugo is the bestselling author behind the Grishaverse. Not just a young adult literary phenomenon, it’s also a Netflix series named after the first book and Bardugo’s debut novel, Shadow and Bone. Across multiple series and mediums, the Grishaverse is a dark fantasy world set in nations that are both familiar and original. The story weaves between multiple characters and locations, which intersect in ways you may not be expecting. It’s a world of magic, monsters, love and darkness, spun across seven addictive novels and several companion books. Why not give the series a go?

The Grishaverse

If you want to get started with the Grishaverse, there’s no better way to begin than the Shadow and Bone Trilogy. These books follow Alina Starkov of Ravka, who discovers she is a Grisha, someone with the ability to manipulate the elements and use them as weapons. These books are described by Bardugo as Tsarpunk - fantasy set in a version of 19th century Tsarist Russia.

The next two books are known as the Six of Crows duology. Describes as Ocean’s 11 meets Game of Thrones, these books follow The Dregs, a group tasked with rescuing the inventor of a dangerous drug from a military stronghold to prevent it from being revealed to the world. These books are set in Ketterdam, inspired by 17th-18th century Amsterdam, and are a great left-turn on any expectations you had after reading the first trilogy.

The final books in the series - for now - are the King of Scars duology, which combines characters from the previous books and sets Ravka on the path to war. These books tie together many of the loose ends left throughout the series and bring it to a satisfying pause. However, Bardugo has “long term plans” for more books in the Grishaverse, so watch this space!

There are several companion books to keep you going in the meantime. The Language of Thorns brings together fairy tale retellings as they’re known in Ravka, perfect for crawling up in front of a fire with. There’s also The Lives of Saints, a book that exists in the Grishaverse and now in our own dimension. Finally, the short story “Demon in the Wood” is being adapted into a graphic novel, due for release in September 2022.

Other books

Bardugo has begun a new series for adults, following the character Alex Stern. These tales of murder and dark magic are set among the Ivy League elite, and began with Ninth House in 2019. The next book, Hell Bent, was published in January 2023. She’s also written Wonder Woman: Warbringer as both a novel and a graphic novel.

The Six of Crows Duology: Six of Crows, Crooked Kingdom

The King of Scars Duology: King of Scars, Rule of Wolves

Other Grishaverse books: The Language of Thorns, The Lives of Saints,  Demon in the Wood (forthcoming)

 

Other books

Alex Stern: Ninth House, Hell Bent

title: Lifestyle Books
description:
An exciting genre for those who want to live the good life—lifestyle non-fiction includes books that focus on leading quality lives. Lifestyle books usually contain ideas and insights about health, wellness, home decor, relationships, meaningful work, food, fashion, leisure activities, and even personal finance.

Authors of the lifestyle genre deep dive into the said topics to provide readers with valuable lifestyle tips and insights that are supported by extensive research and experience, new trends and innovations. Lifestyle books across several sub-categories, are designed to help readers find joy in everyday activities and lead fulfilling lives that are at par with modern times in every aspect.

From mindfulness in adult colouring books to coping with bereavement, we at Books2Door have got a wide selection of books to help you in your day-to-day lives. From inspiring self-help guides to invaluable titles on health, pregnancy and childcare. From lifestyle books on healthy eating and getting in shape to engrossing medical memoirs, first aid manuals, and books about coping with loss and grief, depression and anxiety. We have several lifestyle books in stock so you can use ‘em to feed your soul, strengthen your body and take actionable steps towards achieving greater personal fulfilment.

Adult colouring books

Touted as an approach to self-care and a potential relaxation technique; adult colouring has become something of a trend. It is even regarded as a mental health exercise. From mandalas and detailed scenery to tapestries; adult colouring books are available in various types for different preferences. 

The perfect way to self-soothe and spend some quality time with yourself; adult colouring books can keep you busy for hours on end. It is not just an activity or brain exercise either. Adult colouring can be a therapeutic experience on its own. The therapeutic, stress-busting properties of adult colouring make these adult colouring books a fantastic investment. Simply browse through our collection where we have curated a vast variety of colouring books and give yourself the perfect opportunity to extend your art into more unstructured directions.

Cookbooks 

Whether it’s fine dining or a weekday meal, specialist cookery or baking for a loved one, we’ve got a book for every type of cook! We stock a range of recipe books suitable for a wide range of skill levels and interests. Whether you’re looking for an easy beginner’s guide or a professional chef’s recipe book, we have got it all. And they are available at the lowest possible price!

There are few better bakers out there than Mary Berry. Now, you can discover all of her best recipes from the Queen of Cakes in Mary Berry’s Ultimate Cake Book. This baking bible should be in every kitchen. If you’re looking to combine food and fitness, then Lean in 15 Collection by Joe Wicks is the collection for you. Combining tasty and healthy meals with high-intensity workout sessions, these books are great for setting you on a healthy lifestyle without starving yourself. 

Death and Bereavement 

Dealing with the loss of a loved one or grief of any kind can be life altering for children and adults. For anyone to cope with grief, they need a ton of support, positivity and ways to channel their grief into something productive. Books on grief and loss, we think, can play a pivotal role in doing so. Stories of people that have dealt with grief and loss in positive ways can help a grieving person (irrespective of age) find hope.

We have curated a collection of some of the best selling books on grief and loss, to help people, especially children cope with loss and grief. The Memory Tree by Britta Teckentrup for instance is a heartfelt picture book to help children celebrate the memories left behind when a loved one dies. This gentle story about loss is a perfect grief book for adults and children, that teaches how sharing can bring comfort.

Fitness and Diet 

Contrary to popular belief, the one-size-fits-all approach does not work in fitness. We each have a different body type which has different needs with regard to fitness, nutrition and health. What works for one individual might not always work for another. Precisely why, it is important to read up, educate yourselves before you start following any trending fitness regimen or diet for yourself. Similarly, if you have any particular physical ailment you must avoid certain exercises and not just blindly follow the newest fitness trends. 

To make sure you are treating your body right and consuming what it needs without doing it any harm; we have curated a selection of books to help you live your healthiest possible life! Tiny Habits: Why Starting Small Makes Lasting Change Easy by BJ Fogg for instance is a book all about improving your lifestyle. Whether it's losing weight, sleeping more, or restoring your work/life balance—the secret is to start small. Tiny Habits advocates starting with quick wins and embedding new, tiny habits into our everyday routines in order to initiate big lifestyle and lasting changes in your life and routine. 

Self Help Books 

Self Help Books as the name suggests are designed to help the readers work on themselves and better themselves. Self help books are designed to help the readers overcome their problems. It could be career, productivity, relationships, finding happiness—whatever your human concern; we bet there is a self help book waiting to help you! 


Now we understand, every self help book may not be able to give you advice specific to your situation. However, every self help book without exception, will at its very least guide you to cultivate a more positive attitude, urge you to evaluate your life, assess what needs to change and do better. This honest evaluation of your life allows you to make changes and assess what works for you and what doesn’t. Not to mention, reading the author’s experiences will help you realise that you are not the only one going through something. Mark Manson 3 Books Collection Set - The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fuck for instance is one bestselling self help book that serves some major truth bombs. For decades, we’ve been told that positive thinking is the key to a happy, rich life. "F**k positivity," Mark Manson says. "Let’s be honest, shit is f**ked and we have to live with it." In his wildly popular Internet blog, Manson doesn’t sugarcoat or equivocate. He tells it like it is—a dose of raw, refreshing, honest truth that is sorely lacking today. The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F**k is his antidote to the coddling, let’s-all-feel-good mindset that has infected American society and spoiled a generation, rewarding them with gold medals just for showing up.

title: Light Novel's
description:
Light Novels Collection: The Ultimate Bridge Between Manga and Epic Fiction

Why wait for the next episode when you can read ahead? The Light Novels Collection at Books2Door is a dedicated hub for one of the fastest-growing genres in global literature. Originating from Japan, Light Novels (LNs) offer a unique reading experience—combining fast-paced, serialized storytelling with vibrant, manga-style illustrations. Whether you’re a die-hard anime fan or a Young Adult fiction enthusiast looking for something fresh, our curated sets provide the perfect entry point into these immersive worlds.

At Books2Door, we know that Light Novels are often published in long, multi-volume series that can be expensive to collect individually. That’s why we specialise in Light Novel Box Sets and Bundles, allowing you to "binge-read" your favourite stories while saving up to 50% or more off RRP.

1. Beyond the Anime: Discover the Original Source

Many of the world’s most popular anime series—from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime to Sword Art Online—actually began as Light Novels.

  • Deeper World-Building: Light Novels provide the internal monologues and intricate lore that often get trimmed in anime adaptations. Reading the LNs gives you the "definitive" version of the story.

  • Manga-Style Illustrations: Unlike standard western novels, LNs feature several high-quality illustrations throughout the book, helping you visualise key characters and "epic" battle scenes.

  • Fast-Paced Narrative: Designed for quick consumption, LNs use accessible language and short chapters, making them an excellent choice for reluctant readers or those with busy lifestyles.

2. Dive into Diverse Genres: Isekai, Fantasy, and More

The Light Novel format is the birthplace of many modern tropes, most notably the "Isekai" (trapped in another world) phenomenon.

  • The Isekai Explosion: Explore worlds where ordinary people are transported to magical realms, often becoming "overpowered" heroes or even monsters.

  • Sci-Fi & Cyberpunk: Discover gritty, high-tech futures and psychological thrillers that push the boundaries of imagination.

  • Slice of Life & Romance: Not every LN is about magic; our collection includes heart-warming stories of school life, first loves, and the quiet beauty of Japanese culture.

3. The Books2Door Advantage: Binge-Read for Less

Building a complete Light Novel library is a major commitment. We make it easier and more affordable to own the series you love.

  • Massive Series Bundles: Instead of hunting down Volume 1, then Volume 2, we offer curated multi-book sets. This ensures you have the next installment ready the second you finish a cliffhanger.

title: Manga & Anime Comic Books
description:
Simply put, manga is Japanese comics—an umbrella term for a wide variety of comic books and graphic novels originally published in Japan. The distinct features that differentiate Japanese comic books from English are that manga is usually written and read right-to-left, and their original artwork is very unique in that they are very expressive and have exaggerated emotions. Manga in English therefore retains the original manga artwork, only translating the words. 

In Japan, manga is typically released one chapter at a time, on a monthly or weekly basis through manga magazines that have been in circulation since 1968. For the popular series, however; the chapters are collected and published in the form of volumes called tankōbon volumes, which usually feature a few new chapters of the overall story. 

Manga publishes these volumes approximately the size of a typical paperback novel. A single manga series may take several volumes to tell a complete story. Often, a long-running series will span multiple volumes published in Japan; before they are translated and made available for the rest of the world. This is something to keep in mind when starting a new Manga comic series; as it is imperative you read the volumes in the correct order.

For instance; the long-running Dragon Ball series by Akira Toriyama has 42 volumes. As ardent readers of the Dragon Ball series ourselves; we at Books2Door have curated a complete Box Set of all the volumes in one comprehensive set. Dragon Ball Complete Box Set : Vols. 1-16  by Akira Toriyama. As Goku and friends battle intergalactic evil in the greatest action-adventure-fantasy-comedy-fighting series ever; we wanted to make sure, your Dragon Ball fans have access to all the 16 volumes of the original manga series. 

This Collection Set not only brings you all the volumes but also includes an exclusive double-sided poster and a collector’s booklet featuring fun Dragon Ball trivia and guides as well as an interview with its legendary creator of this global phenomenon. If your kid is a Dragon Ball fan, this is the one comprehensive set that your child will be proud to flaunt to their fellow Manga fans. 

Demon Slayer Complete Box Set: Volumes 1 to 23 By Koyoharu Gotouge for readers aged 14+. This stunning collection features the complete manga box set of the popular Japanese comic series Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba. Included in one large hardcover volume: The Ghost in the Shell (1991) Deep into the twenty-first century; the line between man and machine has been blurred as humans rely on the enhancement of mechanical implants and robots are upgraded with human tissue. 

Overall an action-packed, rapidly converging landscape of cyborgs, cybercriminals, detectives, terrorists, counter-terrorists, hackers and a fusion of multiple identities—there is thrill and a whole lot of adventure in this sci-fi manga for young adults and teens aged 14 plus.

title: Margaret Atwood Books
description:
Welcome to the Margaret Atwood collection page at Books2Door, where we celebrate the ever-trending Canadian author. Join us as we honour a writer who is not just a fleeting trend but has proven her staying power through many years of success. Atwood has consistently delivered one great book after another, leaving us in awe of her talent.

Take a look at this collection of Atwood's works curated for you. Witness her insights into feminist perspectives, environmentalism, and dystopian societies. Get a step closer to great works of literature, learn from, be inspired by, and love and hold.

The Handmaid's Tale and The Testaments: A Dystopian Legacy

We all know The Handmaid's Tale, published in 1985, is the first that comes to mind when we think of Margaret Atwood. Don't we all wonder how her vision of a futuristic dystopian theme got shaped? 

Set in the Republic of Gilead, a totalitarian theocracy has overthrown the government, and society now adheres to strict rules and regulations that suppress sex and gender in the name of religion. As a contemporary reader, if you still need to get your hands on this classic work, it is high time you do and be blown away by the intricacies.

We also suggest you dive into The Testaments, Atwood's classic response to The Handmaid's Tale. This novel will leave you speechless as it answers all the unanswered questions from the prequel while focusing on relevant themes such as resistance, environmental degradation, and her all-time (best) theme, women's rights. You don't have to wait years for the sequel; you get the two together. You jump the anticipation, and that's lucky for you! 

MaddAddam Trilogy: Post-Apocalyptic Narratives

Intrigued? You have to dive into the MaddAddam Trilogy we have as a set now. This trilogy takes us on a journey through a post-apocalyptic world, from Snowman's guardianship of the Crakers in Oryx and Crake to the survival stories of Ren and Toby in The Year of the Flood and finally, to Toby's storytelling in MaddAddam, weaving a narrative that shapes a new world.

Other Notable Works: Beyond Boundaries

Margaret Atwood's literature transcends boundaries, illuminating human behaviour, celebrating the wonders of the natural world, and offering a critical view of materialism. Her books invite readers to delve into the complexities of role reversal and the promise of new beginnings, presented in uniquely refreshing narratives.

Are you looking to connect with this remarkable author on a personal level? We've got just the thing. Dive into Burning Questions, where you can experience Atwood's sharp wit and profound curiosity as she explores various topics. You'll witness her love for exploring the art of storytelling, the climate crisis, the intrigue of zombies, and the mechanics of authoritarian regimes.

Embark with us on an exploration of Margaret Atwood's thought-provoking series and standalone works at Books2Door. Discover the storytelling prowess that has established Atwood as a towering figure in the literary world.

title: Marian Keyes
description:
Marian Keyes is one of the most successful and widely read Irish authors, who is best known as the queen of contemporary fiction. She has written 14 novels, published three collections of her journalism, a cookbook, and won the Irish Book Awards—twice.

Marian however is more than just an author. At this point she is practically a phenomenon! Having sold millions of copies, Keyes is an international bestselling author of some of the most widely loved genre-defying novels of the past thirty years. 

Keyes’ books like Rachel’s Holiday, Anybody Out There and Grown Ups—have millions of readers around the world. Keyes’ fans are known to get drawn to her books by the warmth and wit in her writing, by her fearless honesty, relatable characters, their relationships, and Marian’s sheer storytelling prowess. Having won both critical acclaim and commercial success; Marian’s fourteenth novel Grown Ups went straight to No.1 bestseller in four global territories: UK, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and was shortlisted for the British Book Awards Audiobook of the Year. 

Marian Keyes also has a flair in her writing through which she is able to tackle serious topics in her novels; sensitive subjects like going to rehab, the death of a loved one and living with depression. This combination of heft and heart has made Keyes one of the most beloved and popular authors today. Her latest novel Again, Rachel is the highly-anticipated sequel to Rachel's Holiday, which picks up with the titular star 25 years later. 

Overwhelmed as to where to start with Marian Keyes books? Read on as we curate in this collection, some of the best Marian Keyes books in order…

This Marian Keyes 2 Books Collection Set for adults comes with two spectacularly spellbinding tales that will have you glued to the pages. The first book; The Woman Who Stole My Life, has an intriguing plot. One day, sitting in traffic, Stella Sweeney attempts a simple good deed. When the result is a terrible car accident, she meets a handsome man with a Range Rover who wants her number—no, for insurance purposes and in this meeting a seed is born which will change Stella's life forever. What happens next will blow your mind. Was meeting Mr Range Rover destiny or karma? Find out in this gripping book! Whilst the second book in the set; The Brightest Star in the Sky starts on a bright summer's evening in June on a Monday and into the busy, bustling homes at 66 Star Street slips, unseen, a mysterious visitor. As the couples, flatmates and singletons of No. 66 fall in and out of love, clutch at and drop secrets, laugh, cry and simply try to live; no one suspects the visitor patiently waiting in the wings. For soon, as the light slowly fades to dark, everything is going to change. 

Grown Ups by Marian Keyes Riotously funny and yet touching; hilarious and yet painfully relatable, Grown Ups is the perfect escape into someone else's wonderfully messy family. Comic, convincing and true; Grown Ups has an almost Austenesque insight into character. Keyes knows how to make serious issues relatable and whilst at it, get a few grownup laughs in too.

Watermelon by Marian Keyes Part of the popular Marian Keyes books Walsh Family Series; Watermelon is yet another modern classic by Keyes. Meet Claire Walsh. On the day she gives birth to her first child, Claire's husband James tells her he's been having an affair, and that now's the right time to leave her. Right for who exactly?Exhausted, tearful and a tiny bit furious, Claire doesn't know what to do. So she decides to go back to basics and runs home to Mum and Dad. But it's not the sanctuary she'd been hoping for. Juggling her sisters' drama, her parents' pity and the demands of a baby, Claire desperately misses the way things were. So when James gets back in touch, eager to put things right, Claire faces a choice. Will she forgive and forget? Or can she find the courage to take a chance on herself, and start a life of her own?

title: Marissa Meyer Books
description:
Step into the captivating universe of Marissa Meyer, a literary sorceress whose words have the power to transport readers to realms beyond their wildest dreams. With a vivid imagination and a penchant for reimagining classic tales, Meyer has earned her rightful place among the pantheon of modern-day storytellers. Her journey began with a passion for writing fan fiction, which eventually led her to create her own unique narratives. Her ability to breathe new life into familiar stories and craft unforgettable characters has made her a beloved figure in the world of young adult fiction.

The Lunar Chronicles: A Sci-Fi Fairy Tale Extravaganza

Embark on a thrilling adventure to a futuristic world where fairy tales collide with cutting-edge technology in Marissa Meyer's acclaimed Lunar Chronicles series. The saga kicks off with Cinder, introducing readers to the fearless cyborg mechanic Cinderella, who must navigate a world teetering on the brink of war and revolution. This is just the beginning of an epic journey that weaves together reimagined versions of classic fairy tales like Little Red Riding Hood, Rapunzel, and Snow White into a seamless narrative that will keep you on the edge of your seat. Meyer's ingenious fusion of fantasy and science fiction will leave you yearning for more with every page turned.

The Gilded Duology: Glamour, Intrigue, and Romance in the Gilded Age

Bestselling author Marissa Meyer returns to the fairytale world with this haunting retelling of the classic tale of Rumpelstiltskin. 

Long ago cursed by the god of lies, a poor miller's daughter has developed a talent for spinning stories that are fantastical spellbinding and entirely untrue. Or so everyone believes. When one of Serilda's outlandish tales draws the attention of the sinister Erlking and his undead hunters, she finds herself swept away into a grim world where ghouls and phantoms prowl the earth, and hollow-eyed ravens track her every move.

The king orders Serilda to complete the impossible task of spinning straw into gold or be killed for telling falsehoods. In her desperation, Serilda unwittingly summons a mysterious boy to her aid. He agrees to help her... for a price. Soon Serilda realises that there is more than one secret hidden in the castle walls, including an ancient curse that must be broken if she hopes to end the tyranny of the king and his wild hunt forever.

The Renegades Series: Superheroes and Villains Clash in an Epic Battle

Prepare to be swept up in a world where superheroes and villains reign supreme in Marissa Meyer's Renegades series. Set in a city ruled by prodigious superhumans, this trilogy explores the blurred lines between good and evil, justice and vengeance. Renegades introduces us to Nova, a young villain with a vendetta, and Adrian, a heroic Renegade with secrets of his own. As their paths intertwine, alliances are formed, betrayals are unveiled, and the battle between good and evil takes centre stage. Meyer's storytelling prowess shines as she delves into the complexities of power, morality, and identity, leaving readers with a sense of awe and wonder.

Marissa Meyer's books are more than just stories; they are gateways to imaginative worlds where fairy tales, historical eras, and the superhero genre collide with finesse and creativity. With a masterful hand, she crafts characters that leap off the pages and plots that keep you guessing until the very end. Her ability to infuse classic tales with a modern twist and explore thought-provoking themes sets her apart as a true visionary in the world of young adult literature.

Whether you're a fan of futuristic fairy tales, Gilded Age glamour, or epic clashes between superheroes and villains, Marissa Meyer's books offer something for every reader. So, dive into her enchanting worlds, and let your imagination take flight as you explore the magic of storytelling through the eyes of a truly remarkable author. With Marissa Meyer as your guide, you're in for a literary adventure like no other.

title: Marlon James Books
description:
Join us at Books2Door as we celebrate the narratives crafted by Marlon James and create a collections page with his books for you, our dear avid readers. James is a prominent figure in contemporary literature. His bold storytelling and vivid characterizations have earned him global acclamation, including the prestigious 2015 Man Booker Prize for his novel A Brief History of Seven Killings. 

Born in Jamaica in 1970, James has been well-invested in his cultural heritage. He has incorporated it in his novels, bringing readers like you and me closer to the culture. James is now in New York, continuing to push boundaries as he writes not just for his love of literature but also to provoke thoughts among many.

To begin with, we would like you to start with this explosive tale, A Brief History of Seven Killings, which spans several decades and explores the history of Jamaica through the light of an attempted murder of Bob Markey. 

This book not only won the Man Booker Prize but was also a finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award and the OCM Bocas Prize for Caribbean Literature. It is celebrated not just for its ambitious scope but also for its intense and gritty narrative.

We also have the famous Dark Star trilogy here for you to immerse yourself in and love. Black Leopard, Red Wolf (Dark Star Trilogy Book 1) is a novel that is a finalist for the National Book Award for fiction in 2019, known for its adventurous and innovative take on African mythology and history. Described by critics as an African "Game of Thrones," James' fantasy epic is complex and riveting, featuring a cast of characters drawn from a rich well of African legends.

Following this, we would like to present to you Moon Witch, Spider King (Dark Star Trilogy Book 2), an instalment that further delves into the mystical and the mythical. Esquire praised it, noting how it "masterfully flips the first instalment on its head... James makes the mythic tantalizingly real." 

Marlon James' literature explores identity, power, colonialism, and the intertwining of myth with reality, all set against historical and fantastical backdrops. His characters traverse intricate social and political terrains, reflecting the trials of historical epochs while undergoing deeply personal transformations. Known for his daring narrative style, James deftly blends the real with the imagined, crafting stories that are as intellectually enriching as they are emotionally compelling. 

At Books2Door, we proudly showcase his remarkable body of work, which offers journeys of intrigue and transformation that resonate with new readers and long-standing fans. When one speaks of British culinary legends, few names shine as brightly as Mary Berry. Mary Berry has been the heart and soul of British cooking for over half a century. Her extensive career, spanning decades, has witnessed her evolve from a home cook to a TV sensation, setting the standard for homely yet exceptional British cuisine. She's not just a cook; she's a teacher, guiding countless people through the culinary world with grace and charm.

Her cookbooks are not just recipe collections; they're chronicles of her culinary journey. Every page tells a story, every dish a testament to her passion for food and her deep understanding of what makes a meal truly special.

Mary Berry is an iconic figure in the British culinary landscape, born on March 24, 1935, in Bath, England. Best known as a judge on the hit show The Great British Bake Off from 2010 to 2016, Berry charmed audiences with her expert knowledge, gentle critique, and warm presence.

description:
The Path of the Shinobi: The Masashi Kishimoto Manga Collection

Believe it—or better yet, witness it from the very first page. Few names carry as much weight in the world of Shonen as Masashi Kishimoto. As the visionary architect behind Naruto, Kishimoto didn't just create a story about ninjas; he crafted a multi-generational epic about the pain of loneliness, the weight of legacy, and the indomitable will of an underdog who refused to stay down.

Whether you grew up watching the anime on Saturday mornings or you’re a newcomer looking to experience the "Big Three" era for the first time, the Naruto Manga series remains the gold standard for character-driven action and world-building.

1. The Foundation: Naruto Manga Box Sets

For the ultimate collector, individual volumes are just the beginning. To truly immerse yourself in the Hidden Leaf Village, our Manga Box Sets offer the most comprehensive and cost-effective way to binge-read the journey from academy student to Hokage.

  • Naruto Box Set 1 (Volumes 1-27): This is where the legend begins. Covering the "Pre-Shippuden" era, these volumes introduce the iconic Team 7—Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura—under the tutelage of Kakashi Hatake. It’s a masterclass in establishing emotional stakes, from the tragic Land of Waves arc to the adrenaline-pumping Chunin Exams.

  • The Shippuden Era: As the characters age, so does the complexity of Kishimoto’s art and narrative. The later volumes transition into a darker, more political landscape where the Akatsuki loom large and the search for Sasuke Uchiha becomes a desperate race against time.

2. Kishimoto’s Visual Mastery: More Than Just Jutsu

What sets Masashi Kishimoto’s manga apart from its peers is his cinematic sense of "camera" placement and kinetic energy.

  • Anatomy of a Battle: Kishimoto’s use of perspective makes every Kage Bunshin (Shadow Clone) and Rasengan feel like it's leaping off the page.

  • Cultural Fusion: By blending traditional Japanese folklore with modern urban grit, he created a "Shinobi World" that feels lived-in, textured, and surprisingly relatable.

3. The Legacy Continues: Boruto and Beyond

The story didn't end with the Fourth Shinobi World War. While Kishimoto took a step back to supervise, the world expanded into Boruto: Naruto Next Generations. Exploring the challenges of peace and the friction between tradition and technology, these volumes are essential for fans who want to see how the legendary Naruto Uzumaki navigates the most difficult role of all: fatherhood.

title: Michael Morpurgo Books
description:
Michael Morpurgo is one of Britain’s most beloved children’s authors. He’s written over a hundred books in his nearly fifty-year career, including Private Peaceful and Kensuke’s Kingdom. However, he’s best known for the novel War Horse, which was adapted into a critically acclaimed stage play, and a blockbuster film by Steven Spielberg. He co-created the Children’s Laureate position with then-Poet Laureate Ted Hughes and became the third to hold it, from 2003 to 2005.

Biography

Michael Bridge was born in 1943 in St Albans, the child of two actors. While his father was away fighting in World War II, his mother met Jack Morpurgo. His parents divorced, his mother remarried, and he and his brother took on Jack’s last name. The family lived in London and Essex, and Morpugo was sent away to school in Sussex and Canterbury. He went to army training in Sandhurst on his stepfather’s insistence but left after nine months. 

Morpurgo married Clare, daughter of the founder of Penguin Books, Sir Alan Lane, aged 19, with whom he had three children. Shortly after marriage, he studied English, French and Philosophy at King’s College London. He then became a primary school teacher in Canterbury. He discovered his love of storytelling when he made up tales for his students, and his first book was published in 1974.

The couple established the charity Farms for City Children in 1976, which gives inner-city children an experience of the countryside. They moved to Devon to set it up, where they still live. Over 90,000 children have visited the three farms the charity now runs at. Morpurgo views Farms for City Children as one of the greatest achievements in his life. It’s inspired many of his books, including War Horse.

Best-Known Books

Private Peaceful follows the memories of soldier Tommo, who was stationed in France during World War I. It starts with his early childhood, his father’s death, his friendship with his brother Charlie, and his falling in love with his school friend Molly. It then moves to the trenches, as Tommo lies about his age to join his brother on the front line. It was adapted into a play, a film, and a one-man show by Simon Reade. It also inspired a series of concerts of the same name.

Kensuke’s Kingdom is the story of Michael and his family, who decide to sail around the world after being made redundant. Michael is washed overboard with his dog Stella, and find themselves stranded on a small island. They finally meet Kensuke, the mysterious benefactor who’s been leaving food and fresh water at their cave shelter. Slowly, Michael and Kensuke bond, and conversation turns to the world outside the island. Kensuke’s Kingdom is currently being adapted into an animated film by the producers behind the adaptation of Ethel & Ernest by Raymond Briggs. 

The Butterfly Lion has just celebrated its 25th anniversary. It’s the story of South African boy Bertie, who has to send his orphaned lion cub away to the circus when he is sent to boarding school in England. He becomes friends with a girl called Millie, and the story follows their lives through the Great War, to their search for the lion.
At Books2Door, we stock a variety of Michael Morpurgo’s books, including some great value box sets and collections. For other Children’s Laureates, see our Quentin Blake, Julia Donaldson, and Jacqueline Wilson collections.

title: Michael Rosen Books
description:
Michael Rosen Books 

Michael Rosen is an iconic British poet, author, activist and former Children's Laurette (2007 to 2009). Over his career, he has written some of the most beloved children's books, such as We're Going on a Bear Hunt, Rigatoni the Pasta Cat, Goldilocks and the Three Crocodiles, and so much more. 

Michael Rosen was born in Harrow, England and has based many of his writings on his childhood and upbringing. He has continued working within the field of children's literature throughout most of his career. This also includes teaching children's literature at universities, workshops for school teachers so they can have more resources to teach pupils, and visiting schools and libraries to do readings. Rosen not only started writing at a young age, but he started protesting as a teenager. He stood up for human rights, freedom and against war and racism. 

Poetry 

Michael Rosen has produced some fantastic poetry aimed at children. His poetry is known for being silly and fun as well as poignant and important. A great example of this is a collection of poetry Rosen created, along with illustrator Quentin Blake, called On the Move: Poems About Migration. This beautiful collection conveys some of the heartbreaking and uplifting sides of migrating and what it means to be a refugee. 

For a younger audience, check out Rosen's collection of Bananas in my Ears. The collection is also illustrated by Blake and explores the chaos of breakfast time, the adventures of bedtime and many silly stories to get you and your cheeky one giggling. Another great poetry collection, the perfect books to introduce your child to poetry, is Michael Rosen's A-Z: The best children's poetry from Agard to Zephaniah and Michael Rosen's Book of Very Silly Poems!

We're Going on a Bear Hunt and Other Classic Tales 

We're going on a bear hunt, we're going to catch a big one, we're not scared! This beautiful picture book may well have been the pinnacle of your childhood. Therefore, passing down these much-cherished stories to your children is like passing down a family heirloom. We're going on a bear hunt was written by Michael Rosen and illustrated by Helen Oxenbury, and first released in 1989. It has become one of the UK's favourite picture books and has since been adapted into a moving animated short by Channel 4 in 2016. Soon as you start reading this interactive and engaging picture book, you will quickly see why it is well-loved. For more bestselling children's books and more, check out our bestsellers page. 

If you and your little ones are fans of We're Going on a Bear Hunt, you should check out the picture book Chocolate Cake. Illustrated by Kevin Waldron, this remarkable book is a love letter to every child's favourite treat, chocolate cake. Michael Rosen's books are enjoyed by all ages but are ideal for children aged 5-7-years-old. For more children's books, check out our range of picture books, board books and classic children's stories. With titles up to 80% RRP, you and your family can enjoy the wonder of books and the power of imagination at affordable prices.

title: Miss Marple Books
description:
The Miss Marple books by Agatha Christie are crime classics and one of the most loved detective fiction series of all time. Popular as she is, Miss Jane Marple is actually a fictional character that features in a series of Agatha Christie's crime novels and short stories. Miss Marple lives in the fictitious village of St. Mary Mead (a quaint little place with a surprisingly high crime rate) and acts as an amateur consulting detective. 

Book Set One 

In book set one you will get a fantastic collection of Miss Marple stories such as The Murder at the Vicarage, The Body in the Library, The Moving Finger, Sleeping Murder and A Murder is Announced. 

The Murder at the Vicarage for instance is one of the most popular Agatha Christie novels featuring Ms Marple. Set in a quiet English village, the novel starts with a shocking murder and an unlikely detective. Nobody liked Colonel Protheroe. So when he’s found dead in the vicarage study, there’s no absence of suspects in the seemingly peaceful village of St Mary Mead. In fact, Jane Marple can think of at least seven! The police dismiss her as a prying busybody, but only the ingenious Miss Marple can uncover the truth.

The Body in the Library is yet another Miss Marple crime fiction novel by Agatha. A young woman is found murdered and a scandal ensues. When Mrs. Bantry wakes up to find the body in her library, there’s only one woman to call: her good friend Jane Marple. But Miss Marples’ investigations uncover a scandal far darker than either of them could have imagined, and this time she may be out of her depth.

One of Agatha Christie's best-known characters ever; Miss Marple has been portrayed numerous times on screen. Her first appearance was in a short story published in The Royal Magazine in December 1927, "The Tuesday Night Club", which later became the first chapter of The Thirteen Problems (1932). Her first appearance in a full-length novel was in The Murder at the Vicarage in 1930, and her last appearance was in Sleeping Murder in 1976. Miss Marpel has since stolen the hearts of millions of crime and thriller readers worldwide.

Agatha Christie went on to write a series of twelve full-length novels and multiple popular short stories starring this iconic character. And today, more than four decades after the author’s death, Miss Marple is still one of the most recognised fictional detectives in literature; with Miss Marple's books still selling like hotcakes.

Miss Marple Books in Order: 

  • The Murder at the Vicarage 
  • The Body in the Library 
  • The Moving Finger
  • A Murder is Announced 
  • They Do It With Mirrors 
  • A Pocket Full of Rye 
  • 4:50 From Paddington
  • The Mirror Crack’d from Side to Side 
  • A Caribbean Mystery
  • At Bertram’s Hotel 
  • Nemesis 
  • Sleeping Murder

If you are the kind of reader that enjoys crime thrillers and murder mysteries and have never read the Miss Marple books, then we highly recommend this classic series. We at Books2Door have curated Ms Marple crime fiction novels in many combinations of collection sets; so you can choose the books that intrigue you. 

Box Set Two

Miss Marple Collection 2 by Agatha Christie: 5 Books Box Set, for instance, have some of the last, most nail-biting Miss Marple mysteries. Included in this box set is They Do It With Mirrors, A Pocket Full of Rye, 4.50 from Paddington, The Mirror Crack’d From Side to Side and A Caribbean Mystery. 

4.50 from Paddington two trains side by side for a brief moment. In that very moment, a murder! Elspeth McGillicuddy is positive she witnessed a man strangling a woman to death but it was only the merest glimpse through a carriage window as the trains drew parallel. She is the only witness, there are no suspects, and, most importantly, there is no corpse. Who would then take Miss Elspeth seriously? Enter, Miss Jane Marple! 

Get set one and two in our The Miss Marple Collection by Agatha Christie: 10 Books Box Set is another comprehensive collection of the best Ms Marple crime fiction that will take the reader through her progression as a detective. 

Box Set Three

Our third and final complete box set of Agatha Christie’s Miss Marple is Miss Marple Collection 3 by Agatha Christie: 4 Books Box Set. This collection includes At Bertram’s Hotel, Nemesis, Miss Marple’s Final Cases and The Thirteen Problems. 

The Thirteen Problems is another one of Ms Marple crime fiction classics by Agatha Christie. On a quiet Tuesday in St Mary Mead, a group of friends—The Tuesday Night Club—gather for their weekly dinner. A policeman, a clergyman, a solicitor, an author, an artist, and an unassuming lady with a shrewd gaze—Miss Jane Marple. Conversation naturally turns to crime. Each recounts a seemingly unsolvable mystery. Each thinks they know the answer. But it's the one they least expect who understands the true nature of each wicked act. Never underestimate Miss Marple!

Through these books as the series progresses; Miss Marple transforms from a simpleton into a shrewdly intelligent woman who uses her razor-sharp intuition and skills of deduction to solve criminal; cases across England and beyond. Whilst on the surface Miss Marple is simply an innocent lady who couldn’t scare a goose; she is actually a formidable force who can suspect a lie from a mile away! Ms Marple is sharp, intelligent and has an uncanny ability to join the dots to piece together clues and solve even the most complex criminal cases.

title: Mo Willems Books

title: Modern & Literary Fiction Books
description:
Creative, formula-bending, genre-defying, character-focused, and most importantly, a literary exploration of the human condition—contemporary & modern literary fiction is arguably the most experimental genre within literature.

The landscape of literary fiction is constantly being revolutionised by literary fiction authors; that are known to constantly push the boundaries of genre fiction and blur the lines of distinction between literary fiction and other genres of literature.

Given the creative ambiguity of contemporary literary fiction; the genre witnesses a dazzling lineup of highly acclaimed debuts and fresh progressive voices each year. From trailblazing memoirs to the cultural history of humanity—no other genre captures the exactness of our collective life experience more creatively than literary fiction.

The list of bestselling literary fiction is an exciting mix of very distinct literary techniques and contrasting voices. Precisely why, we at Books2Door bring you and a carefully curated collection of the best literary fiction books of all time whilst also helping you gain an acute understanding of what qualifies as modern & literary fiction.

Formula-bending, genre-defying, and experimental

Modern and Contemporary Literary Fiction or experimental fiction is possibly the literature’s most rebellious genre. It doesn’t follow any literary formulas, nor does it adhere to any rules. In that, literary fiction authors are free to build an unpredictable narrative. Anything can transpire; exciting or unnerving. In literary fiction, any established literary theme can be turned on its head. For instance, literary fiction authors have challenged the good-triumphs-over-evil theme; so common otherwise in genre fiction books.

George Orwell’s social satire Nineteen Eighty-Four is one example. A book best categorised as dystopian literature; (remember the recently trending hashtag #makeorwellfictionagain ?) Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four not only challenged the good vs evil theme but also blurred the lines of distinction between genre fiction and classic literary fiction.

Employees creative storytelling

Considering literary fiction doesn’t adhere to any rules of genre or sub-genre; every literary fiction author is free to be creative and create his own rules. This makes the storyline an adventure, that can take its readers by surprise.

Devoid of any rules, the literary fiction writer is free to break convention and employ his creativity. This practice has birthed some extraordinary literary works. For example, Audrey Niffenegger’s The Time Traveler’s Wife where Niffenegger’s uses dual narrators from the first person point of view, in the present tense.

Thought-provoking and introspective

Like we said earlier, no other genre captures the exactness of the human condition and our collective life experience more creatively than literary fiction. Whilst most genres are designed to entertain the readers, literary fiction is meant to do more than that. Literary fiction seeks to make sense of the world. It is meant to be thought-provoking, and introspective and is meant to push the reader to think critically of the human condition.

Sylvia Plath’s The Bell Jar, for instance, explores the mind of a depressed, anxious, and neurotic young woman. Whilst the book has a coming-of-age plot line; it is the inner dialogue of this character that truly makes it a memorable book. This strong character study is what makes literary fiction a character-focused and introspective genre.

Explores the human condition

Stories in literary fiction do not shy away from dealing with difficult subjects and the realities of the human condition with artistic honesty. Literary fiction, therefore, is not always designed to help the reader escape. It can make the reader uncomfortable and push them to think about issues.

Literary fiction however is not non-fiction; so it doesn’t just report the truth. Instead, it relies on creative techniques and artsy symbolism to convey a deeper meaning. Literary fiction relies on metaphors and creative storytelling to convey meaningful messages. As a result, the takeaway from these stories is more than just the story, the takeaway is the experience, the message, and at times the characters.

Literary fiction is character-driven

Whilst genre fiction is focused on the story, plotlines, and on being an engaging read; literary fiction is more stressed on the characters or on conveying a meaningful message or idea. At times, it is focused on both. The characters in literary fiction can have layers, the depth of a character's actions and psyche are explored to forward the plot. Literary fiction doesn’t just show a character’s story, it shows how their actions and circumstances change the character.

Literary fiction can be as absurd and ambiguous as life itself

Literary fiction is experimental in nature much like absurd art, which means it doesn’t have to have a happy ending or an ending at all. Art movements like absurdism, dadaism and surrealism, are all, artsy cousins of experimental prose.

Literary fiction gives writers the liberty to let a story end abruptly or for the entire plot to be absurd. Stories in this genre don’t necessarily have to resolve but they have to have meaning. The meaning however is left to the reader’s interpretation.

Literary fiction is good for the reader

Because literary fiction pushes boundaries, employs a unique perspective, searches for meaning, and is designed for intellectual and emotional stimulus--it is much like the art you see hanging in galleries and the movies that bring meaningful conversations alive. Just like artsy movies and art itself, the creative genius of literary fiction is largely open to criticism. Some of the best contemporary literary fiction books have won critical acclaim and awards but missed out on winning the masses.

title: Moomin Books
description:
The Moomins were created by Tove Jansson, a Swedish-speaking Finnish author. She published a total of nine books in the series, along with five picture books. She began a comic strip in 1954, which she collaborated on with her brother Lars for two years, who then created it solo between 1961 and 1975.

As a visual artist, illustrator, painter and author; Tove Jansson expanded and transformed her artistic expression tirelessly up to the last years of her life. Her works are a reflection of an entire life philosophy, eliciting enthusiastic responses from children and adults alike, from across all countries where her works are known.

Tove Jansson is easily one of the best-known Finnish artists and also the most widely read Finnish authors. Her lifework is of immeasurable value because of the success she made as a writer, artist and cartoonist. Her most treasured works being the Moomins.

The Moomin books and novels have been translated from Swedish to English and in over fifty other languages and are widely popular specially amongst children. Whilst Tove wrote 12 other very popular novels and short stories during her career apart from Moomin books, including the acclaimed The Summer Book, it is the classic Moomin series that no child should have to miss out on.

The Moomins and the Great Flood by Tove Jansson was published in 1945, and offers an extraordinary glimpse into the creativity and imagination that launched the Moomin books for toddlers.

Moominmamma and young Moomintroll search for the long lost Moominpappa through forest and flood, meeting a little creature (an early Sniff) and the elegantly strange Tulippa along the way. Tove Jansson illustrates her first ever Moomin adventure with stunning sepia watercolour and delightful pen and ink drawings. A treat for Moomin fans.

Comet in Moominland by Tove Jansson: A comet is speeding towards Earth and nobody in Moominvalley knows what to do! Will it destroy everything and everyone? Moomintroll decides to find out. So, with Sniff, he sets off on an expedition to ask the Professor if a comet is really on its way to destroy the Earth. On their journey they meet some interesting people, such as Snufkin the super tramp, and the Hemulen who rescues them from an underground tunnel. They have narrow escapes from menaces like crocodiles and giant lizards and on their way back Moomintroll meets the beautiful Snork Maiden and is a changed Moomin for ever after. But what about the comet, is the World Wiped Out? Give your child the opportunity to find out what transpires in this literary adventure told through Tove’s exciting words and illustrations.

Tales from Moominvalley is yet another classic from the Moomin Books Set that takes Moomintroll on yet another adventure. Allow your child to join Moomintroll as he finds a tiny golden dragon with green paws. If your child and you found a dragon like that, would he know what to do with it? Moomintroll thinks he does, but when he takes his new-found pet home, things don't quite work out as planned. And suppose Too-ticky brought you an invisible child, would you know how to make her visible again? Meet new and delightful characters and re-encounter old friends, such as Snufkin and Little My in this entertaining collection of nine stories about the trials and tribulations of the inhabitants of Moominvalley. There are some new characters to meet, such as the Fillyjonk and the Hattifatteners, as well as old friends, namely Snufkin and Little My - and not to mention dear Moominpappa, Moominmamma and Moomintroll of course!

description:
Mr Men was created by Roger Hargreaves in 1971 and was followed later by the Little Miss Series. It has been over 3 decades since Roger Hargreaves death but his lovable group of characters still continue his legacy and are still loved and enjoyed by millions of children across the world. 

By the end of the 70s, Hargreaves had created 39 Mr Men characters. In 1981, the first Little Miss character—Little Miss Bossy was brought to life followed by several others which led to an animated series in 1983. Legend has it that Hargreaves' creative ideas were sparked by his eldest son’s question: What does a tickle look like? Today, the Mr Men and Little Miss series have sold over 100 million copies worldwide, have been translated into several languages and a movie is in the making.

Mr Tickle has extraordinarily long arms and tickles everyone he sees, Mr. Greedy likes to eat, and ventures on a food hunt. Mr Silly lives in Nonsense Land which is a very funny place to live, that holds a Nonsense competition for the silliest idea; along with several other stories about other Mr Men journeys. These stories teach young children about various personality traits, positive and negative characteristics of these characters and more. 

Read on as we add to this collection, Mr Men and Little Miss books and Mr Men and Little Miss book sets that we know your children will fall in love with and learn from.

Get this cute little set for you toddler and let them decide which Little Miss characters they are!

A lesson and a fun read—just the kind of book you want for your little one.

Little Miss Sunshine from the book by the same name is every bit the ray of sunshine that we all need. Little Miss Sunshine is seen driving home from her holiday, when she runs across a signpost to Miseryland. What will happen to the crying folks of Miseryland when Little Miss Sunshine comes to visit? Children’s Literature

Nadiya's creativity extends into the magical world of children's literature. Her children's books, including My Monster and Me and Today I am Strong, are delightful reads filled with imagination, heart, and important life lessons. Her colorful narratives paired with captivating illustrations appeal to young readers and encourage them to explore their emotions and dreams.

My Monster and Me is a touching story that addresses childhood anxiety. By creating a tangible 'monster,' she enables children to understand their feelings better, making it a fantastic tool for parents and educators.

Today I am Strong is a whimsical adventure, exploring friendship and finding your inner strength, and filled with humour and magic that's bound to capture the hearts of young readers.

Whether you're seeking culinary inspiration, a heartfelt novel, or a vibrant children's story, Nadiya Hussain's books are a treasure trove of creativity and passion. Her cookbooks are more than collections of recipes; they are a celebration of food, life, and love. Her novels and children's books are proof of her ability to transcend the boundaries of her culinary fame, offering meaningful, engaging stories that resonate with readers of all ages.

Nadiya's work is a testament to her incredible versatility, warmth, and talent. Her books are not just about food or stories; they're about connection, inspiration, and the joy of creating something beautiful. Embark on this delightful journey with Nadiya Hussain, and discover a world filled with flavour, imagination, and heart. Her books are more than a purchase; they are an experience, a gift that keeps on giving, and a must-have for any bookshelf.

 About the Author

Nadiya's passion for cooking was ignited at a young age, influenced by her Bangladeshi heritage. Growing up in a family of six, she learned to cook from her mother and used her skills to contribute to family meals. Despite facing racial barriers and identity struggles as a British-Bangladeshi, she held firmly to her dreams.

Nadiya's life took a dramatic turn when she decided to participate in the 2015 series of The Great British Bake Off. With no professional culinary background, she impressed both the judges and the public with her innovative recipes, artistic flair, and emotional honesty. Her victory in the competition was not just a personal triumph but a moment of national pride. Her tearful acceptance of the Bake Off crown was a symbol of overcoming self-doubt, breaking cultural barriers, and embracing one's unique identity.

After winning The Great British Bake Off, Nadiya's career soared to new heights. She became a regular contributor to food programs, wrote columns for major publications, and authored a series of best-selling cookbooks. Her recipes, often blending traditional Bangladeshi flavours with British classics, made her a culinary icon. Nadiya's talents extend beyond the kitchen. She's the author of a critically acclaimed novel and engaging children's books, demonstrating her versatility and creativity.

title: Naruto Manga
description:
Welcome to the captivating world of Naruto by the renowned Japanese manga artist Masashi Kishimoto. If you're an avid reader or simply seeking a thrilling adventure, look no further than this iconic manga and anime series, available now at Books2Door. With its compelling storyline, memorable characters, and profound themes, The Naruto Series is a timeless masterpiece that has captured the hearts of millions worldwide.

Overview:
Naruto revolves around a spirited and determined young ninja from the hidden leaf village, Naruto Uzumaki. Born with the Nine-Tails Fox demon sealed within him, Naruto faces prejudice and isolation from his fellow villagers. Despite this adversity, Naruto embarks on a heroic journey to earn their respect and become the Hokage, the leader of his village.

Readers delve into the series and are introduced to a richly developed world filled with powerful ninja clans, intricate political intrigue, and breathtaking battles. With every page turned, Naruto's growth as a ninja and as a person becomes more evident. Through relentless training, unwavering determination, and the bonds of friendship, Naruto and his comrades face formidable foes and unravel the secrets of their world.

One of the series' standout features is its diverse and well-rounded cast of characters. From the wise mentor Kakashi Hatake to the kind-hearted Sakura Haruno and the enigmatic Sasuke Uchiha, each character brings their unique strengths and struggles to the forefront. The dynamic relationships, fierce rivalries, and profound friendships among these characters are central to the series' appeal.

The Naruto Series delves deep into themes that resonate with readers of all ages. From pursuing one's dreams to searching for identity and acceptance, the series explores the fundamental aspects of the human experience. Kishimoto masterfully weaves these themes into the narrative, making the story relatable and emotionally impactful.

Masashi Kishimoto
Masashi Kishimoto, the creative genius behind Naruto, was born on November 8, 1974, in Nagi, Okayama, Japan. title: Neil Gaiman Books
description:
Neil Gaiman 

This British author's works span sci-fi, horror and fantasy genres for adults and children. Known for his gothic fantasy stories, he was heavily inspired by the work of Lewis Carroll, J.R.R. Tolkien, Mary Shelley and Edgar Allen Poe. Neil Gaiman has produced novels, short stories, poetry and graphic novels. He blends mythologies, folklore, history and religion to create tales 

His first novel, Good Omens, was published, in 1990 alongside legendary fantasy writer Terry Pratchett. However, before this was published Gaiman had been working on graphic novels. After seeing some of his previous comic collaborations, DC Comics hired him in 1987 and this would be where he would begin his work on The Sandman. The comic series ran for seven years, from January 1989 and concluded in March 1996. 

Gaiman’s first solo novel was a novelisation of his television series Neverwhere. Released in 1996, the novel is set in London with two realms, London Above and London Below. Then, in 1999 Gaiman published Stardust, American Gods in 2001 and Anansi Boys in 2005.

He has also turned his hand to children’s literature, in 2002 Coraline was published. The novella follows young Coraline as she navigates her way through an evil alternate universe with the help of a talking cat. Gaiman’s next children's novel was The Graveyard Book, published in 2008, which follows a young boy called Bod who is adopted by the spiritual inhabitants of a graveyard after his family is killed. In 2017 Gaiman published a non-fiction retelling of several famous stories from Norse Mythology. 

All of Gaiman’s works have recognisable illustration styles, he has worked closely with illustrators to ensure his characters and style are represented accurately. Gaiman’s collaboration with Chris Riddell has provided the look for Coraline and The Graveyard Book. Take a look at our Chris Riddell Collection for more titles illustrated and written by Riddell.

As Seen on Screen

Numerous adaptations of Neil Gaiman’s works have been made for film and TV. This includes the 2019 TV series Good Omens starring Michael Sheen as the angel Aziraphale and David Tennant as the demon Crowley. More recently, Netflix’s adaptation of The Sandman starring Tom Sturridge as Dream and Gwendoline Christie as Lucifer Morningstar.

Additionally, the Netflix series Lucifer starring Tom Ellis in the titular role is based on Gaiman’s Lucifer featured in The Sandman comics. There are many other famous adaptations of Gaiman’s work including the stop-motion style animation Coraline and the 2007 movie adaptation of Stardust starring Claire Danes, Charlie Cox and Robert De Niro. 

Gaiman’s work has also been adapted in other ways. Coraline is adapted into a graphic novel and The Ocean at the End of the Lane is adapted into a play. Check out The Sandman Complete Collection which contains all four books with all 75 issues inside. The perfect accompaniment for a fan of the series.

title: Non-Fiction Books
description:
A work of literature that is based on facts, truth, or real-life events can be categorised as non-fiction. Simply put, if a book is not rooted in a fictional narrative or a made-up story, then it qualifies as adult nonfiction. This encompasses several sub-genres within literature—biographies, history, memoirs, self-help, and so on. From intriguing accounts of interesting lives to enlightening accounts of the rich history of our world—experts believe, there are a ton of non-fiction books to read before you die.

One of the many non-fiction classics to read in your lifetime is, Call the Midwife 4 Book Set by Jennifer Worth. Fascinating tales of social history, this one is a midwife’s account of 1950s London. 

The truth they say can be stranger than fiction—this statement arguably sums up the genre that is non-fiction. Non-fiction books for adults are loaded with just as much suspense and thrill as any fictional novel, if not more. 

Whether you want to read something intriguing and thrilling for leisure or you want to read to learn/research—adult non-fiction is a vast gamut of sub-genres and there is plenty to choose from. This makes adult non-fiction just the genre you can immerse yourself in when trying to go back to reading as a habit. Treat yourself to some of the world’s best non-fiction books of all time, whilst you try to get your kids hooked on books or try to inculcate the reading habit.

Why Read Nonfiction?

According to a recent annual report from the Association of American Publishers, the adult nonfiction market in the US showed a revenue increase of 5.4% between 2016 and 2017. That, however, is not why we endorse adult non-fiction for parents and non-fiction for kids. Sales aside, non-fiction books are a great way to feed people’s appetite for knowledge, learning, and bettering their lives. 

Here at Books2Door, we not only understand your hunger for knowledge but also know that the internet with its several web pages, videos, and podcasts is not going to satiate your appetite for information. This is precisely why we believe in the power of books and curating book recommendations.

Non-fiction literature may be a rich and varied genre but that also makes it harder to narrow down a reading list that works for you, from amongst the wealth of titles that exist across the world. This is where we at Books2Door step in and try to curate the best non-fiction books for every age. 

Whilst we do bring you the bestselling non-fiction titles, we also ensure we stock up on books that cater to specific tastes and topics. You can for instance find era-defining non-fiction titles or specific mindfulness and wellness books that speak of parenting and relationships. You can also find a curated collection of non-fiction books for kids to choose from, so you can make the most of your book budget for yourself and your kids.

From poetry to classic works of Mark Twain and Virginia Woolf, to best non-fiction books of 2022, to short stories and more; here are some sub-genres of non-fiction that we have curated for you and your children:

Historic non-fiction: 

Historical non-fiction consists of true accounts of historic events and eras. If you are someone that enjoys reading about historic cultures and events, then this is the non-fiction sub-genre for you. 

Amongst several non-fiction titles that delve in history is Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind that challenges everything we seemingly know about the history of human evolution. We also have books like Survivors: True Stories of Children in the Holocaust that venture into the darker pockets of our world’s political history. 

Biographies:

Biographies, autobiographies, and memoirs—this sub-genre of nonfiction is focused on the life stories of individuals usually with an underlying theme, for instance, a cause they endorsed. Whilst autobiographies and memoirs are written by the subjects themselves; biographies are written in the third person by an author about the life of the subject.

Few genres are as fascinating as biographies; reading about people’s lives, their struggles and their stories. One of our favourites from the genre is Becoming by Michelle Obama. An insight into the life of the USA’s former first lady.

 

Travelogues:

Travelogues and memoirs might seem like cousins because they both present first-person accounts of the author’s experience with something. However, travelogues are more instructive and offer more practical information about travel to a particular destination whilst memoirs are most value and ideology based.

Academic literature and Guides:

Academic textbooks are structurally designed and written to educate and inform. These could be school textbooks or adult textbooks for adults interested in particular trades like music or cars. Whilst books under this genre will only be as useful as your interest in the subject, we do offer some interesting options to pick from. HBR's 10 Must Reads for Sales and Marketing Collection is one such. 

If you are into gothic literature and have a thing for the darker sciences or simply want to ready something spooky for halloween, then here is book you must read Love Witchcraft 2 Books By Arin Murphy & Hiscock 

Philosophy or psychology:

These are most likely to be published by university-affiliated publication houses and are most likely to be written by scholars and academics who are experts on the subject. This genre is a gamut in itself as it may consist of traditional philosophy, psychology, scientific theories, or research papers.

Whilst investing in mental health goes beyond reading about it, we’d say it is a start. Here is book you can consider when working on your emotional health, The Courage to be Happy Book By Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga. 

Journalism:

Arguably the best non-fiction of all time, journalism is another broad sub-genre of nonfiction however it includes several media. If we were to only focus on literary/print journalism it would come down to journals, newspapers, and magazines. This would also include non-fiction books by journalists who have covered wars, unearthed a controversial story or true crime. One of our personal favourites has been We Are Bellingcat: An Intelligence Agency for the People by Eliot Higgins, a British citizen journalist. From the downing of Malaysia Flight 17 over the Ukraine to the sourcing of weapons in the Syrian Civil War; the book digs deep into some of Bellingcat's most successful investigations and thus makes for an intriguing and insightful read.

Self-help and instruction manuals:

Self-help books are more often than not about business success stories, staying organised, money management, health, and wellness, or relationship advice. Self-help non-fiction books also tend to perform very well on the non-fiction book charts and become bestselling non-fiction titles.

Fitness and wellness guides for instance have been popular for sometime now. Men's Fitness 12 Week Body Plan - Paperback by Nick Mitchell

Children’s Non-Fiction Books may be a relatively new genre in literature but it is fast becoming popular. What’s exciting about non-fiction books for children as a genre, is how it has seen a major shift in the recent past and become more focused on kids. Whilst children’s literature has been dominated by fairy tales and story books for years; new-age non-fiction titles for children are now exploring newer grounds with well-researched insights, relevant and relatable true stories, and tight storytelling about compelling issues. 

With better options in the market, it has now become glaringly obvious that there was a big gap that needed to be filled in the non-fiction space for children. Keep an eye out for our Non-fiction books for children and young adults collection because it is only going to get more dynamic with exciting non-fiction titles.

Through the sub-genres like creative non-fiction, home learning books, education books, revision guides and more; let’s explore what awaits your children in the world of non-fiction books.

Home Learning 

A perfect example of new-age, non-fiction for children (aged 5 to 9)—Little People Big Dreams Ground breaking Women & Trailblazing Women by Maria Isabel Sánchez Vegara contains 5 books each from the bestselling series. This book series by Vegara combines creativity with learning whilst also introducing children to some of the most outstanding artists, activists, scientists, and achievers of the world. 

A creative way of introducing influential role models to children whilst also making them aware of relevant causes and issues around the world; Vegara’s books are just what the Children’s non-fiction genre was missing. Each book is dedicated to a pop culture icon or character and tells their story of triumph over adversity. The respective stories of these artists, trailblazers, youth icons, and dreamers are told through facts and photo sections thus making it engaging and interesting for children. 

Whilst there are many sub-genres within non-fiction for children; education books and home learning books by far have proved to be the most innovative, in that they have adopted creative ways to combine creative non-fiction with learning and fun.

History Books 

The Horrible Histories Savage 10 Book Collection by Terry Deary is a hugely popular non-fiction series that teaches history to children in the most fun and engaging way possible. The author chooses to brand this series as history ‘with the nasty bits left in’. He simply makes history fun for kids by ensuring, no fact is too foul, no battle too vicious and no blunder too ludicrous for these books and that is exactly why children love them. The funny (sometimes gruesome) historic facts keep the children entertained whilst the comic strips, illustrations and quizzes make the books even more engaging. Best non-fiction books for 7-year-olds; this series covers almost every historic period that there is (from Ancient History to the Medieval Periods) and also links back to topics that are covered in school. 

Maths Books 

Murderous Maths Collection 10 Books Box Set by Kjartan Poskitt is a non-fiction series for children between 8 and 12-years-of-age; that helps them deal with the agony of algebra. Using hilarious characters, Poskitt presents several tips, tricks, and shortcuts to algebra that schools don’t teach. Employing creative nonfiction writing, colourful design, and fun characters to teach maths; the book series still manages to be entertaining.

The Murderous Maths books allow children to learn math whilst engaging in a battle of wits against Professor Fiendish in the Foul Formula Challenge as Chainsaw Charlie and his gruesome gang learn to deal with murderous maths. 

Geography Books 

A spin-off from the Horrible Histories series, Horrible Geography is also written and designed to get children (aged 9 to 14) interested in geography. All about world geography with the gritty bits left in; this non-fiction series written by Anita Ganeri intends to save children from boring maps and gruelling graphs. Just like the Horrible Histories Series, these books have also been illustrated and filled with fun facts that the school textbooks may have deprived the kids of. Instead of simply listing geographic routes and places, the author delves into trivia and mysteries surrounding geographic locations like the Bermuda Triangle. 

Revision Guides

Just like all work and no play makes Jack a dull boy, so is the case with books. As fun as creative, new-age non-fiction and educational non-fictional books can be for kids, some subjects need practice. This is when step-by-step revision guides come in handy. Also, part of the non-fiction genre; subject-specific revision guides help kids achieve their maximum potential. Available for every individual subject; Cambridge IGCSE and O Level Study and Revision Guides are updated each year with the revised syllabus and are designed to help students revise and practice exam questions and study materials.

When it comes to children’s non-fiction, home-learning books like these make an important part of the genre.
