title: Octavia E. Butler Books
description:
Octavia E. Butler's books stand out for their thought-provoking exploration of social, racial, and gender issues, all within the framework of compelling science fiction narratives. Her works continue to captivate readers and challenge conventions, making her a pioneering and essential voice in the genre. Whether she is delving into the dark chapters of history, imagining dystopian futures, or pushing the boundaries of human nature, Butler's books leave a lasting impact on those who encounter them.

Kindred:

Published in 1979, Kindred is perhaps Butler's best-known work. Blending elements of science fiction and historical fiction, the novel tells the story of Dana, an African American woman who is mysteriously transported back in time to the antebellum South. Kindred explores the brutal realities of slavery, the complexities of racial identity, and the enduring impact of the past on the present. It is a powerful and haunting examination of history and the struggle for survival.

Parable of the Sower and Parable of the Talents:

The Parable series, consisting of Parable of the Sower (1993) and Parable of the Talents (1998), presents a dystopian vision of the future. Set in a near-future America plagued by environmental and social collapse, these novels follow the journey of Lauren Olamina, a young woman with hyperempathy syndrome. Lauren creates a new spiritual belief system called Earthseed, and the novels explore themes of resilience, community, and the search for meaning in a chaotic world. Grab the duology now in stock at Books2Door with The Parable Series 2 Books Collection Set by Octavia E. Butler. 

Dawn (Xenogenesis trilogy):

The Xenogenesis trilogy, comprised of Dawn (1987), Adulthood Rites (1988), and Imago (1989), tells the story of Lilith Iyapo, a survivor of a post-apocalyptic Earth who is chosen by an alien race called the Oankali to help rebuild humanity. Through the lens of science fiction, Butler explores themes of identity, genetic manipulation, and the complexity of human-alien interactions. The trilogy delves into questions of consent, power dynamics, and the consequences of humanity's actions. Purchase The Xenogenesis Trilogy 3 book collection now in stock and available at Books2Door. 

About the Author: 

Octavia E. Butler was an influential American author known for her contributions to science fiction and speculative fiction. Born on June 22, 1947, in Pasadena, California, Butler overcame numerous challenges and obstacles to become one of the most celebrated and critically acclaimed writers of her time. As an African American woman writing in a genre dominated by white male authors, Butler's work broke new ground and challenged the norms of the science fiction community.

Butler's childhood was marked by financial difficulties, shyness, and dyslexia. However, she found solace in books and developed a love for storytelling from an early age. Influenced by science fiction magazines, she began writing her own stories as a young girl. Butler attended Pasadena City College, where she studied various subjects, including creative writing. She later participated in the Open Door Program of the Screenwriters Guild of America, which provided her with resources and guidance for her writing career.

Butler grew up in a modest household and developed an early interest in reading and storytelling. Inspired by science fiction magazines and her love for books, she began writing at a young age. However, it wasn't until she attended a science fiction convention in the 1960s that she realised she could pursue a career as a science fiction writer. Butler often cited her experiences as an outsider and her observations of racial and gender disparities as significant influences on her work.

Butler's writing stands out for its unique blend of science fiction, social commentary, and speculative elements. Her narratives often explore issues of race, gender, power dynamics, and the human condition. Butler's protagonists are typically strong, complex women who challenge societal norms and navigate hostile environments. Through her work, she sought to shed light on social injustices, raise awareness about marginalised voices, and provoke thought about the potential consequences of human actions.

During her lifetime, Octavia E. Butler received numerous accolades and awards for her contributions to literature. She was the first science fiction writer to receive the prestigious MacArthur Foundation Fellowship (commonly known as the "Genius Grant") in 1995. Butler also won multiple Hugo and Nebula Awards, two of the most esteemed honours in the science fiction genre. Her works have been translated into multiple languages and continue to be studied in academic settings.

description:

He studied at the integrated secondary school Hazelwood College, then graduated from the University of Ulster in 2001 soon after which, he shot to fame for his art works, illustrations and writing prowess. 

Today an award-winning children’s author; Oliver Jeffers, is widely popular for his picture books for children and has been published by the world’s top-notch publishers—like HarperCollins UK and Penguin US. His picture books, including The Incredible Book Eating Boy (2006), The Day Crayons Quit (2013) and its sequel The Day The Crayons Came Home (2015, both #1 NYTimes Best Sellers)—have been translated in over 30 languages; German, Spanish and French among others. 

From figurative paintings and installations to illustrations and picture-book making, Oliver Jeffers’ creativity takes many forms. Whilst his paintings are on display across the best art galleries in the world, Jeffers' style of illustration uses mixed media and is recognised for its subtle narrative and use of space in composition. Working in collaboration with Studio AKA, Oliver’s second book Lost and Found (2005) was developed into an animated short film that has received over sixty awards, including a BAFTA for Best Animated Short Film. 

Obviously then, Oliver Jeffers’ children’s books and arts are just the kind of creativity you want to expose your child to. In this collection therefore, we have curated a list of Oliver books that we think ought to be on your child’s bookshelf.

Here We Are : Notes for Living on Planet Earth for children aged 6 and up is an exquisite and thought-provoking Oliver Jeffers book set. Our planet, earth and this world can be a bewildering place, especially for those that have only just got here. Your child’s head will most likely be filled with questions, so allow them to explore what makes our planet and how we live on it. From land and sky, to people and time, these notes can be your child’s guide. With these books, you can get your child started on their journey to getting to know the world. Some things about our planet are pretty complicated, but things can be simple, too: you've just got to be kind. Here We Are is that utterly heartfelt book which will simplify the world for younglings. 

Book of Opposites by Oliver Jeffers for children aged 6 and up is a spectacular concept board book from Oliver Jeffers, based on his million-copy selling, award-winning global picture-book phenomenon Here We Are! This book of opposites is a fun introduction to opposites (as the name suggests) for your babies and toddlers. Explaining the concept of opposites to babies and toddlers can be tricky. Near and Far. Heavy and Light. All opposites and all a bit dull. The Hueys are a bunch of characters in the book who like to learn, but also like a bit of anarchic fun. A cat may be stuck UP a tree, but you can chop it DOWN to help. The Hueys mix the basic idea of opposites and throw in a few curve balls that make the experience more exciting. Get your little one the Here We Are book set and give them a fun way to get to the planet they inhabit.

title: Olivie Blake Books
description:
Alexene Farol Follmuth, more commonly known by her pen-name Olivie Blake, is an American bestselling author. Her latest novels, The Atlas Six and My Mechanical Romance, are no exception, having earned her a spot on the New York Times and Sunday Times list. She is a rising star in the literary world, with a talent for crafting captivating stories that transport readers to other worlds and leaves them breathless with her captivating and extensive world-building. 

Among many of her published titles, a common theme among her works encompass the paranormal and the supernatural as well as revolving around the collective human experience and exploring the definition behind what it means to be human (or not!) as well as the complexities of love, loss and life. 

The Atlas Six is a thrilling adventure that follows a group of six elite students, handpicked from across the globe, as they compete in a high-stakes game of puzzles and riddles. The prize? An invitation to join the secretive and exclusive Society of the Atlas, a group of the world's most powerful and influential individuals. But as the competition heats up, the contestants begin to realize that there is more at stake than just a coveted spot in the Society. Secrets and conspiracies lurk around every corner, and the true nature of the game is shrouded in mystery. With twists and turns that will keep you guessing until the very end, The Atlas Six is a must-read for fans of thrillers and adventure novels. 

The Atlas Paradox is the thrilling and long-awaited sequel to the dark academic sensation The Atlas Six. Six Magicians. Two rivalries. One researcher. And a man who can walk through dreams. Now, all must pick a side: whether to preserve the world as it is or destroy it completely. In this viral TikTok sensation, The Atlas Six, a secret society of Alexandrians, must choose a side and their alliances to see which will hold and which will see their enmity deepen. 

My Mechanical Romance is her first YA debut book, released in 2022, written under her real name and not her pen name Olivie Blake. The story is a heartfelt STEM romance following the story of Bel, who would rather die than think about the future. But when she accidentally reveals a hidden talent for engineering at school, she’s forced into joining the robotics club- but to make things worse, she’s ignored by all the boys and the only other girl on the team. Enter Mateo “Teo” Luna, captain of the club who cares way too much about nationals whilst Bel- not too much. Whilst the nights of after-school work grow longer, the pair realise that they’ve made much more than a combat-fighting robot: they’ve managed to make themselves a winning team, showing exactly why girls belong in STEM. The lighthearted romance explores the significant challenges that girls of colour face in STEM and the vulnerability of first love. 

Olivie Blake's writing is characterized by vivid imagery, engaging characters, and intricate world-building. Whether she is weaving a tale of adventure or exploring the depths of human emotion, her stories are always compelling and deeply resonant. With The Atlas Six series and My Mechanical Romance, she has created two masterpieces that are sure to delight readers of all ages and genres.

If you're a fan of fantasy, science fiction, or romance, you won't want to miss these two incredible novels. Olivie Blake is a rising star in the literary world, and her talent is evident on every page. So why wait? Pick up a copy of The Atlas Six series and My Mechanical Romance today, and get ready to be swept away on an unforgettable journey.

title: One Piece Manga Books
description:
One Piece is a popular manga series created by Eiichiro Oda that has captured the hearts of fans all around the world. The manga has been serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine since 1997 and has since been adapted into an anime series, films, and video games.

The story of One Piece revolves around Monkey D. Luffy, a young boy who gains the ability to stretch his body like rubber after eating a mystical fruit known as the "Devil Fruit." Luffy sets out on a journey to become the King of the Pirates and find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece," which is said to grant unimaginable wealth and power to whoever finds it.

Throughout his journey, Luffy forms a diverse crew of pirates, each with their own unique abilities and personalities, and battles powerful enemies, including other pirates, government agents, and even gods. The story explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the pursuit of dreams, as well as darker themes such as corruption, slavery, and the consequences of violence. Check out the One Piece manga box set 1 with volumes 1-23 action-packed books!

Feature Specification
Series / Brand One Piece Official Franchise (Shonen Jump / VIZ Media)
Author / Creator Eiichiro Oda
Publisher Partners VIZ Media (Subsidiary of Shogakukan & Shueisha Inc / UK Distribution)
Format Architecture Unabridged Trade Paperbacks, Complete Box Sets (Sets 1–4), Omnibus 3-in-1 Editions, Color Walk Compendiums
Target Academic Bracket Ages 12+ (Teen 13+ / Key Stage 3, Key Stage 4, GCSE, YA & Adult Manga Collectors)
Iconic Story Arcs East Blue, Alabasta, Skypiea, Water Seven, Thriller Bark, Marineford/Paramount War, Dressrosa, Whole Cake Island, Wano
Special Value Offerings Multi-volume box set discounts (up to 45%+ off RRP), 10% BookPoints cashback rewards, direct warehouse pricing
Skills Developed Visual-spatial narrative decoding, complex long-term narrative retention, character arc analysis, cross-cultural storytelling appreciation

One of the most remarkable aspects of the One Piece manga is its world-building. Oda has created a vast and intricate fictional world filled with diverse cultures, creatures, and technologies. The world of One Piece is divided into four oceans, each with its own distinct geography and political climate. The world is also populated by a wide range of characters, each with their own backstory, motivations, and abilities.

One Piece has become a cultural phenomenon in Japan and around the world, with a devoted fan base that has followed the series for decades. The manga has sold over 480 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time. The anime series has also been successful, with over 1000 episodes and multiple films.

One Piece Arcs:
One Piece is divided into multiple story arcs, each with its own unique setting, characters, and plot. Some of the most notable arcs include the East Blue Arc, which introduces the main characters and their motivations, the Alabasta Arc, where the crew helps a princess save her kingdom from a tyrant, and the Marineford War Arc, where Luffy faces off against powerful enemies in a battle for the fate of his world. Other notable arcs include the Water Seven Arc, the Dressrosa Arc, and the Whole Cake Island Arc.

About the Author: 
The success of One Piece can be attributed in large part to the skill and dedication of its creator, Eiichiro Oda. Oda was born in Kumamoto, Japan in 1975 and began his career as a manga artist in 1992, working as an assistant to several established manga artists before creating his own series.

Oda's art style is distinctive, with a focus on exaggerated, cartoonish character designs and intricate backgrounds. His storytelling skills are also highly praised, with the ability to balance humour, action, and drama in a way that keeps readers engaged and emotionally invested.

However, what truly sets Oda apart is his dedication to his craft. Oda is known for his intense work ethic, often working 18 hours a day and sleeping only a few hours a night. He is also known for his attention to detail, spending hours researching and planning every aspect of his story and world-building.

Despite the gruelling schedule and pressure of being one of the most successful manga artists of all time, Oda remains humble and dedicated to his fans. He regularly interacts with fans through social media and fan events and has been known to respond to fan letters personally.

In conclusion, One Piece is a beloved manga series that has captivated readers and viewers around the world for over two decades. Its intricate world-building, engaging characters, and powerful themes have made it one of the most successful and beloved manga series of all time. Its creator, Eiichiro Oda, is a true master of his craft, with a dedication to his work and fans that sets him apart as one of the most talented and respected manga artists of his generation. Check out our other manga and anime comic books collection.

Eiichiro Oda stands as a globally revered mangaka pioneer whose record-breaking One Piece saga holds the Guinness World Record for the most copies published for the same comic book series by a single author. Serialised in Weekly Shonen Jump and published in English by VIZ Media (a subsidiary of Shogakukan and Shueisha Inc), this official collection guarantees absolute translation fidelity and authentic print quality. Utilising durable trade paperback bindings, high-opacity paper stock, and crisp line artwork explicitly formatted to minimise visual tracking strain during extended reading sessions, this series complies seamlessly with UK secondary school literacy guidelines (Teen 13+ / Key Stage 3 & Key Stage 4 transition). Recommended by secondary librarians, visual literacy educators, and manga collectives across the United Kingdom, this master series serves as a gold-standard framework for youth reading engagement and graphic novel collection.

Redirecting back to Orchard Books publishing, now an imprint of Hachette Children’s Group, its UK branch is maintained by Hachette UK. Given Orchard Books, UK’s rich history in publishing children’s books; they have still managed to retain their title as an ace children’s book publisher with books for children of every age group.

Orchard Books Rainbow Magic Fairies for instance, were created in conjunction with Early Years reading consultants and are based on the most updated educational research, thus making the Rainbow Magic Beginner Readers a perfect way to introduce your child to reading.

Rainbow Magic Beginner Readers by Daisy Meadows, 8 Books Collection Set for kids aged 3-8 we think is the one set parents should invest in. Young readers who seek adventure and excitement will appreciate the spell-binding tales that bring together fairies along with the beautiful illustrations accompanying them.

In each set of eight books in the series, best friends Kirsty Tate and Rachel Walker, meet a new group of seven fairies, all of whom have something in common (rainbow magic, weather magic, party magic, flower magic, and so on. Perfect for bedtime reading, the books are designed not only to help children become fluent readers but also to trigger their imaginations. As a result, these stories could be a great stepping stone to prompt your child to read aloud more and do so, independently. They’ll soon be reciting their favourite fairy tale and asking plenty of questions along the way. Get ready for an exciting fairy adventure with your kid.

Ancient Myths 16 Books Collection set by Geraldine McCaughrean for children aged 7 to 9 is yet another children’s classic by Orchard Books. Written by McCaughrean, featuring illustrations by Tony Ross, these books provide children with the perfect introduction to the ancient civilizations— Greek and Roman mythology.

If your child loves history and enjoys learning about ancient civilisations; this Ancient Myths series will be perfect for them. Adapted into engaging and easy-to-read short stories, this book set will teach your child about exciting historic trivia and myths. For instance, the Theseus' battle with the murderous minotaur; Jason and his battle for the Golden Fleece; and Zeus' incredible war against the Titans. Gallagher Girls Series by Ally Carter 6 Books Collection Box Set for children Aged 12-17 is a spy novels series that revolve around Gallagher Academy. An adventure series that will keep your young reader engaged in the exciting lives of the students of Gallagher Academy; this one will do more than teach your child to read for entertainment. The series will also stir a curiosity in the young minds and make them look forward to the exciting high school life.

One of the most popular children’s books published by Orion is the Horrid Henry Early Readers 25 Books Children Collection Box Set By Francesca Simon- for children aged 7 to 9. Horrid Henry is an 8-year boy who loves doing unimaginable horrible things. He throws food, he snatches things, he pushes, shoves and pinches. He has a 6-year-old brother called Perfect Peter, an extremely perfect boy who does uncountable good deeds. Peter always says "Please" and "Thank You", he loves vegetables and refuses cake and he never ever picks his nose. The book series is a hilarious series of events (in the form of individual books) that happen to these central characters. Each book makes an interesting read and lesson for young readers.

The Roman Mysteries Epic 10 Books Collection By Caroline Lawrence for children aged 9 to14 is yet another Orion’s children’s book and a bestseller no less. The first in Caroline Lawrence's internationally bestselling Roman Mysteries series, re-issued with a fantastic new cover look. Flavia Gemina is a natural at solving mysteries. The daughter of a ship's captain living in Ostia, the port of Rome, in AD79, she and her three friends, Jonathan, a Jewish boy (and secretly a Christian); Nubia, an African slave girl; and Lupus, a mute beggar boy, must work together to discover who is beheading the watch dogs that guard people's homes, and why. A talented storyteller, Caroline Lawrence has created a delightfully readable and accessible series that your children will want to read time and time again.

A book by Orion Publishing that is sure to be popular with your young teen; The Queen's Gambit by Walter Tevis is an intriguing tale of a Chess genius. Now a major Netflix series, this book is a coming of age tale of a Chess genius. When she is sent to an orphanage at the age of eight, Beth Harmon soon discovers two ways to escape her surroundings, albeit fleetingly. Playing chess and taking the little green pills given to her and the other children to keep them subdued. Before long, it becomes apparent that hers is a prodigious talent, and as she progresses to the top of the US chess rankings, she is able to forge a new life for herself. But she can never quite overcome her urge to self-destruct. For Beth, there's more at stake than merely winning and losing. Few novelists have written about genius and addiction as acutely as Walter Tevis and we are sure this is a book that will inspire your teen.

title: Oscar Wilde Books
description:
Immerse yourself in the world of wit, charm, and thought-provoking paradoxes with the Oscar Wilde Book collection, now available and in stock at Books2Door. Oscar Wilde, a luminary of the 19th-century literary scene, was not just a playwright and poet but also a fearless critic and one of the most celebrated personalities of his time. Born in Dublin in 1854, Wilde's razor-sharp wit, flamboyant style, and audacious commentary on society and morality earned him a place among the elite. More than just his words, it was Wilde's life—filled with both scandal and brilliance—that further solidified his legendary status. A man who was unafraid to challenge societal norms, Wilde's works often reflected his own internal conflicts and the contradictions of the world he lived in.

The Collected Works of Oscar Wilde:

An absolute treasure trove for any literature enthusiast, this collection houses all of Wilde's masterpieces. From his soul-stirring plays to his profound poems, it's a journey through Wilde's brilliant mind. Each page offers a deeper understanding of his vision, making it a perfect collection for both newcomers and dedicated fans.

The Picture of Dorian Gray:

Perhaps one of the most famous of Wilde's works, this novel explores the themes of vanity, moral duplicity, and the pursuit of eternal youth. The story revolves around a young man named Dorian Gray, who, after having his portrait painted, realises that the painting ages while he remains young and beautiful. As Dorian indulges in life's darker pleasures, the portrait becomes a grotesque reflection of his decaying soul. This tale acts as a cautionary exploration of the dangers of unchecked vanity and hedonism.

The Happy Prince:

This touching and deeply symbolic tale showcases Wilde's flair for combining poignancy with profound lessons. The story revolves around a statue of a prince who, despite his outward opulence, is heartbroken over the suffering he sees in his city. With the help of a swallow, he sacrifices his own beauty and wealth to alleviate the suffering of his people. It's a touching narrative on selflessness and compassion.

The Selfish Giant:

Another of Wilde's enchanting tales for all ages, this story portrays the transformation of a Giant's heart. Once selfish and mean, keeping children away from his garden, the Giant undergoes a change of heart when he realises the importance of love, companionship, and the joys of sharing. The narrative delves deep into the themes of love, redemption, and the spiritual essence of innocence.

Embrace the world of Oscar Wilde, a universe where words transcend time, where stories are more than just tales, and where each sentence holds a universe of thought. Whether you're introducing a young reader to the magic of Wilde or rekindling your own love for his works, this collection promises a literary experience that's truly unmatched. Dive in and let the words of one of history's most brilliant minds captivate your soul.

title: Paddington Bear Books
description:
Paddington Bear first appeared in 1958 in the children’s book “A Bear Called Paddington" and since has become an iconic character in British children’s literature. Written by Michael Bond and illustrated by Peggy Fortnum, the Paddington Bear books have been adapted into films, TV series, and the character has appeared on all sorts of merchandise.

The origin of this adorable teddy bear began when this neglected and abandoned toy was tossed and left behind in a department store, only to be discovered by the author Michael Bond who was looking for a gift for his wife during the Christmas Eve of 1956; and since that day Bond began writing a story about this bear for fun, only for it unexpectedly gain popularity among children.

Paddington’s personality resembles a polite and kind-hearted human, always addressing people as “Mr” and “Mrs” and never by first names. Paddington’s charming charisma shows when he gets into trouble innocently constantly by mistake and trying his best to fix things! This lovable bear from Peru usually appears in his old hat and duffle coat, carrying his suitcase with secret hidden compartments!

Fun fact: did you know when the Channel Tunnel was completed in 1994, Paddington Bear was chosen by the British Tunnellers as the first item to be passed through to the French people as a much-loved fictional character from Britain? He famously appeared in a short film with Queen Elizabeth II on her Platinum Jubilee. This led to Paddington appearing in many tributes from the public on the occasion of her death. 

Paddington Bear is ideal for young readers of ages 0-5 and ages 5-7.

title: Palestine Books
description:
Welcome to Books2Door's collection of books on Palestine, a curated selection that aims to provide valuable insights into the history, culture, and literature of this region. This collection not only introduces readers to the complex history of Palestine but also highlights the voices of prominent Palestinian authors. 

Jerusalem & Falastin: A Cookbook 2 Books Collection Set - Non Fiction - Hardback

This collection combines Jerusalem and Falastin, two highly regarded cookbooks by Yotam Ottolenghi and Sami Tamimi. While primarily focusing on culinary delights, these books offer a unique perspective on the flavours and traditions of the region. They provide insight into the vibrant food culture that thrives in Palestine and Jerusalem.

We Are Palestinian: A Celebration of Culture and Tradition By Reem Kassis

In We Are Palestinian, Reem Kassis invites readers on a captivating journey into the heart of Palestinian culture and tradition. Through her engaging storytelling and beautifully curated recipes, Kassis showcases the richness of Palestinian cuisine, customs, and heritage. This book not only serves as a culinary guide but also as a celebration of the resilient Palestinian spirit. It is a testament to the importance of preserving cultural identity and passing it down through generations.

On Palestine by Noam Chomsky & Ilan Pappé

In this sequel to Gaza in Crisis, Noam Chomsky collaborates with Palestinian journalist Ilan Pappé to offer a concise yet powerful exploration of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Through their conversations, they explore the road ahead for the region and the role the international community has to play. 

The Hundred Years' War on Palestine: A History of Settler Colonial Conquest and Resistance by Rashid I. Khalidi

In this meticulously researched work, Rashid I. Khalidi provides a comprehensive history of the conflict, spanning a century. Shortlisted for the 2020 Cundill History Prize, Khalidi's book interweaves history, interviews and his own story to create this personal response to the ongoing issues in the region. 

Against the Loveless World by Susan Abulhawa

Susan Abulhawa, a celebrated Palestinian-American author, weaves a poignant and gripping narrative in Against the Loveless World. This novel delves into the life of Nahr, a Palestinian woman who endures hardship and displacement. Abulhawa's storytelling skillfully explores themes of identity, resilience, and the Palestinian experience.

title: Pan Macmillan
description:
Pan Macmillan UK is one of the largest book publishers in the UK, with imprints including Macmillan, Mantle, Pan, Picador, Boxtree, Sidgwick & Jackson, Bello, Tor, Kingfisher, Macmillan Children's Books, Two Hoots, Bluebird, Campbell Books, Macmillan New Writing and Macmillan Digital Audio. 

Part of Macmillan Publishers International Limited; Pan Macmillan was originally founded back in 1843 by Daniel and Alexander Macmillan, two brothers from the Scottish Isle of Arran. Daniel was the business brain, whilst Alexander laid the literary foundations of the publication house by adding world class authors like Lewis Carroll, Henry James, Thomas Hardy and Rudyard Kipling to the Pan Macmillan authors list. 

Today Macmillan is one of the largest and best-known international publishers in the world. Pan Macmillan now operates in over 70 countries worldwide, with a broad range of award-winning books for children and adults across all categories and formats; to their credit. From bestselling titles for adults to iconic children’s titles that have stood the test of time; Pan Macmillian has an extensive range of books to their credit and here are some of our favourites from the publication house.

If you are a parent that is invested in your child growing up to be a well-read adult then surely you too enjoy reading thought provoking books yourself. One such title by Pan Macmillian books is the Permanent Record: A Memoir of a Reluctant Whistleblower by Edward Snowden. One of the many diverse and brave titles by the publication house; this Sunday Times top ten bestseller by whistleblower Edward Snowden is an expose on the US government’s system of mass surveillance. An intriguing read for any well-informed adult, the book reveals for the first time the story of Snowden’s life, including how he helped to build the mass surveillance system and what motivated him to try to bring it down. 

In 2013, twenty-nine-year-old Edward Snowden shocked the world when he broke with the American intelligence establishment and revealed that the United States government was secretly pursuing the means to collect every single phone call, text message, and email. The result would be an unprecedented system of mass surveillance with the ability to pry into the private lives of every person on earth. Six years later, Snowden reveals for the very first time how he helped to build this system and why he was moved to expose it. The book is an extraordinary account of a bright young man who grew up online - a man who became a spy, a whistleblower, and, in exile, the Internet's conscience. Written with wit, grace, passion, and an unflinching candour, Permanent Record is possibly one of the most crucial memoirs of the digital age.

For young adults, Pan Macmillian has published some iconic titles. The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy by Douglas Adams, for instance, is a classic sci-fi galactic adventure that has been a hot favourite with young adults for generations. A fiction classic, this adventure starts with the last human on Earth, his alien best friend, and a depressed android. Introducing readers to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, this YA edition of the funny sci-fi classic is one literary adventure every young adult must experience. One Thursday lunchtime the Earth gets unexpectedly demolished to make way for a new hyperspace bypass. In the seconds before global obliteration, Arthur is plucked from the planet by his friend Ford Prefect and together the pair venture out across the galaxy on the craziest, strangest road trip of all time! The Percy Jackson book series by Rick Riordan has achieved immense popularity and has become a cultural phenomenon since its debut. With its unique blend of mythology, adventure, and relatable characters, the series has captured the imaginations of readers of all ages, from children to young adults and even adults.

Another factor contributing to the series' success is the compelling and diverse cast of characters. The protagonist, Percy Jackson, is a witty and relatable hero who faces the same challenges and insecurities as any teenager. His friends, Annabeth, Grover, and others, are equally well-developed and add depth to the story. The characters' growth, friendships, and personal struggles resonate with readers, forging strong connections that keep them invested in the series.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians: 

The original series that introduced readers to the incredible universe of Percy Jackson, Percy Jackson and the Olympians, follows the adventures of the titular character, a dyslexic teenager who discovers he is a demigod, the son of Poseidon. Set in a contemporary world where Greek gods and creatures are real, Percy finds himself thrust into a whirlwind of quests and battles as he tries to prevent a catastrophic war among the gods. This seven-book series combines humour, heart, and non-stop action, leaving readers eagerly turning each page. Grab the Percy Jackson Collection 7 Books Set By Rick Riordan. 

The Heroes of Olympus: 

Continuing the story from the original series, The Heroes of Olympus 5 book collection expands the mythology to include Roman gods and introduces a new cast of demigod heroes. As ancient prophecies unfold, Percy Jackson and his friends must join forces with their Roman counterparts to face new enemies and embark on a perilous journey to save both the Greek and Roman worlds. This series masterfully blends humour, adventure, and intricate character development, deepening the connection readers have with their favourite demigods.

The Trials of Apollo: 

In this exciting spin-off series, Riordan explores the fate of the god Apollo after he is cast down from Olympus and transformed into a mortal teenager named Lester Papadopoulos. The Trials of Apollo 5 book collection follows Lester's quest to regain his godly powers by completing a series of dangerous trials set by Zeus. Joined by his demigod friends and a new companion, Meg McCaffrey, Lester must face formidable enemies and confront his own flaws, all while navigating the challenges of being human. Riordan's signature blend of humour, mythology, and fast-paced storytelling shines brightly in this fresh addition to the Percy Jackson universe.

Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard: 

Stepping into the realm of Norse mythology, Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard introduces readers to Magnus Chase, a sixteen-year-old homeless orphan who discovers he is the son of a Norse god. As Magnus embarks on a quest to prevent the apocalypse, he must navigate the Nine Worlds, encounter mythical beings, and forge alliances with diverse and compelling characters. As descendants of powerful Egyptian magicians, they must confront ancient gods, unravel family secrets, and battle the forces of chaos. Through a unique narrative style that alternates between the voices of Carter and Sadie, Riordan immerses readers in a richly detailed world, blending mythology with modern-day settings to create a truly engaging reading experience. With the Percy Jackson book series, Rick Riordan has captivated readers of all ages, reimagining ancient mythologies in a modern context and introducing a new generation to the wonders of these timeless tales. From the original adventures of Percy Jackson to the thrilling spin-offs like The Trials of Apollo, Magnus Chase, and The Kane Chronicles, Riordan's books offer a winning combination of mythology, humour, and heart-pounding action. Join the ranks of millions of readers who have been enthralled by Riordan's masterful storytelling and embark on an unforgettable journey through the pages of this extraordinary series.

About the Author:

Rick Riordan is an acclaimed American author known for his immensely popular young adult book series centred around mythology. Born on June 5, 1964, in San Antonio, Texas, Riordan initially pursued a career as a middle school English and history teacher before venturing into the world of writing.

Riordan's breakthrough came with the publication of the first book in the Percy Jackson & the Olympians series, titled The Lightning Thief, in 2005. The series follows the adventures of Percy Jackson, a demigod son of Poseidon, as he navigates a world filled with Greek gods, monsters, and quests. The success of the Percy Jackson series catapulted Riordan to literary stardom, earning him a dedicated following of readers worldwide.

Drawing inspiration from his own experiences as a teacher and his love for mythology, Riordan skillfully combines action, humour, and relatable characters in his books. His writing style captures the essence of ancient mythologies while infusing them with a contemporary twist, making them accessible and engaging to a modern audience. Riordan's ability to blend ancient tales with relatable themes and issues has resonated with readers of all ages, making his books beloved by children, young adults, and adults alike.

title: Peter Rabbit Books
description:
Peter Rabbit exists today as one of the best-selling children’s books, it was written and illustrated by Beatrix Potter and was published in 1902. The story revolves around a rabbit, a playful and naughty one, with its noncompliance to rules and disregard to certain things leads them into troubles. The story books are splendid for young children as it follows a fun and comical story mixed with adventure. Most importantly, the stories factors in life lessons and morals which is a key aspect for children to take in after reading. The text is straightforward and easy to comprehend, and each page is delightfully illustrated with elegant water style painting. In the story, Peter Rabbit is brave and bold, at first, he does not obey any rules and even breaks them until he falls into an unpleasant mistake which results in Peter being a little wiser. Peter Rabbit has 3 siblings: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail. The World of Peter Rabbit Complete Collection 23 Book Box Set is a wonderful boxset containing 23 books, packed together in a lovely box. 

Potter initially wrote the story of Peter Rabbit in 1893 to provide entertainment to her friend’s 5-year-old son, who was ill. The letter she wrote commenced with: “I don't know what to write to you, so I shall tell you a story about four little rabbits whose names were—Flopsy, Mopsy, Cottontail and Peter.” This followed with Potter publishing more stories, which at first received rejections from publishers before it received positive results. Potter developed her prowess in her ability to draw and illustrate due to her childhood interest in nature surrounding her. As she grew up as a child, she would sketch animals and day by day observation developed her life-like drawing style.

Did you know Potter also studied the plant world meticulously, she produced over 300 paintings of mushrooms by the year 1901 and her study led Potter to submit a paper on spore reproduction. Her continuous hard work and artistry meant that her illustrations in Peter Rabbit have realistic characteristics, even though the characters would wear human clothes, top hats. Check out our Series category for other popular authors and books. Our Books by Age is a useful category to browse books specific to the age you would like to cater to.

One of the best-selling children’s books of all time, the Peter Rabbit books are a children's book series written and illustrated by Beatrix Potter that follow mischievous but resourceful young Peter Rabbit as he gets chased around the garden of Mr. McGregor. Peter Rabbit and his three sisters—Flopsy, Mopsy and Cotton-Tail enjoy spending their days hopping around in Mr. McGregor's vegetable garden but when McGregor's relatives suddenly move in, things change and an adventure begins.

Beatrix Potter first created the title character Peter Rabbit in 1893 in a letter she wrote to amuse the sick child of her former governess. After which, Potter’s friends encouraged her to look for a publisher. However, the book was rejected. Potter then decided to publish the book herself in 1901. The original version had 42 black-and-white illustrations and was printed in a small format, so very young children could also enjoy it. The work proved highly popular, and Frederick Warne & Co. subsequently published it—The Tale of Peter Rabbit was released in 1902. 

The Tale of Peter Rabbit combines humour and adventure while also featuring a moral lesson to its young readers. The original book revolves around Peter Rabbit, who is far more adventurous than his siblings: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail. Their mother warns them to avoid Mr. McGregor’s garden, because their father had an “accident” there and ended up in a pie. However, after their mother leaves, naughty Peter immediately hops in the garden gate to gorge on Mr. McGregor’s vegetables, whilst the other siblings obediently go up the lane to pick blackberries. Mr. McGregor soon spots Peter near the cucumber frame and chases the terrified little rabbit all over the garden, and Peter loses both his shoes and his little blue jacket. After finally locating the gate, Peter returns home frightened but wiser. This is when Mrs. Rabbit gives Peter chamomile tea, but, for his good siblings, she produces a supper of bread and milk and blackberries. A prompt lesson in obedience, this is a book every parent will want for their child.

Peter Rabbit: A Peep-Inside Tale from the Peter Rabbit book series is about an episode when Peter is so busy in the garden eating radishes that he doesn't notice a red tail poking out of the bushes. Will Peter spot Mr. Tod before it's too late? Get this book for your child and allow them to join Peter Rabbit on this adventure story in this brilliant new board book format with flaps to lift and holes to peep through.

The Christmas Tale of Peter Rabbit : Book and CD With this christmas book, screenwriter and actress Emma Thompson continues the adventures of Peter Rabbit. Featuring Beatrix Potter's Peter Rabbit, his comical little cousin Benjamin Bunny, and a pompous turkey called William; this one makes a fun addition to the Peter Rabbit series of books. This Christmas, Peter and Benjamin have put their mischievous ways aside and are working together to try and rescue William from a Christmas dinner he most certainly won't enjoy! This beautiful paperback edition comes with an audio CD read by Emma Thompson, making it the perfect Christmas gift for your young ones.

title: Philip Pullman Books
description:
Philip Pullman 

Philip Pullman was born in Norwich and has had a career spanning over 40 years. His first novel, The Haunted Storm, was published in 1973, but his most popular series is His Dark Materials Series which started with The Northern Lights, called The Golden Compass in the US in 1995. 

Pullman has released many other literary series over the years. The Sally Lockheart series began with The Ruby in the Smoke (1985) and ended with The Tin Princess (1994). He has also released The New Cut Gang series, The Book of Dust Series, and various standalone novels for children and adults. 

His Dark Materials 

Philip Pullman’s Young Adult Fantasy trilogy, His Dark Materials, follows Lyra Belacqua and her animal Daemon Pantalaimon (Pan for short) through an alternate version of our Earth. She is trying to discover more about her family and growing interest in her uncle Asriel’s research in ‘Dust’. 

The first book in the series is Northern Lights, also known as The Golden Compass. Published in 1995, this novel begins with a roughly eleven-year-old Lyra living at Jordon College, Oxford. The adventures continue for Lyra in book two of the His Dark Materials trilogy, The Subtle Knife. Published in 1997, Lyra meets Will Parry, who appears to be from a different world, one much closer to our world. 

Philip Pullman stated that his primary source of inspiration was John Milton’s Paradise Lost. His Dark Materials uses the idea of good and evil, God, Angels and the Devil that Milton describes in his 17th-century epic poem. 

The final book in the trilogy is The Amber Spyglass, published in 2000. However, the adventure doesn’t end here; Pullman also released several short stories and novellas that tie in with the trilogy. These are Lyra’s Oxford, Once Upon a Time in the North, The Collectors, Serpentine and most recently, The Imagination Chamber. 

Other Works

Pullman has produced many other novels through the years, including The Sally Lockhart Series and The Book of Dust Trilogy, with the final book yet to be released. He has also released children’s novels, including Count Karlstein, Spring-Heeled Jack, I was a Rat! or The Scarlet Slippers. Check out our Four Philip Pullman Fairy Tales Boxset or Philip Pullman’s Grimm Tales for Young and Old, an anthology of fairytales specifically chosen by Pullman with an introduction explaining their importance and their background. 

About the Author 

Sir Philip Nicholas Outram Pullman was born in Norwich in 1946. His father was an RAF pilot, so the family travelled significantly due to his role. Throughout his childhood, Pullman travelled to India, Yemen, Sri Lanka, Zimbabwe, and the Canary Islands. His father died in combat in Kenya when Pullman was seven.

He attended boarding schools as a child and studied at Exeter College, Oxford. As he started to build worlds for His Dark Materials, he drew inspiration from his own experiences at school and University. He has been writing full-time since 1996 and specialises in Young Adult and Children’s fiction.

title: Poldark Books
description:
As they say in literary circles; if you are looking for a good period drama, trust the British to give you the best. The bestselling Poldark Books by Winston Graham were published from 1945 to 1953 and continued from 1973 to 2002. The series can be divided in two cycles; the first seven books are set in the 18th century, concluding in 1799. Whilst the remaining five are concerned with the early years of the 19th century and the lives of the descendants of the previous novels’ main characters.

The Poldark series is loved across the world for its Victorian blend of romance, drama, unforgettable characters and a beautifully evocative portrayal of Cornwall. Spanning the late 18th and early 19th centuries—Poldark is a saga that follows the life of Ross Poldark. Ross is a brooding and principled young man who has just returned from the American Revolutionary War, only to find his life and estate disrupted. As Ross returns to his home in Cornwall after three years of war, he finds that his father is dead, his Cornish copper mine is failing and his childhood sweetheart, the beautiful Elizabeth Chynoweth is engaged to his cousin Francis.

A tale of romance, intrigue, betrayal, and one of the most heart-breaking love triangles in modern fiction ensue—as Poldark rescues a young woman, Demelza, from a beating, and takes her on as a kitchen maid while trying to help the people of the village and attempting to gain control of the mines sought after by his rival, the greedy and arrogant George Warleggan. As the plot thickens, Ross falls in love with the charming Demelza and tries to build a better world for her and their children whilst fighting his arch-enemy, the swaggering and ruthless financier, Warleggan.

Written between 1945 and 2002, the twelve Poldark novels made great television content and were eventually adapted for television, and two BBC series—the first starring Robin Ellis and Angharad Rees in the 1970s and the second, which premiered in 2015, starring Aidan Turner and Eleanor Tomlinson—were both enormous successes.

title: Pop-Up and Lift-the-Flap Books
description:
Learning to read can be a daunting task when you are a child. There are so many words to learn and so many different ways to put them together. But with the right resources, it can be a fun and rewarding experience. Both pop-up and lift-the-flap books are fun and interactive ways to help children learn to read. They provide an interactive experience that helps to engage youngsters.

By incorporating elements of movement, sound and visual stimuli, pop-up books can capture a child’s attention, engage their senses, and keep them engaged in the story. The three-dimensional illustrations can also help make the words and concepts more concrete.

Each page of a lift-the-flap book has a word or phrase and a picture that provides a clue. And when you lift the flap, you’ll find another image that reinforces the word’s meaning. This helps them to understand the connection between the words and the visuals, which is an essential part of learning to read. These books can provide a fun and engaging way for children to learn.

Pop-up books can also teach early reading skills such as letter sounds and sight words. They are a great way to introduce young children to new concepts and vocabulary words. They can inspire childrens’ imaginations and encourage them to try new things.

And because both pop-up and lift-the-flap books often tell simple, concise stories, they can be a great way to introduce young children to the concepts of reading and narration. As children follow along with the story, they can begin to develop an understanding of how print works. In addition, lift the flap books are often highly illustrated, which can help to keep children’s attention focused on the story.

Interactive books also allow children to practice their fine motor skills as they turn the pages, lift the flaps and manipulate the pop-ups. As children turn the pages and control the pop-ups, they learn about cause and effect and spatial relationships.

Best of all, pop-up books are widely available and relatively inexpensive, making them an excellent option for parents and teachers looking for an engaging and affordable way to help children learn to read. They are a great way to get kids excited about reading. They offer a unique and engaging experience that can help kids learn to love reading.

Whether you are looking for a bedtime story or a way to help your child practice reading, consider picking up a pop-up or lift-the-flap book. You might be surprised at how much fun you have.

At Books2Door, we have a wide range of great value interactive books. Axel Scheffler’s Flip Flap Series is one of our bestsellers. Get a hilarious assortment of mixed-up animals in this interactive extravaganza. We also sell the Usborne Peep Insideseries, a favourite among flap fans. Make sure you follow us on the socials and subscribe to our newsletter for the latest pop-up and lift-the-flap reading.

title: Quentin Blake Books
description:
Often imitated but never bettered, Quentin Blake is one of the most cherished illustrators in Britain. Blake has written or drawn over five hundred books, alongside exhibitions and public art. He’s best known for his collaboration with Roald Dahl, across books such as The BFG and Revolting Rhymes. You’ll also know his work from The Boy in the Dress by David Walliams, as well as his own writings like Clown.

We have a great selection of Quentin Blake books available here at Books2Door. You may also be interested in other bestselling illustrators, such as Tony Ross and Judith Kerr, or his successors as Children’s Laureate such as Julia Donaldson and Chris Riddell.

Biography

Quentin Blake was born in London in 1932. He went to Sidcup Grammar School, did National Service, studied English at Cambridge, attained a postgraduate teaching diploma from the University of London, and took life classes at Chelsea Art School. He taught for over twenty years at the Royal College of Art. Since the 90s, he’s worked as an exhibition curator in London and Paris.

However, Blake has been making his primary living as an illustrator since he was first published in Punch magazine at sixteen. He drew for them for many years, alongside The Spectator and other magazines. His first children’s book was published in 1960 - A Drink of Water by John Yeoman. He’s illustrated books by many authors, including Sylvia Plath, Michael Rosen, and Dr. Seuss, as well as many astonishing books written by himself. He illustrated David Walliams’s debut novel, The Boy in the Dress, and its follow-up Mr Stink. 

However, Blake’s most enduring partnership was with Roald Dahl. Their collaboration started with the picture book The Enormous Crocodile in 1979 and lasted even past Dahl’s death in 1990. Blake’s work perfectly complements Dahl’s spiky and fablelike tales, and all of the latest editions come fully furnished with Blake’s illustrations. This includes Dahl’s final 1991 novel Billy and the Minpins, which Blake illustrated in 2017.

Blake has won many prizes across his career, including the Hans Christian Anderson Award for Illustration. He has been knighted by the British, admitted to the Legion d’Honneur by the French, and has received multiple honorary degrees. He became the inaugural Children’s Laureate in 1999, a post created to raise the profile of children’s literature.

Beyond the page, Blake has decorated the walls of many hospitals and caregiving establishments with his art, from mental health support centres to maternity wards. He founded the House of Illustration, a centre that promotes the art of illustration, which Blake feels isn’t given the same amount of attention and respect as other types of visual art.

Best-Known Books

The Roald Dahl 16 Book Collection is illustrated throughout by Quentin Blake. It features all of the classic stories, from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory to The Witches, Danny The Champion of the World to George’s Marvellous Medicine. This box set is the cornerstone of any kid’s library, and it’s available now at a great value price.

title: R. F. Kuang Books
description:
Born in Guangzhou, China, and later immigrating to the United States, Rebecca Kuang (also known as R.F. Kuang) uses her unique vantage point to inform her storytelling. Drawing inspiration from 20th-century Chinese history and politics, her books challenge readers to consider complex themes such as war ethics, colonisation, and the moral ambiguity of human actions. If you haven't already devoured her work, brace yourself for a gritty, no-holds-barred look at power dynamics, human resilience, and the immense cost of vengeance.

R. F. Kuang’s Standalone Works

Rebecca Kuang is also known to have branched out to other genres, most notably in her bestselling standalone Dark Academia novel Babel. Set in an alternative version of Victorian England set in the 19th century, a group of young and talented scholars enter Babel- a legendary library at the heart of Oxford University’s prestigious Royal Institute of Translation. In this speculative alternate reality, Britain’s colonial and economic supremacy is fueled by the use of magical silver bars, capturing what is “lost in translation” between words in different languages that have similar but not identical meanings. 

Her most recent work, Yellowface, explores the significance of the appropriation of literature and the boundaries of art. The focal point of the satirical novel is the darker side of the publishing industry, including racial representation, cultural appropriation, and systemic bias that exist within the institution. After Chinese-American Author Athena Liu overcomes an untimely death, her friend and white author, June Haywood, steals her manuscript and attempts to build up her own career through Athena’s work, posing as an ambiguous ethnic author. But June can’t escape Athena’s shadow, and emerging evidence soon brings June’s stolen success to light. 

Purchase both standalone novels Babel and Yellowface with the Rebecca F Kuang 2 book collection set now available and in stock at Books2Door. 

The Riveting Fantasy Series by R.F. Kuang

R.F. Kuang's fantasy series, including the critically acclaimed grimdark high fantasy The Poppy War, The Dragon Republic, and The Burning God, presents readers with an electrifying blend of historical accuracy, gritty realism, and magical lore. Crafted with utmost care, Kuang’s work is an intricate tapestry that melds cultural richness, intricate character development, and spellbinding storytelling into a can't-miss literary experience. Purchase all three books in the series with The Poppy War Series 3 books collection set now available and in stock at Books2Door. 

Set in a world inspired by 20th-century China, particularly the events surrounding the Sino-Japanese War and the Chinese Civil War, Kuang’s series stands out for its rich cultural elements and accurate historical details. Unlike your typical Westernized fantasy settings, you'll find yourself transported to a realm that feels simultaneously fresh and time-worn, offering a break from the usual dragons-and-castles backdrop.

The protagonist, Rin, isn't your run-of-the-mill hero. She's flawed, volatile, and very human. Her journey from a destitute orphan to a fierce warrior compelled by vengeance is rife with moral complexity. She's surrounded by a cast of well-rounded characters that make you question the notions of good and evil. Kuang's character development is so meticulous that every action and reaction feels like a natural progression, leaving readers constantly on the edge of their seats.

At its core, the series isn't just a coming-of-age story or a war-time saga. It's an exploration of the intricate nuances of politics, the agonising decisions in warfare, and the devastating impact of choices that are made in the heat of the moment. You'll find your heart racing through epic battles, your mind buzzing with political intrigue, and your soul aching for the characters ensnared in an unending cycle of revenge and destruction.

If you're a fan of expansive worlds brimming with unique magic systems, mythical creatures, and rich history, this series will captivate you. Kuang's skilful world-building ensures that the landscape of the Nikan Empire and its diverse people are as compelling as the characters who inhabit them. Whether it's the lore of the gods, the description of the landscapes, or the cultural practices, everything is painstakingly researched and skillfully incorporated into the story, making for a vivid and believable world.

title: Ray Bradbury Books
description:
Ray Bradbury Collection: A Journey Through Time, Space, and Consciousness

Nestled within the pantheon of literary legends, Ray Bradbury stands as a beacon of innovative thinking and storytelling. The author, with his unerring knack for blending science fiction, fantasy, and the innately human quest for understanding, has left an indelible mark on the realm of literature. This collection pays homage to some of Bradbury's most iconic works, each bearing testament to his boundless imagination and uncanny ability to tap into the human soul.

Fahrenheit 451

“There must be something in books, things we can’t imagine, to make a woman stay in a burning house; there must be something there. You don’t stay for nothing.”

At the heart of Bradbury's work is often a dystopic cautionary tale, and Fahrenheit 451 is no exception. Set in a dystopian future, this chilling novel takes readers to a world where books are banned and "firemen" ignite flames to destroy any remaining tomes. But beyond the flames and the oppressive government lies a deeper narrative - a tale of resistance, a journey of self-discovery, and a poignant reminder of the power of literature and critical thinking. This is not just a book about the dangers of censorship but a clarion call, reminding us of the essential freedoms we often take for granted.

The Martian Chronicles

“We earth men have a talent for ruining big, beautiful things.”

Travelling far from Earth, The Martian Chronicles offers an episodic account of human colonisation on Mars. But as with all Bradbury tales, this is more than just a space adventure. Through interconnected stories, Bradbury weaves a narrative that delves deep into the consequences of human actions, the cultural shocks, clashes, and the ethical quandaries faced when one race imposes itself upon another. While the setting might be an alien world, the themes are innately human, touching on colonisation, nostalgia, and the unyielding drive of human ambition. Each chronicle serves as a mirror, reflecting the best and worst of humanity, both on Earth and beyond.

Zen in the Art of Writing

“You must stay drunk on writing so reality cannot destroy you.”

Departing from his fictional realms, Zen in the Art of Writing offers readers a chance to delve into the mind of the master himself. This isn't just another writing guide; it's an intimate exploration of Bradbury's love for the craft. With essays that are both instructional and deeply personal, Bradbury sheds light on his creative process, the inspirations behind his iconic stories, and the sheer joy of creation. Aspiring writers will find invaluable insights here, while dedicated fans will cherish the deeper understanding of the man behind the classics.

Bradbury's works have always danced on the edge of reality, drawing readers into worlds that, while often fantastical or futuristic, are rooted in deeply human concerns and emotions. Be it the oppressive regime of Fahrenheit 451, the haunting landscapes of Mars in The Marian Chronicles, or the introspective wisdom of Zen in the Art of Writing, there's an undeniable thread that binds them all: a quest for understanding, meaning, and connection.

About the Author:

Ray Bradbury, born on August 22, 1920, in Waukegan, Illinois, was an American author and screenwriter who illuminated the landscape of speculative fiction. With a career spanning more than 70 years, Bradbury's contribution to the worlds of science fiction, fantasy, and literature at large is beyond monumental.

Though he lacked formal higher education—a factor he attributed to financial constraints—Bradbury was largely self-educated. A voracious reader from a young age, he spent countless hours in libraries and cited authors such as Edgar Allan Poe, Jules Verne, and H.G. Wells as significant influences on his work. Determined to become a writer, Bradbury began publishing stories in fanzines as a teenager, gradually climbing the rungs of literary recognition through an uncompromising commitment to his craft.

Among his many accolades, Bradbury received the Prometheus Award, the O. Henry Memorial Award, the Benjamin Franklin Award, the World Fantasy Award for Lifetime Achievement, and the Grand Master Award from the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (SFWA). In 2007, he received a special Pulitzer citation "for his distinguished, prolific, and deeply influential career as an unmatched author of science fiction and fantasy."

Whether you're revisiting these classics or embarking on these journeys for the first time, this collection promises a reading experience that will both challenge and enchant. Dive into the Ray Bradbury collection, and let yourself be whisked away to worlds of wonder, introspection, and profound insight. Buy now in stock and available at Books2Door.

description:
A page dedicated to the works of the late great British author, illustrator, and cartoonist Raymond Briggs. We well as producing one of the most iconic Christmas characters, The Snowman, he has also created other brilliant stories like Fungus the Bogeyman and UG: Boy Genius of the Stone Age. 

The Snowman 

The Snowman is arguably one of the most recognisable Christmas images on the page and on screen. The original TV adaptation was first shown in 1982 and was introduced by music icon David Bowie. Since then, The Snowman has been a part of the Christmas tradition, with families gathering around their televisions to enjoy the wholesome and nostalgic story. Like the series, the book itself is entirely wordless and drawn using coloured pencils. 

To mark the 30th anniversary of the original short film, The Snowman and The Snowdog was released. The short was released on British TV in 2012 and is based on Briggs's beloved characters. The Snowman and The Snowdog is set in the same house but with a different family to keep the story's magic alive. For more books for this age range, check out our range of picture books. 

Other Works by Briggs 

Raymond Briggs wrote another festive picture book called Father Christmas. Briggs' interpretation of Father Christmas is not the stereotypical jolly figure who only works one day a year but a grumpy old man who lives with his pets, a cat, a dog and two reindeer. His miserable persona has become a beloved Christmas classic as no matter how much he moans, he really does love being Father Christmas and loves giving gifts. Check out our dedicated page to Christmas Books and Christmas TV Books for more festive books. 

Another famous title written and illustrated by Briggs is Fungus the Bogeyman. The 1977 picture book follows Fungus, a member of the Bogey society, as he starts to question the meaning of life and his function within society. The book was adapted into a TV series in 2004 and 2015 and a stage production in 2007 and 2008. For more picture books, check out our extended range of picture books, perfect for children 0-5 years and 5-7-years-old. 

About the Author

Raymond Briggs, born in 1934 in Wimbledon, London, was an illustrator, cartoonist, graphic novelist and author. He graduated from The Slade School of Fine Art in 1957, but before this, he was conscripted into the British Army and served as a draftsman from 1953 to 1955. 

Briggs was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in the 2017 Birthday Honours for services to literature. Briggs passed in 2022, but his work has continued to live on. Whether it's through the numerous adaptations on screen or the classic picture books he created, Raymond Briggs' work remains one of the most recognisable British images of our generation.

description:
Rhonda Byrne is an author, TV presenter and producer who is best known for having created The Secret, a documentary film that swept the world in the year 2006, changing millions of lives and igniting a global movement. The following year Rhonda released the book version of The Secret which also went on to become a bestseller, only strengthening the movement. The book was translated into 50 languages and has sold over 28 million copies in print worldwide making it one of the longest-running bestsellers of the century. 

Born and raised in Australia, Rhonda Byrne began her career as a radio producer before she moved to television production. However, towards the end of 2004; Byrne went through traumatic events in her personal and professional life, following which she discovered The Secret that is today her bestselling work. Rhonda's daughter had given her a copy of "The Science of Getting Rich," a book written in 1910 by Wallace D. Wattles. Rhonda says, "Something inside of me had me turn the pages one by one, and I can still remember my tears hitting the pages as I was reading it. It gave me a glimpse of The Secret, and it was like a flame inside of my heart.” 

Rhonda Byrne had discovered a secret—a secret law of attraction and a principle of the universe that can help you realise any dream into reality. Rhonda followed this discovery with extensive research and investigation tracing ‘The Secret’ back through thousands of years, incorporating almost every religion and field of human endeavour throughout history. Rhonda credits this discovery and research for transforming her life as she began to practise her learnings. title: Richard Osman Books

Join us at Books2Door as we celebrate the author, Richard Osman and his works in this collection.

Osman's work combines thrill, suspense, and humour, making his novels accessible and appealing to a broad audience. His characters, particularly the retired detectives, bring a unique perspective to the detective genre. Dive into Osman's world for an experience that's both intellectually stimulating and thoroughly enjoyable.

Thursday Murder Club Series by Richard Osman: A Guide

The Thursday Murder Club

In this engaging debut, a group of spirited pensioners in a Kent retirement village transform into amateur sleuths. The Thursday Murder Club meets weekly to dissect cold cases. Still, they're thrust into action when an actual murder unfolds at their doorstep. They utilise their diverse skills and life experiences to navigate a labyrinth of secrets and lies. The novel's blend of charming characters, witty dialogue, and clever plot twists not only made it the fastest-selling adult crime debut but also garnered widespread critical acclaim.

The Man Who Died Twice

The Bullet That Missed

He is the number one bestselling author of over twenty novels for young readers, particularly due to the success of the Percy Jackson series. Rick Riordan’s books bring ancient Greek and Norse mythology into the lives of his modern-day teenage characters. 

At Books2Door, we aim to highlight and showcase a diverse range of different authors to give you the very best selection of books. Be sure to browse our full Authors page to view our full list of bestselling authors, illustrators and poets. Whether it’s for a loved one or a little one, let us be part of your next story, it’s only one click away.

Biography 

Born in 1964, Richard Russell Riordan Junior is an American author best known for writing the Percy Jackson & the Olympians series. For fifteen years, Riordan taught English and History at middle schools in the San Francisco Bay Area and Texas. He was awarded the school’s first Master Teacher Award by Saint Mary’s Hall while teaching in San Antonio. He now writes full-time in Boston, where he lives with his wife and two sons. 

To date, over 190 million copies of his books are in print worldwide, and rights have been sold in more than 37 countries. Riordan and his wife, Becky, are both executive producers overseeing TV and film adaptations of his works, including Percy Jackson, the Kane Chronicles and Daughter of the Deep. 

Rick Riordan’s most notable works

If you’re not sure where to start, let us help to give you a few handy recommendations to help get you going. One popular and critically acclaimed series you should definitely check out is the Percy Jackson Collection 5 Books Box Set by Rick Riordan. Perfect for kids aged 9-14, the series follows twelve-year-old Percy Jackson, a demigod- half-human and half-god is the son of the Greek God Poseidon. Despite being born with the advantages of a demi-god, growing up has been hard for Percy. Being diagnosed with ADHD and dyslexia, his body and mind are entirely focused on being a fighter, with Ancient Greek blood flowing in his veins, he is yet to find out his historic legacy and the weight of the future that lies on his shoulders. 

After nearly a decade after the release of his last book in the Percy Jackson series, The Blood of Olympus, the golden trio Percy Jackson, Annabeth Chase and Grover Underwood will star in a brand new adventure. Rick Riordan is back with Percy Jackson and the Olympians: The Chalice of the Gods, releasing in September 2023.

Also, be sure to check out the Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard series 3 Books Set by Rick Riordan. This set features the first three books in the popular series, Magnus Chase and the Sword of Summer, Magnus Chase and the Hammer of Thor, and Magnus Chase and the Ship of the Dead. As an orphan, living rough and sleeping rough on the streets of Boston, things are about to get a lot worse for Magnus Chase. Now on the run, Chase reunites with his obnoxious uncle, who casually informs him that his long-lost father is a Norse god. Totally nothing normal about that! As it turns out, the gods of Asgard are preparing for war. If Chase can’t find his father’s sword, which was lost over two thousand years ago, there will be doom- Doomsday, to be precise.
