title: Rick Stein Books
description:
Rick Stein Collection: A Culinary Journey Across Borders

Welcome to the exquisite world of Rick Stein, the acclaimed British chef, restaurateur, and television presenter. Known for his culinary prowess and love for seafood, Stein is also an extraordinary food writer, passionately sharing his adventures from around the globe. In our specially curated collection, you'll find Stein's signature titles. Each book offers something unique— from exploring the heart of traditional cuisines to stirring the soul with personal stories and scrumptious recipes. Find our extensive collection of Cookbooks now available and in stock at Books2Door! 

Rick Stein's India: In Search of the Perfect Curry

Embark on a gastronomic journey across the Indian subcontinent with Rick Stein's India. After realising that his knowledge of Indian cooking was limited to British adaptations, Stein ventured into various Indian cities, from Delhi to Kolkata, seeking the quintessential curry. This is more than a cookbook; it's an authentic adventure packed with stories, impressions, and recipes that reflect India's diverse culinary landscape. What makes Rick Stein's India a standout is its commitment to authenticity, capturing the essence and complexity of Indian flavours in each dish. The book is an invitation to unravel the mystery and beauty of spices, herbs, and rich gravies that are integral to Indian cuisine.

Rick Stein's Secret of France

From India, we shift our focus to the romantic and flavorful landscapes of France. Rick Stein's Secret of France is an epicurean escapade into the lesser-known yet exquisitely delightful aspects of French cooking. While French cuisine is globally celebrated, Stein goes beyond the usual to explore rural kitchens, local markets, and family recipes that have been passed down through generations. Whether it's the perfect coq au vin or a simple, rustic Ratatouille, Stein uncovers the hidden gems of French gastronomy and makes them accessible to you.

Rick Stein: The Road to Mexico

A confluence of rich flavours, vivid colours, and extraordinary cultures, Rick Stein: The Road to Mexico takes you on an exhilarating journey from California down to Mexico. Stein revives the ancient culinary traditions of the region and pairs them with contemporary flair. The book is a feast for the eyes and soul, filled with dishes that are as vibrant as the Mexican culture itself. Expect a wide array of recipes—from comforting street food like Tacos and Quesadillas to complex and luxurious dishes like Mole Poblano.

Rick Stein at Home: Recipes, Memories and Stories from a Food Lover's Kitchen

Completing our collection is the intimately personal Rick Stein at Home: Recipes, Memories and Stories from a Food Lover's Kitchen. This book is an inside look into the chef's own kitchen and soul. Stein shares his cherished family recipes, kitchen techniques, and heartwarming stories that shaped him as a food lover and creator. It's a love letter to home cooking, touching on the simple joys of making food with love for the ones you love.

Why these are must-have cookbooks from Books2Door

Whether you're a home cook, a culinary student, or simply someone who loves devouring delicious narratives along with mouth-watering recipes, this Rick Stein Collection offers something for everyone. These books are not just compilations of recipes; they are travel diaries, historical chronicles, and cultural documentaries rolled into one. They transport you to different parts of the world, allowing you to experience their culinary wonders without leaving your kitchen.

In essence, the Rick Stein book collection is a treasure trove for anyone keen on embarking on a gastronomic journey that traverses boundaries, celebrates diversity, and enriches the soul. Each title is a distinct voyage into the heart of a specific culinary tradition, yet all are unified by Stein's passionate pursuit of authentic, high-quality cooking. Take your taste buds on an unforgettable journey with this exceptional collection.

title: Roald Dahl Books
description:
Roald Dahl is easily one of the most popular authors in the world. One Dahl book is sold every 2.6 seconds across the world and that is not all,he has sold over 300 million copies of his novels and short story collections. Due to their sheer popularity, his books have been translated into 63 different languages. If that isn’t enough to convince you that he is the one author your child deserves to read growing up, then here are some of his many masterpieces to change your mind.

Known for his deliciously quirky evil characters; Roald Dahl’s books often have a mischievous edge. Packed to the brim with fantasy creatures and utopian places, Roald Dahl’s books will ensure your child’s imagination runs wild and takes flight with every new Dahl book they pick up. Also popular as major motion pictures; some of Roald Dahl’s most popular books for kids are Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. The BFG and Matilda. All part of the Books2Door Roald Dahl collection; these books, amongst others, are available as part of the Roald Dahl Collection 16 Books Box Set, perfect for ages 7 to 9.

All of Roald Dahl's Children's Books in Order: 

  • The Gremlins (1943)
  • James and the Giant Peach (1961)
  • Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (1964)
  • The Magic Finger (1966)
  • Fantastic Mr Fox (1968)
  • Charlie and the Great Glass Elevator (1972)
  • Danny, the Champion of the World (1975)
  • The Enormous Crocodile (1978)
  • The Twists (1980) 
  • George's Marvellous Medicine (1981)
  • Revolting Rhymes (1982)
  • The BFG (1982)
  • Dirty Beasts (1983)
  • The Witches (1983)
  • The Giraffe, and the Pelly and Me (1985)
  • Matilda (1988)
  • Rhyme Stew (1989)
  • Esio Trot (1990)
  • The Vicar of Nibbleswicke (1991)
  • The Minpins (1991)

Born to Norwegian parents in Wales in 1916, Roald first started his career as a spy, then worked as a fighter pilot, and even invented medical equipment. Initially, he was best known for his short stories and then in 1961 he shot to fame with James and the Giant Peach and many more brilliant children’s stories like The Twits and George’s Marvellous Medicine. Roald also wrote screenplays, including for classic movies like You Only Live Twice and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, both adapted from Ian Fleming novels. 

Thirty years after his death in 1990, Roald Dahl’s stories are still popular across generations of readers and are still extremely popular amongst children and adults alike. Some have inherited their love of Dahl’s stories from their parents. Others have come to it through other media - his work has been widely adapted into plays, movies, musicals and animation over the years. They’re so popular that in September 2021, Netflix bought the Roald Dahl Story Company, in order to keep bringing his stories to the latest generation of children. The most recent adaptation of Dahl’s work is Matilda the Musical, an adaptation of the long-running West End show, released on 25th November 2022.

Roald Dahl is also well-regarded as a writer of macabre short stories for adults. Originally published in magazines including The New Yorker and Playboy, they’re best known from collections like Kiss Kiss and Someone Like You. Many were adapted for the classic TV series Tales of the Unexpected. They’re available in eight beautifully designed themed collections.

However, even after all these years, Roald Dahl is still best known as one of the most beloved British children’s authors. His books (The Witches, Fantastic Mr Fox), short books (The Enormous Crocodile) and poetry (Revolting Rhymes) are funny, mischievous, and filled with joyfully inventive language. All of these books have been illustrated by the iconic Quentin Blake, the first Children’s Laureate. His illustrations tend to capture the spiky and subversive side of Roald’s work so well; they have become inseparable from the books. 

One common theme amongst many Roald Dahl’s stories is a young child seeking revenge on evil adults and wrongdoers. Dahl has invented more than 500 memorable words and character names across his work, such as Oompa-Loompa, scrumdiddlyumptious, snozzcumbers and frobscottle. Another interesting (lesser-known) fact about Roald Dahl is that he named his fantasy language Gobblefunk. The Oxford University Press even created a unique Roald Dahl Dictionary, which featured nearly 8000 words he used in his stories.

Many of Roald Dahl’s ideas were inspired by his childhood days and later experience. For example, in his autobiographical book Boy, Dahl says his school used to taste-test Cadbury’s chocolate. This led to the invention of the famous Willy Wonka and his chocolate factory. He also wrote about his experiences in the war, including in the book Going Solo. These years also inspired Dahl’s first book, The Gremlins. Pilots used to describe the malfunctions in their planes as little folkloric creatures causing havoc. These creatures made it into his first two novels, both published in the 40s, and an aborted Disney film.

Need we go on about the works and books of Roald Dahl and why your child stands to benefit from his books at any age? Simply head to our Roald Dahl Collection or browse through our bestsellers category for more of his classics and unique titles. We also stock a 16 book collection of Roald Dahl’s classic children books, a box set of 16 Roald Dahl audiobooks and 7 plays adapted from Roald Dahl stories.

Perfect for little playwrights; Roald Dahl The Plays is a bookset of 7 books for kids aged 7+. A fabulous set of seven plays, adapted from the works of Roald Dahl; this set will introduce the world of theatre to young minds. They will love reading scripts aloud to family and friends; maybe whilst also enacting them as skits and plays.

If you are only just trying to get your kid started on reading and you are having a tough time getting them to read their way into the world of Dahl, then you can get them started on these 16 Roald Dahl audiobooks. The set includes Roald Dahl’s autobiography Boy and shorter stories including Billy and The Minpins and The Giraffe and the Pelly and Me. All of the stories are read by big-name celebrities and actors including Hugh Laurie, Kate Winslet and David Walliams. Please check your CD player is MP3 accessible before placing an order. To listen to the audio, import into iTunes or any other media player, then transfer to your MP3 device or player. Suitable for smartphones, iPads and tablets.

title: Robert Muchamore Books
description:
Born in Islington, London in the early 70s; Robert Muchamore has emerged as a pioneering British author of Young Adult fiction. Muchamore famously worked as a private investigator up until 2005 after which he shot to fame as a YA fiction writer. Trivia has it that Robert was inspired by his nephew to create the CHERUB book series. Robert’s nephew complained about the lack of material for him and his age group to read. Which is what led to the Cherub series.

In this collection therefore, we have curated the best works of Robert Muchamore that we think every pre-teen and young adult will enjoy…

Cherub Series 1 Collection 5 Books Set (Books 1-5) By Robert Muchamore This Collection Set is a captivating and thrilling series that follows the adventures of young spies in training. Written by bestselling author Robert Muchamore, this set includes the first five books in the series, making it the perfect introduction to the world of Cherub by Robert Muchamore.

The Recruit, book one in the set; was also Robert' s very first book and it managed to win the Red House Children's Book Award in 2005. The book introduces readers to James, a 12-year-old boy who is recruited into Cherub - a secret organisation that trains children to become spies. James is sent on a dangerous mission to infiltrate a criminal organisation, and readers are taken along for the ride as he learns the skills he needs to survive.

Throughout the series, Muchamore does an excellent job of creating a world that is both believable and exciting. His characters are well-drawn and realistic, and readers will find themselves rooting for James and his fellow agents as they face danger at every turn. One of the things that set the Cherub series apart from other young adult spy novels is the way that Muchamore handles the violence. 

While there are certainly moments of intense action and danger, Muchamore never shies away from the fact that violence has consequences. His characters feel the weight of their actions, and the consequences of their choices are always front and centre. Another strength of the series is Muchamore's ability to balance the action and adventure with more introspective moments. James and his fellow agents are all dealing with personal issues and struggles, and Muchamore does an excellent job of exploring those in a way that feels natural and organic to the story.

The Henderson's Boys series is another one of the many popular works of Muchamore. A series of young adult spy novels, the books follow Charles Henderson, the creator of the fictitious CHERUB organisation. The protagonist, James, has to bust an inmate out of a high-security US prison. Over the years, CHERUB has put plenty of criminals behind bars. Now, for the first time ever, they've got to break one out. 

Under American law, kids convicted of serious crimes can be sentenced as adults. Two hundred and eighty of these child criminals live in the sunbaked desert prison of Arizona Max. In one of the most dangerous CHERUB missions ever, James Adams has to go undercover inside Arizona Max, befriend an inmate and then bust him out. CHERUB kids are trained professionals, working in everyday situations. Their essential advantage: adults never suspect that children are spying on them. For official purposes, these children do not exist.

title: Robin Hobb Books
description:
Robin Hobb is the pen name for acclaimed author Margaret Astrid Lindholm Ogden. She is best known for her fantasy novels with intricate world-building, complex characters, and vivid storytelling that will keep you hooked from the first page to the last.

Whether you're a longtime fan of fantasy or just looking for a new series to get lost in, Robin Hobb's books are definitely worth checking out. Her books are widely recognised as some of the best in the genre and have earned her a loyal following of fans around the world. Many of her books take place in the same world and feature interconnected characters and storylines.

Read below to find out more about her most famous series, Realm of the Elderlings, and other books by Robin Hobb.

Realm of the Elderlings books in order

The Realm of the Elderlings is a series of 16 books. It consists of multiple trilogies and a tetralogy, each set in different parts of the world. The first book, Assassin's Apprentice, was published in 1995, and the series concluded in 2017 with the final novel Assassin's Fate.

The Farseer Trilogy:

The Farseer Trilogy is the first series written by Robin Hobb and a great place to start reading her books. This trilogy follows the life of FitzChivalry Farseer, a royal bastard who is trained as an assassin in the service of the ruling family. Set in a richly imagined world of magic, intrigue, and political power plays, this series is a must-read for any fan of epic fantasy.

The Liveship Traders Trilogy:

The Liveship Traders Trilogy is set in the same world as the Farseer Trilogy but with a different cast of characters and a new storyline. This series takes place in the city of Bingtown, a bustling port city where liveships, vessels made of wizardwood that come alive and gain magical powers, are the ultimate luxury. The story follows the Vestrit family, who own a liveship called the Vivacia and are caught up in a complex web of family secrets, political machinations, and mystical forces.

The Tawny Man Trilogy:

The Tawny Man Trilogy is a direct sequel to the Farseer Trilogy, and follows FitzChivalry Farseer as he returns from his self-imposed exile and embarks on a new adventure. This series brings back many of the beloved characters from the first trilogy and delves deeper into the world of the Six Duchies, where the fate of the kingdom is once again at stake.

The Rain Wild Chronicles:

The Rain Wild Chronicles is a four-book series set in the same world as the Farseer and Liveship Traders trilogies but with a different focus. This series takes place in the Rain Wilds, a region of the world known for its dangerous, mutated wildlife, and follows a group of dragon keepers as they journey up the treacherous Rain Wild River to try and find a new home for their charges. The Rain Wild Chronicles is a must-read for anyone who loves dragons and adventure.

The Fitz and the Fool Trilogy:

The Fitz and the Fool Trilogy is the final trilogy in the long-running Realm of the Elderlings series, which encompasses all of the previous series mentioned above. This series brings back FitzChivalry Farseer and his beloved companion, the Fool, for one last adventure. It is a fitting conclusion to a sprawling and epic fantasy series and is sure to satisfy fans of Robin Hobb's work.

More books by Robin Hobb

The Soldier Son Trilogy is set in a world where magic exists and follows the life of a young man named Nevare Burvelle, the second son of a noble family who is trained as a soldier. As he grows up, Nevare begins to realize that his destiny may be different from what he expected, as he becomes embroiled in a conflict between the local tribes and the colonisers from his own country.

The trilogy explores themes of identity, tradition, and power, as Nevare navigates his way through a world that is rapidly changing around him. Along the way, he must confront his own personal demons and grapple with the consequences of his choices, as he strives to find his place in a world that seems to have no clear answers.

What should I read next?

For fans of high fantasy and incredibly intricate world-building, check out our collection of Game of Thrones Books! Welcome to Westeros, where you will face a cruel and violent battle between families for the throne. George R.R. Martin’s fantasy epic is arguably one of the most iconic and influential since J R.R. Tolkien’s Lord of the Rings series.

title: Robin Stevens
description:
The Detective Society Is Now in Session: The Robin Stevens Collection

Detective work isn't just for the adults; sometimes, it requires a sharp eye and a Deepdean uniform. The Robin Stevens book collection has single-handedly revitalised the "Golden Age" mystery for a new generation. Best known for the global phenomenon that is the Murder Most Unladylike series, Stevens blends the atmospheric charm of 1930s England with high-stakes "whodunnit" puzzles. For readers aged 9-14 who crave logic, biscuits, and a dash of genuine danger, these novels are the definitive choice for a Middle-Grade mystery binge.

1. The Wells & Wong Mysteries: A Masterclass in Deduction

At the heart of the collection is the iconic Murder Most Unladylike 9 Books Collection Set. This series introduced the world to Daisy Wells and Hazel Wong: two boarders at Deepdean School for Girls who form a secret Detective Society to solve the crimes the adults refuse to acknowledge.

  • A Perfect Partnership: Daisy is the brilliant, albeit slightly reckless, social leader, while Hazel is the meticulous chronicler and the emotional core of the series. Their dynamic explores deep themes of friendship and identity, especially as Hazel navigates 1930s Britain as an immigrant from Hong Kong.

  • Classic Influences: Think Agatha Christie meets Malory Towers. From the snowy rails of the Orient Express in First Class Murder to the misty hills of her homeland in A Spoonful of Murder, the settings are as much a character as the detectives themselves.

2. The Legacy of Unladylike Detection

Robin Stevens didn't stop at Deepdean. Her universe continues to expand, proving that the demand for smart, diverse, and well-plotted mysteries is stronger than ever.

  • The Ministry of Unladylike Detection: Set during the height of World War II, this new chapter introduces a new generation of spies and sleuths. It’s a perfect "next step" for fans who have finished the original series and are looking for a more political, high-stakes atmosphere.

  • Fiction Box Sets for Teens: For those transitioning into Young Adult fiction, Stevens’ work serves as an essential bridge, offering complex plots that never "talk down" to the reader or simplify the darker aspects of history.

3. Why Robin Stevens is Essential for Your Bookshelf

What sets Stevens apart from the "standard" mystery writer is her commitment to inclusivity and historical accuracy.

  • Representation Matters: By placing Hazel Wong, a character of color; at the center of a historical mystery, Stevens has opened the genre to a wider audience, making these ESEA-themed stories both culturally significant and immensely popular.

  • Logical Puzzles: These aren't stories where the answer is pulled out of a hat in the final chapter. Every clue is laid out for the reader to find, encouraging critical thinking, observational skills, and a love for structured narrative.

title: Robot Books 🤖

Raging robots, cuddly cyborgs, killer AI- whatever you’re looking for, we’re guaranteed to have just the right book for you. Ages 0-5

This three-book collection set contains the coolest Robot Books around. Meet five cool robots in this fun addition to the much-loved That’s Not My…series. Perfect for babies and toddlers, these sensory books contain bold illustrations, patches to stroke and hidden animals to spot on every page, all designed to develop sensory and language awareness. 

Ages 7-9

For slightly older children, we have an excellent selection of books to choose from. Check out The Wild Robot by Peter Brown. Say hello to your new favourite robot, Roz. After a hurricane’s brutal wind and lashing rain sink a cargo ship loaded with hundreds of crates, one washed up to Wild Rock Island. Call it fate or destiny, some playful otters stumble upon the broken box and -click!- they activate Roz. In the aftermath of the crash, Roz discovers a single egg signalling the start of a bond between the robot and the surviving gosling. With short chapters for easy reading, this enchanting tale explores many important themes of empathy in a heartwarming story of what happens when nature and technology collide. 

If it’s killer robots that your little ones are after, you have to check out the Five Nights at Freddy’s Fazbear Frights 4 Books Boxed Set by Scott Cawthon. This collection features four volumes, each with three frightening short stories, integrating characters from well-loved survival horror franchises. Readers familiar with the well-loved video game will meet familiar fan-favourite characters in a new twist of terrifying tales. Join a host of new characters as they all navigate through the trials and tribulations of childhood and learn the hard way that in the world of Five Nights at Freddy’s, it’s always in the depth of loneliness where evil creeps in and attracts hungry monsters. 

Teens and YA

For those older teens looking to delve into some of the robot classics, look no further than the works of Isaac Asimov- considered one of the fathers of robotics. His 1950’s I, Robot Series is one of the most influential science fiction books ever published. Combining nine short stories with a framing narrative, it introduced the famous Three Laws of Robotics to the world. However, after some initial years of helping his father with his Laundry business, Roger did succeed in becoming the Creative Director of an advertising firm in London. Following which he also managed to fulfil his illustrator dreams with his first book Mr. Tickle (1971)that went on to grow into a bestselling series called Mr. Men.

Hargreaves has famously said; the inspiration for his first book of ‘Mr. Men’ series called Mr. Tickle was an innocent question his son Adam Hargreaves had asked—‘What does a tickle look like?’ As an answer to which Roger drew a figure in orange colour with floppy arms and round body to represent a tickle. 

Now a popular children’s bestseller, the Mr. Men series includes Mr. Greedy, Mr. Nosey, Mr. Happy, Mr. Sneeze among 44 other books. The stories of these books are simple and illustrated in brightly coloured pictures. These books by Roger Hargreaves became instant hits selling more than a million copies within 3 years. In 1981 Hargreaves’s book ‘Little Miss’ was introduced. It consisted of 33 books. Books in this series include Little Miss Bossy and the renowned Little Miss Naughty.

After his untimely death in the year 1988, Roger Hargreaves’s son Adam Hargreaves—also an author—took over the Mr. Men and Little Miss characters in new stories. Even after all these years of his passing, Hargreaves is still one of the bestselling children’s authors. His work is a timeless classic that still continues to bring joy and laughter to children starting out their reading adventure. Not just the books, his potato styled simple character designs have also created more than 700 merchandise products. 

Given their popularity with little readers, we think, every child’s bookshelf deserves Mr. Men and Little Miss books.

title: Role-playing, War Games & Fantasy Sports Books
description:
Role-playing books are a unique and exciting way to experience storytelling. Unlike traditional novels, role-playing books put you in control of the story, allowing you to make decisions and shape the outcome. Fighting Fantasy RPG books and The Lone Wolf series by Joe Dever are two examples of role-playing books that have captured the imaginations of readers for decades. 

What are Role Playing Games (RPG)? 

Before we continue, it is important to understand what RPG actually means. RPG stands for "role-playing game." In the context of gaming, an RPG is a game in which the player takes on the role of a character in a fictional world. The player is responsible for making decisions for their character, such as what actions to take and how to interact with other characters in the game. In an RPG, the player's choices often determine the outcome of the game's story. For example, if the player chooses to help a certain character or complete a certain quest, it may affect the events that happen later in the game. This allows the player to have a personalized experience and creates a sense of immersion in the game world.

Role-playing games can take many forms, including video games, tabletop games, and books. In video games, the player interacts with the game world through a digital interface. Tabletop games involve players sitting around a table and using physical game pieces to represent their characters and the game world. RPG books, as mentioned in the previous answer, allow readers to create a character and make decisions that determine the outcome of the story.

Fighting Fantasy

The Fighting Fantasy RPG books were created by Steve Jackson and Ian Livingstone in the 1980s. The books were a response to the popularity of role-playing games like Dungeons & Dragons, but they were designed to be played solo. Each book in the series takes the reader on a different adventure, allowing them to create a character and make choices that determine the outcome of the story. The books are known for their detailed illustrations, inventive monsters, and challenging gameplay.

One of the key features of Fighting Fantasy RPG books is the use of dice to determine the outcome of battles and other encounters. The reader is required to keep track of their character's health, equipment, and abilities, and to roll dice to determine the success of attacks and other actions. This adds an element of chance to the game, making each playthrough unique. Here at Books2Door, we have some fantastic fighting fantasy book sets for you to get your teeth stuck into. For starters check out our Fighting Fantasy RPG books 1-5. Continuing with the series, you should then check out our Fighting Fantasy RPG books 6-15! 

The Lone Wolf

The Lone Wolf series by Joe Dever is another popular series of role-playing books. Unlike the Fighting Fantasy RPG books, the Lone Wolf series features a continuous story that spans over a dozen books. The books follow the adventures of Lone Wolf, a warrior monk who must protect his kingdom from the forces of evil. The reader creates a character that joins Lone Wolf on his journey, making decisions that determine the outcome of battles and other encounters.

One of the unique features of the Lone Wolf series is the use of a character sheet to keep track of the reader's progress. The sheet includes information on the reader's character's abilities, equipment, and health, and is used to determine the success of attacks and other actions. The series also features a complex combat system that allows the reader to use a variety of strategies to defeat their enemies. Buy your copy of The Lone Wolf series here, Lone Wolf series books 1-5 set. 

Both the Fighting Fantasy RPG books and the Lone Wolf series offer unique and exciting ways to experience storytelling. The use of dice and character sheets adds an element of chance to the gameplay, making each playthrough unique. The books are also known for their intricate world-building and detailed illustrations, which add to the immersive experience.

One of the benefits of role-playing books is the ability to customise the experience. Players can choose to play as different characters, use different equipment, and make different choices, allowing for endless possibilities. The books also encourage creativity and problem-solving skills, as players must use their wits to overcome challenges and defeat enemies. There has been an increase in the popularity of role-playing games such as Fighting Fantasy and Dungeons and Dragons. Make sure you check out our Dungeon Academy Series by Madeleine Roux 2 Books Collection. 

Another benefit of role-playing books is the social aspect. While Fighting Fantasy RPG books and the Lone Wolf series are designed to be played solo, players can share their experiences with others and compare their progress. This can lead to discussions about strategy and tactics, as well as friendly competition.

Fighting Fantasy RPG books and the Lone Wolf series by Joe Dever are two examples of role-playing books that have stood the test of time. The use of dice and character sheets adds an element of chance to the gameplay, making each playthrough unique. The books also offer intricate world-building, detailed illustrations, and challenging gameplay. Role-playing books encourage creativity and problem-solving skills and can be enjoyed solo or with friends. If you're looking for a unique and immersive storytelling experience, give role-playing books a try.

title: Sally Rooney Books
description:
Sally Rooney is a bestselling fiction writer from Ireland. She has written three published novels: Conversations with Friends (2017), Normal People (2018), and Beautiful World, Where Are You (2021), and one novella, Mr Salary. Two of her books have been made into critically acclaimed television series. The first to hit the screen was Normal People starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Paul Mescal. It was released in 2020 as a 12-part series and was a co-production of BBC Three. In 2022, the same production company released her novel Conversations with Friends into a 12-episode miniseries. Her work is deemed a commercial success by her multiple bestsellers. Rooney is even regarded as one of the foremost millennial writers.

Before watching the highly acclaimed television series, check out the Sally Rooney Collection 4 Books Set Paperback/ Hardback. With all four books in this handy and affordable collection, all for under £25, this makes for the perfect gift for any Sally Rooney fan. This collection contains three novels and even her short story, Mr Salary. 

Conversations with Friends

Considered to be a novel about the harshness of friendship, lust, and jealousy intertwined with the complications o

f adulthood, Conversations with Friends is Rooney’s first published novel. This novel is divided into two books following the story of two college friends and ex-lovers, Frances and Bobbi, who perform spoken-word poetry together. The pair meet and befriend a married couple in their thirties, Nick and Melissa. Over the course of the following few months, as the duos spend more time together, Frances and Nick begin to develop an interest in each other, while Melissa and Bobbi are more drawn to each other. 

Normal People

Rooney has quickly become the face of millennial authors. Her novels all portray a feeling of love, insecurity, identity and class. These themes are present throughout her bestselling novel, Normal People, seeing Marianne and Connell try to fight their feelings for each other whilst coming to terms with their own demons that they are refusing to address. Marianne and Connell grow up in the same small town in the west of Ireland, but that’s all they have in common. In school, Connell is popular and well-liked. In contrast, Marianne is a loner. Their on-again-off-again relationship over time is complicated by their social and socio-economic divisions, exploring the subtlety of class, the electricity of first love and the complex (and often complicated) entanglement of family and friendship. 

Beautiful World, Where Are You

Beautiful World, Where Are You is a question that is deliberated by the two female

protagonists of the novel. Best friends and now on the cusp of thirty, the pair repeatedly grapple with their struggles in figuring out the life they want to live and how to find meaning in a troubled world. The novel centres around four people- Alice, Felix, Eileen and Simon- who live their mundane millennial lives in Ireland against the backdrop of the complications of living and loving in the 21st century. 

About the Author 

Born in 1991 in Ireland, Sally Rooney is an Irish author and Screenwriter. She is considered the best young writer of her generation and possesses an incredible talent for capturing raw emotion within her novels. She was even an executive producer and writer for the screen adaptations of Conversation with Friends and Normal people. Rooney has won many awards and accolades for her work, most notably, she won Costa Book of the Year in 2018 and British Book of the year in 2019 for Normal People.

With 14 distinct imprints to their credit—AFK, Cartwheel Books®, Chicken House®, Graphix™, Orchard Books®, Point™, PUSH, Scholastic en español, Scholastic Audio, Scholastic Focus, Scholastic Inc., Scholastic Press, Scholastic Reference™, and Klutz®—Scholastic is the largest publisher of children's books in the world.

title: Sharpe Books
description:
Follow Richard Sharpe from a private serving in India for the British Army, to a staff officer at the Battle of Waterloo, in this epic historical fiction series from Bernard Cornwell (The Last Kingdom). His inspiration was the Hornblower series by C.S. Forester, and he wanted to make an equivalent for the British Army. The character was made famous by Sean Bean in the acclaimed 90s TV series.

The Sharpe books in order

The Prequels: India, Trafalgar & the Siege of Copenhagen, 1799-1807

  1. Sharpe's Tiger
  2. Sharpe's Triumph
  3. Sharpe's Fortress
  4. Sharpe's Trafalgar
  5. Sharpe's Prey

The Peninsular War, 1809-1813

  1. Sharpe's Rifles
  2. Sharpe's Havoc
  3. Sharpe's Eagle
  4. Sharpe's Gold
  5. Sharpe's Escape
  6. Sharpe's Fury
  7. Sharpe's Battle
  8. Sharpe's Company
  9. Sharpe's Command
  10. Sharpe's Sword
  11. Sharpe's Enemy
  12. Sharpe's Honour
  13. Sharpe's Regiment
    Sharpe's Storm     (forthcoming)

1814 and Beyond: France, Waterloo & Napoleon

  1. Sharpe's Siege
  2. Sharpe's Revenge
  3. Sharpe's Waterloo
  4. Sharpe's Assassin
  5. Sharpe's Devil

What order should I read the Sharpe books?

The first Sharpe novel was published in 1981, and since then it has grown to a 22-book series, stretching across more than two decades of history. The Sharpe books have now been republished in their chronological order, making it easier than ever to follow Sharpe's adventures through Portugal, Spain, and beyond. However, the books were written out of sequence, as you will see below.

Sharpe's first published adventure was Sharpe's Eagle, which took place during the Talavera campaign in July 1809. Cornwell originally planned to only write eleven novels, matching Forester, and achieved this with Sharpe's Waterloo in 1990 by publishing a new book every year. The series followed chronologically from Eagle, covering the period between 1809 and 1815, except for Sharpe's Rifles which was a prequel, and is Sharpe's first adventure on the Iberian Peninsula.

However, Sharpe wasn't done with his creator yet. A twelfth novel, Sharpe's Devil, was published in 1992, and picked up the story five years after the Battle of Waterloo, with Sharpe encountering the exiled Napoleon. The TV series began in 1993, adapting the first eleven books along with two original stories. During this time a brand new novel Sharpe's Battle was published, and was filmed the same year (1995).

The final episode of the TV series was released in 1997, as was the first of five prequels to the original series published over five years. The first three follow Sharpe's campaign in India, from 1799 to 1803, and feature the young private a decade before his most famous adventures. The fourth book detailed his involvement in Trafalgar in 1805, and the fifth his actions at the Siege of Copenhagen in 1807. You can read these books first, or you can start with Sharpe's Rifles and come back to them later.

Three further books were published between 2003 and 2006, all set between other novels in the series. After these three books, Cornwell's attention turned to the Saxon Stories. The first of these was published in 2004, and they were later filmed as The Last Kingdom. The Sharpe TV series returned for two final adventures in 2006 and 2008, loosely adapting the Indian trilogy.

The Sharpe book series made a surprise return in 2021 with its 22nd full-length novel, Sharpe's Assassin, set immediately after the events in Sharpe's Waterloo. Sharpe's Command is forthcoming, and is set in 1812 after the events of Sharpe's Sword.

With that in mind, some fantastic books explore the known facts about space and the universe. There is still so much we do not know, with technologies advancing every day, which allows us to learn even more of the vast unknown. Hawking discussed fundamental topics like space and time and critical cosmological theories like general relativity and quantum mechanics. Ever thought about the fact that right now, we are orbiting a black hole? Peake is a British astronaut who went into space in 2015, but before this, he was an Apache pilot, flight instructor and test pilot for the army. This fantastic autobiography explores what life in space is really like and recalls how he felt when he was up there.

description:

Lift a flap, spark a memory, and find a lifelong friend. Since 1980, the Spot the Dog series has been the gold standard for early childhood reading. The Magic of the "Lift-the-Flap" Experience

What started with the classic Where’s Spot? became a masterclass in tactile discovery. Eric Hill understood that for a child, reading is a physical act. By incorporating interactive flaps, these books transform passive listening into an active game of hide-and-seek.

A Masterclass in Visual Simplicity

Eric Hill’s art style is instantly recognisable: bold outlines, vibrant primary colours, and plenty of white space. This isn't just an aesthetic choice—it’s a developmental one. For very young readers, busy backgrounds can be overwhelming. Spot’s world is clean and focused, allowing children to zero in on the emotional expressions of the characters and the core objects being taught—be it a red ball, a green tractor, or a blue birthday present.

More Than Just a Puppy: Educational Milestones

While Spot's adventures feel like pure play, they are stealthily educational. Each book serves as a foundational building block for early years development:

title: Stephen King Books
description:
Stephen King: Multi-genre Writer 

Stephen King is a household name and world-famous author. His career spans over 40 years, with his first book published in 1974. King is a master of horror and thriller books. He has released many bestselling books and has been awarded numerous literary awards. 

King has transcended different genres and has created iconic characters and storylines that will be cherished for many years to come. He is most famous for his horror writing, but he has also written epic fantasy series like The Dark Tower and crime thrillers like The Bill Hodges Trilogy, which includes Mr Mercades, Finders Keepers and End of Watch. We also have Stephen King 4 Books Collection Set, which contains some of his more recent publications, The Bazaar of Bad Dreams, The Institute, The Outsider and Elevation. 

The Shining, published in 1977, tells the story of the Torrance family, who move to the isolated Overlook Hotel to act as caretakers during the winter season. The young son, Danny, has psychic abilities that allow him to see the hotel's dark and violent history. As the winter progresses, the hotel's supernatural powers begin to take hold of the family, leading to a terrifying climax. The Shining is a masterpiece of horror fiction that combines psychological suspense with supernatural terror. King's skilful character development and vivid descriptions of the hotel's eerie atmosphere make this book a must-read for any horror fan.

Doctor Sleep, published in 2013, is the sequel to The Shining and follows an adult Danny, who now goes by Dan, as he battles alcoholism and tries to come to terms with his psychic abilities. Dan works at a hospice, using his powers to help dying patients pass peacefully into the afterlife. However, he soon becomes entangled with a group of psychic vampires called the True Knot, who feed on children with special powers. Dan must confront his past and use his abilities to protect a young girl with extraordinary abilities from the True Knot. Doctor Sleep is a gripping and chilling sequel that stands on its own as a great horror novel.

Cujo, published in 1981, tells the story of a friendly St. Bernard who becomes infected with rabies and goes on a killing spree. The book is set in the small town of Castle Rock, Maine, and explores the lives of the people who are affected by Cujo's rampage. Cujo is a tense and terrifying novel that shows how even the most innocent creatures can become monsters under the right circumstances.

Salem's Lot, published in 1975, is a vampire story that takes place in the small town of Jerusalem's Lot, Maine. The book follows the arrival of an enigmatic stranger named Kurt Barlow, who moves into a long-abandoned mansion and begins to spread his vampiric influence throughout the town. Salems Lot is a slow-burning horror novel that builds tension and dread as the town's residents slowly succumb to Barlow's power. King's vivid descriptions of the town's dark and eerie atmosphere make Salem's Lot a classic of the horror genre.

One of the reasons King's books are so effective at evoking fear is his ability to create fully-realised characters that readers can empathize with and care about. The horror in his books often comes not just from supernatural threats but also from the characters' own flaws and weaknesses. For example, in The Shining, Jack Torrance's descent into madness is not just a result of the hotel's supernatural influence but also of his own struggles with alcoholism and anger. In Cujo, the horror comes not just from the rabid dog but also from the strained relationships and infidelities of the human characters.

Another reason King's books are so effective at evoking fear is his skill at creating vivid and unsettling settings. Whether it's the haunted Overlook Hotel in The Shining or the vampire-infested town of Jerusalem's Lot in Salems Lot, King's descriptions of these places are so detailed and vivid that they become characters in their own right. The settings are often isolated and claustrophobic, heightening the sense of dread and unease.

Overall, Stephen King's The Shining, Doctor Sleep, Cujo, and Salems Lot are classic examples of horror fiction. King's ability to create fully-realised characters, vivid and unsettling settings, and a sense of inevitability make his books incredibly effective at evoking fear and suspense. His use of symbolism and metaphor adds depth and complexity to his horror novels, elevating them beyond simple scare stories. If you're a fan of horror fiction, these books are a must-read. Don’t miss out on our fantastic Stephen King 5 book set, featuring The Shining, Doctor Sleep, Cujo, Salems Lot and Firestarter. 

For fans of Stephen King, check out other suspenseful authors like Alex Michaelides and his debut novel The Silent Patient or The Burning Girls by British author C. J. Tudor. We also have a full range of Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror available for you to browse. 

As Seen on Screen 

Stephen King's books have been adapted into at least fifty movies over the years. The most famous include Carrie, The Shining, IT, Salem's Lot, The Green Mile, Stand by me, Misery, and so many more. Many of his books, like IT and Carrie, have science fiction elements, making the real-life elements within them seem more shocking. An example is Carrie's explosion of her supernatural power after years of built-up rage bought on by cruel school bullies and the abuse she receives from her mother. 

Take a look at our Stephen King Movies Collection 4 Books Set that contains IT, Pet Sematary, The Shining and Doctor Sleep. This collection is perfect for anyone starting to get into Stephen King books or ideal for an avid Stephen King fan wanting to expand their collection. 

King's work has been adapted into graphic novels and even plays. In 1988, a musical of Carrie was shown on Broadway; it was initially not received well but, in 2012, had a resurgence. Since then, roughly seven adaptations of his works have been turned into plays or musicals; this includes The Body (also known as Stand by Me), Misery and Shawshank Redemption. 

As well as plays, many songs have been released based on Stephen King's books from artists such as The Ramones, Slipknot and Maroon 5. 

About the Author

Born in Portland, Maine, King is an American author of horror, supernatural fiction, suspense, crime, science-fiction, and fantasy novels. Many of King's books are set in Maine or a fictional town in Maine, which transports the reader into his world. 

He was a fan of horror books from a young age, stating that as a child, he read a collection of H. P. Lovecraft's short stories and horror comics, such as Tales From the Crypt, which would go on to inspire his work. King continues to release books, his most recent being Fairy Tale, published in late 2022.

title: Studio Ghibli Books
description:
Studio Ghibli is one of the leading Japanese animation studios. It’s wildly popular amongst children and adults alike for its iconic art style and filmmaking prowess. The movies of Hayao Miyazaki, Isao Takahata, and others are beloved across several age groups and have a substantial fan base across the world.

If you too are a Ghibli fan that is interested in the trivia about the films, the books and the overall franchise that is Studio Ghibli (the complete works)—then we have just the collection for you. As fans of the studio ourselves, we at Books2Door have curated a great collection of books published as part of the Studio Ghibli Library from Viz Media. This includes art books from their blockbuster movies like Spirited Away and Princess Mononoke. On this page you’ll find the original manga of Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind by Miyazaki, which he adapted into the iconic anime. This collection also features the novels behind Ghibli classics such as Howl's Moving Castle, amongst others. It also includes books the founders adapted in their pre-Ghibli careers, like Anne of Green Gables and Heidi.

If you are anything like us—a fan and a collector, then you know nothing beats the fulfilment of owning the best studio Ghibli books and all their various editions. Here are some books that we know will interest you…

My Neighbour Totoro The Novel Not only is this beloved Ghibli classic a popular anime film, but it is now also a children’s novel. In celebration of the 25th anniversary of this classic film, Hayao Miyazaki along with the veteran children’s author Tsugiko Kubo created the novel version of My Neighbour Totoro. The novel also features original illustrations by Miyazaki himself.

A delight for both existing fans and new readers; the novel, just like the film, also follows the story of the eleven-year-old Satsuki and her sassy little sister Mei. As the girls move to a new country home with their father; (to be closer to their ailing mother) they discover Totoro. Totoro is a magical forest spirit who takes the girls on several adventures whilst also teaching them a few life lessons along the way.

Whilst the novel is an exact adaptation of the film; it still makes great reading material for children. The illustrations, the children's protagonists, their adventures, and their fragile relationships—all make it a perfect reading experience for your kids. Also, the novel and the memorabilia about the film are a great way to introduce your kids to Studio Ghibli movies and the franchise at large.

Ghibliotheque: The Unofficial Guide to the Movies of Studio Ghibli by Michael Leader A complete and essential guide loaded with trivia about the magical world of Studio Ghibli movies—this book is a collector’s edition. Adapted from the acclaimed podcast, Ghibliotheque offers highly-informed insights and critiques of some of the greatest animated movies by the studio, including Spirited Away, My Neighbour Totoro, and Princess Mononoke. From Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind to Earwig and the Witch—authors Michael Leader and Jake Cunningham review every Studio Ghibli feature film, providing insightful background information on how the films were made. Beautifully illustrated with stills and posters, portraits of the creative team and the Studio itself; this is a comprehensive, engaging guide and trivia bible to the wonderfully complex, mysterious, and entertaining worlds of the legendary, Oscar-winning animation studio—Studio Ghibli. 

Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind by Hayao Miyazaki is an epic fantasy tale written and illustrated by the legendary Studio Ghibli director Hayao Miyazaki. A modern masterpiece, this set is the story of Nausicaa, a princess of a small kingdom. Set far in the future, after an apocalyptic conflict has devastated much of the world's ecosystem, the few surviving humans live in scattered semi-hospitable environments within what has become a "toxic jungle." Young Nausicaä lives in the arid Valley of the Wind and can communicate with the massive insects that populate the dangerous jungle. Under the guidance of the pensive veteran warrior, Lord Yupa, Nausicaä works to bring peace back to the ravaged planet.

title: Suzanne Collins Books
description:
Suzanne Collins is a renowned American author, best known for her young adult dystopian novel series, The Hunger Games. Collins' books have been translated into over 50 languages, sold over 100 million copies worldwide, and have been adapted into blockbuster films, making her one of the most influential and successful writers of our time.

Born on August 10, 1962, in Hartford, Connecticut, Collins grew up in the military, following her father's career as a U.S. Air Force officer. Her childhood experiences travelling with her family to different countries greatly influenced her later works, particularly in terms of exploring themes of war, power, and survival.

Collins attended Indiana University and studied theatre and telecommunications, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1985. She then pursued a career in writing, working on a variety of children's television shows, including The Mystery Files of Shelby Woo and Clifford's Puppy Days.

Collins' literary career began in 2003 with her debut novel, Gregor the Overlander, a middle-grade fantasy series. The book follows the adventures of a young boy named Gregor, who falls through a grate in his laundry room and discovers a magical underworld full of giant rats, bats, and cockroaches. The series comprises five books and was praised for its unique world-building, captivating characters, and compelling narrative.

However, it was Collins' Hunger Games series that brought her international recognition and catapulted her into the limelight. The Hunger Games is a dystopian young adult series set in the future in the ruins of North America, now known as Panem, which is controlled by a totalitarian government located in the Capitol.

The books follow the story of Katniss Everdeen, a young girl from the impoverished District 12, who is forced to participate in the annual Hunger Games, a televised event where 24 teenagers, known as tributes, fight to the death in a controlled arena. The series explores themes such as inequality, power, propaganda, and the effects of war on individuals and society.

The first book of the trilogy, The Hunger Games, was published in 2008, and it quickly became a global phenomenon, spending over 260 consecutive weeks on the New York Times Bestseller List. It has been adapted into a successful movie franchise starring Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss, which has grossed over $3 billion worldwide.

The subsequent books, Catching Fire and Mockingjay continued to dominate the bestseller lists, with Mockingjay selling over 450,000 copies in its first week of release in the United States alone. The books have been praised for their fast-paced plot, well-developed characters, and thought-provoking themes, which have resonated with readers of all ages.

One of the defining features of Collins' writing is her ability to create complex and multi-dimensional characters, particularly female ones. Katniss Everdeen, the protagonist of The Hunger Games, is a prime example of this. She is strong-willed, resourceful, and fiercely protective of her loved ones, yet also vulnerable, haunted by her traumatic experiences, and struggling with her own moral compass.

Collins also explores the impact of trauma and violence on her characters, particularly in the context of war and conflict. She portrays the emotional toll that violence takes on individuals and communities and how it can lead to trauma, PTSD, and other mental health issues.

In addition to her novels, Collins has also written several picture books, including Year of the Jungle and When Charlie McButton Lost Power, as well as a science fiction series, The Underland Chronicles, which she wrote prior to The Hunger Games.

title: Tahereh Mafi Books
description:
Tahereh Mafi is a celebrated American author of Iranian descent, known for her bestselling book series, Shatter Me. Her unique writing style and captivating storytelling have earned her a dedicated fan base and critical acclaim.

Born in Connecticut in 1988, Mafi spent her childhood immersed in literature, always with a book in hand. She began writing at a young age, and her passion for storytelling only grew stronger with time. She graduated from the University of California, Irvine, with a degree in creative writing and went on to pursue a career in publishing.

Mafi's debut novel, Shatter Me, was published in 2011 and quickly became a New York Times bestseller. The book follows the story of Juliette Ferrars, a girl with a lethal touch who is imprisoned for her abilities. The series takes place in a dystopian world where the environment has been ravaged by climate change and a totalitarian government has taken over. Shatter Me is a gripping tale of romance, betrayal, and self-discovery that has captured the hearts of readers worldwide.

Mafi has since written several sequels to Shatter Me, including Unravel Me, Ignite Me, Restore Me, and Defy Me, as well as numerous novellas and spin-offs. Each instalment in the series delves deeper into the complex characters and their relationships, keeping readers on the edge of their seats.

She has also written other numerous books, such as A Very Large Expanse of Sea and An Emotion of Great Delight. One of her other famed titles includes the This Woven Kingdom Series. The series is a loose re-telling of the fairytale classic Cinderella story but with a Persian mythological twist of clashing empires, forbidden romance and a long-forgotten queen destined to save her people. Follow the story of Alizeh, a disposable servant who is also the long-lost heir to the ancient Jinn Kingdom, forced to seek refuge by hiding in plain sight. Equally, Prince Kamram has heard countless prophecies foretelling the death of his king. But when their paths inevitably cross, never would he have known that the servant girl with the strange eyes would one day soon uproot his kingdom- and the world. 

One of the most notable aspects of Mafi's writing style is her use of unique prose. Her poetic language and stream-of-consciousness narration create a vivid and immersive reading experience. She also employs striking metaphors and imagery to explore themes of identity, power, and love. Mafi's writing has been praised for its beauty and emotional depth, as well as its ability to keep readers hooked from start to finish.

In addition to her success as an author, Mafi is also a champion of diversity and inclusivity in literature. She has spoken out about the importance of representation in fiction and actively works to promote marginalized voices in the publishing industry.

Overall, Tahereh Mafi is a talented and inspiring author whose work has captivated readers of all ages. With her unique voice and compelling stories, she has earned a place among the most beloved young adult authors of our time. Whether you're a fan of dystopian fiction, romance, or just great storytelling, you won't want to miss out on the Shatter Me series.

title: Takeshi Obata Manga
description:
Takeshi Obata:
Takeshi Obata is synonymous with artistic brilliance in the world of manga, with his incredible talent and captivating storytelling. He was born on February 11, 1969, in Niigata, Japan. Obata's journey into the realm of manga began at a young age. His incredible dedication and unwavering passion for the art form have earned him a well-deserved place among the greatest manga artists of all time.

Obata's early years were filled with a deep fascination for comics and manga. His artistic talent was evident from the moment he could hold a pencil, and he soon began drawing his own characters and stories. This early interest set the stage for his future as one of the industry's most influential figures.

The turning point in Takeshi Obata's career came when he met writer Tsugumi Ohba, and together, they embarked on a creative journey that would leave an indelible mark on the manga world. Their collaboration gave birth to one of the most iconic and gripping series ever created, Death Note. 

At Books2Door, we proudly offer a curated collection of Takeshi Obata's works, including Death Note and Bakuman. Obata's artistry and storytelling prowess will leave you enthralled, whether you are a seasoned manga enthusiast or are new to Japanese comics.

Death Note: A Battle of Minds
Death Note is a psychological thriller that takes readers on a riveting journey through the twisted mind of a high school student named Light Yagami. When Light stumbles upon a mysterious notebook known as the Death Note, he gains the power to kill anyone by writing their name in it. What follows is a cat-and-mouse game between Light, who aims to rid the world of criminals, and the brilliant detective known only as L, who is determined to catch him.

Obata's meticulous artwork perfectly complements the intricate storyline of Death Note. His detailed character designs and dramatic use of Light and shadow enhance the tension and suspense, making each page a visual masterpiece. The series explores complex themes of morality, justice, and the consequences of absolute power, captivating readers with its thought-provoking narrative.

Bakuman: A Glimpse into the Manga Industry
Following the success of Death Note, Takeshi Obata continued to captivate audiences with another remarkable series, Bakuman. Teaming up once again with Tsugumi Ohba, they shifted their focus from the world of crime and punishment to the inner workings of the manga industry.

Bakuman provides readers with a fascinating behind-the-scenes look at the challenges and trials aspiring manga artists face as they strive to make a name for themselves. The story follows the journey of two young manga creators, Moritaka Mashiro and Akito Takagi, as they navigate the competitive world of manga publication. Obata's skilful portrayal of the character's emotions and the intricate details of the manga-making process make Bakuman an engaging and educational experience.

In conclusion, Taylor Jenkins Reid is a talented author whose work has captured the hearts of readers around the world. Her ability to write deeply emotional and relatable stories is what sets her apart, and her book series, including The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo and Daisy Jones & The Six, are must-reads for anyone looking for a beautifully written and engaging story. Her life and work continue to inspire many, and we look forward to seeing what she will write next.

title: Terry Deary Books
description:
A popular British children’s author, Terry Deary has published over 320 fiction and non-fiction books in the last 40 years. He has also sold over 33 million copies that have been translated into 40 languages. One of the most recognised works of Deary is the bestselling children’s book series Horrible Histories, which has been widely adapted and re-imagined as a television series on BBC, stage shows, and has even inspired a film.

Deary however wears several other hats—apart from being a bestselling children’s author, he has also pursued a career in acting, film, and singing across films, books obviously, television and radio. Whilst Deary’s work spans across mediums and formats of storytelling; his most popular works are centred around content for children, with a special focus on history.

 

A strong advocate of education beyond schools, Deary is an outspoken critic of conventional school culture, which he believes was a Victorian idea to keep kids off the streets and the same ideologies reflect in his work. He has, for instance, famously called to "ban Horrible Histories from schools", because he believes "classrooms take all the fun out of his stories". This brings us back to the author’s ability to make educational books fun. A perfect example of which is the Horrible Histories books series. The books in the series pack all sorts of absurd, disgusting, horrendous, and fun events of history, most of which you may not have been taught in school but only through these peculiar books. Some of the highlighted periods in this series include Stone Age and World War 2 amongst others.

Much like Terry Deary, we at Books2Door are also strong advocates of children reading beyond the school curriculum and that is precisely why we have stocked up on Terry Deary’s books. All of which are fun and more reader-friendly versions of educational books.

An engaging story about the culture of Ancient Egypt; this is a tale of Neria, who works in the House of Death helping her father make mummies. Neria enjoys her work, but when the pharaoh dies, everyone is so busy that Neria is given the responsibility of mummifying the pharaoh's cat, to accompany him to the afterlife. The trouble is, Neria doesn't want to kill and gut the cat! Can she find a way to save it without being caught and punished? Terry Deary's Egyptian Tales thus explores the world of Ancient Egypt through the eyes of children. His stories feature real people and take place in some of the most iconic Egyptian times. The new editions of the book also feature notes for the reader to help extend learning and exploration of the historic Egyptian period. 

A fresh take on the classic Horrible Histories style—Vile Victorians by Terry Deary is a horribly hilarious read that exposes foul facts about the Vile Victorians. This one is a fun but informative read, designed to educate children whilst also keeping them glued to the reading habit.

The second book of a spellbinding new fiction series from Terry Deary; Wiggott's Wonderful Waxworld 2: Fire Flight welcomes young readers to the strange town of Wildpool. There's a new mayor in Wildpool (though not the one that everyone voted for!) and there's a danger the Ladies Who Crunch will be forced to move home and that Wiggott's Wonderful Waxworld - about to be reopened - will actually be demolished. Can Molly and Boy save the day? Will Wildpool ever be the same? This one by Deary is a leisure fiction read for your little ones aged 7+.

title: Terry Pratchett Books
description:
Terry Pratchett was the master of satire, fantasy, and children's literature. He holds the honour of being one of the most shoplifted authors. The Discworld series is still loved by fans across the world, and his collaboration with Neil Gaiman, Good Omens, has gained new popularity after its adaptation as a TV series starring Michael Sheen and David Tennant.

Sir Terry Pratchett OBE has written over fifty bestselling novels. His first book, The Carpet People, was published in 1971, and his last novel, The Shepherd's Crown, was published in August 2015, five months after his death. He wrote science fiction, fantasy and children’s novels over his career and is still considered one of the greatest British authors of all time. 

Pratchett collaborated with numerous different authors throughout his career. One was Science Fiction author Stephen Baxter. Together they released a series based around parallel Earths The first book, The Long Earth, was published in 2012. For all five books in the series, check out The Long Earth by Terry Pratchett & Stephen Baxter: The Complete Books. 

He’s also well-known as an author of children's books. The Johnny Maxwell series follows a young boy living in an English town as he encounters aliens, ghosts and time travel. The book also deals with real issues like Johnny’s parents splitting up and his struggle to fit into the usual school cliques. We have the three Johnny Maxwell books available in our Johnny Maxwell Complete Collection. 

Another great Pratchett series for children is The Bromeliad Trilogy. These books follow a tiny group called the Nomes that are hidden amongst people. This series is also called The Nome Trilogy and is great for 9-11-year-olds. 

Discworld 

Discworld is the fictional setting of one of the most iconic series, and there are a total of 41 Discworld novels. All the Discworld novels take place in a flat, circular world which sits on the back of four elephants, which stand on the back of a giant star turtle. Although this world may look and sound completely different to our own, the Discworld novels explore a multitude of very human issues. 

The first book in the series is The Colour of Magic; however, the books can be read in any order. If you are new to the series and you aren’t sure where to start, check out our Terry Pratchett's Discworld Starter Collection 4 Books Set. 

Collaboration with Neil Gaiman 

In 1990 Good Omens: The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch was released. The book follows the Angel Aziraphale and the demon Crowley as they try to prevent the end times after the birth of the antichrist. Both Aziraphale and Crowley have grown fond of their lives in England and therefore set out to save the Earth. Written by two iconic British authors, Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman, the comedic triumph is a perfect read for any fantasy fan. For more books by Neil Gaiman, check out our Neil Gaiman Collection. 

For more books within a similar genre, check out our Sci-fi, Fantasy and Horror section!

title: Tessa Bailey Books
description:
Dive into Passionate Romances with Tessa Bailey Books!

Welcome to Books2Door, where we take great pride in offering an extensive collection of literary gems. Among our most sought-after offerings are the books by acclaimed author Tessa Bailey. For more romance books, why not check out our incredible collection of Romance Books and Family Sagas? 

It Happened One Summer & and Hook, Line, and Sinker 2 Book Bundle

It Happened One Summer and Hook, Line, and Sinker 2 Book Bundle is a captivating collection that will leave you breathless. It brings together two standalone novels that showcase Tessa Bailey's talent for creating compelling stories.

In It Happened One Summer, you'll meet the fierce and determined Piper Bellinger, a privileged socialite who finds herself exiled to a small coastal town. Unprepared for the challenges that await her, Piper crosses paths with Brendan, a brooding fisherman whose rough exterior hides a heart of gold. In this enemies-to-lovers romance, as they clash and come together in a whirlwind of emotions, they discover that love can bloom in the most unexpected places.

In Hook, Line, and Sinker, prepare to be swept off your feet by Captain Jamie "Fish" Hooker. A former Navy SEAL turned charter boat captain, Jamie is used to being in control. But when his childhood crush, who is now a sexy romance author, joins him on a fishing trip, he finds himself caught in a storm of desire and longing. Their chemistry is undeniable, but can they overcome their past and navigate the treacherous waters of love?

Both novels in this bundle offer a delightful blend of scorching chemistry, delightful humour, and heartwarming moments that will make you believe in the power of love. Indulge in these captivating stories, and you'll be hooked from the very first page.

Hot and Hammered 3 Book Series

If you're looking for a series that will keep you hooked until the last page, the Hot and Hammered series is the perfect choice. This series takes place in the small town of Port Jefferson, where sparks fly and passions ignite.

In Fix Her Up, we meet Georgie Castle, a talented clown-turned-party planner, and Travis Ford, a former major league baseball player. When Travis returns to his hometown, Georgie sees an opportunity to transform the man she's always admired from afar. As they embark on a fake relationship, their connection deepens, and they discover that love can be found even in the most unlikely circumstances. Fans of fake dating tropes are guaranteed to love this steamy romance!

The second book, Love Her or Lose Her, introduces us to Rosie and Dominic Vega, high school sweethearts whose marriage has lost its spark. Determined to save their relationship, Rosie takes a leap of faith and enlists the help of a marriage boot camp. As they confront their past and rekindle their passion, they discover that true love is worth fighting for.

In the third book, Tools of Engagement, we follow the story of hair salon owner Bethany Castle and Wes Daniels, the uptight contractor she can't stand. Forced to work together on a charity renovation project, they clash at every turn. But beneath the surface, a scorching attraction simmers, and they soon realise that their differences might be what bring them closer together.

With its engaging characters, steamy romance, and a healthy dose of humour, the Hot and Hammered series is a must-read for fans of contemporary romance. Get ready to lose yourself in the world of Port Jefferson, where love and happily-ever-afters await.

Whether you're seeking stories filled with sizzling chemistry or heartwarming moments, these books deliver. Available in stock at Books2Door, these captivating novels are waiting to be discovered by romance enthusiasts craving a dose of love, laughter, and happily-ever-afters. Dive into Tessa Bailey's enchanting world today and prepare to be swept off your feet!

About the Author:

Tessa Bailey is a talented and highly acclaimed contemporary romance author known for her captivating storytelling, dynamic characters, and sizzling chemistry. Her books have garnered a devoted following and have earned her numerous accolades and awards within the romance genre.

With her signature blend of passion, humour, and emotion, Tessa Bailey has a unique ability to bring her characters to life and create stories that resonate with readers. Her writing style is often described as engaging, fast-paced, and infused with a healthy dose of steamy romance. She excels at crafting witty banter and creating intense, electric connections between her protagonists, making her books a thrilling and addictive reading experience.

Tessa Bailey's novels span various subgenres within the romance category, including contemporary romance, romantic comedy, and erotic romance. Whether she's writing about small-town romances, workplace dynamics, or enemies-to-lovers relationships, Tessa Bailey consistently delivers stories that are both emotionally satisfying and delightfully entertaining.

Whether you're a longtime fan of Tessa Bailey or just discovering her work, you can expect to be swept away by her captivating storytelling and unforgettable characters. Her books offer a perfect escape into the world of love, desire, and happily-ever-afters.

description:

title: The Adventures of Tintin Books
description:
European comic strip The Adventures of Tintin is among the most popular in print. It made its creator Georges Remi, better known as the Belgian cartoonist Hergé, one of the most influential artists in the world. His work influenced everyone from Andy Warhol to Charles de Gaulle. The comic was adapted into a movie in 2011 by Steven Spielberg and Peter Jackson.

The bande dessinées of The Adventures of Tintin were serialised continuously in Belgian newspaper Le Vingtième Siècle from 1929 to May 1940, when the German occupation shut the paper down. Serialisation resumed in Tintin magazine from 1948 to 1967, and Studio Hergé created the BD from 1950. A final story, Tintin and the Picaros, was serialised between 1975 and 1976. The stories were reprinted as BD albums nearly every year from 1930 to 1944 and 1948 to 1954. After this, six completed albums were released, the last in 1976.

The Adventures of Tintin follows a character called Tintin, an adventuresome and fearless wander or traveller that journeys across the world to explore the wonders we dreamed of. Along his way, he is supported by trusted friends like Captain Haddock, who is always weary but self-assertive, Professor Calculus, and the cute little dog Snowy which accompanies Tintin’s side in every new adventure, truly a devoted and loyal friend!

In each book, you explore the astonishment and awe of real places in this world, from historical locations to the wild uncharted areas, as well as fictional areas. Herge collected historical pieces combined with his imagination to create this series, and using his experience as an illustrator and storytelling he entertained many children around.

This series was translated to over 80 languages and sold more than 230 million copies worldwide, a popular series of meticulously illustrated books of the 20th century. Some popular titles in this series include The Secret of the Unicorn, Destination Moon and The Blue Lotus. The variety of plots includes daring adventures that mix in with action, fantasy, mysteries, science with embarrassing humour. Explore the amazing book sets in this category or browse other series here.

title: The Bad Guys Books
description:
What happens when you cross a gang of animal crooks trying their best to do good and show people they aren’t really that bad? Well, you get the Bad Guys! Join these anthropomorphic animals as they try to change society’s perception of them as notorious criminals by performing good deeds. But of course, things don’t always go as planned…

Now a major motion picture from Dreamworks, the studio behind How to Train Your Dragon and Shrek starring Sam Rockwell, Awkwafina, Anthony Ramos and more. Be sure to read The Bad Guys book series before heading out to see the film!

Buckle up for the funniest, naughtiest and coolest books you'll ever read! It's time to meet The Bad Guys...

About the series:

The infamous Bad Guys series is an illustrated children’s graphic novel by Australian children’s author Aaron Blabey. It centres around the adventures of a misfit gang of animal criminals who are on a quest to desperately prove that they aren’t as bad as their species’ reputations may seem. Mr Wolf, Mr Snake, Mr Piranha, Mr Shark and Mr Tarantula are scary-looking and dangerous animals who are on a mighty mission to do some dangerously good deeds, but as we all know, plans often change and their efforts usually go slightly askew.

This series is a hilarious read full of snappy jokes and quips between good friends with lots of potty humour in between. The series’ overarching themes touch on heartfelt friendship and loyalty amidst all the disasters. Children can learn the importance of how things don’t always go according to plan in a fun and educational way. 

The Bad Guys collection is perfect for mischievous children. Primarily aged for children aged 6-9, these books are filled with action-packed adventures mixed with some hilarious jokes and fun. Getting your children to read doesn't always have to be boring. This rib-tickling collection of adventurous animals brings some exciting action and adventure to reading for both children and adults. With a combination of laugh-out-loud illustrations and text, this book series makes for a fun and easy read to keep your children entertained and engaged for hours on end.

Fans of Aaron Blabey’s best-selling series should be sure to check out Dav Pilkey’s Captain Underpants series for more hilarious adventures, or even the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series by Jeff Kinney. There’s guaranteed to be something for everyone!

About the Author: 

Aaron Blabey is an Australian author of some of the best-selling children’s books. Until the mid-200s he was also an actor, best known for his lead roles in two Australian television dramedies. He is the creator of the graphic novel series The Bad Guys, and the author behind the two picture book series Pig the Pug and Thelma the Unicorn. Blabey has around 30 million books currently in print, with his books spending over 120 weeks on the New York Times Bestseller List. He is also the co-executive producer of The Bad Guys movie and the upcoming Netflix movie-musical adaptation of Thelma the Unicorn.
