Mog the cat has been a staple title on children’s bookshelves for many years, the combination of beautiful storytelling alongside the illustration makes for a beautiful read. The books remain very popular today as children love reading about Mog’s adventures and seeing the world through her eyes. For our full Judith Kerr collection click here. 

Similarly, Oliver Jeffers' The Day the Crayons Quit was an instant bestseller, not only does it have vibrant illustrations and easy-to-read handwritten letter style but it has a very prevalent message about workers' rights and equality as well as a great way to learn colours as they lodge their complaints to a young boy who is just trying to colour in with them. 

Year 2 students are expected to have a clear understanding of phonics and sounding out words themselves. By using picture books such as these they will have the images to refer to when attempting to sound out new words. 

Magical Stories 

At this age children’s imaginations are starting to develop more and might be starting to create their own stories. Reading something fantastical and magical could help inspire their creativity so finding some of the best year 2 books to suit their abilities and imagination will encourage them to keep reading. 


Rainbow Magic Fairy series in total has over 200 books, we have a collection of 52 different stories ranging from Sky the Blue fairy to Marissa the science fairy. The wide variety of themes within the rainbow magic series will keep any child entertained for a very long time. Our collection A Year of Rainbow Magic aims to encourage children to read a book a week for the whole year. They are the perfect book for a child beginning to read independently or if you wish to read with them. They are wonderful and light-hearted stories, the illustrations within the books and the stories themselves make great year 2 books, often children will continue to read the series throughout KS1 and beyond.

title: Year 3 Books
description:
During the early stages of Key Stage 2, Year three children start to further develop their language, literacy and vocabulary skills. That’s precisely why we, at Books2Door, have specially curated a list of amazing primary school books, recommended by teachers, to help make learning just that little bit easier! We’ve got an extensive collection of back-to-school books, featuring some of the most famous publishers from Penguin to Piccadilly Press that are perfect for all our little 7-year-old readers. Our collection of Key Stage two reading books has been specially hand-picked to ensure the perfect books are chosen by our mighty little readers. Featuring some of the most invigorating and adventurous titles, our selection has all the best books that are guaranteed to make your child’s imagination go wild. We’ve got an extensive collection of the greatest back-to-school books, featuring some of the most famous and best children’s book authors including popular series such as Captain Underpants, Horrid Henry and Dog Man. There’s definitely sure to be something for all our mighty young readers. 

Year 3 level literacy aims to introduce your child to a wide range of genres and writing styles for them to read and perform out loud. They will start to think about inference and begin to make predictions about what will happen in a story as they read. When looking at Key Stage two reading books, children will be able to start reading independently as well as participate in guided reading sessions with a teacher or an adult to help them understand the text and start to read with a purpose. Children will be able to explain what they have read in their own words, which is a great practice to help them gain confidence and boost their comprehension skills when reading. Our selection features some of the best children’s books that not only help to develop these essential reading skills but also kick-start their imaginations in a fun and engaging way to help make learning fun.

Each child is unique and experiences their own individual reading journey. As they grow, your child will start to celebrate new reading milestones as they begin to learn new words, develop new reading strategies and extend their range of vocabulary. From year 3, it becomes essential for your child to independently choose books for themselves and learn which books and genres they prefer. From this year onwards, your child will begin to experiment with different writing styles and authors to find out which style suits them. Guided reading sessions with a teacher or an adult will help to feed your child’s imagination and opens up a treasure-house of wonder and joy for curious young minds. 

As the year progresses, your child will start to further develop their language, literacy and vocabulary skills through reading. That is why our teachers’ picks feature a broad variety and range of books for even the pickiest little readers that want to explore the wide selection of collections and box sets available for you at an affordable price. We, at Books2Door aim, to make reading a fun and enjoyable experience for your little ones by providing a diverse range of affordable collections and box sets for children to explore as they go back to school. Our teachers’ selection features a range of books for readers of all abilities to develop at their own pace to improve and progress their reading ability and gain confidence along the way.

Fan Favourite books for 7-year-olds

Avid 7-year-old readers who love to have some hilariously fun adventures will enjoy the popular titles by award-winning author and illustrator Dave Pilkey. The Captain Underpants book set features 10 titles that are full of wacky ideas, naughty schoolboy errors and big, bad plots. Join Harold and George as they become waistband warriors in this hilarious collection as the duo try to save the world with the right blend of seriousness and silliness. Evil villains like Professor Poopypants and the Wicked Wedgie Woman are no match for the mighty pair.

Fans of Dave Pilkey will also love his Dog Man book collection which was the top-selling £1 fiction title for World Book Day in 2020. Featuring the mighty Dog Man, a fearless cop with the head of a dog and the body of a man, who is on a mission to protect the city with his best friends. Readers aged 7-8 will explore rib-tickling jokes and adventures exploring positive themes of kindness, persistence and the importance of being true to one’s self. This hilariously funny series features the adventures of the crime-fighting canine that is the perfect book collection for 7-year-olds. 

Francesca Simon’s best-selling Horrid Henry series is the perfect book for year three children. Join our horrid hero in a series of 30 hilarious books featuring the naughtiest boy in the whole world with wacky illustrations by Tony Ross. Readers are in for a treat as the wickedest boy in town wreaks hilarious havoc on his pesky neighbour Moody Margaret, his bogey babysitter and even the queen!? With the most rule-breaking trickery and elaborate practical jokes, kids are in for a rib-tickling adventure with the nation's most horrid boy and his most admired little brother, Perfect Peter. Join Horrid Henry as he causes mayhem and mischief with his friends. These books are an enjoyable way to integrate reading with literacy and comprehension skills for an enjoyable read of mischief and mayhem for both children and parents.

Finished these titles and want to try something brand new and challenging to improve your reading skills? Try our selected top teachers’ picks for Year 4 books, with a whole new selection of quality book box sets and collections for those mighty older readers eager for a new and exciting challenge.

title: Year 4 Books
description:
Year 4 book club

Children are expected to begin to explore different books in a variety of genres within this school year. They are also expected to start reading more difficult books and explore language and grammar more in-depth. With this in mind, our Year 4 books collection aims to make selecting their next read a little easier and give you some guidance as to what your child may want to try next. 

Year 4 curriculum highlights the importance of active participation in conversations, asking appropriate questions and imagination. Meaning their reading level and reading material may begin to change and broaden their reading genres. Offering them a wide selection of books with different subject matters, narrators and writing styles. 

Finding your child’s next read 

Have they already read Roald Dahl? If so they may want to enter the world of David Walliams. You may have seen the adaptations of his novels on TV, however, there is nothing like reading the original text. Illustrated by Tony Ross and Quentin Blake, the man who brought Roald Dahl’s classics to life, these books bring hilarious humour and unique stories into the heart of the reader's imagination. 

Diary of a Wimpy Kid has become a household name. With the live-action and animated adaptations of the infamous series, it is impossible to miss them. They are brilliantly animated and have important messages and relatable characters. The first in the series is set around the main character, Greg, starting middle school and juggling with the fear of older students and the stress of growing up all told through drawings and diary entries. If your child has read Diary of a Wimpy Kid and enjoyed it, they should check out Planet Omar. 

Diverse year 4 books 

Planet Omar follows 9-year-old Omar as he moves house and changes school in the first instalment of the series. The book not only has a similar writing style to Diary of a Wimpy Kid but it also educates young readers on other cultures, for example in the first book Omar talks about his excitement for Eid. This title is a fantastic example of diverse children’s books, as it does educate some readers about other cultures but it also is very important for children to be able to read about characters that may have the same beliefs and cultural background as them. 

The No.1 Car Spotter by Atinuke is another example of diverse and beautifully written children’s literature. Set in Nigeria, these stories are very highly entertaining but also important for young readers based outside of Africa to introduce them to different cultures and different childhoods as well as children or their families that may have had a similar lived experience as the narrator, No.1. The books are also set out in short chapters which is a great introduction to reading chapters to young readers. 

Anisha, Accidental Detective follows 10-year-old Anisha as she has to solve the case of her missing Uncle Tony before his wedding to Aunty Bindi. This hilarious and fast-paced series follows Anisha’s adventures with her multi-generational British Indian family and her best friend Milo. 

Horrible Histories

Horrible Histories is now a well-known TV series in its own right, however, the original books by Terry Deary are still fantastic. The combination of gruesome unusual facts presented with comedic delivery has made these books so enjoyable to read. Often the facts included in the books aren’t something children would learn at school, the facts are delivered in memorable and gory ways which are bound to keep most children and adults entertained. The books are excellent as they are captivating and interesting to read but they’re also historically accurate. Starting to read Deary’s books may spark an interest in history that they may not have felt from their school history lessons alone. Our Horrible Histories Savage Collection contains eight books including Awful Egyptians, Rotten Romans and Vicious Vikings and many more. Take a look at our Terry Deary Collection for our full selection of Horrible History titles. 

DK Find Out

If they have enjoyed Horrible Histories, or maybe they enjoy learning the facts but not the gruesome details, we have a DK Find out Collection. This collection delves deep into the animal kingdom, science, space and more. As well as the clear and informative information, these books are set out with lots of photos and visual elements to help them to picture the details it is teaching them about. DK has been publishing detailed reference books for children for many years. Meaning that they have a unique style and highly knowledgeable content aimed directly at young readers. 

Also from DK is our First Encyclopaedia, this two-book collection contains lots of information to keep the reader occupied for hours. One book is about how things work, from magnets to sound waves and from search engines to what makes rockets fly. The other encyclopaedia covers geography including human, physical and geology. Explaining how our planet works, including weather, different environments and other important skills and facts like how to use maps and global warming. 

Children’s Classics 

At this age, children may want to explore some classics like E.B. White’s Charlotte's Web or Stuart Little. Both have well-known film adaptations which, if they have seen them, could inspire them to read the books. Our Collection contains three classic children’s literature titles but E.B. White, they are a great introduction to longer books with more grown-up themes. 

Another childhood classic is The Magic Faraway Tree Collection by Enid Blyton. Our collection contains the four books from the series by one of the world’s best-loved children’s authors. Blyton’s books have been bestsellers for over eighty years with titles like The Famous Five and Malory Towers. They have provided hours of entertainment for adults and children alike. For more Enid Blyton books, see our full collection here. 

Study Guides

A lot of children will be feeling exam pressure ready for their SATS in year 6. We have a selection of KS2 revision guides and exam practice exercise books to help prepare them and allow them to feel more confident working in exam conditions. Our Quick 10 Minute Test books will help them practise their Maths and English skills, particularly focusing on verbal and non-verbal reasoning as well as core topics within their key stage. 

We also have individual CGP year 4 KS2 revision books and practise papers available to order. We have CGP KS2 Maths and English SATS practise papers or Practise KS2 English and Maths Activity Books specifically aimed at year 4 students. 

Here at Books2door we take pride in our passion for Children’s Literature and encouraging children to read. This collection aims to suggest the best year 4 books that might suit your child's interests.

title: Year 5 Books
description:
As your child enters Year 5, they reach the intermediate stage of Key Stage two learning. At Books2Door, we have specially curated a list of the best children’s books for 9-year-olds as they enter the new school year. Our back-to-school books range features a compiled collection of teachers’ top picks that are perfect for all adventurous readers aged 9-10. Our collection of Key Stage two reading books has been specially hand-picked and recommended by teachers to ensure the perfect books are chosen by our mighty little readers. Featuring some of the most invigorating and adventurous titles, our selection has all the best books that are guaranteed to make your child’s imagination go wild! We’ve got an extensive collection of Key Stage two reading books from a range of best-selling popular authors including C.S. Lewis, Jill Murphy and even Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. There’s guaranteed to be something interesting for 9-year-old bookworms of all reading abilities.

During Year 5, your child will further develop their reading and comprehension skills further to help them become more independent and confident readers. At this stage, their vocabulary and language have become more complex and their focus is on developing these skills to identify language, structure and presentation in texts. In KS2 reading books, they will be able to spot recurring themes, ask questions about the various books they have read and also summarise the information or plot in a book as they have understood it. Reading widely and often increases your child’s vocabulary because they encounter words that they would rarely hear or use in everyday speech. As a result, your child starts to build on and extend their own bank of vocabulary which will help them as they progress through school.

In year 5, children will start to be able to identify and analyse figurative language features and their intended effect on the reader. They will also discuss their understanding of the meaning of words in context and improve on their inference skills by justifying identifications made in the narrative with evidence from the text. During this year, it is crucial to maintain and improve your child’s reading ability as they continue to develop their love for reading by exploring different authors and genres. Implementing guided reading sessions with a teacher or an adult will help to feed your child’s imagination and opens up a treasure-house of wonder and joy for curious young minds.

Fan Favourite books for 9-year-olds

Junior-level primary school books are perfect for helping children to continue to develop their literacy and comprehension skills and build the necessary skills to transform them into confident and passionate readers. Browse through our selection of top teachers’ picks, there’s sure to be something for everyone. During Year 5, children will be able to read from an increasingly wide range of books, with texts that are both modern and old. Don’t worry we have plenty of simplified and children-friendly classics for Year five children to explore. Check out our box set of The Sherlock Holmes Children’s Collection, the perfect books for year five children. With engaging illustrations, this simplification of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s Sherlock Holmes stories easily introduces children to the world of mystery books and classics. 

Is your child not a fan of mystery books? Well, don’t worry we have a wide range of classics for your child to discover. Have a look at our “easy classics” including the Shakespeare’s Children Stories Book Collection by Macaw Books. This captivating collection of classic Shakespearean tales features 20 of the most beautifully narrated plays, simplified for an easy read, alongside enchanting illustrations that children are guaranteed to love. Our classics don’t stop there, be sure to check out Tracy Mayhew’s The Legends of King Arthur Books Box Set. In a modern retelling of the Arthurian legends, this collection of “easy classics” has been adapted and illustrated, perfect for Year 5 children wanting to delve into classic folklore. Explore epic battles, thrilling quests and forbidden love combined in the medieval story of the boy who would be king. 

For readers still exploring new and different genres, check out our fantastic range of children’s fantasy books ideal for transporting young minds into the most fantastical adventures. Adam Blade’s Beast Quest The Battle Collection contains all the books from series 4,5, and 6. For those who are fans of the first three series, young readers can expect to move on to the epic next steps in the series. As a popular choice for both parents and children, these best-selling children’s books provide plenty of mystery, fantasy and adventure as your child dives into the excitement with Tom and Elenna in Avantia, where the clever pair attempt to restore peace to the land by stopping magnificent beasts from causing mayhem and destruction.

Why not check out The Chronicles Of Narnia book collection? This beautiful edition features 7 titles of the popular children’s fantasy series complete with cover and interior art by the original illustrator, Pauline Baynes. Let your 9-year-old discover the magic and wonder of Narnia as they adventure with Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy Pensive in the English countryside from London. With the help of Aslan, a talking lion, the Pensive children must save Narnia from the evil White Witch who has reigned over the land for a century of perpetual winter with no Christmas. This collection is the perfect collection for those Key Stage 2 readers that love the hero and villain's trope alongside positive messages of courage and forgiveness in the face of danger. 

Finished these titles and want to try something brand new and challenging to improve your reading skills? Try our selected top teachers’ picks for Year 6 books, with a new selection of advanced, quality book sets and collections for those confident older readers eager to explore a new and exciting challenge.

title: Year 6 Books
description:
As your child reaches the final level of Key Stage 2, their literacy skills will have become more developed and grown over time since starting their reading journey. At this stage, your child has mastered the basics of reading and comprehension and it becomes essential to maintain these skills that they have learned. That’s precisely why we, at Books2Door, have specially curated a list of primary school books perfectly fit for junior-level readers, recommended by teachers, to help make learning just that little bit easier. Our collection of Key Stage two reading books has been specially hand-picked and recommended by teachers to ensure the perfect books are chosen by our mighty little readers. Featuring some of the most invigorating and adventurous titles, our selection has all the best books that are guaranteed to make your child’s imagination go wild! We’ve got an extensive collection of back-to-school books, featuring some of the most famous and best children’s book authors including J.K. Rowling, Rick Riordan and even Jaqueline Wilson and more- a perfect selection fit for all our mighty 10 year-old readers. 

Our selection of Key Stage two reading books has been specially hand-picked and recommended by teachers that are the perfect books for 10-year-olds. Reading widely and often increases your child’s vocabulary because they encounter words that they would rarely hear or use in everyday speech. As a result, your child starts to build on and extend their own bank of vocabulary which will help them as they progress through school. Reading for fun and with a purpose helps to feed your child’s imagination and opens up a treasure-house of wonder and joy for curious young minds. Our list features some of the boldest and most adventuresome titles that are guaranteed to make your child’s imagination go wild. Lead them on quests of bravery with the Alex Rider Collection, experience twisting tales and terrible frights with the Goosebumps Series, or join the exhilarating seaside adventures with the Mallory Towers Collection- there’s guaranteed to be something for everyone.

Year 6 level literacy aims to bridge the gap between KS2 and KS3 by enabling children to become increasingly independent in their reading and comprehension abilities. At this stage, their vocabulary and language have become more complex and their focus is on developing these skills to identify language, structure and presentation in texts. In Key Stage two reading books, they will be able to spot recurring themes, ask questions about the various books they have read and also summarise the information or plot in a book as they have understood it. A mixture of independent reading and guided reading with a teacher or adult allows for children to advance their inference on a broader level by discussing characters’ feelings through providing evidence. By doing this, children can comprehend the book at their own pace and develop the ability to discuss literary features such as language and plot development, which is a key skill necessary for the transition into secondary education. 

Fan Favourite books for 10-year-olds

Our year 6 children’s books are perfect for readers that want to experience adventurous quests with righteous heroes. Harry Potter is nothing short of a household name with the global success of blockbuster movies. Check out J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter Complete Collection Book Set, based on the well-loved book series. A tale of magic and wonder is in store for those that want to join the famous trio, Harry, Ron and Hermione on a wondrous journey at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Meeting new foes, the trio must stick together and help uncover the secrets of the dark Lord Voldemort.

If your child has read Harry Potter, then they should definitely check out the Percy Jackson Collection Books Set by Rick Riordan. For readers that want to learn more about greek mythology, this collection is a perfect starting point for readers aged 10-11. Join Percy Jackson and his best friends Grover, a satyr, and Annabeth, daughter of Athena as they journey across the US to catch a thief who has stolen the most mighty of weapons- Zeus’ infamous lightning bolt. These books are a fun way of getting children to discuss the plot in their own words and talk about the inference and motivations of the characters with these fast-paced, story-driven plots.

Want to read something more spooky and frightening? Our top picks features the Goosebumps: The Classic Series Collection. Those courageous readers that are brave enough to delve into R. L. Stine’s twisting and creepy box set are in for a series of thrills, frights and spooks to keep them on the edge of their seats. This collection features ten tales of slimy monsters, horrifying mummies, malicious garden gnomes and, of course, Slappy- the scariest ventriloquist dummy you’ll ever meet. This is the perfect book for 10-year-olds and fans of the brilliant and classic Goosebumps series. 

Advanced Readers’ Books

For those more advanced readers ready for a real challenge, why not have a look at The Complete Jane Austen Collection? Featuring 6 of her most popular titles, confident readers can start tackling some of the most respected classics in literature. Don’t be alarmed, they’re not as daunting as you think, your child will be a literature classics bookworm in no time! These original classics are slower-paced but provide a fun way to discuss some of the major themes and characters for those independent readers confident enough to delve into them.

Now that your child has mastered the basics of reading and comprehension, their unique reading journey starts to become an exciting experience for children as they explore new genres, meet new characters and delve deeper into heroic and mysterious adventures. No matter their reading ability, children should be encouraged to develop their independent reading skills and gain the confidence they need to thrive during their transition into secondary school. At Books2Door, our top teachers’ book picks for all year groups from Year 1 to Year 6 provide all the necessary tools for children to be able to grow and expand their reading capabilities. For parents and teachers, these books aimed at children of all reading levels provide avenues of discussion to help monitor your child’s progression and celebrate their achievements.
